about: Plain-language summaries of every plugin in the directory: what it does and the problem it solves. Written by Claude (AI) from each repo's README and descriptions, the most-downloaded on 2026-09-24 and the rest on 2026-11-06; not part of the deterministic census. Keyed by GitHub owner/repo.

retorquere/zotero-better-bibtex.does: Generates stable, clash-free citation keys and exports to BibTeX/BibLaTeX with proper Unicode-to-LaTeX conversion. Auto-export rewrites your .bib file whenever a collection changes.
retorquere/zotero-better-bibtex.pain: Writing in LaTeX or Markdown with Zotero's stock export means unstable keys, mangled special characters and re-exporting by hand. BBT keeps a live, correct .bib file your documents can rely on.

windingwind/zotero-better-notes.does: Turns Zotero's note editor into a knowledge workspace: linked notes with backlinks and outlines, templates that build notes from metadata and annotations, two-way Markdown sync, and export to Word, PDF or mind maps.
windingwind/zotero-better-notes.pain: Stock Zotero notes are isolated, hard to structure and hard to get out. Better Notes lets you build a connected knowledge base without moving to another app.

windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates text as you select it in the PDF, EPUB or web reader, plus titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services (Google, DeepL, LLMs and more) and a dictionary for single words.
windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading papers in a second language means constant copy-paste into a translation site. This puts the translation next to the text and can save it with your annotations.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-reference.does: Adds a reader sidebar listing the paper's references, parsed from the PDF or fetched from Crossref, Semantic Scholar or arXiv. Preview any reference's abstract and add it to your library in one click, linked to the paper that cited it.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-reference.pain: Following a citation normally means scrolling to the bibliography, copying the title and searching for it. This lets you explore and collect references from where you're reading.

l0o0/jasminum.does: Fetches metadata for Chinese-language PDFs from CNKI, matches manually downloaded PDF/CAJ files to their items, installs community Chinese translators and citation styles, and splits or merges Chinese author names.
l0o0/jasminum.pain: Zotero handles Chinese literature poorly: lookups fail and CNKI saves often arrive without the file. Jasminum is the standard fix for Chinese-language research.

syt2/zotero-addons.does: A plugin store inside Zotero: browse, search, install and comment on community plugins from a curated index, with Gitee and proxy mirrors for users who can't reach GitHub.
syt2/zotero-addons.pain: Zotero has no official plugin directory, so finding plugins means hunting through GitHub and installing .xpi files by hand.

northword/zotero-format-metadata.does: Lints item metadata: sentence-case titles with rich text (italics, sub/superscript), journal abbreviations, language detection, normalized dates, DOIs and pages, duplicate warnings on import, and one-click refresh from a DOI or arXiv ID.
northword/zotero-format-metadata.pain: Imported metadata is inconsistent, and the errors surface later as messy bibliographies. Linter fixes them in bulk, at the source.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger.does: Manages attachment files: attach your latest download to an item with one shortcut, rename files with Zotero's naming template, and move them into a folder tree built from metadata or collections, ready for Dropbox or OneDrive.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger.pain: Zotero stores files in folders named by opaque item keys, and ZotFile doesn't run on Zotero 7+. Attanger is its modern replacement for keeping PDFs in a readable, syncable folder.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-citation.does: Speeds up citing in Microsoft Word: insert the selected Zotero item at the cursor with the ' key or by drag-and-drop, merge adjacent citations ([1][2] becomes [1, 2]), and gather everything a document cites into a Zotero collection.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-citation.pain: Zotero's Word add-in makes you open a search dialog for every citation and never shows what a document cites. This brings citing closer to EndNote's workflow.

jlegewie/zotfile.does: The classic attachment manager: renames and moves PDFs into a custom folder, attaches new downloads, sends PDFs to a tablet folder and back, and extracts PDF annotations into notes.
jlegewie/zotfile.pain: It solved file clutter and mobile reading before Zotero had its own reader and renaming. It only runs on Zotero 6 and is unmaintained, so its downloads are mostly historical; ZotMoov and Attanger took over.

redleafnew/zotero-updateifsE.does: Adds journal-ranking columns from easyScholar: JCR quartile, CAS partition, impact factor, EI, and Chinese core lists such as CSCD and the Peking and Nanjing lists. Also journal abbreviations, metadata refresh and author/title fix-ups. Needs a free easyScholar key.
redleafnew/zotero-updateifsE.pain: Researchers in China constantly need a journal's tier when choosing what to read or where to publish. Green Frog shows it for every item instead of requiring a separate lookup.

windingwind/zotero-actions-tags.does: A rules engine for Zotero: run actions (add or remove tags, run custom scripts) when an item is added, opened or closed, or from a shortcut or menu. Comes with a community library of ready-made scripts.
windingwind/zotero-actions-tags.pain: Library chores like tagging unread papers, copying item links or translating new titles are repetitive. This automates them without writing a plugin.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-style.does: Restyles the item list with new columns: reading time per page shown behind the title, annotation density, bold for unread, tag and journal-rank columns, and ratings. Adds saved column layouts, nested tags, quick filters and a graph view.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-style.pain: The stock list shows only bibliographic fields, so you can't see what you've read, how far you got or which journals rank highly. This puts reading state and rank in the main view.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-figure.does: Detects and extracts figures, tables and equations with their captions, using a model that runs locally inside the plugin. Browse and compare them across papers, copy them, or add them to notes. Formula-to-LaTeX is optional via SiliconFlow.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-figure.pain: Getting a figure out of a paper means screenshots and cropping, and comparing results across papers means flipping between PDFs. This builds a figure library instead.

dvanoni/notero.does: Syncs items from chosen Zotero collections into a Notion database, one page per item with its metadata, and optionally its notes and annotations. Pages update when items change and link back to Zotero.
dvanoni/notero.pain: People who plan and write in Notion otherwise re-enter references by hand. Notero keeps a Notion reading list in step with Zotero automatically.

ChenglongMa/zoplicate.does: Catches duplicates the moment you import and asks whether to keep the new copy, the old one or both, then merges without losing attachments or notes. Also bulk-merges existing duplicates and remembers false positives.
ChenglongMa/zoplicate.pain: Zotero's duplicate pane works only after the fact, one pair at a time, so large libraries pile up duplicates that are tedious to clean.

syt2/zotero-scipdf.does: Registers Sci-Hub mirrors as a Zotero PDF resolver, so Find Full Text and automatic downloads fetch papers from Sci-Hub for any item with a DOI.
syt2/zotero-scipdf.pain: Researchers without institutional access hit paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

018/zotcard.does: Card-based note-taking: templates for concept, quote, character and review cards pre-filled from item fields, plus tools to batch-edit, sort, print, randomly review and chart your cards.
018/zotcard.pain: Zettelkasten-style reading notes need consistent structure, and Zotero's blank notes give none. ZotCard makes writing uniform, atomic cards quick.

wileyyugioh/zotmoov.does: Moves or copies attachments into a folder you choose as linked files, automatically on import or by right-click. Deletes the file when you delete the item, and attaches the newest file from a folder.
wileyyugioh/zotmoov.pain: A lightweight ZotFile successor for Zotero 7+. It keeps PDFs in your own synced folder, so you don't need Zotero's paid file storage.

volatile-static/Chartero.does: Records which pages you read and for how long, then charts it: per-item dashboards, a library overview, a progress column, a scrollbar minimap of read pages and annotations, and a sidebar of every image in the PDF.
volatile-static/Chartero.pain: Zotero doesn't track reading at all. Chartero shows what you've actually read and where your time went.

redleafnew/delitemwithatt.does: Deletes an item or a whole collection together with its files, linked files on disk included. Adds shortcuts to delete only attachments, snapshots or notes, or to clear the Abstract and Extra fields.
redleafnew/delitemwithatt.pain: Deleting an item in Zotero leaves linked files behind, so disks fill with orphans. This removes them in the same step; linked files skip the trash, so it's irreversible.

yilewang/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI assistant in the reader: chat with a PDF, selection, figures or several papers, with citations that jump to the source passage. Saves answers to notes or Markdown; agent mode can search, tag and organize the library. Works with API keys, local models, ChatGPT, Codex or Claude Code.
yilewang/llm-for-zotero.pain: Asking an LLM about a paper usually means uploading it to a chat site and losing the link to the source. This keeps answers grounded in your library and saves them there.

guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates entire PDFs with PDFMathTranslate, keeping equations and layout intact, and attaches bilingual side-by-side or translated-only copies to the item. Runs through a local Python server with the LLM or translation service you choose.
guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: Translating selections doesn't work for whole papers, and general translators wreck equations and layout. This produces a readable translated paper, mostly into Chinese.

MuiseDestiny/zotero-gpt.does: A floating GPT chat window: ask about the open PDF or selected text, summarize papers and search your library, with shareable command tags that save prompts as one-click buttons. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
MuiseDestiny/zotero-gpt.pain: One of the first ways to use GPT on papers without copying text out of Zotero. Command tags turn repeated prompts into a single click.

l0o0/tara.does: Backs up Zotero preferences, installed plugins, citation styles, translators and locate engines to a file, and restores them on another machine or rolls back to an earlier state.
l0o0/tara.pain: Zotero sync doesn't carry settings or plugins, so a new computer means reinstalling and reconfiguring everything by hand.

qnscholar/zotero-if.does: Writes each paper's JCR impact factor and CAS journal partition into item fields (Library Catalog and Call Number), automatically for new items or on demand, using the June 2026 JCR and March 2026 CAS data.
qnscholar/zotero-if.pain: Checking impact factors and partitions one paper at a time is tedious. This shows them in sortable library columns.

UB-Mannheim/zotero-ocr.does: Runs Tesseract OCR on scanned PDFs and saves a searchable copy with a text layer, optionally with a note holding the text or hOCR files. Needs Tesseract and Poppler's pdftoppm installed locally.
UB-Mannheim/zotero-ocr.pain: Scanned PDFs have no text, so Zotero can't search, index or text-highlight them. OCR makes them usable.

iliasbeshimov/zotero-atlas.does: Adds a Tools → Zotero Atlas window that lists every plugin on zoteroplugins.org, filtered to your Zotero version, with each one's grade and the line that explains it, and installs the exact file the directory analysed (Zotero checks its SHA-256). Once a day it compares your installed plugins with the directory and tells you when one drops a grade, when a pending update is graded worse than what you have, when Zotero's blocklist blocks it, or when it has stopped working with your Zotero. Made by the people who run the directory.
iliasbeshimov/zotero-atlas.pain: Finding plugins means trawling GitHub, and a plugin that was safe when you installed it can change hands or change behaviour without you noticing. Atlas puts the directory's grades inside Zotero and keeps checking after you install. It never sends your library or anything that identifies you; sending your plugin list is opt-in and off by default.

dominic-dallosto/zotero-reading-list.does: Adds a read status to each item (New, To Read, In Progress, Read, Not Reading, or your own labels) in a sortable column. Set it from the right-click menu or Alt+1 to Alt+5, label new items automatically, and update the status when you open the PDF.
dominic-dallosto/zotero-reading-list.pain: Zotero has no built-in way to mark what you've read or plan to read. This turns your library into a reading list without leaving Zotero.

bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up DOIs and shortDOIs for selected items through the Crossref API and flags invalid DOIs. It can also verify stored DOIs and strip prefixes such as doi: or a publisher URL from the DOI field.
bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Missing, malformed or dead DOIs break citations and lookups. This finds and cleans them in bulk instead of item by item.

ethanwillis/zotero-scihub.does: Downloads PDFs from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI, through a right-click menu entry or automatically when you add new papers. Works with Zotero and Juris-M and has a preferences tab, plus notes on DNS-over-HTTPS.
ethanwillis/zotero-scihub.pain: Researchers without institutional access hit paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

wshanks/zutilo.does: Adds extra editing commands to Zotero through a right-click submenu and keyboard shortcuts. It can copy, paste and remove sets of tags, relate several items at once, and copy items to the clipboard in several formats. Other shortcuts focus or hide parts of the interface.
wshanks/zutilo.pain: Power users repeat small chores that stock Zotero has no command for. Each Zutilo function can be switched on or off, so the menus stay uncluttered.

retorquere/zotero-open-pdf.does: Adds a right-click option to open a PDF the opposite way from your Zotero setting. That means the system viewer if Zotero uses its built-in reader, and vice versa. You can add your own viewers through config editor entries.
retorquere/zotero-open-pdf.pain: Zotero lets you pick only one default PDF opener. This gives you a quick second choice, such as Skim, Preview or Edge, without changing the setting.

syt2/paper-chat-for-zotero.does: An AI chat panel and floating window for papers. Ask about the open PDF, translate selected text beside the passage, search your library and scholarly sources, save replies as notes, and generate PowerPoint slides. Needs a PaperChat sign-in or your own OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek or custom API key.
syt2/paper-chat-for-zotero.pain: Discussing a paper with an AI usually means copying text out of Zotero. This keeps questions, translation and note-taking next to the PDF.

daeh/zotero-markdb-connect.does: Scans a folder of Markdown notes for citation keys or Zotero item keys and adds a coloured tag to the matching items. A right-click entry opens the note in Obsidian, logseq or your default Markdown editor.
daeh/zotero-markdb-connect.pain: If you keep reading notes in Obsidian or similar apps, Zotero can't show which papers already have notes. This makes that visible and gets you to the note in one click.

fkguo/zotero-inspire.does: Integrates INSPIRE-HEP, the high-energy physics literature database. It updates item metadata and citation counts, copies BibTeX, citation keys and links, and adds panels for references, citations, related papers and author papers, plus a citation graph and academic family tree.
fkguo/zotero-inspire.pain: Physicists otherwise jump between Zotero and the INSPIRE website to find references, citations and clean metadata. This brings them into the item pane.

windingwind/zotero-pdf-preview.does: Shows a preview of an item's PDF pages in the right-hand item pane, either under the info tab or in its own Preview tab. You choose which pages to preview, and can zoom, show annotations and use a dark mode.
windingwind/zotero-pdf-preview.pain: Checking an attachment meant opening it. Zotero 7 now has native attachment preview, and this plugin is archived.

tefkah/zotero-night.does: A dark theme for the Zotero 6 interface and PDF reader. It has two PDF dark modes, a quick toggle between filters, and some tab bar and animation tweaks, based on the Nord colour scheme.
tefkah/zotero-night.pain: Reading papers late at night is hard on the eyes. Zotero 7 has its own dark mode, and the author has stopped development.

allanchain/zotero-arxiv-workflow.does: Merges an arXiv preprint and its published version into one item. The merged item keeps the preprint's ID, and the plugin can also search online for published versions and download the latest PDF. You choose which PDF opens by default.
allanchain/zotero-arxiv-workflow.pain: Zotero can't merge items of different types, so a preprint and its published paper stay separate. This fixes that without losing annotations or data that other plugins attach to the item ID. It is alpha software.

papersgpt/papersgpt-for-zotero.does: An AI research assistant that chats with PDFs and answers questions across your whole library with clickable citations. Also offers Literature Radar and AutoPilot. Works with cloud models (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and others) or local ones including Ollama, and has a built-in MCP server.
papersgpt/papersgpt-for-zotero.pain: Single-paper chat tools don't scale to a large library. This indexes your PDFs on your machine so you can ask across many papers, with local models if you prefer to keep data private.

scitedotai/scite-zotero-plugin.does: Adds item list columns showing Scite Smart Citation counts: supporting, contrasting and mentioning, plus totals. A View Scite Report button opens the citation snippets in your browser. No account or API key is needed.
scitedotai/scite-zotero-plugin.pain: A raw citation count doesn't say whether later papers agree or disagree. This shows how each paper in your library has been cited without leaving Zotero.

steven-jianhao-li/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads PDFs with an LLM and saves structured summaries as Zotero notes, for new items automatically, in bulk for old ones, or from the right-click menu. Also makes mind maps, multi-paper reviews, a one-image poster summary and a sidebar for follow-up questions. Needs your own LLM API key.
steven-jianhao-li/zotero-ai-butler.pain: Papers pile up unread, and sending them to an AI one by one is slow. This summarises them as they arrive and keeps the notes with the items. Interface and documentation are mainly in Chinese.

l0o0/garden-for-zotero.does: A helper for Chinese-language Zotero users. It provides a free model quota that works as a translation engine for Translate for Zotero, Awesome GPT and LLM for Zotero, sets up many LLM providers in those plugins, and downloads CSL styles from the Chinese community site.
l0o0/garden-for-zotero.pain: Setting up AI and translation plugins by hand is fiddly, and Chinese citation styles are scattered. This is a one-stop setup and resource hub for users in China.

jlegewie/beaver-zotero.does: An AI research agent inside Zotero that answers questions over your library and the open PDF with sentence-level citations. It can add highlights and notes, search annotations, and edit notes and library items, asking for approval first. Needs your own Google, OpenAI or Anthropic API key, or a paid Beaver account.
jlegewie/beaver-zotero.pain: Asking an AI about your papers normally means copying text out and losing track of sources. Beaver works on your actual library and creates real, editable Zotero annotations.

nutstore/zotero-plugin-nutstore.does: Signs you in to Nutstore (Jianguoyun) in one click and configures Zotero file sync to use it, so you don't set up WebDAV by hand. A second feature enhances WebDAV through the Nutstore desktop client, on Windows only.
nutstore/zotero-plugin-nutstore.pain: Nutstore is a common cloud storage service in China, and its WebDAV setup is awkward. This makes syncing Zotero files through it simple. You need a Nutstore account.

redleafnew/zotero-updateifs.does: Fetches journal impact factors and JCR and CAS quartiles from the Justscience site by journal name and stores them in item fields. Also gets journal abbreviations, and a toolbox adds author bolding, case changes and clearing of the Extra field. Aimed at Chinese-language use.
redleafnew/zotero-updateifs.pain: Checking a journal's ranking by hand for every reference is slow. This fills it in for selected items. It only supports Zotero 6.

github-young/zotero-better-authors.does: Adds item list columns for the first author, the last author, and a customisable authors list. You choose how many authors to show, the separators, a symbol marking the last author, and the name order.
github-young/zotero-better-authors.pain: In some fields the last author matters most, but Zotero's creator column shows only the first. This lets you scan authorship at a glance.

egh/zotxt.does: Exposes your Zotero library to plain-text tools through a local API. It works with the pandoc-zotxt.lua filter so Better BibTeX citation keys in Markdown become formatted citations, and with an Emacs package.
egh/zotxt.pain: Writing in Markdown, reStructuredText or LaTeX with pandoc otherwise means exporting your bibliography by hand. This lets pandoc read from a running Zotero.

eschnett/zotero-citationcounts.does: Fetches citation counts for selected items from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP and Semantic Scholar. It stores them in the Extra field and tags the result with the date. Google Scholar is not supported.
eschnett/zotero-citationcounts.pain: Zotero has no field for citation counts. This records them so you can compare papers. It only supports Zotero 6.

frianasoa/ze-notes.does: Shows your notes and annotations as an editable table per collection, with items as rows and tags as columns. You can translate cells with Google or DeepL, run AI prompts on them, OCR images with Tesseract, and export to DOCX, XLSX, HTML or Markdown. AI and DeepL need your own API keys.
frianasoa/ze-notes.pain: Zotero shows notes one at a time, which makes a literature review hard to compare across papers. This lays them out in a matrix inside Zotero.

justinribeiro/zotero-google-scholar-cita.does: Fetches citation counts from Google Scholar for selected items or collections and writes them to the Extra field. It has a sortable column and an option to pull counts automatically for new items. A CAPTCHA window appears if Google Scholar asks for one.
justinribeiro/zotero-google-scholar-cita.pain: Zotero doesn't record how often a paper is cited. This adds Google Scholar's figure, which the author warns is only a rough guide.

zotero-cita/zotero-cita.does: Adds a Citations tab to items for storing citation lists, pulled from Wikidata, Crossref, Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex, with two-way syncing to Wikidata. It also draws local citation and co-authorship networks. Wikidata syncing needs an OAuth token.
zotero-cita/zotero-cita.pain: Zotero holds items but not which papers cite which. This adds that data and lets you visualise how your library connects.

noedgeai/doc2xzoteroplugin9.does: Sends PDFs to the Doc2X AI service for layout-preserving translation, bilingual output, or parsing into Markdown notes saved on the item. This build is for Zotero 9 and 10 and handles several PDFs in turn. Needs a Doc2X sign-in and authorisation.
noedgeai/doc2xzoteroplugin9.pain: Translating a PDF usually breaks its layout and formulas. This keeps the original format. Aimed mainly at Chinese-speaking users.

zzlb0224/zotero-annotation-manage.does: Manages annotations and tags. It adds annotations with colour-coded preset tags, exports annotations to notes (needs Better Notes), links annotations to each other, and highlights chosen words in the reader. Mainly documented in Chinese.
zzlb0224/zotero-annotation-manage.pain: Annotations pile up without structure, so reviewing them is hard. This lets colours and tags sort them into categories you can summarise, which suits writing a literature review.

argenos/zotero-mdnotes.does: Exports item metadata and notes as Markdown files from the right-click menu, creates a blank notes file per item, and can batch export. It was designed with Obsidian in mind.
argenos/zotero-mdnotes.pain: Getting Zotero notes into Markdown tools means copying by hand. This is legacy software for Zotero 5 and 6, and the author recommends Obsidian's Zotero Integration plugin instead.

immersive-translate/zotero-immersivetran.does: Translates Zotero PDFs with BabelDOC through the Immersive Translate service. Right-click a file, choose a target language and model, and follow progress in a task window. Needs an Immersive Translate Pro authorisation code.
immersive-translate/zotero-immersivetran.pain: Translating a whole paper by copy and paste loses its layout. This returns a translated PDF you can open in the reader. Documented in Chinese.

cookjohn/zotero-mcp.does: Runs a Model Context Protocol server inside Zotero so AI clients such as Claude Desktop can use your library. They can search it, read PDF text and annotations, and create notes, tags and items. Semantic search can use a local or hosted embedding model.
cookjohn/zotero-mcp.pain: AI assistants can't see your reference library by default. This connects them to your local Zotero so they can search and cite it.

theigrams/zotero-pdf-custom-rename.does: Renames selected items' PDFs by a fixed pattern of short journal name, year and short title, from the right-click menu or Ctrl+D. A Jab/# tag can set the journal abbreviation.
theigrams/zotero-pdf-custom-rename.pain: Downloaded PDFs have unhelpful names. This gives them short, consistent ones. Custom rules in preferences are not implemented yet.

retorquere/zotero-folder-import.does: Adds an Add files from folder entry to the File menu that imports a folder of attachments, turning its subfolders into a collection hierarchy. It is a one-time import, not a watched folder.
retorquere/zotero-folder-import.pain: Zotero has no way to bring in an existing folder tree of PDFs while keeping its structure. This saves rebuilding it by hand.

panhaoyu/zotero-categorial-tags.does: Manages tags written in a #Category/TagName format. It adds an item list column for them and a shortcut (Ctrl+T by default) that opens a dialog to add or remove tags, with fuzzy and pinyin search. It only binds existing tags and can't create new ones.
panhaoyu/zotero-categorial-tags.pain: Long flat tag lists are hard to navigate. Grouping them by category and picking them from a searchable dialog keeps a big tag set manageable.

retorquere/zotero-pmcid-fetcher.does: Fetches PMCID and PMID numbers for items that have a DOI, from the right-click menu or automatically via a hidden preference. It can also add them as tags.
retorquere/zotero-pmcid-fetcher.pain: Some funders and repositories require PubMed Central IDs. This finds them in bulk instead of looking each one up.

noedgeai/doc2xzoteroplugin.does: Sends PDFs to the Doc2X AI service for layout-preserving translation, bilingual output, or parsing into Markdown notes saved on the item. This build is for Zotero 7 and 8 and handles several PDFs in turn. Needs a Doc2X sign-in and authorisation.
noedgeai/doc2xzoteroplugin.pain: Translating a PDF usually breaks its layout and formulas. This keeps the original format. Aimed mainly at Chinese-speaking users.

inciteful-xyz/inciteful-zotero-plugin.does: Starts searches on Inciteful.xyz from your library. Run a Graph Search from selected items or collections to find related papers, or select two items and use Connect Papers to find literature linking them.
inciteful-xyz/inciteful-zotero-plugin.pain: Finding related work normally means re-entering your papers into a discovery site. This sends them straight from Zotero.

lifan0127/ai-research-assistant.does: Aria is a chat assistant in a Zotero window, opened from the toolbar or Shift+R. Drag items and collections into the chat, use autocompletion for authors and tags, analyse images with GPT-4 Vision, and save chats as notes. Needs an OpenAI API key.
lifan0127/ai-research-assistant.pain: Asking GPT about your library otherwise means pasting references into a chat. Aria queries Zotero directly.

retorquere/zotero-storage-scanner.does: Scans your attachments from the Tools menu and tags items #duplicates or #broken as it finds duplicate or missing attachment files. It has no interface and works in the background.
retorquere/zotero-storage-scanner.pain: Duplicate imports and PDFs deleted outside Zotero leave broken or repeated attachments. It has been superseded by Zotero Attachment Scanner.

wdcpclover/ai4paper.does: An AI research workbench for Zotero. It translates whole PDFs keeping their layout, searches literature from a built-in database, answers questions over your library, writes AI notes, mind maps and review reports, and shows journal rankings in the item list. Largely Chinese-language and account-based, with a 7-day trial.
wdcpclover/ai4paper.pain: Finding, reading, organising and writing up papers normally takes several tools. This puts them in one place, with a focus on Chinese-language research and journal rankings such as CAS and CSSCI.

windingwind/bionic-for-zotero.does: Shows PDFs in the Zotero reader in bionic reading style, with the first letters of each word in bold. You toggle it from the View menu.
windingwind/bionic-for-zotero.pain: Some readers find that bolding word beginnings helps them read faster. Its developer notes that its effectiveness is debated.

dcartertod/zotero-plugins.does: Two small tools: a Preview tab that shows a citation next to the Related tab, and an Abstract Cleaner for abstracts. The preview uses your chosen style, and the cleaner fixes line endings in the abstracts of selected items.
dcartertod/zotero-plugins.pain: Abstracts pasted from PDFs come with broken line breaks. Zotero 7 now previews citations natively, and the preview is currently disabled.

l0o0/magiczotero.does: Translates whole papers inside Zotero using engines such as MinerU, pdf2zh and Doc2X. Also uses AI to summarise papers, outline them and build comparison matrices. Offers a 7-day trial, then a paid licence. Documented in Chinese.
l0o0/magiczotero.pain: Reading a foreign-language paper means translating it piece by piece. This translates the full text while keeping layout.

imperialsquid/zotero-zotts.does: Reads text aloud with your computer's built-in voices. It speaks titles and abstracts in the library, and selected text, annotations or the whole paper in the reader, with shortcuts, queueing, voice settings and text substitutions.
imperialsquid/zotero-zotts.pain: Listening saves your eyes when reading long papers. The author says Zotero's own text to speech makes major updates unlikely.

juris-m/zotero-odf-scan-plugin.does: Converts plain-text citation markers in ODT and DOCX files into live Zotero citations, and back. Markers are Scannable Cite or pandoc [@citekey] syntax. Conversion needs LibreOffice or Microsoft Word with their Zotero plugins.
juris-m/zotero-odf-scan-plugin.pain: Word processors like Scrivener have no Zotero plugin. This lets you cite with markers while writing, then convert for formatting.

dominic-dallosto/zotero-annotations-coun.does: Adds an item list column showing how many annotations each item has, with a preference for its format. Needs Zotero 7 or later.
dominic-dallosto/zotero-annotations-coun.pain: Zotero doesn't show which papers you've marked up. This lets you sort and spot them at a glance.

dominic-dallosto/zotero-pin-items.does: Pins items to the top of a collection with a right-click or a click in a Pinned Items column, with sorting options in preferences. Pins are kept separately for each collection. Needs Zotero 7 or later.
dominic-dallosto/zotero-pin-items.pain: Papers you are working on sink down a long list as you sort. Pinning keeps them in view.

018/zotero-excalidraw.does: Opens an Excalidraw whiteboard from the right-click menu. A side tree lets you drop items, notes and comments onto the canvas, and you can export text, PNG or SVG and use Excalidraw libraries.
018/zotero-excalidraw.pain: Sketching how papers and ideas connect usually happens outside Zotero. This puts a whiteboard next to your notes and references.

askyourpdf/zotero_plugin.does: Chat with your Zotero documents through AI models such as GPT-4, Claude and Mixtral. Open the AskYourPDF panel and pick the files to ask about. Needs an AskYourPDF account.
askyourpdf/zotero_plugin.pain: Asking questions of a paper otherwise means uploading it to a chat site. This runs the questions from inside Zotero.

timetrapzz/zotero-ccf-info.does: Looks up the China Computer Federation (CCF) rating, venue and citation count for selected papers from a right-click entry. Venues missing from the CCF catalogue can be added in the source.
timetrapzz/zotero-ccf-info.pain: Computer science researchers, especially in China, use CCF ratings to judge venues. This saves checking each paper by hand.

introfini/zotseek.does: Semantic search for your library that runs locally. Find papers by meaning, find items similar to one you select, or search from selected PDF text, using local embedding models. Results can be saved as collections, and an optional read-only MCP server serves AI agents.
introfini/zotseek.pain: Keyword search misses papers that use different wording. This finds them by concept without sending your library to the cloud.

frangoud/zoteroduplicatesmerger.does: Merges duplicates in two modes: smart merge for selected items, and bulk merge through the whole Duplicate Items pane without prompts. You choose whether the newest or oldest copy is the master and how to handle differing item types.
frangoud/zoteroduplicatesmerger.pain: Zotero's duplicate merging is one pair at a time. The author warns bulk merge can freeze on lists of about 5,000 or more items, and the plugin is legacy.

sciimage/zotero-attachment-scanner.does: Scans your library for items with missing, absent or duplicate attachments and tags them. It can also list orphaned files in the attachment base directory and adds item-list columns for attachment count and total size.
sciimage/zotero-attachment-scanner.pain: Zotero gives no overview of broken or missing attachment links, so problems surface only when you try to open a file. This finds them across the whole library, or only for selected items, in one pass.

kazgu/zotero-chatgpt.does: Puts ChatGPT inside Zotero with a right-click menu and a reader pane for questions with streamed answers. Also summarises attached PDFs, fetches BibTeX from DBLP and translates text into Chinese. Needs an OpenAI API key.
kazgu/zotero-chatgpt.pain: Using ChatGPT on papers normally means copying text out of Zotero into a browser. This keeps the questions, summaries and translations next to the item you are reading.

maxkuehn/zotero-scholar-citations.does: Fetches the number of citations for your items from Google Scholar and stores it in the Extra field, so you can sort by it. Supports batch updates and opens a browser window when Google Scholar asks for a CAPTCHA.
maxkuehn/zotero-scholar-citations.pain: Zotero has no citation count field. A fork of beloglazov/zotero-scholar-citations that is deprecated; its developer points to plugins that use real APIs, such as zotero-citationcounts.

roadtodream/zotmeta.does: Updates metadata in bulk: journal articles from DOI records, books from ISBN records and arXiv preprints from arXiv IDs. Can find DOIs in the PDF text, create parent items for loose PDFs and tags items that failed or were skipped.
roadtodream/zotmeta.pain: Imported items often arrive with thin or wrong metadata, and fixing them one by one is slow. This enriches a whole selection at once and marks what it could not fix.

aidenlx/zotlit.does: Connects Zotero to Obsidian: creates Markdown literature notes from items using your templates and inserts citations. Also imports Zotero notes and shows annotations in a sidebar. This is the Zotero-side companion for live updates.
aidenlx/zotlit.pain: People who write in Obsidian otherwise copy references and highlights over by hand. ZotLit keeps literature notes in your vault in step with your Zotero library.

frlars21/zoterocitationcountsmanager.does: Fetches citation counts for journal articles from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP and Semantic Scholar, automatically for new items or by right-click. Adds a sortable Citation Counts column and reports per-item errors.
frlars21/zoterocitationcountsmanager.pain: Zotero shows no citation counts, so judging which papers matter means looking each one up. This fills a column you can sort by. It is a refactored version of Erik Schnetter's plugin for Zotero 7.

windfollowingheart/zotero-paper-agent.does: A chat assistant in the Zotero reader sidebar: ask questions about a paper, upload files to query, and use history, saved prompts and keyword search. Default chat runs on Kimi through the author's site; other models need their own keys.
windfollowingheart/zotero-paper-agent.pain: Lets Chinese-speaking researchers chat with papers without leaving Zotero or copying text into a separate chatbot.

wangqian06/zotero-pdf-background.does: Changes the PDF reader's background colour to reduce eye strain. Offers several background modes, a custom colour in settings, an eye button on the toolbar to switch modes, and follows system dark mode.
wangqian06/zotero-pdf-background.pain: Plain white pages tire the eyes on long reading sessions. The author says it will not be updated now that Zotero 8 and 9 have their own theme options.

wilddatax/suppr-zotero-plugin.does: Translates PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and HTML files from the right-click menu through the Suppr (超能文献) service. Keeps the layout and attaches the translated file to the item. Needs a free Suppr account; files are processed on the developer's server.
wilddatax/suppr-zotero-plugin.pain: Reading papers in another language otherwise means uploading files to a translation site by hand. Mainly aimed at Chinese-language users, with new accounts getting a free translation allowance.

isharestuff/zoterotheme.does: Adds theme support to Zotero, with a way to reset to the default theme from the theme editor in preferences. No further features are documented.
isharestuff/zoterotheme.pain: Probably for people who want to change how Zotero looks. It is built on the zotero-pdf-translate template and borrows utility code from Zotero PDF Background.

samreading/zotero-mindmap.does: Creates mind maps inside Zotero that you can open in a tab, with Markdown and maths in nodes, PDF annotations dragged in as nodes, xmind import and PNG export. Catalyst features (summaries, boundaries, callouts, xmind export) need an active code.
samreading/zotero-mindmap.pain: Linking reading notes into a map normally means leaving Zotero for a separate mind-mapping app. Here the map sits next to the papers and their annotations.

pubpeerfoundation/pubpeer_zotero_plugin.does: Shows whether the references in your library have comments on PubPeer, matching items by DOI.
pubpeerfoundation/pubpeer_zotero_plugin.pain: Researchers who want to know if a paper has been criticised or questioned otherwise have to look it up on PubPeer one paper at a time.

leonkt/zotero-memento.does: Archives web pages you save through the browser connector to the Internet Archive and archive.today. It records the archived URL in Extra and a note, lets you archive manually and adds five export translators that include the archive link.
leonkt/zotero-memento.pain: Links in a bibliography go dead over time. This saves a durable copy at the time you add the item. Works fully only for sites that support the Signposting standard.

rphone/zotero-tab-enhance.does: Adds a searchable vertical tab sidebar to Zotero with persistent, colour-coded tab groups and drag-and-drop ordering. Also adds right-click actions on tabs: show file in folder, reload reader, copy citation, and open selected items into a group.
rphone/zotero-tab-enhance.pain: With many papers open at once, Zotero's single row of tabs becomes hard to navigate. This lets you search, group and restore tabs as a reading workspace.

stevenglee/zotero-author-browser.does: Lists every creator in your library with item counts and aliases, opens all items by an author, and searches authors on Google Scholar or CNKI. Also suggests and merges alternative spellings of the same author, with review windows for ambiguous cases.
stevenglee/zotero-author-browser.pain: The same author often appears under several spellings, which splits their items. This helps you see and clean that up. Chinese names are searched in the correct order.

visterainer/aidea-zotero.does: An AI side panel for the library and the PDF or EPUB reader: chat about papers, translate selected text, and translate whole papers into bilingual PDFs. Connect through ChatGPT, Gemini or GitHub Copilot sign-in, any OpenAI-compatible API, or local models such as Ollama and LM Studio.
visterainer/aidea-zotero.pain: Lets you use an AI subscription you already pay for, or a local model, on your papers without an API key or leaving Zotero.

retorquere/zotero-date-from-last-modifie.does: Fills an empty Date field from the web page's Last-Modified header when an item has a URL. Runs automatically after an item changes, and you can limit it to chosen item types through a hidden preference.
retorquere/zotero-date-from-last-modifie.pain: Web pages saved to Zotero often have no date, which breaks citations. This supplies a reasonable one without typing it.

mronkko/zoteroquicklook.does: Previews attachments with a quick look window: macOS's native QuickLook, Gloobus-Preview on Linux, or the QuickLook app on Windows. You can set a custom viewer command.
mronkko/zoteroquicklook.pain: Checking a file otherwise means opening it in a full application. No longer actively maintained, and it may not work with current Zotero versions.

daeh/zotero-citation-tally.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, Semantic Scholar and INSPIRE for new items and shows them side by side in a sortable Citations column. Can refresh outdated counts at startup or on demand. An optional Semantic Scholar key is supported.
daeh/zotero-citation-tally.pain: Zotero has no citation count field, so ranking papers by impact means looking each one up. Counts are kept in the Extra field so they sync.

siriusxt/zotero-scholar-rank.does: Shows CCF rank for conferences and journal rankings in the Call Number column. For journals it adds CCF rank, impact factor, JCR quartile and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) partition. Intended mainly for Chinese-language computer science research.
siriusxt/zotero-scholar-rank.pain: Judging where a paper was published normally means looking up each venue in several ranking lists. This shows the rankings next to each item.

wbthomason/zotodo.does: Creates Todoist tasks for papers added to Zotero, automatically on import or for existing items. Task and comment text come from templates with authors, title and abstract, plus project, section, due date and labels. Needs a Todoist API key.
wbthomason/zotodo.pain: Keeps a reading queue in Todoist without retyping each paper. Task links can open the item or its PDF in Zotero.

retorquere/zotero-report-customizer.does: Lets you edit Zotero's item reports in place: remove fields, reorder them and save the layout. Can show a bibliography rendering instead of the title and shows Better BibTeX keys if that plugin is installed.
retorquere/zotero-report-customizer.pain: Zotero reports include every field, so they need cleaning before use. This replaces the copy-and-paste clean-up step of Jason Priem's Report Cleaner.

federicotorrielli/zotero-metadata-hunter.does: Finds missing DOIs and abstracts using Crossref, DBLP, Semantic Scholar, arXiv, PubMed and OpenAlex. Replaces arXiv preprints with their published versions while keeping attachments and annotations, and fills sparse fields on items imported from Google Scholar.
federicotorrielli/zotero-metadata-hunter.pain: Items saved from Google Scholar or as preprints often lack DOIs, abstracts or venue details. This repairs them in batches from the right-click menu, Tools menu or shortcuts.

retorquere/zotero-auto-index.does: Keeps your attachments full-text indexed automatically, with settings in Zotero's Search preferences.
retorquere/zotero-auto-index.pain: Without it, new PDFs stay unsearchable until you index them yourself.

bairuic/bibgenie.does: An AI research agent in the Zotero sidebar that answers questions using items, PDFs, notes, snapshots, images or collections as context. Search and compare papers and save answers as notes. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and others by key, or local Ollama and LM Studio. Includes a local Zotero MCP server.
bairuic/bibgenie.pain: Gives you an AI assistant that works on your own library, with reviewable plans for batch tag and collection changes, instead of a separate chatbot.

zotero/scaffold.does: An integrated development environment for writing Zotero translators, the scripts that capture metadata from web pages.
zotero/scaffold.pain: Mostly of interest to translator developers. Since Zotero 5.0.73 Scaffold is built into Zotero under Tools, Developer, so this separate add-on is no longer needed.

syt2/zotero-tldr.does: Automatically fetches the TL;DR one-sentence summary from Semantic Scholar for your items and shows it in the item pane. No configuration is needed.
syt2/zotero-tldr.pain: Gives a quick idea of what a paper says without opening it, which helps when triaging a long reading list.

alima-webdev/zotero-review-assistant.does: Lets you mark articles as Included, Excluded or Unsure with a reason for each, and generates a PRISMA flow diagram from those decisions. Works with Zotero 7 only.
alima-webdev/zotero-review-assistant.pain: Systematic reviews need a record of screening decisions and a PRISMA diagram, which are tedious to keep in spreadsheets. This keeps them with the items.

theratramnus/zotero-download-digivatlib-.does: Downloads whole DigiVatLib (Vatican Library) manuscripts as one PDF through the Zotero Connector button. You choose the page range, and the PDF is attached to the new item. Very large manuscripts of around 700 pages may fail.
theratramnus/zotero-download-digivatlib-.pain: Saving a digitised manuscript otherwise means downloading it page by page. Aimed at medievalists and manuscript researchers.

franzbischoff/zotero-pdf-metadata.does: Writes the Title and Author from a Zotero item into the metadata of its attached PDF whenever the item changes. Works in the opposite direction to metadata retrieval. Marked work in progress.
franzbischoff/zotero-pdf-metadata.pain: Zotero only renames files and leaves the PDF's own metadata stale, which matters when you export PDFs to other tools that index by that metadata.

zoushucai/zotero-journalabbr.does: Updates journal abbreviations from a built-in table based on JabRef and ISO-4 data. Offers optional abbr tags, custom abbreviation lists, case and dot options and Chinese-language support. Also copies bibliography text and exports item data as CSV.
zoushucai/zotero-journalabbr.pain: Many journals require abbreviated journal names, and entering them by hand is slow. The author warns the built-in table may be inaccurate, so check exported data.

groundbreakerlhy/ccf-rank.does: Shows the CCF rank (A, B or C), category and abbreviation of conferences and journals as item-list columns, using the 2026 China Computer Federation list. You can correct a wrong match from the right-click menu. For Chinese computer science research.
groundbreakerlhy/ccf-rank.pain: Checking a venue's CCF rank means searching the official list for every paper. This shows it next to each item.

etshaw-zh/zotracer.does: Records your research activity in Zotero, such as reading, note-taking, saving and tab use, and shows it as a timeline you can use to reopen items. Can export notes to Flomo using a webhook from your own account.
etshaw-zh/zotracer.pain: Helps you find what you were reading or working on recently and see your study habits, which Zotero does not track.

yhmtsai/keepzotero.does: Stops Zotero closing by accident: the window close button minimises it instead. It can also ask for confirmation before closing, and remaps Ctrl/Cmd+W, Ctrl+Q and Alt+F4 to minimise. Each behaviour can be switched off.
yhmtsai/keepzotero.pain: A stray shortcut or click closes Zotero and interrupts syncing or reading. This keeps it in the taskbar instead.

wshanks/lyz.does: Inserts citations from Zotero into LyX documents with a Cite in LyX command. Keeps a BibTeX database updated automatically, with custom key formats and unique key checks. Needs LyX with its LyXServer pipe set.
wshanks/lyz.pain: Writers using LyX otherwise export BibTeX by hand and keep keys in step themselves. Only runs on old Zotero versions.

404neko/zoteroquicklookreload.does: Previews attachments with a quick look window: macOS native QuickLook, Gloobus-Preview on Linux, or the QuickLook app on Windows.
404neko/zoteroquicklookreload.pain: Checking a file otherwise means opening it in a full application. A fork of mronkko/zoteroquicklook; its README doesn't say what it changes.

mjthoraval/weavero.does: A set of reader and library additions, each switchable: clickable links, filters, bookmarks, an editable PDF outline and tab management. Links work in annotation comments and notes. Also adds tab groups and sessions, moving tabs between windows, and extra columns.
mjthoraval/weavero.pain: Fills gaps in navigating a large library and many open PDFs. Bookmarks are stored locally and are not synced across computers. Built against Zotero 10 beta.

pandaaigc/zotero-doi-fix.does: Retrieves missing DOIs, updates existing ones and validates DOIs by searching the Crossref API with title, authors and year. Runs on selected items from the right-click menu and shows progress for each item.
pandaaigc/zotero-doi-fix.pain: Missing or wrong DOIs break lookups and citations. This fills and checks them in batches without an API key.

corajr/zotero-voyant-export.does: Exports a Zotero collection as a zip of its full texts, ready to upload to Voyant Tools for text analysis. Needs a collection with full-text files.
corajr/zotero-voyant-export.pain: Gives researchers who analyse text a quick way to view a reading collection in Voyant. Unmaintained, and written for Zotero 5.

swcxito/zotero-ai-bar.does: An AI toolbar and agent for Zotero that acts on selected text, chats, translates and searches your library. The agent can search the document, find papers online and add them to a collection. Supports 27 providers by key.
swcxito/zotero-ai-bar.pain: Puts AI help for reading papers where you are already working. You supply an API key, with OpenAI as the default.

windingwind/zotero-plugin-template.does: A starter template for building Zotero plugins in TypeScript. Includes examples of menus, columns, preference panes, shortcuts and dialogs, plus build, hot reload and release automation.
windingwind/zotero-plugin-template.pain: For plugin developers who want a working skeleton instead of building one from scratch. It adds nothing to Zotero by itself.

xuhan-rgb/zotero-ai-sidebar.does: An AI sidebar that reads the PDF, or the arXiv LaTeX source when available, to answer questions about the paper. Offers API or web-chat modes, quick-ask, immersive translation, a paper overview and writing answers back to notes. Works with Anthropic, OpenAI or compatible endpoints.
xuhan-rgb/zotero-ai-sidebar.pain: Keeps paper Q&A, translation and note-taking in one place in Zotero. Data stays local unless you turn on WebDAV sync to your own server.

oneoneliu/zotero-annotation-summary.does: Opens a window listing all annotations in your library, which you can search by text or comment, filter by colour, tag or date, and jump from to the source. Lets you add or remove tags on annotations in bulk and shows colour and tag charts.
oneoneliu/zotero-annotation-summary.pain: Zotero shows annotations only one document at a time. This gives a single place to review highlights across the whole library.

nicolemayer/zotero-save-with-tag.does: Tags every item you save through the Zotero Connector with To-Read. To use another tag you must edit the code and repackage the plugin.
nicolemayer/zotero-save-with-tag.pain: Gives a simple reading queue for newly saved items. Written by its author for personal use, with no settings.

chikit-l/zotero-fulltext-translate.does: Parses a PDF with MinerU, translates it through Translate for Zotero, and attaches an HTML copy with figures to the item, in Chinese only or bilingual. A MinerU token gives better parsing. Needs Translate for Zotero installed.
chikit-l/zotero-fulltext-translate.pain: Reading a translated paper with its images and tables intact is hard when PDF translation loses layout. The author warns it was built with heavy AI help and results should be checked.

janbaykara/zotero-syllabus.does: Turns collections into syllabi and reading lists, with items ordered by class. Browse in a gallery, track what to read next, follow due dates in a reading schedule and review highlights in an annotation feed.
janbaykara/zotero-syllabus.pain: Students and teachers otherwise keep reading lists and deadlines outside Zotero. This keeps them with the references.

xujialiu/zotero-openreader.does: Adds more text-to-speech voices to Zotero 10's Read Aloud, including Fish Audio, Azure, OpenAI, Cloudflare, Speechify and local Kokoro servers. Highlights words and sentences in your colours, adds shortcuts, resumes where you stopped and syncs settings and position over WebDAV.
xujialiu/zotero-openreader.pain: Zotero's own voices and controls are limited. This gives more voices and finer control over listening to papers.

edwintuan/pdf-ai-bookmarks.does: Generates a nested table of contents for a PDF using Google's Gemini AI and writes it into the file as bookmarks, from the Tools menu. Splits very large PDFs. Needs a Gemini API key; the PDF is sent to Google.
edwintuan/pdf-ai-bookmarks.pain: Many PDFs have no bookmarks, which makes long books hard to navigate. This adds them without touching your highlights or notes.

bluebluekitty/zotero-ainote.does: Generates AI summary notes for selected PDFs with reusable prompt templates and streamed output, in batches. Works with Azure OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and OpenAI keys, or ChatGPT's web page through a browser extension. Also tidies note formatting and headings. Mainly documented in Chinese.
bluebluekitty/zotero-ainote.pain: Writing reading notes for many papers takes time. This produces consistently structured notes saved straight into Zotero.

occasional16/researchopia.does: Connects Zotero to the Researchopia (研学港) academic community site and syncs PDF annotations to the cloud. Also joins shared reading sessions and shows other people's annotations and comments. Works alongside the project's website and browser extension.
occasional16/researchopia.pain: For researchers who want to share annotations and read papers together. Mainly aimed at a Chinese-speaking audience, and an account on the site is probably needed.

tenglvjun/mktero.does: Converts Zotero PDFs into source-linked Markdown and opens it in a reading-first tab with formulas, tables, figures and citations. Sends the PDF to MinerU or Mistral OCR, caches the result locally, and can translate the article, edit recognition errors and keep your annotations. Needs a MinerU token or Mistral API key.
tenglvjun/mktero.pain: Two-column papers with formulas and tables are hard to read and reflow badly in a PDF viewer. This gives a continuous reading view that still jumps back to the exact place in the PDF.

dschaehi/zotero-focused-mode.does: Toggles a distraction-free reading mode that hides the tab bar, annotation toolbar, sidebars and context pane and enters fullscreen. Bound to Ctrl+Cmd+F on Mac and F11 on Windows and Linux.
dschaehi/zotero-focused-mode.pain: Stock Zotero keeps toolbars and panes on screen while you read. A fork of wmstack/Zotero-Toggle-Bars; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jadense-ai/jadense-in-zotero.does: An AI reading assistant for Zotero aimed at Chinese users. Ask questions about the paper you are reading, keep notes beside the source text, translate selections or whole papers, run local OCR and explain figures. Also checks and imports references. Needs your own API key or a Jadense account, and is licensed for non-commercial use only.
jadense-ai/jadense-in-zotero.pain: Reading a difficult paper normally means copying text into a separate chat tool. This keeps questions, translation and fact-checking inside Zotero next to the paper.

study-233/zotero-pdf2zh-pro.does: Translates PDFs into a translated or bilingual PDF through a local Python service running pdf2zh_next, then imports the result back into the item. Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs and offers task progress, retry, partial re-translation and request metrics. You must install the local service and supply an API key.
study-233/zotero-pdf2zh-pro.pain: Translating a whole paper while keeping its layout otherwise means leaving Zotero and re-importing files by hand. Here you submit from the right-click menu and the translated PDF comes back as an attachment.

astro-koko/deepseek-copilot-for-zotero.does: A reading chat in the Zotero side panel powered by the DeepSeek API. Ask, summarise and explain the open paper, with a separate saved conversation per paper, slash commands, Markdown and LaTeX rendering and optional web look-ups. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
astro-koko/deepseek-copilot-for-zotero.pain: Using a general chat tool for papers means repeatedly pasting context and losing track of which discussion belongs to which paper. This ties each conversation to one paper.

replynow20/gemini-zotero.does: Analyses paper PDFs with Google Gemini from a toolbar popup, the right-click menu or a selection popup in the reader. Supports chat, custom analysis templates, and Visual Insights that draw schematic, concept or flowchart images. Saves output as Zotero notes. Needs a Gemini API key or a compatible proxy key.
replynow20/gemini-zotero.pain: Summarising papers and turning them into diagrams usually happens in a separate browser tab. This runs Gemini on the PDF from inside Zotero and files the results with the item.

bowen-0x00/zotero-action-cmd.does: Adds a right-click menu on items that runs your own commands: a local JavaScript file, a system command or an HTTP request. Which mode is used is set in the Config Editor.
bowen-0x00/zotero-action-cmd.pain: For people who want to hand part of their workflow to an external script or program that Zotero can't do itself.

1ywan/zotero-odh.does: Brings the Online Dictionary Helper to Zotero: look up words and send them to Anki through AnkiConnect. Supports ODH system scripts; Anki web service and user-defined scripts aren't done yet.
1ywan/zotero-odh.pain: For people who learn vocabulary from papers and want dictionary look-ups to become Anki cards without leaving Zotero.

rafael-silva-oliveira/nzbridge.does: Syncs Zotero with Google NotebookLM in both directions. It pushes chosen PDFs and URLs from a collection as notebook sources, and pulls notes written in NotebookLM back into Zotero. Needs a companion Chrome or Edge extension and a Google account with NotebookLM access.
rafael-silva-oliveira/nzbridge.pain: Moving papers into NotebookLM and its notes back out is manual and repetitive. This automates both directions and skips items already uploaded.

drinktea905/zotero-paper-outline.does: Uses an AI model to write a whole-paper summary saved as a note, plus a page-linked outline in the reader's outline pane. The outline has short section summaries. Runs automatically on new items or from the right-click menu. Scanned PDFs can go through MinerU. Works with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Kimi, Ollama and others; mostly Chinese-language.
drinktea905/zotero-paper-outline.pain: Getting the gist and structure of a paper before reading takes time. This gives a clickable table of contents and a summary without opening a chat window.

qiwei-ma/zotero-pdf-sethorizontal.does: Sets your PDF view defaults automatically: horizontal or wrapped scrolling, zoom to page height, and an automatically enabled hand tool. Applies when items are added or tabs are opened.
qiwei-ma/zotero-pdf-sethorizontal.pain: Zotero's reader doesn't remember your preferred scroll, zoom and hand-tool settings, so you reset them for each PDF.

qrkks/zotero-annotation-markdown.does: Renders annotation comments in the reader sidebar as Markdown and LaTeX math while leaving the stored text unchanged. Adds highlight syntax, automatic links, a floating outline for long comments, and experimental SVG and Mermaid diagrams. Supports PDF and EPUB on Zotero 9 and 10.
qrkks/zotero-annotation-markdown.pain: Annotation comments in Zotero are plain text, so formulas and structured notes are hard to read. This shows them formatted without changing what you typed.

mungell/zotserver.does: Adds a local-only HTTP API to Zotero, built on its port 23119 server, with a search endpoint that takes JSON conditions such as quick search or tag. Lets other desktop apps query your library without internet.
mungell/zotserver.pain: For developers who want to link or search Zotero items from a note-taking app or editor without direct database access.

creling/zotero-metadata-scraper.does: Looks up an item by title on DBLP and Semantic Scholar from the right-click menu and updates the item's metadata. You pick the right match if there are several. Has an optional Semantic Scholar API key for higher rate limits.
creling/zotero-metadata-scraper.pain: Imported papers often have incomplete or wrong publication details, particularly preprints. This fills them in from scholarly databases.

theratramnus/riopacaddchapter.does: Adds the parent book details to chapters saved from the RI OPAC catalogue. It works with the Zotero Connector, fixes common title and creator mistakes, and can fetch the publisher through Google Books. Its developer says it currently doesn't work and points to an alternative.
theratramnus/riopacaddchapter.pain: Chapters saved from the RI OPAC arrive without the parent book information, which medievalists then add by hand. Retired.

theliterature/theliterature-zotero.does: Adds a context-menu entry that fetches a PDF from Sci-Hub. It tests mirrors for one that responds, finds missing DOIs through Crossref, handles captcha challenges and imports the PDF. Zotero 6 only.
theliterature/theliterature-zotero.pain: Saves hunting for paywalled papers by hand. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

windingwind/know-ur-zotero.does: Monitors Zotero's own status: an activity monitor showing CPU use by activity, a status indicator in the toolbar and an activity log written to file. Also exposes a profiler API to other plugins.
windingwind/know-ur-zotero.pain: Mainly for plugin developers who need to find what is slowing Zotero down.

54yyyu/zotero-mcp.does: Connects your Zotero library to AI assistants through an MCP server and a command-line tool. It also adds a Zotero Agent chat panel that runs your own agent such as Claude Code or Codex next to the PDF. Searches by meaning, reads full text, annotates, adds papers and manages collections. Needs a Python install and an AI client.
54yyyu/zotero-mcp.pain: Lets AI tools work on your actual library instead of pasted excerpts, with page citations that link back to the PDF.

jyjulianwong/polarrec-zotero-plugin.does: Gets academic paper recommendations from the PolarRec service for items in your library. It uses public data such as authors, venues, publication dates and citations. Adds a simple interface inside Zotero.
jyjulianwong/polarrec-zotero-plugin.pain: Finding related papers means searching elsewhere by hand. This suggests new reading based on what you already have in Zotero.

b3000kcn/minimize-zotero-to-tray.does: Minimises Zotero to the system tray when you close the window instead of quitting. A tray icon click or a customisable global hotkey shows it again, and it can start hidden on login. Quit from the File menu.
b3000kcn/minimize-zotero-to-tray.pain: Keeps Zotero running in the background without a taskbar button, which suits people who launch it at startup.

infinity4b/zotero-hjfy-split-reader.does: Fetches the Chinese translation of an arXiv paper from hjfy.top (Hallucination Translation) and opens the original and translated PDFs side by side in one tab. Matches the exact arXiv version, saves the translation as an attachment and reuses it later. Zotero 8 to 10.
infinity4b/zotero-hjfy-split-reader.pain: Comparing a paper with its translation otherwise means finding the file and arranging windows yourself. This does both from one right-click.

chen7447/sci-download-for-zotero.does: Downloads paper PDFs from Sci-Hub mirrors by DOI, PMID or title, with batch download from the right-click menu and a reader toolbar button. Races several mirrors at once, looks up metadata on Crossref and PubMed, and files PDFs into a chosen collection without duplicates.
chen7447/sci-download-for-zotero.pain: Researchers without institutional access hit paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

quillamio/bilingual-reader.does: Shows an English-to-Chinese paragraph-by-paragraph bilingual view in Zotero 10's reading mode. Uses Translate for Zotero's engine or Ollama, caches translations, can skip the reference pages, and can try to export the bilingual text as a PDF attachment.
quillamio/bilingual-reader.pain: For Chinese readers who want the translation under each paragraph of the original while doing close reading.

moonweave-research/zotero-reading-flow.does: Tracks reading progress with item list columns, bookmarks and reading statuses. Adds Progress, Status and Last Read columns, saved PDF positions to resume from, statuses such as To Read, Reading and Read, and a Reading Statistics dashboard. Works with Zotero 9 and 10.
moonweave-research/zotero-reading-flow.pain: Zotero doesn't show which papers you have read or where you stopped, so you open PDFs just to find out.

dralkh/seerai.does: An AI research assistant: chat with your papers, search scholarly sources and run systematic reviews. It searches 11 scholarly sources at once, does semantic search over your library, OCR and structured data extraction, and includes a standalone MCP server and agent skills. Needs an AI provider key for most features.
dralkh/seerai.pain: Bundles paper chat, discovery and literature-review tooling in one place instead of several separate apps.

liozhang/z-transplit.does: A translation toolkit for Zotero 10 covering selections, whole PDFs and side-by-side reading. It translates reader selections, translates whole PDFs while keeping layout and saves them as attachments, opens original and translation side by side, and has bilingual or translation-only reading mode. Also reads aloud. Downloads a layout parser and Java runtime on first use.
liozhang/z-transplit.pain: Reading foreign-language papers normally needs several tools. This puts selection translation, full-text translation and side-by-side reading in one plugin.

williamsliang/zotero-skr.does: Generates literature reviews and search queries from the papers you select. It also summarises each paper's research question, methods and experiments, and writes sectioned reviews from items under a tag. Results are saved as notes. Needs an OpenAI-style API or a model you host.
williamsliang/zotero-skr.pain: Writing a review across many papers means reading and summarising each one by hand. This drafts the structure and summaries from your library.

jetxa/zotero-ai-assistant.does: A chat panel in the item pane that uses the item's title and abstract, or optionally the PDF full text, as context. Adds translate and explain buttons for selected text in the reader, keeps multiple saved sessions per item and works with OpenAI-compatible APIs, including Ollama. Needs an API key.
jetxa/zotero-ai-assistant.pain: Lets you ask questions about a paper without copying text into an outside chat tool.

royshare/zotero-spotlight.does: A command-palette style quick launcher for finding any item from the keyboard. Press Cmd or Ctrl+P to fuzzy-search items, notes, PDFs, annotations and collections across all libraries, and Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+P for commands. Supports filters for tags, years and exact phrases, and switching between open tabs.
royshare/zotero-spotlight.pain: Zotero's search covers only the current collection and needs the mouse. This jumps to any paper from the keyboard.

echouniverse/zotero-translator-next.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader into the side panel, tidying line breaks and hyphens first. Tries free and paid services in a fallback order, including MyMemory, Bing, Google, DeepSeek, Tencent, Baidu and any OpenAI-compatible service. Keeps a translation history and can summarise the translation with AI. Mostly aimed at Chinese users.
echouniverse/zotero-translator-next.pain: Copied PDF text often breaks translators with stray line breaks, and free services fail now and then. This cleans the text and falls back to another service automatically.

introfini/mcp-server-zotero-dev.does: Lets an AI assistant build, test and debug Zotero plugins through a 28-tool MCP server. Works with Claude Code, Cursor and similar: screenshots, DOM inspection, running JavaScript in Zotero, logs, read-only database access and plugin reload. The Zotero plugin turns on the remote debugging port.
introfini/mcp-server-zotero-dev.pain: For plugin developers who want an AI assistant to see what Zotero is doing instead of guessing from code.

shangkaijie/zotero-hover-translate-eudic.does: Translates a word when you hover or click it in the PDF or reading mode, using the Translate for Zotero engine. Adds words to Eudic, Shanbay, Maimemo, a local word list or a Zotero note, with pronunciation and optional PDF annotations. Syncing to those apps needs their tokens.
shangkaijie/zotero-hover-translate-eudic.pain: For readers building vocabulary from papers, so look-ups and word lists don't mean switching to a dictionary app.

windfollowingheart/zotero-copy-anything.does: Copies an item's attachment files to the system clipboard so you can paste them into a folder or message. Works with several attachments at once, has a configurable shortcut, and works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Downloads a helper binary on first use.
windfollowingheart/zotero-copy-anything.pain: Zotero can't copy attachment files to the clipboard, so sharing a PDF means finding it in storage.

josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder.does: Watches a folder and imports PDFs dropped into it, looking up metadata and renaming files. It skips duplicates by content hash and applies rules for tags and collections. Optionally mirrors subfolders to collections in both directions, with a recoverable trash for deletions. Works on Zotero 7 to 10.
josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder.pain: Saves dragging every downloaded PDF into Zotero by hand and keeps disk folders and collections in step.

zzq-02/zotero-vocab-builder.does: Collects unfamiliar English words while you read into a vocabulary note. Select a word, press Alt+A or click the pop-up button, and it is added with translation, phonetics, definition and a link back to its place in the PDF. Uses Youdao and Free Dictionary or a custom API. Exports to CSV, Anki, Quizlet and Mochi.
zzq-02/zotero-vocab-builder.pain: Looking up words and writing them down interrupts reading. This captures each word with its context in one step.

zar-rok/zotero-add-collection-tag.does: Tags new items, and their attachments, saved with the Zotero Connector with the name of the collection currently selected in Zotero.
zar-rok/zotero-add-collection-tag.pain: Saves tagging each import by hand. Its developer says it doesn't support recent Zotero versions.

tianlrz/zotero-reading-bilingual.does: Adds a bilingual button to Zotero 10's reading mode that inserts translation cards under each paragraph, and translates tables and tables of contents as units. Skips references, caches translations next to the attachment and resumes after interruptions. Works with Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenAI and other compatible services. Needs your own API key.
tianlrz/zotero-reading-bilingual.pain: Reading papers in a second language needs the translation next to the text. This keeps the original untouched and avoids paying again for translated paragraphs.

tobihol/zotero-mas-metadata.does: Adds estimated citation counts from the Microsoft Academic Search API to the Extra field of selected items. Needs a Microsoft Academic API key.
tobihol/zotero-mas-metadata.pain: Saves looking up citation counts one paper at a time. The API was retired in 2022, so this no longer works.

tangqi001/zotero-ai-assist.does: An AI literature agent that queues papers for summaries and deep-reading notes. Adds a reading sidebar, comparison tables, one-picture summaries and mind maps, and drafts reviews across collections. Works with several providers and OpenAI-compatible endpoints using your API key.
tangqi001/zotero-ai-assist.pain: Batch-processes new papers into structured notes. A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler that strengthens the agent, queue and sidebar.

peterdresslar/zotero-gemini-notebook.does: Sends Zotero PDFs to Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM). Pick sources from your collections in a Tools menu, stage them, and a companion Chrome extension uploads them. An optional MCP interface lets an AI assistant queue sources.
peterdresslar/zotero-gemini-notebook.pain: Zotero stores PDFs in many key-named folders, so gathering files for a notebook by hand is tedious. This hands them off directly.

l0o0/scholar-sketch.does: Adds Markdown notes and visual whiteboards to Zotero. Notes have live preview, [[wiki-style]] links, backlinks, Mermaid diagrams and math, and whiteboards connect papers, annotations and notes. Uses plain .md and JSON Canvas .canvas files, with export for Obsidian. Needs Zotero 9, 10 or 11.
l0o0/scholar-sketch.pain: Zotero's built-in notes are basic and unlinked. This gives an Obsidian-like note and canvas workspace tied to your papers and annotations.

chen7447/word-translator-zotero.does: Translates words, phrases and sentences selected in the PDF reader into Chinese and saves them as cards in a per-item word list in the side pane. Starts with free services and can use LLMs or machine-translation APIs such as DeepL, Baidu and Tencent. Can read words aloud.
chen7447/word-translator-zotero.pain: For Chinese readers of English papers who want look-ups collected per paper instead of lost after each translation.

isharestuff/zoterofields-plugin-for-zote.does: Fills fields such as impact factor from a local CSV file you supply, matching journal names or abbreviations. It also supports school and place details for theses. Updates selected items or a whole group. Mostly Chinese-language.
isharestuff/zoterofields-plugin-for-zote.pain: Saves typing journal metrics into each record by hand. You must supply and maintain the CSV.

paulusm/zotero-trilium.does: Exports items and notes to a Trilium Notes server: right-click an item to send its reference and library links, or export a note built from PDF annotations. Needs your Trilium server URL, ETAPI key and a parent note.
paulusm/zotero-trilium.pain: For Trilium users who keep research notes there and don't want to copy references and annotations across by hand.

srt117/litmtrans-zotero.does: Translates and reads PDFs parsed by MinerU, including scans, with layout kept. Produces layout-preserving or flowing translations, bilingual PDFs, AI chat over the full paper, mind maps, research flowcharts and copyable LaTeX formulas. Needs a free MinerU token and, for AI features, a model API key. Mostly aimed at Chinese users.
srt117/litmtrans-zotero.pain: Gets translated papers with formulas and layout intact without leaving Zotero, including scans that have no text layer.

angjustinl/zotero-plugin-hjfy.does: Downloads the Chinese translation of an arXiv paper from hjfy.top (Hallucination Translation), based on its LaTeX source, and attaches it to the item. Finds the arXiv ID in the DOI, URL or Extra field and works on several items at once.
angjustinl/zotero-plugin-hjfy.pain: For Chinese readers who want a good translation of arXiv papers without hunting for it on the site.

lisontowind/zotero-mineru.does: Parses PDF attachments with the MinerU API and saves them as Markdown or HTML with images. It then adds AI summaries and translations of the parsed text, including bilingual HTML. Needs a MinerU token and optionally an LLM API key. Works on Zotero 8 to 10.
lisontowind/zotero-mineru.pain: Turns PDFs into clean text with formulas and images so they can be summarised, translated or reused, rather than copying out of the PDF.

dawaltconley/zotero-center-pdf.does: Centres the PDF page in the view when you use the page navigation buttons.
dawaltconley/zotero-center-pdf.pain: Useful on e-ink readers and similar devices where scrolling is awkward. The author calls it a hacky solution.

lika-shing/git4zotero.does: Gives Word manuscripts attached to Zotero items a local Git version history. Check changes, create and restore versions from a right-click menu, with a paragraph-level diff for .docx files, and back up or import a history. Needs Git installed. Works with .docx and .doc on Zotero 8 to 10.
lika-shing/git4zotero.pain: Keeps drafts, revisions and submission versions beside the reference, without a cloud service, and lets you roll back safely.

018/zoturead.does: A mixed toolbox for managing Chinese-language books, tied to the uread.today site. Shows Chinese Library Classification numbers and subjects, searches Douban, JD, Dangdang and library services, updates Douban ratings or CNKI citation counts, and files books by subject. Also updates translators.
018/zoturead.pain: For people managing a library of Chinese books in Zotero who need classification and catalogue data.

melat0nin/zotero-roam-export.does: Exports items, multiple items or whole collections to Roam Research's JSON import format. It targets Zotfile-extracted highlights and annotations, so they can be referenced block by block in Roam. Optional settings turn underlines into headings and use Better BibTeX citekeys as page titles.
melat0nin/zotero-roam-export.pain: Getting a paper's metadata and highlights into Roam by hand is slow. The author no longer maintains it and moved to Logseq.

jmiba/zotero-add-items-from-text.does: Pastes unstructured text containing references into a dialog, uses an AI model to extract them, and imports the ones you pick into your collection.
