Optional checks against Crossref, OpenAlex, Library of Congress and other indexes validate and fill in fields. Needs a Gemini or OpenAI-compatible key, or a local Ollama model.
jmiba/zotero-add-items-from-text.pain: Turning a pasted bibliography or footnotes into proper Zotero items normally means retyping each one or fixing broken lookups. This parses a whole block of text in one go, with a preview before import.

whacked/zotero-special-tags-column.does: Adds a Special Tags column to the item list that shows only the tags you choose, optionally mapped to emoji or custom-styled labels.
whacked/zotero-special-tags-column.pain: Zotero's tag display is easy to overlook in a long list. This gives an at-a-glance marker column, for example a row of icons for rating or status.

aginetz/semantic-zotero.does: Shows the references of a selected paper from Semantic Scholar through a right-click menu, with authors, abstract and citation contexts for each. Add any reference to your library in one click, with its PDF if available, into chosen collections and tags.
aginetz/semantic-zotero.pain: Following a paper's bibliography usually means searching for each reference separately. A personal Semantic Scholar API key is optional but avoids frequent rate-limit rejections.

luckyang1/zotero2eagle.does: Exports PDF image annotations to the Eagle image manager, keeping a zotero://open-pdf backlink plus title, authors, year and page tags. It also adds an Eagle-style image manager tab inside Zotero for browsing, filtering and cleaning up image annotations and note images. Needs Eagle's API URL and token.
luckyang1/zotero2eagle.pain: Figures you clip from papers end up scattered across Zotero annotations. This collects them in one browsable place and sends them to Eagle with a link back to the source page.

manuelarunge/zotitle.does: Changes the titles of selected items to UPPERCASE, lowercase, Sentence case, Title Case or headline-style capitalisation. Headline style keeps minor words lowercase and preserves abbreviations such as WHO and COVID-19.
manuelarunge/zotitle.pain: Imported titles arrive in inconsistent capitalisation, which then shows up in bibliographies. This fixes a whole selection at once.

milekpl/zotero-ner.does: Finds and fixes variant author names across your library. It groups variants (diacritics, initials, spelling, prefixes) into suggestions in a review dialog, which you apply per group or in bulk. A Normalize Field tool does the same for publishers, places, journals and any other text field.
milekpl/zotero-ner.pain: The same author or publisher entered several ways splits searches, counts and citations. This finds the variants and unifies them, only writing changes you approve.

urschrei/pdferret.does: Downloads PDFs for items with a DOI from configurable providers, with Sci-Hub and Anna's Archive built in and custom providers by URL template. It registers them as Zotero PDF resolvers, so a Retrieve PDF menu entry and automatic download on import both work.
urschrei/pdferret.pain: Researchers without access hit paywalls on items they add. Note that Sci-Hub and Anna's Archive distribute copyrighted material without permission, and using them is illegal in many jurisdictions.

nico-zck/zotero-scholar-citations.does: Fetches citation counts for your items from Google Scholar and stores them in the Extra field so you can sort by them. It updates in batches with random delays, handles reCAPTCHA prompts and can update automatically.
nico-zck/zotero-scholar-citations.pain: Zotero has no citation count field. This fork of Zotero Scholar Citations is tuned to work better with Google Scholar, especially from China, and only runs on Zotero 6.

patrixe/zotero-scihub.does: Adds an Update Scihub PDF right-click entry that downloads a PDF from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI and attaches it. It also fetches PDFs automatically for newly added items.
patrixe/zotero-scihub.pain: Saves manual hunting for papers behind paywalls. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions. A fork of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub; its README doesn't say what it changes.

juris-m/propachi-vanilla.does: Replaces Zotero's citation (CSL) processor with an alternative version through a monkey-patch, for the Juris-M variant of Zotero.
juris-m/propachi-vanilla.pain: Probably for people who need citation output from a different processor version than Zotero ships; little else is documented.

lricher7329/zotero-mcp-claude-code.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants can use your library. Claude Code, Codex and other clients connect over HTTP to search items, read PDFs and annotations, generate bibliographies, and create items and collections. Optional token authentication and semantic search with an embeddings provider or local model.
lricher7329/zotero-mcp-claude-code.pain: Lets an AI tool work with your actual Zotero library without a separate server process. A fork that adds Claude Code compatibility and write operations.

forrtproject/flora-zotero.does: Checks your library for items that have replications or reproductions in the FORRT FLoRA database. It matches by DOI hash prefixes so your library contents are not sent. It tags and links items, adds notes with outcomes, and can copy originals and replications into your library.
forrtproject/flora-zotero.pain: Researchers rarely know whether a paper they cite has been replicated. This surfaces known replications and their outcomes inside Zotero.

thejieee/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Shows a translate button when you select text in the PDF or EPUB reader and opens a floating translation card beside it. Single words use Google's free endpoint, sentences use an OpenAI-compatible model, with MyMemory and automatic fallback. Translations can be copied or saved into an annotation.
thejieee/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading papers in another language otherwise means copying text to a translation site. This works like a browser translation extension inside the reader. The interface is in Chinese and English.

asianfleet/mineru-for-zotero.does: Sends PDF attachments to the MinerU API for parsing, then shows MinerU's layout boxes over the PDF in the reader. Click boxes to copy text, titles, tables, formulas or captions, several at once in reading order, or copy the full Markdown. Needs a MinerU API key.
asianfleet/mineru-for-zotero.pain: Copying tables, formulas and multi-column text from a PDF normally gives garbled results. Structured parsing makes the copied content usable.

jagaldol/zotero-cite-preview-resizer.does: Enlarges the hover preview that appears over citations in the reader and lets you drag its corner to resize it, saving the new size as the default. You can also hide previews or fix the size in preferences.
jagaldol/zotero-cite-preview-resizer.pain: Zotero's default citation preview is too small to read reference pages or figures. This makes it as large as you need.

birugit/zotero-grounded-qa.does: Lattice lists every annotation across your library in one window, filterable by colour, tag and keyword, and exports them with citations. It turns highlights into linked idea notes, builds outline-based drafts from tagged quotes, and answers questions about PDFs with clickable page citations using Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Grok or a local Ollama model.
birugit/zotero-grounded-qa.pain: Zotero shows annotations one PDF at a time. This gathers them across papers so notes and quotes can be filtered, linked and reused when writing.

kevin65536/zotero-openreview-plugin.does: Imports papers from an OpenReview venue or workshop URL into a new collection through File, Import from OpenReview. It can download PDFs, import reviews and comments as notes, keep only accepted papers and skip duplicates.
kevin65536/zotero-openreview-plugin.pain: Collecting a conference's papers and reviews from OpenReview by hand is slow. This brings a whole venue in at once.

isharestuff/backup-plugin-for-zotero.does: Backs up Zotero's data and profile folders on Windows and Linux into a dated folder, either at your request or when Zotero starts. You can choose a settings-only backup or a full backup including PDFs.
isharestuff/backup-plugin-for-zotero.pain: Moving to another computer means copying data and configuration by hand. These backups can be restored on another device.

ottersem/zotero-reference-linker.does: Highlights bibliography entries in the PDF reader whose papers are already in your library and opens the PDF or selects the item when clicked. Unmatched references offer opening the DOI, searching Google Scholar or copying the title. Matches use DOI, arXiv ID, title and a bibliographic fingerprint.
ottersem/zotero-reference-linker.pain: Checking which cited papers you already own means searching your library one by one. This shows it directly in the reference list.

zhi-11/zotero-ai-sidebar.does: Translates a PDF sentence when you click it, in a floating card with a machine translation next to an AI translation, explanation or Q&A. The machine translation comes via Translate for Zotero. You can save the result as a colour-coded highlight. Needs an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible key. The interface is in Chinese and English.
zhi-11/zotero-ai-sidebar.pain: Reading papers sentence by sentence normally means selecting and copying text. A fork of xuhan-rgb/zotero-ai-sidebar; its README doesn't say what it changes.

nebularaven/zotero-refolio.does: Adds journal metrics (impact factors, JCR quartiles, PKU Core, CSSCI, CSCD labels) to your library. It also adds citation and author graphs and academic genealogy from Wikidata. Other features include nested tags, reading status, saved column layouts, PDF appearance and optional reading-time tracking. Online ratings use an EasyScholar or Garden key.
nebularaven/zotero-refolio.pain: Judging journal quality, tracing citations and organising a large library all need separate tools. A fork of Ethereal Style for Zotero 10, useful for Chinese-language research.

sneakers-the-rat/zotero-scihub.does: Adds an Update Scihub PDF right-click entry that downloads a PDF from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI and attaches it. It also fetches PDFs automatically for new items. The Sci-Hub address and automatic download are set in the Config Editor.
sneakers-the-rat/zotero-scihub.pain: Saves manual hunting for papers behind paywalls. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions. A fork of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub; its README doesn't say what it changes.

ydeng11/zotero-zotadata.does: Finds missing metadata, DOIs and ISBNs for items and removes broken attachment links. Lookups use CrossRef, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, OpenLibrary, Google Books and DBLP. It retrieves PDFs from Unpaywall, CORE, arXiv, Internet Archive, Library Genesis and Sci-Hub, and finds published versions of arXiv preprints.
ydeng11/zotero-zotadata.pain: Cleaning up incomplete records and missing PDFs in a large library is slow by hand. Note that Library Genesis and Sci-Hub distribute copyrighted papers without permission, and using them is illegal in many jurisdictions.

albertshenc/zotero-literature-manager.does: Fills in data for arXiv papers automatically. It adds citation counts and published venue from Semantic Scholar, code links from Papers With Code, a SciTLDR summary and related papers from Connected Papers, and tags new items to_read. Zotero 6 only.
albertshenc/zotero-literature-manager.pain: Keeping track of a paper's impact, code and related work normally means checking several sites. This collects them into item fields. It is modified from zotero-citationcounts.

david3684/zotero-tab-limiter.does: Caps the number of open tabs in Zotero and automatically closes the least recently used tabs when you go over. The limit is set in the plugin's preferences.
david3684/zotero-tab-limiter.pain: Opening many PDFs leaves a long tab bar that slows reading. This keeps it tidy without manual closing.

heimi98/zotero-figure-overview.does: Opens an Eagle-style overview of all your image annotations from a tab-bar button. Filter by annotation colour and collection, adjust thumbnail size, and double-click a thumbnail to jump to its annotation in the Reader.
heimi98/zotero-figure-overview.pain: Figures you clip while reading stay buried inside individual PDFs. This lets you browse them all together.

vvvastrong/marginmind.does: Adds an AI chat sidebar that uses the open paper's title, authors, abstract and full text as context. Selected text gets quick actions such as explain, critique, summarise and translate, replies can be saved as PDF annotations, and PDFs can be parsed to Markdown with MinerU. Needs an API key for your chosen model provider.
vvvastrong/marginmind.pain: Discussing a paper with an AI normally means copying text into a separate chat. This keeps the conversation beside the PDF and saves useful answers back.

gaviiiinnnn/zotero-settings-sync.does: Syncs Zotero preferences, plugin settings and installed plugin files, custom citation styles and Quick Copy site settings across devices. It uses Zotero's own sync through a dedicated collection, excludes file paths and account credentials, and has toggles for each category.
gaviiiinnnn/zotero-settings-sync.pain: Zotero sync doesn't carry settings or plugins, so each new computer needs setting up by hand. This needs no external account.

justinfjx/zotero-ai-collection.does: Suggests collections for items using an AI model. For each selected item it recommends one to three existing collections from the title and abstract, then shows a confirmation dialog where you accept or reject. It supports per-item or batch review, an archive collection and multiple API profiles. Needs your own API key.
justinfjx/zotero-ai-collection.pain: Filing a backlog of new papers into the right collections is repetitive. This suggests placements and leaves the decision to you. Its developer marks it as early beta.

edtechhub/zotero-edtechhub.does: Companion plugin for the EdTech Hub team. It adds KCite menu entries for Google Docs citations, copying select links and item URIs, saving item IDs to Extra, and duplicating attachments. It records merged items' fields in a note and warns if short-dois, Zutilo or ZotFile are missing.
edtechhub/zotero-edtechhub.pain: Built for EdTech Hub's workflow of sharing citations and keeping item IDs stable across merges, for people using the same Google Docs add-on.

b3000kcn/daily-folder-for-zotero.does: Adds a toolbar calendar button for creating and opening daily collections under a root Daily Folder, arranged as year, month and day. A Today's Folder button creates and opens the current day's collection.
b3000kcn/daily-folder-for-zotero.pain: People who file clippings, notes and reading by date otherwise create and find day collections by hand.

brycewg/zotero-ai-tags.does: Generates tags for selected items with an OpenAI-compatible model from the abstract and the first page of the best PDF attachment. It supports your own tagging rules, collection-specific rules, and settings for tag limits and request rates. Needs an API key.
brycewg/zotero-ai-tags.pain: Tagging a large library by hand is tedious and inconsistent. This applies your rules automatically. A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template; its README doesn't say what it changes.

juris-m/jurism-word-for-windows-integrat.does: Repackages the Zotero Word for Windows integration for use with Juris-M, with a chooser that prevents the Juris-M and Zotero versions being installed together.
juris-m/jurism-word-for-windows-integrat.pain: For people using Juris-M with Microsoft Word on Windows who need the citation integration.

ares960826/zotero-grouptag.does: Groups PDF reader tabs the way Chrome groups tabs, with coloured named headers and underlines. You can create, rename, recolour, collapse and delete groups and assign tabs by right-click, and groups persist between sessions.
ares960826/zotero-grouptag.pain: Many open PDFs make the tab bar hard to read. Grouping organises them without closing anything.

phdemotions/zotero-citegeist.does: Adds citation metrics from OpenAlex to your library. Sortable columns show citation count, field-weighted impact, percentile, journal metrics and rankings (UTD24, FT50, ABDC, AJG), alongside citation trends, author h-index and retraction flags. A browser follows citations both ways with one-click adding. A free OpenAlex key raises the daily limit.
phdemotions/zotero-citegeist.pain: Zotero has no built-in citation metrics. This lets you rank papers and snowball through citations without leaving the library.

018/zotupdate.does: Updates books' Chinese Library Classification numbers and Douban ratings, pulls tables of contents as notes, and tries to download sample chapters and e-books. It targets Chinese books, many sourced from Douban.
018/zotupdate.pain: Its features have moved into the zoturead plugin and it is no longer maintained.

garlicwu/filetrans_ai.does: Sends a selected PDF to an AI translation service and imports the translation, a side-by-side version, or both back to the item. It shows upload and processing progress. The source language is detected, the target is chosen in settings, and unfinished jobs resume after restart. Needs a service activation code, and the PDF is uploaded.
garlicwu/filetrans_ai.pain: Gives full-document PDF translation without leaving Zotero. The interface and documentation are Chinese.

leike0813/zotero-agents.does: An agent workbench for your library. Workflows cover literature analysis, search and import, tag normalisation, deep reading and topic synthesis, with an assistant sidebar and a CLI and MCP bridge for external agents. It needs an AI agent backend such as ACP agent tools or a Skill-Runner instance.
leike0813/zotero-agents.pain: For people who want AI agents to work inside their library on paper analysis and review preparation rather than answering one-off questions.

mobench/zotero-annotation-links.does: Makes zotero:// links in annotation comments clickable, so you can cross-reference annotations within a PDF or across documents. Copy a link with a right-click or Ctrl+Shift+C, paste it into another annotation, and the target is selected and highlighted on click. It makes no network requests.
mobench/zotero-annotation-links.pain: Zotero annotation comments don't support clickable links, so connecting related passages across sources is manual.

yueneiqi/zotero2eagle.does: Saves PDF image annotations to the Eagle image manager with their source details. It adds document title, authors, year, page and a backlink to the PDF, and optionally copies images to a local folder. Needs Eagle's API token, and its developer says it was tested only on macOS.
yueneiqi/zotero2eagle.pain: Clipped figures stay inside Zotero, away from your visual library. This sends them to Eagle with their source details.

zhouyi654/zotero-title-translator.does: Translates item titles and abstracts into Chinese and shows them in an item list column and the info sidebar, leaving the original fields unchanged. It translates selected items, collections or whole libraries, can translate on import, and supports a terminology list. Services include DeepL, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen or a local model.
zhouyi654/zotero-title-translator.pain: Scanning a foreign-language library is hard without translated titles. Translations are stored in Extra and sync with the item.

mpatelh/zbatch.does: Adds an item context menu for batch editing. Clear the Extra field of all selected items, or set any common field to a template string that can insert other fields such as title and date. A preview shows changes before they are applied. Zotero 6 only.
mpatelh/zbatch.pain: Editing the same field across many items one at a time is tedious. Its developer warns to back up your database first.

avi7ii/zotero-glass.does: Gives Zotero native macOS glass using NSVisualEffectView across the main library, PDF reader sidebars and annotation popups. Transparency, blur, colour and material are adjustable in settings. It switches Zotero to dark mode, and only works on macOS with Zotero 9.
avi7ii/zotero-glass.pain: For Mac users who want Zotero to look like a native macOS app rather than a flat window.

luckyang1/pdf-to-md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown or HTML with MinerU and saves the result as an attachment, with images, optionally automatically for new PDFs. It supports the MinerU Token API, a lightweight mode, or a local MinerU server, and can export attachments to a folder.
luckyang1/pdf-to-md.pain: Gives external AI agents and tools Markdown versions of papers rather than raw PDFs. Local MinerU keeps files off mineru.net.

shangkaijie/zotero-dual-title.does: Shows a translated title or short remark as a second line under each title in the item list. Row height, spacing, font size and colours for light and dark themes are adjustable, and it can use Zotero PDF Translate to translate new items' titles automatically.
shangkaijie/zotero-dual-title.pain: Reading a foreign-language library is easier when the translation sits beside the original without an extra column.

taotaozsky2025-beep/zotero-var-highlight.does: Highlights every occurrence of selected text across the whole PDF in the reader, with the first occurrence in green as the likely definition. Hovering over another match shows a preview of the page with the first occurrence. Colours, opacity and preview size are adjustable.
taotaozsky2025-beep/zotero-var-highlight.pain: In papers heavy with symbols, finding where a variable was defined means scrolling back. This shows it immediately.

0xc1c4da/zotero7-scidb.does: Adds a Download from SciDB right-click entry that fetches a PDF for items with a DOI from SciDB or Sci-Hub and attaches it. The endpoint can be changed in settings.
0xc1c4da/zotero7-scidb.pain: Saves manual hunting for papers behind paywalls. SciDB and Sci-Hub distribute copyrighted papers without permission, and using them is illegal in many jurisdictions. A Zotero 7 version of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub.

aarongig/pdf2zh-desktop.does: Connects Zotero to the pdf2zh-desktop translation app. A right-click entry translates a PDF, and the result returns as an attachment in side-by-side, bilingual or translation-only form. It needs the separate app, plus a key for a paid translation service or a local model.
aarongig/pdf2zh-desktop.pain: Translating whole papers while keeping formulas and layout normally means command-line tools and manual re-attaching. This links the process to your library.

qinsihan/zotero-paper-partner.does: Answers questions you write as Q: lines inside a Zotero note, inserting the answer below in the background after a short delay. Answers can be brief or detailed, and stale answers are flagged if you edit the note. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service, DeepSeek by default.
qinsihan/zotero-paper-partner.pain: Asking an AI about a confusing passage normally means leaving your notes for a chat window. This keeps question and answer in the note.

boan-anbo/cite-non-english.does: Manages metadata for non-English sources so citations show original script plus romanisation and translation. A CNE panel stores parallel titles, creators and publishers, and curated Chicago, APA and MLA styles are installed with it.
boan-anbo/cite-non-english.pain: Stock Zotero and its official styles can't print citations like 'Hua Linfu (华林甫)' with a romanised and translated title, which English-language humanities guides require. The usual workaround was the separate Juris-M.

sheny-bio/marginalia.does: An AI chat sidebar in the PDF reader that discusses the open paper using its full text. It adds quote-based questions, one-click translation of selected text into Chinese and chat history saved per paper. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service.
sheny-bio/marginalia.pain: Asking an AI about a paper otherwise means pasting text into a separate chat site. This keeps the conversation next to the PDF and can link a Zotero collection so the AI can search it.

juris-m/propachi-upper.does: Replaces Zotero's built-in CSL citation processor with an alternative version that capitalises subtitles. It is a patch for the Juris-M ecosystem and Zotero 6 only.
juris-m/propachi-upper.pain: For people whose citation style needs uppercase subtitles and whose styles the stock processor handles differently. Little else is documented.

lisontowind/zotero-copilot.does: A chat sidebar in the Zotero main window for asking questions about library items and PDF attachments. Keeps multi-session history, accepts dragged items as context, can use MinerU Markdown results, and lets you configure model providers and system prompts.
lisontowind/zotero-copilot.pain: Lets you question your papers without leaving Zotero or copying text into a web chat, with conversations kept per session inside your library.

makinteract/notero-notes.does: Syncs Zotero items into a Notion database, one page per item, and also writes Zotero notes into a ZoteroNotes field in that database. Syncs on modification or from the right-click menu.
makinteract/notero-notes.pain: A fork of dvanoni/notero that adds a notes field to the Notion database. Its author warns that newer Zotero versions break note syncing for many users and suggests the original Notero.

xiaoducomrade/zotero-margin-comments.does: Shows highlight comments and standalone notes as editable cards in the left or right margin of the PDF page, joined to the annotation by a leader line. Edits save back to the Zotero annotation. Works in Zotero 9 and is documented in Chinese.
xiaoducomrade/zotero-margin-comments.pain: Zotero shows annotation comments only in the reader sidebar, so your eyes keep jumping between text and explanation. This puts each comment beside the passage it explains.

kaguratart/literature-review-with-llm.does: A paper chat workbench that generates Markdown summaries of papers as linked attachments. It answers questions about a selected paper and compares several papers into a literature matrix and collection-level review drafts. Works with many LLM providers, including local ones such as Ollama.
kaguratart/literature-review-with-llm.pain: Turns reading and reviewing a set of papers into saved Markdown notes with evidence labels, instead of ad hoc chats. Its developer says it is usable but still early.

chen7447/rapidocr-for-zotero.does: Runs OCR on scanned PDFs inside Zotero using the bundled RapidOCR engine and saves a searchable copy as a separate [OCR] attachment. You can OCR a drawn region or the current page. Mainly aimed at Chinese and mixed Chinese-English documents.
chen7447/rapidocr-for-zotero.pain: Scanned PDFs can't be searched, selected or translated, and most OCR tools need Python or Tesseract installed. This needs no external software and sends nothing over the network.

dirreke/zotero-metadata-translator.does: Creates English versions of Chinese journal articles and writes English citation metadata. It writes original-title, original-author and original-container-title lines into the Extra field, taking titles and authors from indexed PDFs or snapshots, with pinyin as a fallback for authors. Commands are in the right-click menu.
dirreke/zotero-metadata-translator.pain: For people who must cite Chinese journal papers with English metadata in CSL styles, and would otherwise type it by hand.

xiaoducomrade/zotero-reading-heatmap.does: Tracks the time Zotero is active and shows it as a GitHub-style heatmap in the side panel. It shows week or month views with total, streak and active-day statistics. It can sync with a group through a server you deploy and import data from Zotero Style.
xiaoducomrade/zotero-reading-heatmap.pain: Zotero doesn't tell you how much you actually read. This gives a running record of reading time and streaks, and lets a reading group compare.

iu-parvej/zotero-pdf-copier-renamer.does: Copies the PDFs of selected items into a folder you pick, renamed after each item's title. A right-click command handles many items at once, removes illegal filename characters and numbers duplicate names.
iu-parvej/zotero-pdf-copier-renamer.pain: Zotero hides PDFs in randomly named storage folders with generic filenames, so exporting a batch to a USB stick, cloud folder or tablet means opening each folder by hand.

aidecameron/zotero-annotation-color-cust.does: Replaces the default colour names in the PDF reader's annotation colour tooltips and right-click menu with names you choose, such as a meaning for each colour. Switch between default and custom mode in settings. Works in Zotero 7.
aidecameron/zotero-annotation-color-cust.pain: If each highlight colour means something to you, like methods or results, Zotero still shows plain names like Yellow. This lets the labels say what you mean.

papermachines/papermachines.does: Analyses and visualises a collection's full text for digital humanities research. It offers word clouds, phrase nets, maps of places mentioned, topic modelling and DBpedia annotation from the collection's right-click menu. Needs Java.
papermachines/papermachines.pain: Lets historians and other researchers explore a large corpus without programming skills. It is unmaintained and no longer works on current Zotero; its author suggests Voyant Tools.

rafael-silva-oliveira/numify.does: Adds hierarchical numeric prefixes such as 1, 1.1 and 1.1.1 to collection names and keeps them in step when you create, rename or delete collections. Set the depth, separator and zero padding, and reorder by editing a prefix.
rafael-silva-oliveira/numify.pain: Zotero sorts collections only by name and has no way to reorder them freely, so a numbered outline of your library is hard to keep tidy by hand.

lelelelelelelelelelelelele/arxiv-marker.does: Finds the real publishing venue of arXiv preprints and writes it back to the item. It looks up Semantic Scholar, DBLP and OpenReview, shows CCF or CORE tier and citation counts in a review dialog, then converts the item type. A Semantic Scholar key is optional.
lelelelelelelelelelelelele/arxiv-marker.pain: Preprints have no venue field, so journal ranking and citation plugins show nothing for them. This fills in the venue so those plugins can work, and leaves uncertain matches for you to review.

zhang-hz/zotero-autofetch.does: Automatically downloads PDFs for new items from Sci-Hub and Google Scholar. It is a Zotero 6 era plugin with no further documentation.
zhang-hz/zotero-autofetch.pain: Saves hunting for papers behind paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

tangzhao20/zotero-citation-counts.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP or Semantic Scholar and shows them in a sortable Citations column. Counts load automatically for new items or from the right-click menu, and it can search Crossref by title when there is no DOI.
tangzhao20/zotero-citation-counts.pain: Zotero has no built-in citation counts, so judging or ranking a reading list means looking papers up one at a time elsewhere.

max3925vats/zotero-docling.does: Converts PDF attachments to structured Markdown using a local docling-serve server and attaches the .md file to the same item. Offers OCR, table and formula options, optional auto-convert on import, image removal and a zip export of Markdown files.
max3925vats/zotero-docling.pain: Markdown works better than PDF for Obsidian, AI pipelines and text analysis. You must run the docling-serve converter yourself, and the first conversion downloads model weights.

imagontutu/zotero-filelink-bridge.does: Runs a small local HTTP endpoint inside Zotero so scripts and AI agents can attach an existing file to an item as a linked file, with a dry-run check first. Supports Windows and WSL paths.
imagontutu/zotero-filelink-bridge.pain: Tools that produce OCR text, Markdown or reports leave files elsewhere, and Zotero's web API can't create a desktop linked-file attachment. This links them without copying into Zotero storage.

scigreat/zotbox.does: A Chinese-focused research helper that shows journal rankings, impact factors and citation counts beside each item. It adds impact factors, JCR and CAS quartiles, Peking and Nanjing core journal lists and CCF ranking, with citation counts from CNKI, Google Scholar, Crossref and Semantic Scholar. It also checks retractions, translates titles and abstracts and offers AI summaries.
scigreat/zotbox.pain: Judging a journal or paper's standing means checking many databases by hand. This puts the indicators beside each item, with Chinese university rankings too. Some data sources and AI features need their own API keys.

beaugunderson/zoteroquicklookng.does: Opens the selected item's PDF in macOS Quick Look when you press space in the items list. An attachment opens itself, an item opens its first PDF, and several selections open together. macOS only.
beaugunderson/zoteroquicklookng.pain: Previewing a paper normally means opening it in a Zotero tab. A fork of mronkko/ZoteroQuickLook, rewritten for Zotero 7 and later.

aokellermann/zotero-nexus.does: Adds Nexus, an IPFS-backed paper search site, as a last-resort source to Zotero's PDF resolver, so Find Full Text can fetch PDFs for items with a DOI. Separate downloads exist for Zotero 6 and 7.
aokellermann/zotero-nexus.pain: For researchers who can't reach a paper through open access or their institution. Its developer warns to keep your local laws in mind, as such sources may distribute papers without permission.

xutaoya/paper-mind.does: An AI chat sidebar in the Zotero PDF reader: ask about the paper, attach its full text, send screenshots of selected figures, and save bookmarks from answers. Works with OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek and others using your own API key, with MinerU parsing as a fallback.
xutaoya/paper-mind.pain: A fork of syt2/paper-chat-for-zotero that adds automatic continuation of cut-off replies, LaTeX in exported notes and model speed tests, and drops slide generation and the built-in service.

psiqaq/zotero-agent.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero with 47 tools so an AI client can operate your library. An AI client such as Claude Code or Codex can search, tag, import, de-duplicate and enrich items, fetch PDFs and synthesise annotations. Writes default to dry-run, and a JavaScript tool can be enabled.
psiqaq/zotero-agent.pain: Lets an AI assistant do bulk library clean-up through a local connection instead of manual work. Its PDF tools can use Sci-Hub and Anna's Archive, which distribute copyrighted papers without permission.

xiaoducomrade/zotero-margin-notes.does: Makes a widened copy of a selected PDF with extra blank margin on any side, imported as a sibling attachment named like paper.margin.pdf. You annotate the added space with Zotero's own text and drawing tools. The original is not modified.
xiaoducomrade/zotero-margin-notes.pain: Zotero's reader gives you no room to write beyond the printed margins. A separate setting also reopens the last PDF you opened for items with several PDFs.

drusagi/colorful-bionic.does: Adds bionic reading to the Zotero reader: bolds the start of each word and colours verbs, nouns and conjunctions differently. Uses the compromise language library, so word-type detection is imperfect.
drusagi/colorful-bionic.pain: Aimed at readers who find long papers hard to follow, such as people with ADHD, by making sentence actions and structure stand out.

sciencelivehub/science-live-platform.does: Creates signed nanopublications from Zotero items using template forms, and searches and imports existing nanopublications into your library. Publishing needs a free Science Live Platform account, and the plugin connects to your Science Live account by API key.
sciencelivehub/science-live-platform.pain: For researchers who want to publish findings as structured, citable FAIR nanopublications and link them to their bibliography.

zorrostardust/zotero-vim-plus.does: Vim-style keybindings for the Zotero PDF reader and note editors. You can scroll, jump between annotations, move a text cursor, make visual selections, create highlights and set marks. Every key can be remapped, and snapshots and EPUBs get a smaller set.
zorrostardust/zotero-vim-plus.pain: Lets keyboard-driven readers navigate and annotate papers without the mouse. A fork of the original Zotero Vim project.

ben-ai-cybersec/zotero-publication-ranki.does: Adds a sortable Ranking column showing SJR quartiles, CORE conference ranks, ABS, FT50 and VHB ratings for each item's journal or conference, colour coded. Includes manual overrides and a command that writes the ranking into the Extra field.
ben-ai-cybersec/zotero-publication-ranki.pain: Checking a venue's standing normally means looking it up on separate ranking sites. This shows it beside each item without changing your metadata.

chen7447/journal-tags.does: Adds Journal Tags and Impact Factor columns to the items list using EasyScholar data, with configurable fields, colours and sorting, and a local cache. Needs your EasyScholar secret key. Documented in Chinese.
chen7447/journal-tags.pain: A lean version of the journal indicator feature of Zotero Style, for Chinese-language researchers who want only ranking tags and impact factors.

ievlevpn/zotero-time-tracking.does: Adds a toolbar button to the reader with a stopwatch, pomodoro timer and manual time entry, and totals the time per item in a Reading time field and column. A history window shows streaks and a heatmap of sessions in its own SQLite database. Built for Zotero 10.
ievlevpn/zotero-time-tracking.pain: Zotero doesn't record how long you spend on a paper or book, so there is nothing to look back on or set goals against.

huachuanchuan/zoterofastread.does: Translates English PDFs into a bilingual copy with the layout kept, shown with original on the left and Chinese on the right and scrolling together. Built on Babel-Doc, with single and batch jobs. Needs a translation model API key (DeepSeek by default) and Python.
huachuanchuan/zoterofastread.pain: Reading English papers in Chinese usually loses the layout. This keeps figures and formulas in place, though the author says a paper takes around five minutes.

haohaomin/zotero-codex.does: Connects Zotero and Better Notes to the Codex AI client through a local MCP server. It has 43 tools to read PDF pages and images, see the current paper and selection, read annotations and edit notes live. Needs Zotero 10, and Better Notes for note work.
haohaomin/zotero-codex.pain: Lets you discuss the paper you are reading and write notes with Codex without copying text between apps. Selected paper and note content is passed to your AI client.

lyz-623/zotassets.does: Gives each attachment a role such as main PDF, supplement, data, code, scan or preprint. Roles are detected from the first page of the PDF, previewed before applying, and PDFs can be renamed safely by template with the originals recoverable.
lyz-623/zotassets.pain: Items with many attachments are hard to tell apart when files are all named alike. This labels each file's purpose and shows it.

x1aox1a/zofiles.does: Mirrors your collections as real folders, one per paper, with the PDF, full-text Markdown, BibTeX, an AI review from papers.cool and notes as Markdown. Syncs on every library change and includes Claude Code skills. Works for papers with arXiv IDs.
x1aox1a/zofiles.pain: AI agents and other tools can't read Zotero's database directly. This gives them an ordinary folder tree to read, summarise and cite from.

babylonehy/zetero-babeldoc.does: Translates PDFs into side-by-side bilingual PDFs by running the local BabelDOC command. It has a task queue, retry, and automatic import of results under the original item. Needs BabelDOC installed and an OpenAI-compatible model with its base URL.
babylonehy/zetero-babeldoc.pain: Translates papers while keeping their layout and puts the result in your library, using a model you control instead of a third-party service.

juris-m/bluebook-signals-for-zotero.does: Adds a drop-down menu of standard Bluebook signals to the Prefix field in the word processor citation dialogs of Zotero and MLZ. Legacy plugin.
juris-m/bluebook-signals-for-zotero.pain: Lawyers citing in Bluebook style can pick a signal such as 'See' or 'Cf.' instead of typing it each time.

yimmy23/zotero-refs.does: Adds References, Cited By, Related and Citation Graph sections to the item pane in the library and the reader. The reference list merges the PDF's own reference text with Crossref, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex data, and can import or copy entries. Keys are optional.
yimmy23/zotero-refs.pain: Finding what a paper cites and who cites it normally means leaving Zotero. This shows both, marks what is already in your library and adds the rest.

tomyu2023/zone.does: A PDF download assistant for Zotero 10 that downloads and attaches PDFs automatically. It also searches ResearchGate and pre-fills DOI help requests on the Chinese site Ablesci (科研通).
tomyu2023/zone.pain: For researchers who can't get a paper's PDF through Zotero's built-in lookup and want other places to find it.

pierreadorni/zotserver.does: Adds a local HTTP API to Zotero's built-in server, with a search endpoint that takes JSON conditions such as quick search or tag. Other desktop apps can query your library without internet.
pierreadorni/zotserver.pain: Lets note-taking and other tools search and link to Zotero items offline. A fork of MunGell/ZotServer; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jorgepb96/nodus.does: An item-pane research assistant that works with the separate Nodus Research desktop app. It offers semantic search over full text, citations tied to sources, OCR and visual document understanding, and the app also has vaults for databases, genealogy, study and teaching.
jorgepb96/nodus.pain: For researchers who want a connected idea graph, argument maps and cited writing built from their Zotero corpus.

ievlevpn/zotero-latex-suite.does: Renders LaTeX in PDF annotation comments as you type. It also brings Obsidian Latex Suite snippets to annotations and notes, including auto-fractions, tabstops, matrix shortcuts and bracket sizing, with about 220 default snippets you can edit.
ievlevpn/zotero-latex-suite.pain: Zotero renders equations in notes but not in annotation comments, where most reading notes get written. It also makes typing LaTeX quick if you use Obsidian.

lilykun064/autotag_zotero_plugin.does: Suggests and adds tags to selected items using an LLM, with a choice of what item information and full text to send. Providers are OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter or a local model through Ollama. Cloud providers need your own API key.
lilykun064/autotag_zotero_plugin.pain: Hand tagging doesn't scale and drifts over time, so similar papers end up with different tags. This applies consistent, content-based tags in bulk.

nightwatcher314/zotero-pdf2zh-next.does: Translates PDFs through a local Python service running pdf2zh_next, outputting Chinese or bilingual PDFs, with a task panel for progress, cancel and retry. The service installs through Homebrew, uv or Docker, and you configure your own LLM API.
nightwatcher314/zotero-pdf2zh-next.pain: A fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh, trimmed to the plugin plus one local service, with a task manager and simpler setup. Preserves layout while translating papers into Chinese.

zerolfl/zotero-split-view-reader.does: Shows two PDFs, or the same PDF twice, side by side in one reader tab, opened from the command palette. You can swap, replace or separate the panes, and set a primary view so the other pane follows its scrolling and zoom.
zerolfl/zotero-split-view-reader.pain: Zotero's reader shows one document per tab, which makes comparing two papers or reading a main text with its supplement awkward.

daxiaxiong88/zotero-research.does: A reading sidebar for Zotero 10 that sends the current page, selection or full text to AI chat. The text goes to web AIs such as Gemini, DeepSeek, ChatGPT, Kimi or Claude through a Tampermonkey script, or to an API you configure. Answers return to Zotero with page-linked evidence. MinerU parsing is optional.
daxiaxiong88/zotero-research.pain: Lets you use AI chat sites you are already logged in to, without copying questions and answers back and forth or needing an API key in web mode.

jarvis-towne/paper-feed-zotero.does: Fetches journal RSS feeds, filters them by keyword rules, and serves the matches as a local RSS feed that Zotero subscribes to. Optional AI summaries of new papers use your OpenAI-compatible API and your research-interest prompt.
jarvis-towne/paper-feed-zotero.pain: Keeps up with new papers in your field without external scripts or GitHub Actions. It only runs while Zotero is open.

slowphil/zotexmacs.does: Inserts a citation tag for the items selected in Zotero into the active GNU TeXmacs document. Needs both Zotero and TeXmacs installed, plus a plugin folder copied into your TeXmacs settings.
slowphil/zotexmacs.pain: For TeXmacs authors who manage references in Zotero and don't want to look up or guess citation keys.

quertt/zotero-keyword-highlighter.does: Highlights your own keyword lists in the open PDF with Ctrl+Shift+H, with a colour per named category. Uses the reader's search highlighting, so no annotations are created and highlights vanish when the PDF closes. Interface in English, German, Spanish and French.
quertt/zotero-keyword-highlighter.pain: Lets you scan papers for terms like methods or key concepts without cluttering your library with annotations.

mengqi97/codex-bilingual-reader-for-zote.does: Turns a PDF into a layout-preserving English and Chinese bilingual PDF using the local Codex CLI or an OpenAI-compatible API such as OpenAI or DeepSeek. Supports batch queues, cost tracking, and imports the result next to the original. Paper text goes to your chosen provider.
mengqi97/codex-bilingual-reader-for-zote.pain: Reading English papers in Chinese usually loses figures, formulas and tables. This keeps them in place. Windows setup downloads a separate engine of about 600 MB.

liozhang/z-search.does: Searches 13 academic sources in parallel from one window and imports results into your library with open-access PDFs. Result cards show citation counts, impact factor, JCR and CAS quartiles and warning or predatory-journal flags from bundled offline data. It also offers citation traversal, full-text fetching, abstract translation and vector search of your library.
liozhang/z-search.pain: Finding papers, checking journal quality and importing them normally means several websites and manual steps. This gathers search, journal-quality checks and import in one place inside Zotero.

alleyf/zotero-duplicate-cleaner.does: Scans your library for duplicate items, byte-identical duplicate PDFs, duplicate notes, orphan PDFs and broken attachments, then lets you review and clear them. Duplicate PDFs are matched by SHA-256 hash locally, nothing is uploaded, and deletions go to Zotero's trash. Aimed at Chinese-speaking users, with a Chinese interface.
alleyf/zotero-duplicate-cleaner.pain: Large libraries collect duplicate records, repeated PDFs and attachments whose files have gone missing. This lists them for review so you can tidy up without deleting anything blindly.

xfl031129/zotero-pdf-outline-builder.does: Generates PDF bookmarks for papers whose outline panel is empty, via a right-click command on selected items or PDF attachments. Headings are detected locally with a Python and PyMuPDF engine, no AI service or API key, and the outline is written into the PDF itself. The Windows release bundles the helper; scanned PDFs need OCR first.
xfl031129/zotero-pdf-outline-builder.pain: Papers without an outline give you nothing to jump between in Zotero's reader. This builds one from the document's own headings so you can navigate long PDFs.

juris-m/jurism-word-for-mac-integration.does: Repackages the Zotero Word for Mac integration so it works with the Juris-M referencing platform. It includes a chooser that stops the Juris-M and Zotero versions from being installed at the same time.
juris-m/jurism-word-for-mac-integration.pain: For legal researchers who use Juris-M and want to cite from Microsoft Word on a Mac.

anfang886/zotero-doi-column.does: Adds a DOI column to Zotero's items list, so you can read DOIs down a list without opening each item. You switch it on from the column picker under More Columns.
anfang886/zotero-doi-column.pain: Zotero stores the DOI as a field but doesn't offer it as a column. Seeing DOIs side by side helps when checking a reference list or spotting duplicates that Zotero's own matching missed, and sorting by DOI roughly groups items by publisher.

bulletproof-system/zotero-maimemo-sync.does: Syncs highlighted words and annotations from Zotero into a cloud word list in the Maimemo vocabulary app, or exports them as a text file. You choose append or overwrite, split by annotation or by word, and filter by highlight colour. Needs a Maimemo open-API token.
bulletproof-system/zotero-maimemo-sync.pain: For people who read papers in another language and use Maimemo to learn vocabulary: it saves retyping marked words into the app. The exported text file also imports into other word-learning apps.

juliusbairaktaris/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up DOIs and shortDOIs for selected items through the Crossref API and checks that stored DOIs are valid. It can replace a DOI with its short or long form, strip prefixes such as doi: or a publisher URL, and tag invalid, missing or ambiguous DOIs. A fork of bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi, updated for Zotero 10.
juliusbairaktaris/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Messy or missing DOIs break lookups, citations and duplicate detection. This finds, cleans and validates them in bulk and only ever writes to the DOI field.

ouyangjiahong26/bibtex-clean.does: Cleans item fields from the right-click menu so BibTeX export comes out tidier: author separators become 'and', and No. and Vol. prefixes (and the Chinese characters for issue) are stripped from issue and volume. You preview changes first and can undo the last clean. It also bulk-removes chosen linked attachments and notes and duplicate attachments.
ouyangjiahong26/bibtex-clean.pain: Metadata imported from Chinese databases or patents often exports to BibTeX with malformed authors and issue numbers. This fixes the fields in one step and clears leftover duplicate attachments after merges.

suraj1kc/zotero-folder-drop-importer.does: Imports a folder from your computer into Zotero as nested collections that mirror the directory tree, with each file added as an attachment item. Start it from File, a collection's right-click menu, or by dragging folders onto Zotero. Files are copied into Zotero storage or imported as linked files.
suraj1kc/zotero-folder-drop-importer.pain: Bringing in an existing, organised folder of PDFs otherwise means recreating the collections and importing files by hand. This keeps your folder structure in one step.

ziondoki/confucius.does: A research assistant chat inside Zotero that discovers papers through OpenAlex, fetches available full text and reads or compares papers with you. It can write notes, reports and PDF annotations, and shows a diff before anything is saved to Zotero. Needs an OpenAlex API key, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama, Codex or Kimi for the model.
ziondoki/confucius.pain: Literature search, reading and note-taking usually happen in separate tools. This keeps a research question, candidate papers and evidence in one conversation connected to your library.

arqueon/zotero-tagnavigator.does: A separate tag explorer window with three panes: tags on the left, items in the middle, details and actions on the right. You filter items by tag, text, creator, year or PDF availability, save filter views, and rename, merge or remove tags. It also adds batch and drag-and-drop tagging and copies citation keys or formatted citations.
arqueon/zotero-tagnavigator.pain: Zotero's tag selector gets slow and cramped in big libraries. This gives a roomier workspace for browsing, combining and editing tags across personal and group libraries.

binbinsh/zotero-easytrans.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader entirely offline with the TranslateGemma 4B model running locally, and saves the translation as an annotation. Supports 14 languages including English, Chinese, Spanish, French, German and Japanese. The model is a one-time download of about 2.5 GB.
binbinsh/zotero-easytrans.pain: For readers who don't want to send paper text to an online translator or pay for an API. Nothing is uploaded, and translations stay attached to your reading.

rtliang/zotero-codex.does: A sidebar in the item pane and PDF reader for discussing a paper with Codex. You can attach citation details, the abstract or selected PDF text, add images, and continue conversations in Codex Desktop or the command line. Needs the Codex CLI installed and signed in with codex login.
rtliang/zotero-codex.pain: Saves switching between Zotero and a separate Codex window when you want to ask questions about the paper you are reading, with each paper remembering its conversation.

ievlevpn/zotero-djvu-converter.does: Converts DJVU attachments to PDF, prompting automatically when you add one or from a right-click menu. It can add an OCR text layer in 12 languages, compress the PDF, drop the cover page, keep bookmarks and replace or keep the original. Needs DjVuLibre installed, plus ocrmypdf and Tesseract for OCR and compression.
ievlevpn/zotero-djvu-converter.pain: Zotero's reader doesn't open DJVU files, so scanned books in that format can't be read or searched. This turns them into ordinary PDFs.

qnscholar/zotero-clear-field.does: Adds a Clear Field command to the Tools menu that blanks the fields you choose on one or several selected items. Has a Chinese interface.
qnscholar/zotero-clear-field.pain: Clearing the same field on many items by hand is slow. This does it in one step.

yansh258/zotero-dailypaper.does: Scores new papers from your Zotero feeds against research directions you set, using DeepSeek or another OpenAI-compatible model. It adds high scorers to a target collection, sorts them into existing sub-folders, extracts keywords and writes Chinese reading notes. Scores and reasons are stored in the Extra field, and scoring can run daily. Needs an API key.
yansh258/zotero-dailypaper.pain: Feeds deliver far more papers than anyone can read. This filters and files them against your own topics so you only open the relevant ones.

1654842532/zotero-ai-assistant.does: Summarises a paper from the right-click menu by extracting the PDF text and sending it to DeepSeek. It writes a structured note with metadata, a Chinese title translation, a plain-language overview, key points and a subject classification, and tags the item. An optional local Python server can extract text from large PDFs. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
1654842532/zotero-ai-assistant.pain: Reading a paper just to decide whether it matters takes time. This produces a structured Chinese summary note and tags straight from the PDF.

danieleongari/zotero-openalex.does: Looks up items on OpenAlex by DOI and stores the Work ID and citation count in the Extra field, refreshing counts when they get old. Adds a Citations column, an item menu entry to open the OpenAlex page and a collection command that draws citation, per-year and co-author graphs. An OpenAlex API key is optional.
danieleongari/zotero-openalex.pain: Zotero has no built-in citation counts. This keeps them current and lets you see how the papers in a collection cite and relate to each other.

ievlevpn/zotero-feed-riffle.does: Deals unread RSS feed items one card at a time: left arrow discards, right arrow files into a collection. You pick it by fuzzy search, with optional tags and a note. Keys 1 to 9 file straight into recent collections, skipped items stay unread, and cards already in your library are marked.
ievlevpn/zotero-feed-riffle.pain: Zotero's feed reader needs several clicks per item, so large backlogs never get cleared. This makes each decision a single keypress.

jlegewie/zotfile-recovery.does: Recovers attachment files that ZotFile sent to a tablet folder and that Zotero 7 can no longer reach. A right-click menu item is enabled only when you select an attachment with such a tablet file, and it moves the file back, like ZotFile's Get from Tablet.
jlegewie/zotfile-recovery.pain: ZotFile doesn't work on Zotero 7, which can leave tablet-mode files stranded in the tablet folder. This brings them back.

paulmrg2/zotero-highlight-descriptions.does: Adds your own text labels, such as Important or Disagree, to highlight colours. They appear in the annotation right-click menu, the text-selection popup and the toolbar colour picker. Labels are edited and reordered in the plugin settings, and uninstalling removes them cleanly.
paulmrg2/zotero-highlight-descriptions.pain: Zotero shows highlight colours with no meaning attached, so you have to remember what each colour stood for. Labels make your colour system visible while you annotate.

loooookk/zotero-deepseek.does: Connects Zotero 9 to DeepSeek for summaries, full-text paper Q&A and comparison tables for 2 to 15 papers. It also builds structured reading notes from your notes and annotations. In the PDF reader you can translate selected text into Chinese or ask about a passage. Results save as notes. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
loooookk/zotero-deepseek.pain: Gives Chinese-speaking researchers a way to summarise, question and compare papers without leaving Zotero or pasting text into a chatbot.

liunuozhi/zotero-scholar.does: Fetches a citation count from Semantic Scholar for arXiv papers.
liunuozhi/zotero-scholar.pain: Gives a quick measure of how often an arXiv paper has been cited. It works for arXiv papers only.

milekpl/zotero-search-replace.does: Searches fields such as title, creators, abstract, tags and DOI and replaces text in bulk, using regular expressions, exact match or SQL LIKE patterns. You preview changes before applying them, and it includes 23 preset patterns for common bibliographic errors. Searches are limited to the selected collection, and results can be saved as a collection.
milekpl/zotero-search-replace.pain: Fixing the same metadata mistake across hundreds of items by hand is tedious. This applies one pattern to all of them with a preview first.

qingpy/zotero-pdf2md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown with the MinerU service and attaches the .md file next to the PDF. It can also copy chosen attachment types to a folder. A free MinerU token raises the page and size limits; without one a limited light API is used. PDFs are uploaded to mineru.net.
qingpy/zotero-pdf2md.pain: Markdown is easier to search and uses less context than PDF when feeding papers to language models, agents or scripts.

zuphilip/zotero-open-citations.does: Looks up selected items by DOI in the OpenCitations COCI service and adds the result as a note. The latest references are saved in a special collection in Zotero.
zuphilip/zotero-open-citations.pain: Adds open citation data to items in your library. Its developer marks it as early, with more functions still to do.

et06731/zotero-paper2slides.does: Turns a paper's PDF into an HTML slide deck or a structured Markdown note with a right-click command, using an LLM. Choose DeepSeek, Kimi, OpenAI, Gemini and others, or a local Ollama model, plus slide styles, prompt presets, note templates and Chinese or English output. Needs an API key unless you use a local model.
et06731/zotero-paper2slides.pain: Preparing a talk or reading summary from a paper is slow manual work. This drafts both from the PDF and saves them with the item.

yimmy23/zotero-zest.does: Records reading time per page and shows it as a heat bar in the item list, with columns for read status, star rating and journal data. Also provides an item info panel, annotation tools, a library relationship graph, reading statistics, nested tags and vertical tabs. Journal data comes from local sets, easyScholar or OpenAlex. Chinese-focused, for Zotero 10.
yimmy23/zotero-zest.pain: Zotero doesn't track how much of a paper you have actually read. Zest adds reading records and journal rankings to the list view, mainly for Chinese-language research.

kongyan66/arxiv2zh.does: Translates arXiv papers into Chinese through the hjfy.top service and saves the translated PDF to the item. It finds the arXiv ID from the item, uses the TeX source when it can, and otherwise uploads the attached PDF of up to 50 MB. Handles several items at once and can create a preprint item from an arXiv link. Needs an hjfy.top account.
kongyan66/arxiv2zh.pain: Reading English papers in Chinese usually means running a separate translation tool. This sends the paper for translation and files the result with the original.

ievlevpn/zotero-tag-explorer.does: A window for browsing your annotation tags: fuzzy-search every tag, then read the highlights and comments behind it, grouped by book, with LaTeX typeset. You can limit it to one collection, search all highlights, rename tags, browse by book with related books, and review possible duplicate tags.
ievlevpn/zotero-tag-explorer.pain: Tags on highlights are hard to use in stock Zotero, where you can't easily read everything you marked under one tag. This turns them into a searchable reading view.

lanl/zotero-robust-links-extension.does: Creates Robust Links for web resources from within Zotero, building on web archives and the Memento protocol. Its developer points to external instructions for use.
lanl/zotero-robust-links-extension.pain: Links to web pages break over time. Robust Links add archived copies so a reference stays reachable.

sharpevo/zotero-pdfkit.does: Adds two right-click commands. Set as Default makes a chosen PDF open on double-click by changing its Date Added, and Copy URI copies a zotero://select link to the item.
sharpevo/zotero-pdfkit.pain: Items with several PDFs always open the same one first, and sharing a link to an item needs a workaround. This handles both.

mxlapan/zotero-prism.does: Four optional modules: library analytics, an AI assistant, layout-keeping full-text translation and reading management. Analytics covers reading heat, journal quartiles, citation counts, ratings, a relationship graph and an annotation manager. The AI and some translation engines need API keys. Chinese-focused interface.
mxlapan/zotero-prism.pain: Brings reading tracking, journal rankings, AI help and translation into Zotero in one place, mainly for Chinese-language researchers.

windlx/paper_plane_x.does: Side panel for the Paper Plane X research workbench. Send PDFs from Zotero for parsing, view processing status, link projects and browse structured analysis and fact-check results. The backend runs separately and needs Python, uv and your own LLM and PDF parser settings.
windlx/paper_plane_x.pain: For researchers who want AI-assisted reading and review writing grounded in their own papers and kept on their own machine.

pobrien333/citationstyler-client-sync.does: Installs and updates custom citation styles you bought from CitationStyler.com. You enter your purchase email and licence key in Zotero's settings, then install or update each style. A Zotero account must be signed in. A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template.
pobrien333/citationstyler-client-sync.pain: Lets customers of the CitationStyler service get their styles into Zotero and keep them current without installing files by hand.

fangziyang0910/zotero-ccf-plus.does: Labels items with their CCF rating (A, B or C, using the 2026 seventh-edition list), fills in the full journal or conference name and fetches a citation count. It uses Semantic Scholar and DBLP, shows colour tags and a citations column, and stores the result in a child note. For computer science, using the Chinese CCF list.
fangziyang0910/zotero-ccf-plus.pain: Checking CCF rankings and citation counts by hand for each paper is slow. This does it in one right-click.

rafael-silva-oliveira/paperzorro.does: Searches PubMed, arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv with a visual boolean query builder. An AI model judges each result YES or NO with a reason, then approved papers are imported into a collection. Searches can run daily or weekly. It uses local Ollama by default, or optional OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini keys.
rafael-silva-oliveira/paperzorro.pain: Literature alerts bring in a lot of irrelevant papers. This filters results against your own criteria before anything reaches your library.

qiujv/zotero-hashtags-column.does: Adds a column to the item list that shows only tags starting with a special prefix such as #, @, -, !, %, ^, & or *.
qiujv/zotero-hashtags-column.pain: Items with many imported tags bury the ones you added yourself. A separate column keeps your prefixed tags visible.

kevin65536/zotero-datacheck-plugin.does: Analyses table text you select in the PDF reader for statistical oddities and shows a report. It flags repeated rows and number sequences, out-of-range percentages and p-values, rounding pile-ups and low-variation columns, and gives a Benford's law hint when the sample allows. Runs locally.
kevin65536/zotero-datacheck-plugin.pain: Helps reviewers and readers spot table data worth a closer look. The report marks risk signals only and doesn't prove a problem.

ievlevpn/zotero-sentence-focus.does: A reading ruler that highlights one sentence at a time in PDFs, EPUBs and web snapshots, stepping with keyboard shortcuts or clicks. It understands equations, tables, abbreviations and hyphenated words, can turn the current sentence into a Zotero highlight or underline, and remembers your place in each document.
ievlevpn/zotero-sentence-focus.pain: Line-by-line rulers cut sentences apart when they span lines, columns or formulas. This follows the sentence instead, which helps focused reading of dense papers.

juris-m/jurism-libreoffice-integration.does: Repackages the Zotero LibreOffice integration so it works with the Juris-M referencing platform. Alongside the official Zotero plugin it offers a chooser that prevents both versions being installed at once.
juris-m/jurism-libreoffice-integration.pain: For legal researchers who use Juris-M and want to cite from LibreOffice.

ub-unibe-ch/zotero-swissbib-bb-locations.does: Checks shelf locations of selected titles in Swisscovery at the University Library Bern through its SRU interface, writes the result into a field and sets tags. It also builds order notes from tags, with searchable pickers for DDC classes and order codes. Needs an Ex Libris Alma API key. The interface is in German.
ub-unibe-ch/zotero-swissbib-bb-locations.pain: Built for acquisition work at UB Bern, where staff need to see what the library already holds and record order details on titles in Zotero or Jurism.

heimi98/zotero-random-read.does: Adds a dice button that opens a random readable attachment from the collections you choose, favouring documents you've never opened or haven't opened lately. History is stored locally on your device and can be cleared. It also sets a default PDF page size for the built-in reader.
heimi98/zotero-random-read.pain: Large libraries hold papers you saved and never read. This brings them back into view.

by1907047/zotero-management-bridge.does: A local bridge that lets automation agents and scripts manage Zotero through a controlled set of operations. They can query items, create or update items and collections, link attachments, find duplicate attachments, and trash or erase by key. Requests are JSON files read from a folder, risky operations run as a dry run first, and a Python CLI is included.
by1907047/zotero-management-bridge.pain: For people who drive Zotero from scripts or AI agents and want predictable, auditable changes rather than arbitrary code.

gokoruri007/zotero-api-plus.does: Extends Zotero local API with extra endpoints. These cover a health check, adding items by identifier (DOI, ISBN, PMID) into a chosen collection, and reading the selected collection. Zotero local server must be enabled.
gokoruri007/zotero-api-plus.pain: For developers connecting other tools or scripts to Zotero who need to add items by identifier through the local API.

ppavlidis/better-find-full-text.does: Goes beyond Zotero's Find Available PDF to attach full text. It tries the built-in finder, then a direct PDF download, opens paywalled articles in your browser, saves web snapshots and fetches patents from USPTO or Google Patents. Duplicates created by the Zotero Connector are merged into your existing item.
ppavlidis/better-find-full-text.pain: Built-in lookup often fails on paywalled or non-article items. This chains more fallbacks and tidies the duplicate that the Connector usually creates.

yuriyagn/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates PDFs into Simplified Chinese from the right-click menu, running PDFMathTranslate Next and BabelDOC locally and a SiliconFlow model for the text. The Chinese PDF is added as a child attachment, with formulas, tables and layout protected. Needs a SiliconFlow API key and a Python environment, and the original is never changed.
yuriyagn/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: Gives Chinese readers a layout-preserving translation of English papers without leaving Zotero.

ljeagle/zotero-chatpdf.does: Chats with your PDFs inside Zotero using models such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude, or local models like Llama, Gemma and Mistral on Mac. It opens with a keyboard shortcut, and conversations and insights can be saved. Branded papersgpt; its developer now points to a newer repository.
ljeagle/zotero-chatpdf.pain: Lets you ask questions of a paper without copying text out of Zotero. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-gpt; its README doesn't say what it changes.

huoyuuu/zotero-github-links.does: Adds a collapsible item pane section listing the GitHub repository links tied to a paper. Links are taken from the URL and Extra fields, and optionally from the PDF's indexed full text. You can open or copy them.
huoyuuu/zotero-github-links.pain: Finding a paper's code usually means digging through the PDF. This lists the repository links in the item pane.

digitalartificialint-cmd/zotero-med-impa.does: Adds columns for quartile, JCR impact factor, CiteScore, Scopus quartile, SJR and a source label for selected items. Citation counts come from OpenAlex and Crossref by DOI. Clarivate and Elsevier Scopus API keys are optional, and a local CSV of quartiles can serve as a fallback. Aimed at medical literature, with English and Turkish interface.
digitalartificialint-cmd/zotero-med-impa.pain: Checking a journal's quartile and impact for each reference by hand is slow. This fills the data into your library list.

nayuta-9/zotero-geyi-translator.does: Translates the PDFs of selected items with the Geyi cloud service, keeping the original layout or reflowing it with AI. It can also output a bilingual side-by-side version. The result is attached as a child file of the same item. Needs a Geyi account, which you sign in to through the browser.
nayuta-9/zotero-geyi-translator.pain: Translating a paper normally means exporting the PDF, uploading it elsewhere and re-importing the result. This does it from a right-click and files the translation under the original item. Aimed mainly at Chinese-language users.

zhongrubo/translation-notebook.does: Translates selected text in the reader: single words go to a dictionary, longer text to an AI model. Results appear inside Zotero's own selection popup and are editable, and you can save original passages to a searchable list. Needs an API key for your chosen AI service, or a local Ollama model.
zhongrubo/translation-notebook.pain: Reading in a second language means switching to another window for every unknown word or sentence. This keeps lookups in the reader and lets you build a personal list of passages worth keeping. Settings are mainly aimed at Chinese-language users.

j-cyoung/paperviewzoteroplugin.does: Runs the same LLM question over many selected papers at once, either as separate queries or one merged query, and opens the answers in a result page. Also offers OCR caching and a query history. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service (SiliconFlow by default) and Python 3.10 or later, with a local service started from within Zotero.
j-cyoung/paperviewzoteroplugin.pain: Tasks like summarising the method or checking the GPU used across dozens of papers are repetitive manual reading. This sends the same question to each paper and collects the answers.

luckeryan/zotero-scipdf.does: Fetches and attaches PDFs for selected items from several sources: Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, Unpaywall, OpenAlex and built-in Sci-Hub-style mirrors. Batch fetching runs several items in parallel with progress cards and reports not found separately from errors.
luckeryan/zotero-scipdf.pain: Collecting PDFs for a long list of items by hand is slow. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions. A fork of syt2/zotero-scipdf that adds batch workers, more sources and clearer results.

solvesaint/rssrch-for-zotero.does: Turns RSS feeds into a research discovery workflow: organise feeds into folders and filter articles with customisable rules. It also scores papers by relevance to your interests. Includes AI-assisted setup of rules and importable scoring configurations. Built for Zotero 10.
solvesaint/rssrch-for-zotero.pain: Large feed collections bury the few papers that matter to you. This filters and ranks them so relevant research surfaces first. Its documentation is still being developed.

retorquere/zotero-link-local-files.does: Links dropped or imported files instead of copying them into Zotero storage. This happens whenever the file already lives in your configured linked attachments base directory. It applies Zotero-wide and has no settings.
retorquere/zotero-link-local-files.pain: For people who keep PDFs in their own synced folder, such as one shared with a tablet, it saves manually converting each imported file to a link. Linking breaks if files are renamed, and linked files do not sync to other users.

bairuic/zoterocopilot.does: An AI chat window for Zotero that can use the PDF you are reading or any PDF attachment in your library as context. Works with OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, OpenRouter and local Ollama models, with saved conversation history and a prompt template library. Now continued as BibGenie.
bairuic/zoterocopilot.pain: Asking an AI about a paper otherwise means copying text and PDFs out of Zotero into a chat site. This keeps the conversation next to your library and remembers past chats.

struggle1999/zotero-ai-notes.does: Turns your PDF highlights and comments into Markdown notes written around the passages you marked, checked against the paper's text for unsupported claims. Can also build a mind map, exported as OPML or imported from XMind files. Notes are written back as Zotero child notes or exported as Markdown. Needs an API key for Gemini, OpenAI-compatible, DeepSeek or a custom service.
struggle1999/zotero-ai-notes.pain: Annotations pile up as fragments that are hard to turn into coherent reading notes. This organises them by topic while keeping the notes tied to what you actually highlighted.

xiaoducomrade/zotero-manual-sort.does: Lets you drag items into a custom order within an ordinary collection, and the order is saved in Zotero's own database. Adds collection menu commands to show the manual order or save the current column sort as the manual order.
xiaoducomrade/zotero-manual-sort.pain: Zotero only sorts by fields such as title or year, so a reading order or chapter sequence cannot be kept. Manual order is stored locally and Zotero does not sync it across devices.

jacse/zotero-sjr-rankings.does: Tags selected journal articles with their SJR quartile and writes the journal's H index into the Journal Abbr field. You run it from a right-click command to update rankings.
jacse/zotero-sjr-rankings.pain: Zotero has no built-in journal ranking. Storing it as a tag and in a field lets you sort and filter your library by journal quality.

hockeykharlamov/journal-impact-factor-zo.does: Shows the 2024 Journal Impact Factor and quartile for journal articles, as a sortable item list column and as a value in the item detail pane. Data covers about 20,000 journals and is matched by ISSN first, then journal name. The plugin sends an anonymous daily usage heartbeat containing only its version.
hockeykharlamov/journal-impact-factor-zo.pain: Checking a journal's impact factor means looking it up elsewhere for each article. This puts the figure beside every journal article in your library so you can sort by it.

alex-roc/zotero-agent.does: A small bridge plugin that gives Zotero's read-only local API a token-protected write endpoint. It is used by the zotero-agent command line tool, MCP server and agent skill. Together they let a terminal or AI agent search, bulk-edit, tag, deduplicate, import by DOI and export. Needs the companion Python package, and no cloud account or API key.
alex-roc/zotero-agent.pain: Zotero's local API can only read, so scripts and AI agents normally have to write through the web API with an account and sync. This lets them edit your local library directly.

retorquere/zotero-opds.does: An early-stage plugin for an embedded OPDS server inside Zotero; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
retorquere/zotero-opds.pain: Probably meant to let e-reader apps browse a Zotero library as an OPDS catalogue, but the repository does not say.

understandlxy/mineru-html-parser-zotero.does: Sends a PDF attachment to the MinerU parsing service and imports the result back as an HTML attachment, opening it automatically when finished. The HTML is cleaned for paper reading, with rendered formulas, split references and tables fitted to the page. Needs a MinerU API token, which is free to apply for.
understandlxy/mineru-html-parser-zotero.pain: Dense PDF pages are awkward to read on small screens or to copy from. This produces a reflowed HTML version of the paper stored under the same item.

dominic-dallosto/zotero-custom-item-fiel.does: Lets you define your own extra fields on items, such as Relevant or When read, edited under Settings. The fields can also be shown as columns in the item list.
dominic-dallosto/zotero-custom-item-fiel.pain: Zotero has a fixed set of fields, so personal tracking data ends up crammed into Extra or tags. This gives it proper fields you can sort by.

dzackgarza/zotero-local-write-api.does: Adds write endpoints to Zotero's local HTTP server for creating and changing items, notes, attachments, collections and tags, plus a version check. Documented in an OpenAPI file with a TypeScript client. Needs no API key, but Zotero must be running.
dzackgarza/zotero-local-write-api.pain: Zotero's built-in local API is read-only, so local scripts and tools cannot add or edit anything. This fills that gap for developers writing local integrations.

welpdx/zotero-citationcounts.does: Fetches citation counts for selected items from Crossref, InspireHEP, Semantic Scholar and Google Scholar. It stores them in the Extra field and Call Number field. A second command switches between counts already saved. Works on items without a DOI, such as books.
welpdx/zotero-citationcounts.pain: Zotero shows no citation counts, so judging an article's influence means searching elsewhere. This records counts in your library, where you can sort by them. A fork of eschnett/zotero-citationcounts for older Zotero versions.
