4965898/zotero-ai-ocr.does: Runs OCR on PDFs and image annotations with PaddleOCR, MinerU or AI vision models, saving the result as a Markdown note. Supports batch runs, chosen page ranges and automatic OCR on new PDFs. Needs a token or API key for the chosen engine.
4965898/zotero-ai-ocr.pain: Scanned PDFs have no text for Zotero to search or copy. This extracts the text, formulas and tables into notes. Interface and settings are available in Chinese and English.

peekabooxt/zotero_paper_classification_x.does: Sorts your library into topic collections and adds matching tags, using a language model that reads each paper's title, abstract and keywords. Offers full and supplemental classification runs and a cleanup command, and reuses existing collections where they fit. Needs an API key for DeepSeek, Alibaba Model Studio or another OpenAI-compatible service.
peekabooxt/zotero_paper_classification_x.pain: Organising a large library into collections by hand is tedious. This builds a category tree for you, and you can run it again later on only the new papers.

heimi98/zotero-deduplicator.does: Detects duplicate PDF attachments that are byte for byte identical, using SHA-256 hashes. It asks for confirmation before moving the duplicate to the Zotero trash. Checks new PDFs as they are added, and scans existing ones on demand from the Tools menu.
heimi98/zotero-deduplicator.pain: Zotero's duplicate pane compares metadata, not files, so identical PDFs under different titles go unnoticed. This finds exact file duplicates safely.

dnnunn/zotero-auto-tagger.does: Adds keyword tags to selected items from PubMed MeSH terms or a local Ollama model. AI tags carry an 'ai: ' prefix so they can be removed in bulk. Needs Ollama running locally; a PubMed key is optional.
dnnunn/zotero-auto-tagger.pain: Tagging a library by hand is slow and inconsistent. This fills in tags without per-item cost, and keeps everything on your own machine.

wmstack/zotero-toggle-bars.does: Adds three View menu items that show or hide the tab bar, the annotation toolbar and the sidebar.
wmstack/zotero-toggle-bars.pain: Gives you more room for reading on a small screen without digging through settings.

acatechnic/obsidian-notepad-for-zotero.does: Edits each item's linked Obsidian Markdown note inside the Zotero item pane and syncs your PDF highlights into it. Notes are found by citekey, link field or filename pattern, and can be created from a template. Needs an Obsidian vault.
acatechnic/obsidian-notepad-for-zotero.pain: If you read in Zotero but write in Obsidian, your literature notes live in two places. This brings the note and your highlights into one window while the file stays plain Markdown.

littview/zotero-openalex-pdf.does: Finds legal open-access PDFs for selected items through OpenAlex and attaches them, matching by DOI, PMID, arXiv ID or an exact title. A window reports the outcome for each item and skips items that already have a PDF. Needs no account or API key.
littview/zotero-openalex-pdf.pain: After importing hundreds of references from a database search, many have no PDF. This fills in the gaps, including items without a DOI that Zotero's own lookup misses.

rikochyou/zotero-smart-clipboard-import.does: Imports references from clipboard text containing DOIs, URLs, BibTeX or plain-text citations. It resolves metadata through doi.org, Crossref, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex. Shows an editable preview table with quality checks before import, and can bulk-import an author's papers from Semantic Scholar. An OpenAI-compatible API key is optional, for parsing citations the other sources cannot.
rikochyou/zotero-smart-clipboard-import.pain: Turning a pasted list of references into proper Zotero items normally means handling each one separately. This splits, looks up and previews them in one batch.

reginalluna/zotero-doi-manager.does: Retrieves shortDOIs, resolves long DOIs, validates and cleans DOI fields, and searches Crossref for items missing a DOI, from the right-click menu. Can process new items automatically and verifies DOIs in My Library monthly, tagging invalid or ambiguous results. Contacts DOI.org, shortDOI.org and Crossref.
reginalluna/zotero-doi-manager.pain: Wrong, missing or messy DOIs break lookups and citations. This checks and repairs them in bulk and keeps doing so over time. A continuation of Zotero DOI Manager by Brenton M. Wiernik.

lingyupeng/zotero_highlight_collector.does: Collects your PDF highlights and underlines into a local dataset you can filter by colour and category, with a link back to the original page and annotation. Categories map from annotation type and colour. Exports to CSV or an Anki-importable text file. Includes translations that other plugins write into annotation comments.
lingyupeng/zotero_highlight_collector.pain: Highlights stay scattered across individual PDFs. This gathers them into one searchable, exportable table so you can review and reuse them.

helloxiaolaodi/zotero-staticsync.does: Exports collections to GitHub as Markdown with Hugo front matter, or to Supabase with a share link. A collaborative mode applies web-side actions such as claiming or adding by DOI back to your library. Can also export collection items to CSV. Needs a GitHub token or Supabase project.
helloxiaolaodi/zotero-staticsync.pain: Sharing a reading list on a website or with a group otherwise means copying references out by hand. This publishes a collection and can take changes back.

chaoplayer/zotero-glossary.does: Shows a Term Lookup button beside text you select in the reader. An LLM explains the term with a Chinese explanation, English definition, field and example sentence. Saved terms go into your own glossaries, organised in multiple books. Needs an API key for DeepSeek or another OpenAI-compatible service.
chaoplayer/zotero-glossary.pain: Unfamiliar technical terms and acronyms interrupt reading. This explains them in your research field and builds a personal bilingual glossary. Aimed at English and Chinese readers.

sum-su/yaobian-zotero.does: Applies one of 36 colour themes to both the reader and the library interface, with a light and dark version of each. Also supports a custom background image with adjustable transparency and frosted-glass blur. Changes apply without restarting, and settings sit under Settings and the Tools menu.
sum-su/yaobian-zotero.pain: Zotero's appearance options are limited. This gives it a coordinated look, with many themes inspired by Chinese colour traditions.

fre-ms/zotlook.does: Previews the selected attachment when you press Space, using the system's own preview panel: Quick Look on macOS, GNOME Sushi on Linux and QuickLook on Windows. Includes an EPUB preview, your annotations drawn onto the preview, a page contact sheet and notes preview. Needs the system previewer, and is tested on Zotero 10.
fre-ms/zotlook.pain: Checking an attachment normally means opening it in the reader or another app. This gives the quick, file-manager style preview, with your Zotero annotations visible. A fork of gchapron/ZoteroQuickLookMac.

tiberavonltd/estravon-plugin.does: Adds a right-click command to extract a page range of a PDF to Markdown, attached to the item, using the Marker API through a backend server. Also exports sections to a clean workspace folder, converts between Markdown attachments and Zotero notes, and trims large PDFs before upload. Needs the hosted backend with an API key, or your own self-hosted backend.
tiberavonltd/estravon-plugin.pain: Reading or feeding book chapters to an LLM from a PDF is awkward. This extracts just the sections you need as Markdown files that tools like Obsidian can read.

lyz-623/journallens.does: Lets you follow journals found through Crossref and browse their recent papers inside Zotero, with abstracts, validated figures and captions. Includes feed search, translation of titles and abstracts, and adding a paper to your library by DOI. Recovers missing abstracts from Crossref, Europe PMC and publisher pages. Needs no API key.
lyz-623/journallens.pain: Keeping up with journals means moving between publisher sites, abstracts and manual imports. This brings the daily paper-scanning routine into one Zotero window.

danepps/zotero.does: Opens a signal picker with Ctrl+S in the Prefix field of the citation dialog, for inserting Bluebook signals such as See, Accord and E.g. into a citation. The repository also holds a companion Bluebook Citations Fixer for rules that CSL cannot express.
danepps/zotero.pain: Made for legal scholars writing law review articles, who otherwise type citation signals by hand each time.

lss3765/zotero-bilingual-reader.does: A side-by-side English and Chinese reading view for papers, with each English paragraph followed by its translation. Uses structured full text from PMC or publishers where available, falling back to PDF parsing. Also supports figure and table caption translation, multicolour highlights and notes. Needs Windows, a DeepSeek API key, and a bundled local service installed with it.
lss3765/zotero-bilingual-reader.pain: Reading medical and scientific papers in English is slow for Chinese-language readers. This puts the translation next to the original text. Aimed at Chinese-language research.

ievlevpn/zotero-theorem-list.does: Adds a reader toolbar button listing every theorem, lemma, definition and similar block in the PDF, with search. Click an entry to jump to it. Keywords and stripe colours are editable and can be written in any language.
ievlevpn/zotero-theorem-list.pain: Finding a particular result in a long mathematical paper means scrolling. This gives a clickable index of its statements.

oekeur/zotero-linked-mindmaps.does: Builds a knowledge graph of your sources with named, typed links between items and notes, grouped into multiple mindmaps that open in their own Zotero tab. You can drag nodes, group them and link across mindmaps. Links are created from the item pane or right-click menus, and data syncs as a Zotero note.
oekeur/zotero-linked-mindmaps.pain: Zotero's related items and tags show that two sources connect, not how, such as one critiquing the other. This records the nature of each connection for literature reviews and thesis work.

saytanz0815/annotation-color-memory.does: Remembers the last colour you used for highlights, underlines, notes and image annotations, and restores it when the reader opens, including after a restart. Stores it only in Zotero preferences with no network requests.
saytanz0815/annotation-color-memory.pain: Zotero forgets your annotation colours when you switch tabs or restart, so you reselect them each time.

leike0813/zotero-skills.does: An agent workbench that runs AI workflows on your library. Includes an assistant sidebar connected to agents, and a CLI and MCP bridge for external agents. May need an agent CLI installed or a Skill-Runner service, plus provider keys.
leike0813/zotero-skills.pain: Handing routine literature work to AI agents usually means leaving Zotero. This runs them against your library and keeps the results as notes you can check. Formerly named Zotero Skills.

jehyunlee/paper-curio.does: Chats with a paper's PDF, compares several papers and generates a structured review of a selected item, written out as HTML. Optionally links to a paper-curation Python setup for more tools. Needs an API key for Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, or a local Ollama model for summaries and questions. Local review runs on macOS and Linux only.
jehyunlee/paper-curio.pain: Reading and comparing many papers is slow. This lets you ask questions of a PDF and produce review write-ups from inside Zotero. Its documentation is mainly in Korean.

zhongrubo/zotero-tag-sort.does: Adds a sort menu to the tag selector for ordering tags by date added, alphabetically or by name length, in either direction. Also lays the tags out in a framed single column. Native tag filtering is unchanged and the sort choice is remembered. Added time is approximated by tag ID.
zhongrubo/zotero-tag-sort.pain: Zotero's tag list is hard to scan when you have many tags of varying lengths. This makes it tidier and sortable.

junyeolyu/line_focus.does: Adds a reading ruler to the PDF reader that highlights one line of text, moved with the [ and ] keys or by clicking, and scrolls across pages. A toolbar button toggles it, and the colour is set in Settings.
junyeolyu/line_focus.pain: Helps you keep your place when reading dense PDFs line by line.

garlicwu/fanyipaiban-zotero.does: Translates a PDF attachment with the FanyiPaiban service, keeping the original layout, and attaches the translated PDF to the same item. Optionally also attaches a comparison PDF and a Markdown version. Target is Simplified Chinese by default, and you can change it. Needs a FanyiPaiban API key and credits.
garlicwu/fanyipaiban-zotero.pain: Reading a long foreign-language PDF without losing its figures and layout is hard with plain-text translators. This returns a translated copy that looks like the original.

nyaru177/ccf-for-zotero.does: Shows CCF ranks (A, B, C and T1 to T3) and CAS journal quartiles (zones 1 to 4) as badges in item list columns, matched by DOI, ISSN or publication name. Runs offline from built-in data, with batch refresh, manual override and search. Built for Chinese computer science researchers and tested on Zotero 10.
nyaru177/ccf-for-zotero.pain: Checking whether a venue is on the CCF list or in a given CAS zone usually means searching separate tables. This labels each item in your library.

cboulanger/zotero-rag.does: Lets you ask questions about the papers in your library and get answers with links to sources, including page numbers and text anchors. Indexes PDFs, HTML, EPUB and DOCX files through a backend server you run, which can serve a whole research group, and supports local or remote models. Needs that backend and a model setup.
cboulanger/zotero-rag.pain: General document chat tools need manual uploads to a cloud service. This indexes your Zotero library directly and keeps the index in step with your changes.

oneoneliu/zotero-research-copilot.does: An AI assistant with reader sidebar chat, a library-wide assistant window and multi-paper analysis. Sessions are saved to notes. Needs an API key for Gemini, DeepSeek, Doubao or an OpenAI-compatible service.
oneoneliu/zotero-research-copilot.pain: Asking questions about a paper, or synthesising across several, normally means moving text to a separate chatbot. This keeps the conversation tied to your library.

sbilmis/zotero-project-manager.does: Exports Zotero collections into ordinary folders with PDFs, metadata, notes and annotations, updating them incrementally and never changing your library. Also copies Org, Markdown or Zotero links to collections, items and reader pages, and has an Emacs paper picker. A separate Python command line tool offers dry runs and pruning.
sbilmis/zotero-project-manager.pain: People who work with AI tools, Emacs or Obsidian need research files in plain folders. This keeps a collection mirrored there and gives you links back to Zotero.

retorquere/zotero-debug-log.does: Sends Zotero debug logs to the community developers of Zotero plugins.
retorquere/zotero-debug-log.pain: Developers need a log to diagnose a problem, and this helps users send one without assembling it by hand.

stevepowell99/causalmap-zotero.does: Turns a Zotero item into a Causal Map project: a diagram of factors and the causal claims between them, each backed by a quote from the paper. Choose Make a Causal Map from the right-click menu; the text goes to the hosted Causal Map app, where you explore and edit the map. Needs a free Causal Map account, approved in the browser.
stevepowell99/causalmap-zotero.pain: Reconstructing a paper's argument about what causes what means careful reading. This produces the map with its supporting quotes, useful for interviews, theory of change and literature reviews.

mcxcc303/just-enough-color.does: Lets you give highlights and underlines any colour, from a random pick or a full colour picker. Custom-coloured annotations keep their comments, tags and colour switching. Interface in English and Simplified Chinese.
mcxcc303/just-enough-color.pain: Zotero offers only eight annotation colours. This widens the palette without losing normal annotation features.

alessmor/zotero-citation-map.does: Builds an interactive citation-network graph for a library, collection or selected papers, and adds citation and reference counts as item list columns. Data comes from Crossref, Semantic Scholar, OpenCitations, INSPIRE-HEP and OpenAlex (which needs an API key). You can export the map as PNG, CSV or JSON.
alessmor/zotero-citation-map.pain: Seeing how papers cite each other usually means leaving Zotero for tools like ResearchRabbit or Litmaps. This keeps the map, the counts and the discovery of missing papers inside Zotero.

zhongrubo/zotero-annotation-filter.does: Filters reader annotations by type with a toolbar under the annotation list. Choose any mix of highlight, underline, note, inserted text, area or drawing; hidden annotations are not changed.
zhongrubo/zotero-annotation-filter.pain: Zotero's reader can filter by colour but not by type, so finding the notes or image areas among hundreds of annotations is slow. Written with Chinese-language users in mind, with an English interface too.

gracefullight/pkgs.does: Copies a bibliography to the clipboard in the UTS APA 7th format, the referencing variant used at the University of Technology Sydney. It is one package in a monorepo of unrelated open-source projects.
gracefullight/pkgs.pain: Students following the UTS referencing guide otherwise have to adjust standard APA 7th output by hand.

irism6/alphapulse.does: Adds two item list columns: alphaXiv likes and citation counts, the latter from Google Scholar by default, or OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar. It matches arXiv papers automatically and saves the numbers in the Extra field. No API key is needed.
irism6/alphapulse.pain: Zotero has no quick view of how much attention a new paper is getting. These columns let you sort a reading list by likes or citations, and offer 11 colour styles for the numbers.

andypeng09/zotero-ima-sync.does: Syncs selected items, a collection or the whole library, together with their PDF attachments, to a Tencent ima knowledge base (ima.qq.com). Synced items are marked in the Extra field so repeat runs skip them. Needs an ima Client ID and API key.
andypeng09/zotero-ima-sync.pain: People who keep a searchable literature library in Tencent ima otherwise upload PDFs by hand. This pushes them from Zotero in bulk, with progress shown for each item.

ildon/zotero-semantic-search.does: Searches the full text of your PDFs by meaning rather than keywords, in many languages, with results linked to the item and page. A local model runs inside Zotero, and a built-in local MCP server lets AI assistants search your library.
ildon/zotero-semantic-search.pain: Keyword search misses passages that use different words from your query. Pasting a paragraph of your draft and getting the supporting pages back helps when you are writing and citing.

suzuka24/paper-chat-for-zotero.does: Chats with the paper open in Zotero from the reader sidebar, using the current PDF, selections, annotations and notes as context. It reuses your local Codex sign-in, so no OpenAI API key is needed, but a local bridge installer must be run first.
suzuka24/paper-chat-for-zotero.pain: Lets people who already have a ChatGPT or Codex account ask questions about a paper without paying for separate API credits. Conversations can be saved to Zotero notes.

liotou/zotero-annota.does: Runs a prompt you set per highlight colour on every highlight you make in the PDF reader, and writes the model's reply into the annotation's comment. Works with Mistral, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama, the Claude Code CLI or Apple Intelligence.
liotou/zotero-annota.pain: Writing a summary, translation or critique for each highlight by hand is slow. Assigning a prompt to a colour fills the comment as you read, and nothing runs until you give a colour a prompt.

maverickzyc/zotero-context-translate.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader along with its sentence and paragraph context. A local dictionary answers first, then an LLM explains the usage. It can also build a bilingual English and Chinese HTML of a whole paper. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API.
maverickzyc/zotero-context-translate.pain: Translating a selected phrase on its own often gives a fluent but wrong rendering of terms and references. Built mainly for Chinese researchers reading English papers.

wweiyiwang/biread.does: Adds bilingual reading to the PDF reader. It splits the text into blocks and translates them with a provider set in Zotero's Translate settings, showing original and translation side by side or immersively. You can create annotations from selected text.
wweiyiwang/biread.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that adds whole-document bilingual reading. It is marked beta, and scanned PDFs without selectable text are not supported.

etshaw-zh/zotero-career-tracker.does: Charts the growth of your library with daily added-item bars and a cumulative line, for all items and for items carrying a focal tag you choose. Marks your My Publications dates and copies the chart as an image for sharing.
etshaw-zh/zotero-career-tracker.pain: Gives researchers a visual record of reading and publishing progress over time, which Zotero does not show. The share image is made for pasting into social apps.

justanotherjurastudent/zotero_flexannota.does: Creates annotations for printed books with no attached file, using page or paragraph locators. Cite them in Word or LibreOffice with the reference only, and import the Citavi quotes that Zotero normally drops.
justanotherjurastudent/zotero_flexannota.pain: Zotero only annotates items with a PDF, EPUB or snapshot, which fails fields such as law and history that cite printed commentaries. Aimed at those users and people moving from Citavi.

white-ink-cell/lingkuma-zotero.does: Click a word in the PDF or EPUB reader for its meaning, or a sentence to translate and analyse it. Also plays pronunciation. A port of the LingKuma reader; AI explanations need your own AI endpoint and key.
white-ink-cell/lingkuma-zotero.pain: Reading papers in a language you are still learning means constant trips to a dictionary. This is an unofficial Zotero port of LingKuma that keeps vocabulary building inside the reader.

cannolis/zotread.does: Ranks unread papers by relevance to your own papers or a research idea, using an OpenAI-compatible LLM such as DeepSeek or a local Ollama. Adds a sortable Relevance column, a sidebar rationale and an auto-maintained top-papers collection.
cannolis/zotread.pain: A large pile of unread papers makes it hard to decide what to read next. This ranks the queue against your own work and explains each score.

phoenixchenlu/zotero-local-mcp-bridge.does: Hosts an MCP endpoint inside Zotero for local AI agents to manage your local library. They can search, edit and organise items, attachments and annotations, and import or export BibTeX, RIS and CSL JSON. Writes start as a dry run, with approval, audit and undo.
phoenixchenlu/zotero-local-mcp-bridge.pain: Lets AI agents manage a library through Zotero's own APIs rather than editing the database. Run modes range from read-only to automatic, and it never touches online libraries.

ievlevpn/zotero-tag-fuzzy-search.does: Makes tag autocomplete fuzzy in the item pane, note editor, reader tag popup, advanced search and tag selector. Suggestions are ranked best first, and the words of your query can come in any order.
ievlevpn/zotero-tag-fuzzy-search.pain: Zotero only matches the start of a tag, so typing 'learn' never finds 'machine learning'. This finds tags from any part of the name.

endoretic/zotero-wallpaper.does: Sets a wallpaper behind Zotero 10's interface. Supports separate light and dark images, one image or a folder, shuffle without repeats, opacity, and Cover, Contain, Center or Stretch layouts.
endoretic/zotero-wallpaper.pain: For people who want to personalise Zotero's look. It may conflict with other theme plugins.

lightwindw/zotero-better-vertical-tabs.does: Adds a vertical tab sidebar to the main window and reader that expands on hover, with tab search, drag-and-drop, and categories for grouping tabs. It can close idle PDF readers or unread tabs automatically to free memory.
lightwindw/zotero-better-vertical-tabs.pain: Zotero's horizontal tab bar becomes unmanageable with many open papers, and every open PDF reader uses memory. This makes tabs easier to find, group and close.

lovethestar7/zotero-closeflow.does: On Windows, changes the main window's close button: it asks whether to minimise Zotero to the system tray or quit, and can remember your choice. A tray menu restores or closes Zotero.
lovethestar7/zotero-closeflow.pain: Clicking close in Zotero on Windows quits it outright, which is annoying if you want it running in the background. Its interface is available in Chinese and English.

ppavlidis/group-tabs-by-collection.does: Groups open reader and snapshot tabs by collection into collapsible, coloured chips like Chrome's tab groups. You can drag tabs between groups, close a whole group, and open selected items in groups from the right-click menu.
ppavlidis/group-tabs-by-collection.pain: With many PDFs open, Zotero's tab bar is one flat list. This organises it by collection, and the grouping survives restarts. The author says to drop it if Zotero adds an official feature.

lss3765/zotero-display-title-public.does: Adds a personal marked-title column to the item list and citation picker, stored in the Extra field, without changing the real title or citations. It can also detect the true title from the PDF and fill in metadata.
lss3765/zotero-display-title-public.pain: Items with messy imported titles are hard to recognise in the list. This lets you see a name that makes sense to you while citations still use the official title. Windows only; Chinese interface.

gchapron/zoteroquicklookmac.does: On macOS, previews the selected item's attachment when you press Space. PDFs open in a PDFKit window with selectable text and your Zotero annotations, and other files use macOS QuickLook. Also previews notes and a PDF contact sheet.
gchapron/zoteroquicklookmac.pain: Zotero has no Finder-style quick preview. It is a successor to the Zotero 4 to 6 QuickLook plugin, which stopped working with Zotero 7.

soyami/zotero-pick2anki.does: Sends words from the reader to Anki. Select an English word or phrase to see five online dictionaries (Youdao, Bing, Cambridge, Oxford, Collins), then add a card with its source sentence. Needs Anki desktop with AnkiConnect.
soyami/zotero-pick2anki.pain: Looking up words and then making flashcards from them are separate chores when reading English papers. This does both from the selection popup, and it works alongside Translate for Zotero.

ysqander/listen2papers-zotero.does: Adds a Listen to this paper command that uploads the selected local PDF to listen2papers.com for audio. The audio comes with read-along text, readable on the web or in an iOS app. Needs a plugin token from a listen2papers account.
ysqander/listen2papers-zotero.pain: For people who want to listen to papers while walking or commuting, with saved progress. Only the PDF you choose and its metadata are sent, not your library.

c7w/papersgpt-for-zotero-sidebar.does: A sidebar chatbot that answers questions about text you select, using any OpenAI-format API with your own base URL, model and key. Prompts are customisable, and setup is done in Zotero's preferences file.
c7w/papersgpt-for-zotero-sidebar.pain: A modified version of PapersGPT by c7w that disables its online sign-in, so you can use your own LLM endpoint instead. The author notes long-context models have made selected-text questions less useful.

heidihelena/fullvahti.does: Finds and attaches open-access PDFs through Unpaywall and PubMed Central. It also checks references for retractions in PubMed and Crossref and compares citation metadata with Crossref. Items get status tags, and one report note lists what was not found.
heidihelena/fullvahti.pain: Gives systematic reviewers a ready list of papers to request through interlibrary loan and a way to catch retracted papers. It never bypasses paywalls, and the metadata check is read-only.

zbigfish/zotero-ccf-rank.does: Identifies the CCF rank and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) journal zone of computer-science papers and shows a one-line summary in a column. CCF data comes through DBLP and CAS data from LetPub; results are saved in the Extra field.
zbigfish/zotero-ccf-rank.pain: Chinese computer-science researchers need to know a venue's CCF and CAS tier but must look it up by hand. This fills it in for new items and scans the whole library.

groele/zotero-metaflow.does: Cleans and enriches reference metadata. It applies 59 offline rules for case, authors, pages and DOIs, adds ISO 4 journal abbreviations, merges duplicates and matches arXiv preprints to published versions. Online options add JCR, CAS and CCF ranks in a Journal Insights panel.
groele/zotero-metaflow.pain: Records imported from databases and web clips often have wrong capitalisation, reversed author names and missing abbreviations. Chinese-language interface; part of the Zotero Flow plugin series.

ppavlidis/condense-info-view.does: Declutters the Info panel by hiding empty fields, dimming empty ones that matter for the item type, and collapsing three or more authors to first and last. A show-empty button reveals everything.
ppavlidis/condense-info-view.pain: The Info panel lists 20 to 30 rows for every item even when most are blank, which wastes screen space.

wcmendes/mdbundle-for-zotero.does: Exports matching PDF and Markdown pairs to a folder, reports which items lack a PDF or Markdown copy, and generates Markdown from PDFs. It can also read a Word .docx file and select the cited items in your library.
wcmendes/mdbundle-for-zotero.pain: People who feed papers to LLMs, RAG pipelines or Obsidian need Markdown versions of their PDFs kept in step. Items whose PDFs have no extractable text are tagged needs-ocr.

huoyuuu/zotero-ai-latex.does: Adds an AI LaTeX area to the item pane: drop, paste or pick an image of a formula and an OpenAI-compatible vision model returns LaTeX, copied to the clipboard. You set the base URL, API key and model.
huoyuuu/zotero-ai-latex.pain: Retyping equations from papers into LaTeX is tedious. This converts a screenshot of the formula in one step.

xoyapeng/zotero-hide-fields.does: Lets you hide chosen fields in the item Info pane for each item type and drag the remaining fields into your own order. Item types without their own setting use a default configuration, and changes apply immediately.
xoyapeng/zotero-hide-fields.pain: The Info pane shows many fields most users never fill in. This trims it to the ones you use. The settings are in Chinese.

dominic-dallosto/zotero-api-endpoint.does: Provides an HTTP server endpoint inside Zotero so other programs can interact with it. What the endpoint exposes is not documented.
dominic-dallosto/zotero-api-endpoint.pain: Probably for people who want to script or connect external tools to Zotero. It is a legacy plugin.

yiyangbyts/twintext-releases.does: Shows the original text and a translation side by side in Zotero's PDF reader. This repository is the public release and update channel, and it documents no features or setup.
yiyangbyts/twintext-releases.pain: For reading papers in another language next to the translation. Which translation service it uses is not stated.

sum-su/zotero-js-bridge.does: Exposes nine local HTTP endpoints so scripts, including a bundled Python client, can run JavaScript inside a live Zotero. Includes structured queries, a library health check, duplicate merging with a dry run, a batch editor and backups. Every call needs a token.
sum-su/zotero-js-bridge.pain: Zotero's plugin API has no channel for outside programs, so bulk jobs like merging duplicates or editing fields mean pasting code by hand. The endpoints run arbitrary JavaScript with full library access.

haozhihuiymh150/zotero-agent.does: A chat box in Zotero for searching arXiv and PubMed, downloading papers into your library, and asking about a selected paper or PDF text. Needs an API key for an LLM such as Doubao, DeepSeek or an OpenAI-compatible service.
haozhihuiymh150/zotero-agent.pain: Combines paper search, download and Q&A in one conversation, with Chinese-hosted models so no VPN is needed. Described as beta, and inspired by Zotero-GPT.

serbernardo/zotero-assistente-ia.does: Reads, summarises, appraises and compares articles from the item pane and a multi-article window, with answers that cite PDF pages. It checks quotes, pages and numbers against the PDF text and flags mismatches. Works with Gemini, ChatGPT, OpenAI API or IAEdu using your own account.
serbernardo/zotero-assistente-ia.pain: AI answers about papers can invent details. This restricts the model to your PDFs and checks its citations. Interface in English and European Portuguese.

gchapron/zoteroollama.does: Chats with the selected item's PDF using a local Ollama model. Answers stream in as Markdown, with quick prompts such as Summarize and Methods, follow-up questions, and saving answers as child notes. Needs Ollama running with a model pulled.
gchapron/zoteroollama.pain: For people who want to ask questions about papers without sending them to an online service, since everything runs on your own machine.

liusirai/tree-koala.does: Translates a whole PDF paper while keeping the original layout, and exports the translated PDF. The translation service and settings are not described.
liusirai/tree-koala.pain: For reading papers in another language with figures and formatting intact. The author says its code was entirely generated by AI.

menyoung/zotldr.does: Adds an AI Chat panel to the item pane for asking Google Gemini questions about the open paper, sending the full PDF on the first message. A shared context note in your library holds the API key, model, quick-action buttons and a system prompt.
menyoung/zotldr.pain: Built for research teams who want everyone to get consistent, domain-aware answers from one shared configuration. Chats can be saved as notes. Needs a Gemini API key and Zotero 8.

veiluna/babeldoc-for-zotero.does: Translates a PDF into Simplified Chinese with layout and formulas kept, or makes a bilingual side-by-side PDF. Uses BabelDOC and your own OpenAI-compatible API. Windows only; it downloads its own Python environment on first run.
veiluna/babeldoc-for-zotero.pain: Ordinary translation breaks the formatting of scientific PDFs. This puts the Chinese text back in place and adds the result as a new attachment, leaving the original untouched.

airalinknowledge/zotero-book-splitter.does: Splits PDF and EPUB books into separate chapters, each as its own citable Zotero item, while keeping the complete original. It reads the table of contents from bookmarks, EPUB navigation or a scan, or uses an AI service you configure. Needs Zotero 9.
airalinknowledge/zotero-book-splitter.pain: Edited volumes and anthologies are hard to cite chapter by chapter from one big file. Chapter titles, authors and pages are reviewed before anything is created. Chinese-language interface.

hansjoakimpersson/zotero-file-utility.does: Keeps each attachment's title matching its filename on disk. Adds a Tools menu option to convert stored files into linked files inside your linked attachments base directory.
hansjoakimpersson/zotero-file-utility.pain: Zotero can convert linked files to stored ones but not back, and its titles and filenames drift apart. This helps users who keep files in iCloud, Dropbox or Google Drive.

xiaoxuan353/zotero-paper-radar.does: Watches journal RSS feeds and Crossref on a schedule. An LLM rates each new paper against your research direction, and high and medium matches are saved to a collection with tags and an AI review note. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
xiaoxuan353/zotero-paper-radar.pain: Replaces weekly manual scanning of journal tables of contents; low-relevance papers are skipped and never enter your library. Its defaults suit civil and bridge engineering and are in Chinese.

huangkiki/zotero-ai-sidebar.does: A chat sidebar beside the PDF reader for asking, translating and explaining selections, with conversations saved per paper. Connects through a local Codex ChatGPT sign-in, the OpenAI API or compatible services, or the Anthropic API.
huangkiki/zotero-ai-sidebar.pain: A fork of xuhan-rgb/zotero-ai-sidebar; its README doesn't say what it changes. Its developer says local ChatGPT access is still being verified, and Anthropic can't read whole PDFs by itself yet.

guokelei1/zotero-export-pdf.does: Exports the PDF attachments of selected items or a collection to a folder you choose, renamed by item title. Notes can be exported as Markdown files in a timestamped subfolder.
guokelei1/zotero-export-pdf.pain: Makes it quick to collect papers and notes for AI-assisted reading. It does not include sub-collections.

starkujo/zotero-wordbook.does: Saves English words or phrases selected in the PDF, EPUB or web reader to a personal wordbook with a Chinese translation and the source paper. A side panel supports searching, sorting, editing and export to JSON or CSV. Needs Translate for Zotero installed.
starkujo/zotero-wordbook.pain: Gives Chinese-speaking readers of English papers a place to collect vocabulary where they found it, without a separate app.

wuok0618/zotero-sidemark.does: Reads and edits Markdown notes linked to items in the item pane and PDF reader sidebar, with GFM tables, KaTeX, Mermaid and Obsidian links. Optional AI features convert PDFs with MinerU, translate notes, write deep-read reports and chat about the paper, with your own API.
wuok0618/zotero-sidemark.pain: Keeps literature notes as plain .md files that Obsidian, Git and AI tools can use, while showing them beside the PDF. Interface in Chinese and English.

adolinjonathan-bot/zotero-toolkit.does: Matches downloaded PDFs to existing items by their content: DOI, arXiv ID, embedded metadata and first-page text. Shows the evidence before attaching. The repository also holds an MCP server for Zotero.
adolinjonathan-bot/zotero-toolkit.pain: Stops people attaching PDFs by filename guesswork. Nothing is written until you confirm in a review dialog, which suits systematic and scoping review workflows.

smlum/zotero-scholar-citations.does: Fetches citation counts from Google Scholar when you add or update an item and saves them as a plain number in the Extra field for sorting. Batch updates are limited because Google Scholar blocks automated queries.
smlum/zotero-scholar-citations.pain: A fork of an older fork of MaxKuehn/zotero-scholar-citations that stores just an integer, which sorts and fits better. Zotero 6 only, and large batches trigger captchas.

centrefordigitalhumanities/lidia-zotero.does: Captures PDF reader annotations as structured linguistic diagnostic arguments, stored as YAML in the annotation comments. A separate web application reads them out to build a database of such arguments. Built for Zotero 6 and 7, tested on 6.
centrefordigitalhumanities/lidia-zotero.pain: Made for the LIDIA project at Utrecht University, where linguists share a Zotero folder and describe diagnostic arguments in a uniform format. The project has ended and the repository is archived.

andrusha/zotero-scihub.does: Downloads PDFs by DOI from Sci-Hub and attaches them to your items, through an "Update Scihub PDF" right-click command or automatically for newly added papers. Has a settings tab and notes on DNS-over-HTTPS for Zotero.
andrusha/zotero-scihub.pain: Saves hunting for paywalled papers by hand. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions. A fork of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub, and it only runs on Zotero 6.

chen7447/item-pane-organizer-zotero.does: Lists every panel in the Zotero item pane, built-in and from other plugins, and lets you drag the rows to reorder them. Saves your order, restores the default with one click, and greys out plugin panels that aren't rendered yet. For Zotero 9 and 10.
chen7447/item-pane-organizer-zotero.pain: Plugins that add item-pane sections often offer no way to change their position, so the sidebar order is hard to tune. This gives one place to arrange all of them. The interface is in Chinese.

hanxiangmin/zotero10-scholar.does: Shows CCF rank, JCR quartile, impact factor and 2025 Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) journal tier in the Call Number column, using bundled tables. Also tidies titles, DOIs, pages and journal names, and can look up missing metadata through Crossref.
hanxiangmin/zotero10-scholar.pain: People who choose venues or sort reading lists by CCF, JCR or CAS tier otherwise look the rankings up by hand. Each update shows a before-and-after table, and Zotero's undo works. Aimed mainly at Chinese-language research; for Zotero 10.

origin652/zotero-assistant.does: A chat-based AI assistant inside Zotero 9 that organises references, adds tags, creates notes and updates metadata. Needs an API endpoint, model name and key of your own.
origin652/zotero-assistant.pain: Routine library housekeeping means many manual clicks. Here you ask in plain language, with approval prompts for sensitive reads and writes, a local audit log, and deletions sent to the trash.

guoxin-ink/codex-zotero-bridge.does: Lets the Codex client on your computer search, inspect and update your Zotero library through a Zotero extension and a local MCP server. It lists records and collections, finds duplicates, previews metadata fixes, and manages tags, notes and collections. Needs Zotero 8 or 9 and Python.
guoxin-ink/codex-zotero-bridge.pain: Gives an AI coding agent controlled access to your library. Reads need pairing, writes start disabled and expire after ten minutes, changes are previewed first, and nothing is permanently erased.

nian1147/-61-.does: Translates medical papers with AI models, using medical prompts, an abbreviation scan and a glossary pass for consistent terms. You supply an API key for the model you choose. It is a fork of Translate for Zotero.
nian1147/-61-.pain: General translators handle clinical abbreviations and terminology unevenly. This aims at consistent medical translation of papers, with Chinese-language descriptions suggesting it is meant for Chinese-speaking readers.

migueldlm/zotero-paper-search.does: Adds search buttons to the PDF reader's selection popup for Google Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, Semantic Scholar and more. A custom URL prefix can search a selected DOI. Available in English and Spanish.
migueldlm/zotero-paper-search.pain: Looking up an unfamiliar term or reference from a PDF means copying it into a browser. This sends the selection straight to the database you choose.

wandonwe/papermirror-for-zotero.does: Shows a translated page next to the original in Zotero's PDF reader, with figures, tables and formulas kept in place and only the body text re-flowed. Also has an overlay mode, an AI explain tool, glossaries and save-to-note. Bring your own key for DeepL, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or Ollama.
wandonwe/papermirror-for-zotero.pain: Reading foreign-language papers usually means translating text separately and losing the layout. This keeps the page structure and translates it in the reader. Free Bing and Google engines work without a key.

rischconsulting/citation-phoenix.does: Adds Juris-M-style legal citation support to Zotero 8 to 10, with jurisdiction and court fields for case items. Case data is kept in sync with Juris-M's Extra field format.
rischconsulting/citation-phoenix.pain: Lawyers and legal scholars who cite across jurisdictions need Juris-M features that stock Zotero lacks. This brings them to current Zotero versions.

mlfc0422/zotero-puls.does: Draws an author and tag relationship graph for a collection and adds read status, star marks and paper counts. Also offers AI tag suggestions, selection translation in the PDF reader and EasyScholar journal data.
mlfc0422/zotero-puls.pain: Helps you see how a collection clusters and what you have read. AI tags need a DeepSeek or OpenAI key and EasyScholar needs its own key. The interface is in Chinese.

nikhilweee/zotfetch.does: Adds a "Zotfetch: Relocate" command that downloads PDFs for attachment entries whose file is missing on disk. Built for Zotero 7.
nikhilweee/zotfetch.pain: Find Available PDFs only appears when no PDF entry exists, and it creates a new one. Zotfetch refills the existing entry, so annotations stay usable when file sync is off.

dnnunn/zotero-scihub-fetcher.does: Downloads PDFs for items with a DOI, trying OpenAlex's archive first if you add your own API key and falling back to Sci-Hub mirrors. Works on batches from the right-click or Tools menu, with progress, rate limiting and skipping of items that already have PDFs.
dnnunn/zotero-scihub-fetcher.pain: Saves fetching paywalled papers one by one. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions. OpenAlex downloads cost $0.01 each from your account.

daniel5u/zotero-paper-translator.does: Translates whole PDF papers or chosen pages inside Zotero's reader, keeping layout, formulas and figures. Includes a batch queue and a translation column. Installs a Python environment on first run.
daniel5u/zotero-paper-translator.pain: Translating a paper through a website breaks its layout and loses the formatting. This produces a translated copy in the original layout. The first set-up downloads about 1 GB.

groele/zotero-taskflow.does: A task manager for reading that turns a PDF selection or annotation into a to-do with its page reference. Includes reading templates, an item pane card and Markdown, CSV or JSON export. Data stays in a local file.
groele/zotero-taskflow.pain: Reading lists kept in separate to-do apps lose their link to the paper. This ties tasks to items and PDF pages. The interface and documentation are mainly in Chinese.

northword/zotero-mica.does: Applies Windows Mica, Mica Alt or Acrylic backdrop materials to the Zotero main window and dialogs, with live switching and tint control. Uses the native backdrop on Windows 11 22H2 and later and an Acrylic blur on Windows 10. Needs Zotero 10.
northword/zotero-mica.pain: Gives Zotero the translucent look of modern Windows apps. It is cosmetic and Windows-only.

06-month/paperflow.does: A Zotero reader sidebar that summarises and translates papers into Korean with Gemini, then answers questions about them in a chat. Handles layout, figures, tables and LaTeX formulas, and resumes interrupted translations. Needs a Gemini API key.
06-month/paperflow.pain: Reading a paper in another language usually means moving between a PDF viewer, a translator and a chatbot. This keeps summary, translation and questions in the reader. The interface is in Korean.

jajaho/zotero-citation-graph.does: Builds a force-directed citation graph from a collection or selection, mostly from your own PDFs, with optional OpenAlex lookups. Edges come offline from PDFs or optionally from OpenAlex; cited works can be added to Zotero in one click. Needs Zotero 10.
jajaho/zotero-citation-graph.pain: Shows how the papers in your library relate and which important works you might have missed, without leaving Zotero for tools like Connected Papers or ResearchRabbit.

cai-aa/zotero-one.does: Adds a sortable number column to the item list and a space-bar preview window for a selected item's abstract and details. Available in English and Chinese.
cai-aa/zotero-one.pain: Gives a quick way to count and refer to items by number and to peek at an abstract without opening the file or looking at the side pane. The author says it was built with AI coding tools.

jhj223/zotero-ai-guided-reader.does: Generates a guided reading of a PDF in Chinese, with claims that link back to the exact source text. Needs a MinerU token and an LLM key or a signed-in Codex or Claude CLI.
jhj223/zotero-ai-guided-reader.pain: Helps with reading dense papers by linking every claim to its source passage. Trial then paid licence for new generation; the plugin interface is in Simplified Chinese.

karlhegbloom/propachi-texmacs.does: Replaces Zotero's citeproc-js and parts of its word-processor integration so citations come out in a TeXmacs LaTeX format. Adds hyperlinks to bibliography entries and back-references. Required by the zotero-texmacs-integration plugin.
karlhegbloom/propachi-texmacs.pain: Lets the TeXmacs editor use Zotero or Juris-M for citations. A fork of Juris-M/propachi-upper, written for Zotero 5, so it is legacy.

iiwenwen/zotero-update-metadata.does: Refreshes an item's metadata from the page its URL field points to, with per-item review and undo of the latest batch. Currently works only for items saved from Douban.
iiwenwen/zotero-update-metadata.pain: Saves re-saving a web page just to refresh its record. Its coverage is narrow, so it mainly suits Douban books and films; the interface is in Chinese.

groele/zotero-mindflow.does: Builds editable mind maps from papers, annotations and ideas, with a free canvas and an outline view. Maps are saved as .mindflow attachments or exported as standalone HTML.
groele/zotero-mindflow.pain: Keeps knowledge organisation inside Zotero instead of a separate mind-mapping app. Part of the Zotero Flow series; the documentation is mainly in Chinese.

noahxie83/zotero-lexibridge.does: Looks up words in the PDF reader from local MDX, StarDict and DSL dictionaries or optional online translators. Saves words and notes, with CSV and Anki export. Bring your own dictionaries.
noahxie83/zotero-lexibridge.pain: Looking up words while reading papers otherwise means switching to a dictionary app. Online sources are off by default and send the queried text to the provider.

mcxcc303/zctr.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader through a right-click command, with a popup, streamed output and a cache. Works with DeepSeek, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible API, and supports termbases you can import and save terms into.
mcxcc303/zctr.pain: A lightweight way to get consistent translations of passages using a model of your choice, including a local one.

yihtsy/zotlink.does: A Windows manager for linked attachments that repairs broken links by file ID and moves files as collections change. Also rebuilds a library from a folder by DOI or ISBN, renames PDFs and copies Markdown links for Obsidian. Needs Zotero 10.
yihtsy/zotlink.pain: For people who keep PDFs in ordinary folders instead of Zotero storage, so that files survive renaming or moving. Interface mixes English and Chinese.

poesein/zotradar.does: A dashboard for literature subscriptions that gathers papers from feeds and scores them against your research interests. Shows evidence, journal ranking via easyScholar, and lets you correct scores. Needs Zotero 10.
poesein/zotradar.pain: Following many feeds buries you in papers of mixed relevance. This sorts new papers by priority so you can read the important ones first. Interface in Chinese and English.

vishnutskumar/zotero-ai-explain.does: Explains selected passages in the PDF reader in a popup, with sidebar follow-up chat and an "Ask your library" chat. Runs on Ollama, a Codex or Claude Code login, or OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini keys.
vishnutskumar/zotero-ai-explain.pain: Gets help on a hard passage, or a question across your library, without copying text out of Zotero. Answers cite the item and page they came from.

x-t-e-r/zotero-mcp-neo.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor and Codex can search, read and write your library through six tools. Writes preview first and permissions are layered; optional semantic search needs an embedding provider. A redesign of cookjohn/zotero-mcp.
x-t-e-r/zotero-mcp-neo.pain: Lets you drive your library in natural language from an AI client. The dry-run-first model and default Create-only access limit what an assistant can change.

adellife/zotero-skimread.does: Highlights the sentences that carry a paper's main argument across a whole PDF or EPUB, as coloured overlays in the reader. Runs on a local Ollama model by default or a cloud OpenAI-compatible server after consent.
adellife/zotero-skimread.pain: A triage aid for deciding what to read closely in a long paper. It is not a summary, and cloud use sends extracted text off your machine.

stark1tty/zotero-watch-folder-zotero8.does: Watches a folder and imports new PDFs and other files into Zotero 8 with metadata retrieval, renaming by pattern, duplicate checks and smart rules. Can mirror subfolders as collections in both directions and run bulk reorganisation. A fork of josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder.
stark1tty/zotero-watch-folder-zotero8.pain: Saves manual dragging of downloads into Zotero. A fork of josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jkroes/zotero-hide-citation-highlights.does: Removes the blue boxes the PDF reader paints over detected citations and internal cross-reference links, such as LaTeX hyperref links. Links stay clickable and their popups still work.
jkroes/zotero-hide-citation-highlights.pain: In papers full of linked citations the boxes clutter the page and can't be turned off in stock Zotero.

firekern/zusia.does: A chat beside the PDF that answers questions about the paper you are reading, with LaTeX, drawings and numbered theorem boxes whose references link back. Uses Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity through your own login, with no API key in the plugin. Saves answers as notes.
firekern/zusia.pain: A study aid for maths-heavy papers. The assistant gets the paper's metadata and your annotations, not the full PDF text.

zxyl1003/inthes.does: A sidebar assistant for asking, summarising and comparing up to five papers, or analysing a collection of up to 200. Answers carry source citations that jump to the PDF page. Connects to ChatGPT or Antigravity accounts or API keys, optional MinerU parsing, and saves chats as notes.
zxyl1003/inthes.pain: Gives cited answers across several papers or a collection without leaving Zotero. Your questions and paper content go to the model service you choose. The interface is in Chinese.

tlzh/paperworm.does: Adds an AI chat panel to the PDF reader that knows the paper's text and metadata. Offers summaries, quoted selections and screenshot analysis of figures. Sessions are saved as child notes that sync. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Ollama and others, with optional MinerU extraction.
tlzh/paperworm.pain: Lets you ask questions about the paper you are reading without pasting text into a chatbot. You bring a provider key or a local Ollama model.

poesein/zotquery.does: Searches the text of your PDFs and your notes with local embeddings, and exposes the results to AI clients through MCP tools. Tracks which passages were read and confirmed, keeps surveys across sessions and offers output templates. Needs Zotero 10 and a connected AI client.
poesein/zotquery.pain: For literature reviews where an AI should draw on your own library with traceable evidence, not guess. It separates found passages from verified ones. Interface in Chinese and English.

ajs7270/zotero-ai-summary.does: Saves AI-written paper summaries and "pinpoint lessons" from Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI as formatted child notes. The plugin exposes a local HTTP endpoint; Poppler and Python are needed for the skills.
ajs7270/zotero-ai-summary.pain: Turns an AI agent's paper reading into lasting Zotero notes instead of loose Markdown files. Text sent to a cloud model is no longer private.

roderickvella/zotero-item-key-column.does: Adds an Item Key column to the item list and advanced search results, and a read-only Item Key row in the Info pane. The key is Zotero's internal identifier, such as ABCD1234.
roderickvella/zotero-item-key-column.pain: Useful when scripting, using the API or debugging, where you need an item's key and Zotero doesn't show it.

andrew-healey/open-inline-citation.does: Lets you Cmd-click an inline citation in the PDF reader to open the cited paper in a new tab. Written for Zotero 6 and untested on 7.
andrew-healey/open-inline-citation.pain: Saves searching for a reference when a citation catches your eye while reading.

young-bo-i/zotero-enterscholar.does: Translates text selected in the PDF or EPUB reader, and annotations from a right-click menu, with an LLM. Uses either the EnterScholar forum's shared configuration after you sign in or your own endpoint and key (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek or compatible). Caches results.
young-bo-i/zotero-enterscholar.pain: Gives LLM translation inside the reader. Mainly for users of the EnterScholar community, which is Chinese-language.

wu-uk/zotero-feishu.does: Publishes items, child notes, images and PDF attachments to Feishu cloud documents, one document per item, from a right-click menu on items or collections. Sets up a personal Feishu application through your browser. Needs a mainland Feishu account.
wu-uk/zotero-feishu.pain: For people who keep research notes in Feishu. Sync is one way, so Feishu edits can be overwritten, and annotations must go into a note first.

dnnunn/zotero-doi-finder.does: Finds missing DOIs, and abstracts, by searching Crossref with an item's title, first author and year, accepting only close title matches. Runs on selected items, a collection or the whole library, optionally for new items. No API key needed.
dnnunn/zotero-doi-finder.pain: Many records lack DOIs, and adding them by hand is slow. This fills them in bulk, with a configurable match threshold and request delay.

018/zotflomo.does: Publishes a Zotero note to Flomo, the note-taking service, from a right-click command, using your Flomo API URL. Works with ZotCard by converting card headings and label lines into Flomo tags.
018/zotflomo.pain: Sends reading notes to Flomo without copying. Written for Zotero 6, so it is legacy. Documentation is in Chinese.

roey-angel/zotero-semantic-tagger.does: Tags new items with the Claude API by choosing only from tags already in your library, never creating new ones. Reads the title, abstract and optionally PDF text, and also runs on selected items. Has synonym groups, a strictness slider and a token warning. Needs an Anthropic API key.
roey-angel/zotero-semantic-tagger.pain: Keeps a large library tagged consistently with your own vocabulary instead of new variants.

wyhao2333/zotero-paperpilot.does: A reading assistant for Zotero 10 with selection translation, AI interpretation, per-PDF chat and a full-paper digest. Exports chats as notes. Works with several LLM providers and local Ollama.
wyhao2333/zotero-paperpilot.pain: Keeps translation, questions and summaries in the reader. Free translation services may receive your selected text. Interface in Chinese.

amogh-joshi/zotero-rsvp.does: Speed reading in the PDF reader: shows a page or selection one word at a time at 150 to 900 words per minute. Needs a PDF with a text layer.
amogh-joshi/zotero-rsvp.pain: A way to read quickly without moving your eyes. Free for noncommercial use under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence.

lee-lab-skku/zotero-tara.does: Backs up Zotero preferences, installed plugins, citation styles, translators and locate engines. It restores them on another computer or from an earlier backup. Buttons sit in the toolbar. Sync account details are excluded.
lee-lab-skku/zotero-tara.pain: Zotero sync doesn't carry settings or plugins. A fork of l0o0/tara; its README doesn't say what it changes.

ma-ji/zotero-cc.does: Fetches citation counts for journal articles from OpenAlex, Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP, Semantic Scholar or Scopus, and field-weighted impact from OpenAlex. Adds sortable Citation Counts and FWCI columns, runs on new items or by right-click. Scopus needs an API key.
ma-ji/zotero-cc.pain: Lets you order a long reading list by citation count. A fork of FrLars21/ZoteroCitationCountsManager with more sources and the FWCI column.

jimustafa/zotero-jabbr.does: Fills the Journal Abbr field for selected journal articles through a right-click command, only when the field is empty, so nothing is overwritten.
jimustafa/zotero-jabbr.pain: Citation styles that need abbreviated journal names are tedious to satisfy by hand. For older Zotero versions, so it is legacy.

qyangcv/zopilot.does: An AI chat in the Zotero sidebar for reading papers, with @ mentions to add papers to the context. Use an OpenAI-compatible API key or a Codex CLI login. Needs Zotero 9, macOS or Windows.
qyangcv/zopilot.pain: Lets you ask about papers and collections without leaving Zotero. Parsing very long documents can be slow.

flychen50/zoterocitationcountsagent.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP, Semantic Scholar and NASA ADS, automatically for new items or on demand from the right-click menu. Adds a sortable Citation Counts column; NASA ADS lookups need your own ADS API key.
flychen50/zoterocitationcountsagent.pain: Zotero shows no citation counts, so judging how influential a paper is means looking it up elsewhere. This puts the number in your item list, where you can sort by it.

zhi-11/zotero-ai-paragraph-notes.does: Sends paragraphs and figure captions from MinerU-parsed PDFs to an OpenAI-compatible AI service. It works via LLM for Zotero and writes each interpretation as a native Zotero note annotation. Includes a queue manager tab and a reader button to hide the notes.
zhi-11/zotero-ai-paragraph-notes.pain: Reading a dense paper paragraph by paragraph with AI help usually means pasting text elsewhere. This puts the explanations on the PDF pages themselves, built for use with the Margin Comments plugin. Its interface is in Chinese.

redkiezhang717/vocabu_text.does: A vocabulary book inside Zotero: collect words and phrases while reading a PDF. Each entry can keep a translation, the original sentence and page, and you get flashcard review and Anki export. Also tracks read or unread status and notes per paper.
redkiezhang717/vocabu_text.pain: Learning words from papers in a second language normally means copying them into a separate app and losing the context. This keeps them tied to the source sentence and paper. Its interface is in Chinese.

zouyonghao/zotero-sync-to-tablet.does: Copies a selected attachment file to a target folder you set in the settings, and retrieves it back from that folder, overwriting the original. It has no other features, such as annotation extraction.
zouyonghao/zotero-sync-to-tablet.pain: Useful if you read PDFs on a tablet through a synced folder and want a simple send and fetch step without a larger tool.

solsongli/deepread.does: AI deep reading in the PDF reader: margin cards with per-paragraph summaries and explanations. It also has hover translation, an outline bar, figure cards and questions tied to the source text. You supply your own API keys for the AI service.
solsongli/deepread.pain: Reading a difficult paper in a second language usually means switching between the PDF and a chatbot. This keeps explanations and translations beside each paragraph. Its interface is mainly in Chinese.

e-zz/zotserver.does: Runs a local HTTP API on your machine so other desktop applications can search and read your Zotero library without internet access. This fork adds a Selected endpoint aimed at connecting Zotero to Logseq.
e-zz/zotserver.pain: Lets note-taking and other tools talk to Zotero locally. A fork of MunGell/ZotServer that adds an endpoint for the currently selected items, for Logseq integration.

ajdavis/zotero-duplicates-plugin.does: Finds duplicate parent items by comparing PDF content hashes and title similarity. It shows the groups in a review window from the Tools menu, and tags them 'duplicate' so the main window filters to them for cleanup.
ajdavis/zotero-duplicates-plugin.pain: Zotero's own duplicate detection relies on metadata, so it misses copies whose records differ. Comparing the PDFs themselves catches those.

fenghsu2019/zotero-mineru-obsidian.does: Syncs the Markdown and images that LLM for Zotero produces from MinerU PDF parsing into a local Obsidian vault, one way, for the collections you choose. Saves multiple sync rules and writes to raw/papers and raw/assets folders.
fenghsu2019/zotero-mineru-obsidian.pain: For people building an Obsidian LLM Wiki from their papers, this moves the parsed text over automatically instead of by hand. It does not run MinerU itself.

bionux-th/zotero-translate-for-readingmo.does: Translates a paper paragraph by paragraph in Zotero 10's PDF reading mode and shows the translation under each original paragraph. Uses Ollama, Google, DeepL, Bing and other services, and saves the translation as a JSON attachment you can edit.
bionux-th/zotero-translate-for-readingmo.pain: Reading papers in another language otherwise means copying text into a translator. Translating only when you press the button, and saving the result, avoids repeated requests. Default target language is Simplified Chinese.

techne-tools/logios.does: Chat with the Hermes Agent in a Zotero sidebar tab, with selected items attached as context. Includes commands to save chats as notes, read and write PDF annotations, build citations in a chosen style, and suggest tags. Needs Hermes Agent installed.
techne-tools/logios.pain: Gets an AI agent that knows your library without copying item details into a separate chat. An experimental plugin for people already using Hermes.

chen7447/rebootero.does: Adds a Restart Zotero entry under Quit in the File menu, which closes Zotero and reopens it. The label is in Chinese for a Chinese interface and Reboot otherwise.
chen7447/rebootero.pain: Plugins often need a restart after installing or updating, and stock Zotero makes you quit and relaunch by hand.

cavalloscuro/lgfetcher.does: Searches Library Genesis mirrors for the selected item using its DOI, ISBN, title and author. It ranks the matches and lets you pick a copy from a window showing cover, author, publisher, year and format before attaching the file.
cavalloscuro/lgfetcher.pain: Finding a full-text book or article by hand is slow when the publisher page has no free copy. Note that LibGen hosts copyrighted material without permission, and downloading from it may be unlawful where you live.

paulluis-roehl/zotero-cover-view.does: Adds a cover grid view beside Zotero's list view, with a toolbar button to switch between them, plus a Cover column with thumbnails. Covers come from an image attachment, the first page of an EPUB or PDF, or optionally an ISBN lookup.
paulluis-roehl/zotero-cover-view.pain: A plain text list suits papers poorly when your library is mostly books. Covers make a book collection easier to browse by sight.

wangzikai01/zotero-row-colors.does: Colours whole rows in the item list from a right-click menu: Read, Important and Not Useful shortcuts, 12 preset colours, or a custom hex colour. Works on multiple selected items and keeps the colour when deselected.
wangzikai01/zotero-row-colors.pain: Zotero marks items with small tag dots only. Coloured rows show reading status at a glance across a long list. Its interface is in Chinese and English.

groele/zotero-paperflow.does: Tracks manuscripts through submission inside your Zotero library. It records stages, submission rounds, journal history, reviewer comments, your replies and key dates, organised with PaperFlow tags. Part of the Zotero Flow series.
groele/zotero-paperflow.pain: Keeping track of where each paper is in peer review usually happens in a spreadsheet outside Zotero. This keeps it next to the references.

najibprog/zotero-reference-checker.does: Lists the references of the article open in the PDF reader and shows which are already in your library, with a green, orange or other status. Opens their PDFs in one click, jumps to where they are cited, and adds missing ones to a collection.
najibprog/zotero-reference-checker.pain: While reading a paper, finding out which of its sources you already hold, and fetching the rest, normally means searching your library reference by reference.

bwiernik/zoteroquicklook.does: Previews a selected attachment with QuickLook: macOS's native Quick Look, Gloobus-Preview on Linux, or a custom preview command you set.
bwiernik/zoteroquicklook.pain: A fork of mronkko/ZoteroQuickLook; its README doesn't say what it changes. Quick Look lets you glance at a file without opening a full viewer.

guotuanwang/cesi.does: Finds duplicate items within a chosen collection and its subcollections by exact DOI, exact ISBN, or normalised title with year and author tolerance. Either gathers duplicates in a subcollection or keeps the best item and trashes the rest.
guotuanwang/cesi.pain: Zotero's duplicate pane covers the whole library, which is awkward when you only want to tidy one project's collection. Available as English and Simplified Chinese builds.

haohaomin/zotero-except.does: Hides the internal SettingsSync configuration entries from My Library and Recently Read views, while keeping the data. They still show when you open the SettingsSync collection directly.
haohaomin/zotero-except.pain: If you use a settings sync plugin, its configuration items clutter your library and recent reading lists. This removes them from view.

kinranlau/zotero_tag_recommender.does: Suggests tags for a paper from its title and abstract, matched to your existing tag vocabulary, using OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or DeepSeek models. Also adds tag autocomplete that matches any part of a tag name, which needs no key.
kinranlau/zotero_tag_recommender.pain: Tagging consistently by hand is slow and tags drift over time. Suggestions drawn from your own tags keep a library uniform. You need your own API key for the AI suggestions.

xiaoxiao937/li-yue-zotero.does: Reads several selected PDFs one by one with the same custom prompt and saves each AI answer as a separate child note on its item. Works with DeepSeek, OpenAI and compatible APIs, with cost estimates, retries and long-PDF chunking. Needs your own API key.
xiaoxiao937/li-yue-zotero.pain: Asking the same question of many papers means repeating it in a chatbot and copying answers back. This runs the batch and files each answer on the right item. Its interface is in Chinese.

regulust/zoteroquicklook.does: Previews a selected attachment with QuickLook: macOS's native Quick Look, Gloobus-Preview on Linux, or a custom command. This fork adjusts the code to work with Zotero 6 and was only tested on macOS.
regulust/zoteroquicklook.pain: Lets you glance at a file without opening a full viewer. The author says it is not actively maintained and may not work with current Zotero versions.

fdossi/zotfetch.does: Downloads PDFs for many selected items at once, trying open-access sources in turn. Sources include Unpaywall, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Europe PMC and CORE, plus publisher pages. Has fast modes, rate limiting and retry for failed items. Built for Zotero 8.
fdossi/zotfetch.pain: Fetching missing PDFs one item at a time is slow. This batches it across many sources and shows live progress. A free CORE API key is recommended.

usepa/epa-zotero-plugin.does: Disables Zotero's built-in cloud sync features. Built from the Make It Red template for use at the US Environmental Protection Agency, on Zotero 7 only.
usepa/epa-zotero-plugin.pain: Organisations that cannot send data to Zotero's servers need sync switched off. This does it for the whole installation.

bpiwowar/zotero-remarkable-sync.does: Syncs PDFs and annotations between Zotero and a reMarkable tablet through the reMarkable cloud. Items with a chosen tag are pushed to the device; in the default safe mode it only uploads PDFs and pulls annotations back. Experimental.
bpiwowar/zotero-remarkable-sync.pain: Reading and marking up papers on an e-ink tablet otherwise means moving files and annotations by hand. The author warns it can damage data, so back up first.

marco0431/askgpt-zotero.does: Select text in a paper, press Ctrl+K and ask an AI in a floating panel, with the full text of PDF, HTML or Markdown attachments as context. Renders formulas and tables, saves answers as notes, and works with DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible API.
marco0431/askgpt-zotero.pain: Asking AI about a hard passage normally means copying it into a web chat. This keeps the question inside Zotero and sends the full paper only once. Needs an API key.

xuebastudy/zotero10-hide-citation-highli.does: Hides the persistent blue backgrounds on citations and internal cross-reference links in the Zotero 10 PDF reader, keeping the links clickable. Can optionally disable citation and internal link clicks to prevent accidental jumps.
xuebastudy/zotero10-hide-citation-highli.pain: The blue boxes over every citation make dense pages harder to read. This removes them without touching your annotations.

liuwenbo0/zotero-local-translate.does: Translates PDFs into a monolingual and a bilingual attachment using PDFMathTranslate and BabelDOC, with your own OpenAI-compatible API. Works on selected items, collections or the whole library, and offers to translate new PDFs. Built for Zotero 10.
liuwenbo0/zotero-local-translate.pain: Translating whole papers while keeping their layout and formulas usually needs separate tools. This adds the translated PDFs next to the original. It downloads engines on first use, needing about 4 GB.

sstraume97/zotero-highlight-popup-ui-plu.does: Replaces the reader's text selection popup rows with one row of colours for highlights and one for underlines, so colour and style are chosen in a single click. Offers four visual styles and normal or tablet button sizes.
sstraume97/zotero-highlight-popup-ui-plu.pain: Zotero's popup needs two choices, a colour and a highlight or underline mode, which is fiddly if you switch between them often.

groele/zotero-refflow.does: Finds references, citing works and related research for an item from local documents and online sources. It shows them in Zotero with a Connected Papers style graph, and lets you filter and import candidates. Part of the Zotero Flow series.
groele/zotero-refflow.pain: Tracing where a paper's ideas come from, or what cites it, otherwise happens on websites outside your library. It is derived from Zotero Reference.

kenanking/zotclip.does: Copies attachment files to the system clipboard from the library or reader. It also generates tags for selected items with an OpenAI-compatible AI service: DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio or a custom URL. Built for Zotero 8 to 10.
kenanking/zotclip.pain: Pasting a PDF into an email or chat otherwise means finding the file on disk. AI tagging saves typing tags by hand; hosted services need your own key, local models do not.

rickwashon/astrozotero.does: Astronomy workflow based on NASA ADS: stores ADS bibcodes, enriches metadata and downloads the best or latest published PDF. It also shows an embedded literature map of citations where you can add papers to your library. Needs a NASA ADS API token.
rickwashon/astrozotero.pain: Astronomers rely on ADS rather than generic sources, and Zotero doesn't link to it. A fork of samuelyeewl/zot-nasa-ads that adds enrichment and the literature map.

retorquere/zotero-prosec-linker.does: Creates links from items using URL templates you define with {PDF}, {TITLE} and {DOI} placeholders, through a right-click Create Prosec Links command.
retorquere/zotero-prosec-linker.pain: Built for the PROSEC tool. It is mainly for people who already use PROSEC.

jiahaohong/mineru-to-zotero.does: Parses PDFs into Markdown from a right-click menu using MinerU, markitdown, docling, vision OCR, Baidu OCR, TextIn or Doc2X. It carries your PDF highlights into the Markdown with their colours. Can also export a highlights-only file with the PDF outline.
jiahaohong/mineru-to-zotero.pain: Getting readable Markdown out of PDFs, with your highlights intact, is useful for notes and LLM workflows. Some backends need your own API credentials or a local tool.

lvyrana/papermind-zotero.does: Adds a right-click item command that sends the item's metadata and best PDF to the PaperMind service and opens its reading page in your browser. You paste your personal PaperMind link into a settings dialog.
lvyrana/papermind-zotero.pain: Moves a paper from Zotero into an AI reading assistant in one click instead of uploading it by hand. It is a public test version.

00sapo/zotero-skimming.does: Guides a first pass through a PDF by choosing key sentences and highlighting them temporarily, with an explicit save step. Runs locally with Ollama or through an OpenAI-compatible API. Requires Zotero 9.
00sapo/zotero-skimming.pain: A quick orientation read before the full read, without AI-written summaries. The author warns that automated sentence selection can be biased, so it is not for in-depth study.

oekeur/zotero-timeline.does: Author research timelines inside Zotero where each event has a title, date, description and tags. Events carry typed links to library items such as supports or contradicts. Draws several timelines on one axis. Pre-release, for Zotero 8 to 10.
oekeur/zotero-timeline.pain: For historians and others building chronologies where the sources matter, this keeps events tied to the exact items that back or dispute them.

iiwenwen/zotero-quicklook.does: Previews a selected file with the space bar using macOS Quick Look. Only supports Mac.
iiwenwen/zotero-quicklook.pain: Lets you glance at an attachment without opening it in another application.

luishcalderon/scihub-zotero-8.does: Downloads PDFs for items with a DOI from Sci-Hub in Zotero 8 and later, tests mirrors, and updates PDFs from Sci-Hub. Based on ethanwillis's Zotero 6 plugin.
luishcalderon/scihub-zotero-8.pain: Lets you fetch papers behind paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

maizipiaopiao/inkbridge.does: Chinese and English translation in the PDF reader: select text to translate, plus dictionary lookup. It also offers screenshot translation that keeps formulas as LaTeX, and English pronunciation. Runs on local models you set up; no online services are used.
maizipiaopiao/inkbridge.pain: Academic reading across Chinese and English without sending text to a cloud service. Text and screenshot translation need an NVIDIA GPU with vLLM; the dictionary and speech parts need less.

jaeyoonsung/zotero-plugins.does: Two plugins in one repository, ZotPoP and Style Custom. ZotPoP searches for papers by author, journal, title or keywords across several indexes and imports them with citation metrics. Style Custom is a research workbench with extra columns, journal metrics, author tracking and a citation graph.
jaeyoonsung/zotero-plugins.pain: Gives Publish or Perish style literature search inside Zotero, and adds reading status and metrics to your list. Keys for OpenAlex, AI services and easyScholar are optional.

jun0404/zotero-scihub.does: Downloads PDFs for items with a DOI from Sci-Hub automatically in Zotero and Juris-M.
jun0404/zotero-scihub.pain: A fork of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub; its README doesn't say what it changes. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.
