whiteofalien/zotero-ai-tab.does: Chat with an AI in the Zotero sidebar through any OpenAI-compatible API, including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen and Doubao. You enter your API key, the full chat completions URL and the model name in settings.
whiteofalien/zotero-ai-tab.pain: Keeps AI conversation inside Zotero rather than a browser tab. Needs your own key from a provider.

hrs0986/zoteropdf.does: Exports PDF attachments to a folder you choose, from selected items or a whole collection via the right-click menu, with a progress indicator.
hrs0986/zoteropdf.pain: Zotero stores PDFs in opaque folders, so sharing or copying a set of papers means digging them out by hand.

eric-tramel/zoty.does: A Zotero bridge for the zoty MCP server, which lets AI agents search your local library by title, abstract and indexed full text. The plugin enables remote access so agents can attach PDFs and assign collections. Needs Python and the Zotero local API enabled.
eric-tramel/zoty.pain: For people using AI agents such as Claude Code who want them to read and add to their Zotero library locally, without a hosted service.

volatile-static/zotero-inspector.does: Adds a Show DOM Inspector command under Tools, Developer that injects an inspector into all of Zotero's HTML frames.
volatile-static/zotero-inspector.pain: A tool for plugin developers who need to inspect Zotero's interface structure.

yanchou3/zotero-lastread-format.does: Changes the Last Read Time column from the full date and time to a compact MM-DD HH:mm format. Sorting still uses the real timestamp.
yanchou3/zotero-lastread-format.pain: The default column is wide and cluttered. A short format saves space in the item list.

ajdavis/zotero-metadata-search-plugin.does: Updates items with metadata searched from bibliographic databases: Crossref, DBLP, OpenAlex and arXiv.
ajdavis/zotero-metadata-search-plugin.pain: Fixes incomplete or wrong records by pulling the details from an authoritative source instead of retyping them.

socratic-irony/zotero-snowball.does: Finds the references and citing works for selected items or collections through OpenAlex. It shows them in a sortable, filterable review dialog, and adds the ones you pick to your library. Needs your own OpenAlex API key.
socratic-irony/zotero-snowball.pain: Snowballing through a paper's references and citations is a standard literature review step that otherwise means searching each paper by hand.

dklsgui/zotmod.does: Updates item metadata and DOIs from online sources, with a choice of which item types to update, and adds tags automatically or by hand.
dklsgui/zotmod.pain: Cleans up incomplete records and tags without manual editing.

justanotherjurastudent/zotero_book-group.does: Groups book sections and encyclopedia articles under their edited volume in the item list, using Zotero's existing Related links. Contributions are ordered by first page, with indentation, background colours and an outline per volume.
justanotherjurastudent/zotero_book-group.pain: Book chapters otherwise sit alphabetically scattered, apart from the volume they come from, which is awkward with handbooks, commentaries or Festschriften. It writes nothing to your library, so sync and export are unaffected.

waynehfut/paper-miner.does: An AI reading assistant that also shows journal rankings and warnings in the item list. It adds a PDF chat panel, AI summaries saved as notes, editable slide decks and selection translation. Needs your own OpenAI-compatible API key.
waynehfut/paper-miner.pain: Chinese-language researchers otherwise juggle separate sites for journal tiers, paper chat, summaries and translation. Journal data comes from EasyScholar, which needs its own free key; citation counts come from OpenAlex.

ruijie-xi/zotero-chat-pdf.does: Adds a persistent chat panel to Zotero for discussing one or more PDFs with an OpenAI-compatible model, converting PDFs through MinerU. The assistant can search your library, and optionally the web, and add papers.
ruijie-xi/zotero-chat-pdf.pain: Asking questions about a paper normally means leaving Zotero for a chat site. Needs a MinerU token and an LLM API key (DeepSeek by default); converted text and chats are cached locally and shared with local MCP clients.

alansirius/zotero-exitem.does: Uses AI to extract structured fields from selected papers into a Review Manager tab. It can merge a folder of records into a synthesis, export them, or turn them into Zotero notes. Relies on the zotero-gpt plugin being set up.
alansirius/zotero-exitem.pain: Building a literature table by hand means rereading each paper for the same fields. This extracts them in batches of up to five and folds in your highlights and annotations, for literature-review workflows.

fuchsi3010/zotero-selection-popup-on-alt.does: Hides the text-selection popup in the Zotero reader until you hold Alt while selecting. Works in the PDF reader and, on a best-effort basis, the EPUB and snapshot readers.
fuchsi3010/zotero-selection-popup-on-alt.pain: The popup gets in the way if you mostly read without annotating. This makes it opt-in, so selecting text shows nothing unless you ask for it.

xcjames/zotero_timer.does: Adds a small draggable clock, stopwatch and countdown timer window to Zotero, with a semi-transparent look.
xcjames/zotero_timer.pain: Useful for timing paper-reading sessions or research sprints without leaving Zotero for a separate timer app.

forgeters/zotero-fig.does: Lists the figures and tables found in a PDF in a reader side pane, jumps to each one, and opens an enlarged figure preview you can zoom and drag. Needs Python with PyMuPDF installed.
forgeters/zotero-fig.pain: Finding a specific figure in a long paper means scrolling. This gives a clickable list; where image regions can't be matched it falls back to jumping to the caption, and tables get no preview.

zzangho/zotero-gemini.does: A chat window for talking to Google Gemini about selected items, using the PDF full text and existing notes as context. Saves answers as notes and can merge an item's notes into one summary. Needs a Gemini API key.
zzangho/zotero-gemini.pain: Lets you question a paper with Gemini without copying text out of Zotero. Chats are kept per item, and answers keep their tables and formulas when saved as notes. Interface in English and Korean.

equalang/equalang-zotero-plugin.does: Translates PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Excel attachments with the layout kept, plus selected text in the reader. Results attach to the original item, and PDFs can come back as bilingual editions for side-by-side reading.
equalang/equalang-zotero-plugin.pain: Reading papers in another language otherwise means pasting into a translation site and losing the layout. Needs an Equalang account; translation is paid for with credits shared with the Equalang website.

wncfht/texlate.does: Zotero companion for TeXlate, which translates arXiv papers into Chinese by translating LaTeX source paragraphs and recompiling a bilingual PDF. The plugin attaches the resulting PDF to your item; needs a TeXlate server and your own model key.
wncfht/texlate.pain: Chinese readers of arXiv papers get a translated PDF with the original layout, formulas and citations protected. This listing is the Zotero part of a larger tool, which is a Python server you run yourself.

zx33/zotero-cool-paper.does: Adds two item-pane panels: papers.cool KIMI paper readings, and related papers found in your own library. The local panel matches by tags, title and abstract and sends nothing out.
zx33/zotero-cool-paper.pain: Saves switching to the papers.cool site while reading, and helps you rediscover related papers you already hold. Results are cached locally, and double-clicking a local result opens its PDF.

shen-zhang-42/abstractin.does: A reader discussion panel for asking about the current page, passage, theorem or chapter. Chats are organised by chapter and saved as editable notes. Runs through a local Codex command-line tool you install and sign in to.
shen-zhang-42/abstractin.pain: A study companion for books and scientific papers, with separate reading flows for each. A fork of firekern/zusia; its README doesn't say what it changes. Model processing still happens through the assistant's online service.

chrislucy838-collab/zotero-research-copi.does: An AI research chat beside the item or reader, using the open paper, selected text, extra papers and images as context. Also searches OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref to import papers, and translates selected text. Works with OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
chrislucy838-collab/zotero-research-copi.pain: Keeps paper discussion, discovery and translation inside Zotero rather than in separate tools. Hosted models need an API key; a local endpoint needs none. Chats and memory stay in Zotero's data directory.

etshaw-zh/zotero-evidence.does: AI-assisted systematic literature reviews, from screening to synthesis. You import references, confirm AI screening suggestions, extract data into a codebook table backed by highlighted quotes, and group findings into themes. Exports PRISMA data and CSV.
etshaw-zh/zotero-evidence.pain: Systematic reviews involve repetitive screening and coding across many papers. This keeps every extracted value traceable to its source and measures AI-human agreement. Needs an AI provider endpoint and key.

haobbc/zotero-ai-notes.does: Generates a structured AI summary note for selected papers from the right-click menu, covering purpose, methods, contributions, results and limitations. Uses the PDF text, or the abstract if there is no PDF. Needs a Grok (xAI) API key.
haobbc/zotero-ai-notes.pain: Writing a first-pass summary of each paper by hand is slow. This batch-processes a selection into tagged child notes and skips papers that already have a PDF-based summary. English and Traditional Chinese.

bjtupupil/word-zotero-bridge.does: Batch-inserts native Zotero citations into copies of Word documents and relinks old items in existing citations. Driven by a batch file and a PowerShell controller; Windows only, built for Zotero 9.0.6.
bjtupupil/word-zotero-bridge.pain: Fixing or adding many citations in a Word manuscript by hand is slow and error-prone. It works only on copies, checks each step by item key, and can resume after a failure. Very narrow, built around one fixed collection.

fredyyoussif/zotero-extra-columns.does: Lets you add your own text or number columns to the item list, editable in the Info section. Values are stored as Key: value lines in the Extra field, so they sync. Can also export standard and extra fields as a table.
fredyyoussif/zotero-extra-columns.pain: Zotero has no custom columns, which makes literature grids and review matrices awkward. Because values live in Extra, they sync with your library, support batch editing and sort numerically.

2246024816/zotero-mcp.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants such as Claude can use your library. They can search, read full text and annotations, browse collections, and create notes, tags and items. Includes semantic search over embeddings.
2246024816/zotero-mcp.pain: Lets an AI client work directly with your library without exporting data. A fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp; its README doesn't say what it changes.

kirinccchang/zotero-perma-archiver.does: Archives any Zotero item that has a URL to perma.cc when you save it, or in bulk from the right-click menu, tagging failures. The perma.cc link then appears in your Word citations. Needs a perma.cc API key.
kirinccchang/zotero-perma-archiver.pain: Aimed at law-review writers following Bluebook 22nd edition Rule 18.2.1(d), which requires archiving online sources. It replaces visiting perma.cc and pasting the link back for each item.

excellentenough/scholarpop.does: Explains selected PDF text with AI using the surrounding paper as context. You can also draw a box over a formula or figure for a vision model to explain. Supports follow-up chat. Needs an API key.
excellentenough/scholarpop.pain: Explaining a hard passage normally means copying it into a chatbot. Works with Kimi, DeepSeek, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible service, and is mainly written for Chinese-speaking users.

forxhunter/deduplication_by_folder_zoter.does: Finds and merges duplicates within one collection only, from a right-click menu item. Matches on DOI or on normalised title, year and first author, shows groups for review, and merges with Zotero's own merge.
forxhunter/deduplication_by_folder_zoter.pain: Zotero's Duplicate Items view scans the whole library. This lets you clean up one collection at a time.

luke-evan/zotero-keep-window.does: Makes the close button and Alt+F4 minimise the Zotero main window instead of quitting. Use File then Quit or Ctrl+Q to really exit. Windows only; the PDF reader and other windows are not affected.
luke-evan/zotero-keep-window.pain: Keeps sync and the Zotero Connector running in the background when you close the window by habit. Settings let you turn each behaviour off.

cydoimos/zotero-abbreviation-helper.does: Finds where a paper defines each acronym or abbreviation and shows the meaning on hover in the PDF reader. Also offers optional lookup links for gene, protein, cell line and chemical names, and lets you add your own definitions.
cydoimos/zotero-abbreviation-helper.pain: Skimming a PDF full of short forms otherwise means scrolling back to find the first use. The scan runs locally and you can ignore wrong detections.

pikapei/zotero-default-attachment.does: Adds right-click options to set or unset a default PDF on an item with several attachments, so double-clicking the item opens that one.
pikapei/zotero-default-attachment.pain: Zotero always opens the first PDF added, which is wrong when an item holds several versions or supplements.

reginalluna/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text, annotations, titles, abstracts, notes, PDFs, EPUBs and webpages. It uses 20+ services such as Google, DeepL, GPT, Gemini and Claude, with a dictionary and session history.
reginalluna/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that adds a history browser, one-click reverse translation, language detection from longer selections, and a fix to the inferred-language metadata written to items. Some services need API keys.

momisback/protpeek.does: Detects PDB, UniProt and AlphaFold identifiers in a paper's PDF or HTML attachments and opens the structures in a bundled Mol* viewer window. Also opens local PDB, mmCIF and GRO files, and exports PNG or mmCIF.
momisback/protpeek.pain: Lets structural biology readers inspect a protein without leaving the paper. Scanning is local, and structures are downloaded from RCSB PDB or AlphaFold DB only when you open one. The Zotero version is described as a prototype.

zhonghaoyi/zotero-ai-reading.does: Sends a paper's PDF and a saved prompt to a web AI such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek from the right-click menu. It uses a Google Drive link, a pasted PDF file or extracted text, and can open the web AI in a reader side panel.
zhonghaoyi/zotero-ai-reading.pain: Uses the web chat services you already have instead of API keys. Sending is partly manual, since web pages can't be reliably controlled, and PDF file mode depends on the site accepting pasted files. The PDF file mode is described in terms of the macOS clipboard.

jsglazer/enhanced-notes.does: Expands Zotero notes with Liquid templates, a richer editor and two-way sync to Markdown files such as an Obsidian vault. Sync merges edits three ways, allows several synced notes per item and has a Sync Manager. Needs Zotero 8.
jsglazer/enhanced-notes.pain: A fork of windingwind's zotero-better-notes that replaces its JavaScript templates with Liquid, adds annotation colour labels and merge handling, and improves exports to Obsidian.

junyankang/paper-loom.does: Reads papers aloud offline and shows translations beside the original text. It adds hover cards for in-text citations and maps co-author networks from your library. Includes an AI research assistant using your own model.
junyankang/paper-loom.pain: Keeps listening, translating and citation lookup next to the paper instead of in other tools. Voice packs install on demand for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows; Chinese-language interface.

zhaopuee/zotero-eye-care.does: Adds four soft reading themes to the Zotero reader's Appearance panel: pale green, warm cream, misty blue-grey and a dark grey night theme. They apply to PDF, EPUB and snapshot readers.
zhaopuee/zotero-eye-care.pain: Gives low-glare backgrounds for long reading sessions using Zotero's own theme system. The Zotero 10 version is a beta. Disabling the plugin removes only its own four themes.

dinosv/zottablet.does: Sends PDFs to an external folder for tablet reading and brings them back. The folder can be synced by Dropbox, Google Drive or USB. It also detects externally changed files, keeps a tag-based reading list and imports annotations from other PDF readers.
dinosv/zottablet.pain: A successor to the abandoned ZotFile for Zotero 7 and 8, covering the send-to-tablet and annotation-extraction workflow with copy or move modes.

citestamp/zotero-plugin.does: Checks whether a reference resolves to a real work, in the item pane or from a right-click check. It also shows recorded refutations, failed replications and its place in the CiteStamp citation graph. Includes an ORCID claim link.
citestamp/zotero-plugin.pain: Helps catch invented or contested citations before you rely on them. Lookups use OpenAlex, Crossref, DataCite and CiteStamp's public graph; it flags retractions only when a retraction exists.

dingdinglz/zotero-translate.does: An Agents sidebar in the PDF reader for asking Codex, Pi or OpenCode about a passage or a figure screenshot. Each paper keeps its own chat history. Previews interactive charts the agent writes.
dingdinglz/zotero-translate.pain: Connects the coding agents you already run on your computer to the paper you are reading. Needs one of them installed locally; tested on macOS with Zotero 9, with Windows support not validated.

houxin2024/zotero-bilingual.does: Reads layout-preserving bilingual PDFs side by side, highlighting the matching translated sentence when you click one. The Windows bundle installs PDF2zh for one-click translation, with a free SiliconFlow default or your own service.
houxin2024/zotero-bilingual.pain: Comparing a paper with its translation otherwise means flipping between files. Parsing and sentence mapping run locally; translated text goes to the service you choose. Windows 10/11 one-click package.

groele/zotero-citeflow.does: Shows in the item list which items are cited in a Microsoft Word document. It keeps plugin-owned citation tags and lets you drag items into Word as editable Zotero citations. Needs Zotero's Word integration.
groele/zotero-citeflow.pain: While writing in Word, it lets you see from Zotero which sources you have already cited. Status comes only from citations it recognises, so unrecognised ones are not treated as never cited.

shourovj/zotero-tab-groups.does: Groups open reader tabs into named, coloured, collapsible clusters like browser tab groups. Add tabs from the right-click menu or by drag and drop, rename and recolour groups, and restore membership after a restart.
shourovj/zotero-tab-groups.pain: Reading for several projects at once leaves a long strip of tabs. Grouping and collapsing them keeps each project's PDFs together.

samyateia/zotextract.does: Asks an LLM the same questions across selected papers and tabulates the answers. Cited lines link back to the PDF, and results export as XLSX, CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown or HTML.
samyateia/zotextract.pain: Comparing methods or results across many papers by hand is slow. Works with local servers (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Jan) or online providers like OpenAI, OpenRouter and Gemini, whose keys you supply.

mtillman14/open-alex-work-id.does: Looks up an item's DOI in OpenAlex from a right-click menu item and stores its OpenAlex Work ID in the Extra field as OpenAlex Work ID.
mtillman14/open-alex-work-id.pain: Handy for linking Zotero items to OpenAlex records. It needs a DOI, which you can type into Extra if the item lacks one.

marysethomas/zotero-read-tracker.does: Marks papers as read with a right-click item and a Read Status column, storing the date and time in Extra. A Tools menu item plots a GitHub-style reading heatmap in your browser, saveable as SVG, PNG or HTML.
marysethomas/zotero-read-tracker.pain: Zotero has no built-in read marker or reading history. This shows which papers you have read and how your reading is spread over time.

cabdoge/pdf2notelink.does: Click a highlight in the PDF reader to open the Zotero note that cites it in the side pane. If several notes cite it, a small chooser appears next to the annotation. Optionally needs Ctrl or Command with the click.
cabdoge/pdf2notelink.pain: Finding which note refers to a highlight otherwise means searching your notes. It works only for notes that kept the native annotation reference, such as dragged-in highlights, and for Zotero 10 on macOS and Windows.

chrisshank/zemble.does: Connects Zotero to Semble, a social knowledge network for researchers. Columns show how many people saved an item, plus its collections, connections and notes, and you can save items and sync collections.
chrisshank/zemble.pain: Lets you see how others have used the papers in your library. Read-only by default; saving items or publishing collections needs a Semble API key. Marked work in progress.

muisedestiny/zotero-night.does: A dark theme for Zotero's interface and PDFs based on the Nord colour scheme, with a quick toggle between PDF filters, a cleaner tab bar and some animations.
muisedestiny/zotero-night.pain: Easier on the eyes for late-night reading. A fork of tefkah/zotero-night; its README doesn't say what it changes. It only runs on Zotero 6, and its dark PDFs use a slow CSS filter.

yebuqiu/zotero-papilot.does: An AI reading assistant for Zotero. It covers selection and side-by-side PDF translation, chat, library-wide Q&A, AI notes and mind maps, journal subscriptions, Obsidian export and reading progress. Works with many model providers or a local Ollama.
yebuqiu/zotero-papilot.pain: Gathers the reading workflow for Chinese-language research into one plugin, with free translation engines and your own model keys. The account and membership service behind its official gateway is not part of the plugin.

tiansuya/zoterochat.does: A reader sidebar chat for asking about the open PDF. You can attach highlighted passages or have a selection explained or translated, with Markdown and LaTeX answers. Chats are saved per PDF. Needs a chat-completions API key.
tiansuya/zoterochat.pain: Lets you discuss a paper without leaving the reader. Defaults to DeepSeek, and the paper text is kept as a stable prompt prefix to help provider-side caching.

9527crazy-2025/zotmind.does: Builds a local vector index of your library for semantic search. A ChatPDF sidebar answers about one paper, several or whole folders with clickable source quotes, plus a selection toolbar and optional Obsidian export.
9527crazy-2025/zotmind.pain: Goes beyond keyword search when reviewing many papers. Works with OpenAI-compatible providers or Ollama, with your own keys, and can route chat through a browser bridge to save tokens. Mainly Chinese-language.

alfakini/zotero-remarkable-plugin.does: Syncs PDFs, highlights and notes both ways with a reMarkable tablet via its cloud. Zotero annotations are burned into the PDF; tablet highlights, handwriting and typed text return as annotations and notes.
alfakini/zotero-remarkable-plugin.pain: Reading and marking up papers on e-ink otherwise means moving files by hand. It never modifies your own Zotero annotations, and updates the PDF without losing what you wrote on the tablet.

onyxaegis/zotero-tag-cited.does: Reads a saved Word document, finds the Zotero items cited in it, and tags them with cited followed by your abbreviation. Also creates a saved search so the list appears like a folder, and re-running updates both.
onyxaegis/zotero-tag-cited.pain: Lets you check from inside Zotero which sources you have cited so far while writing. Needs a .docx whose citations are live Zotero fields, and Zotero 8 or later.

septyagu/zotero-margin-fit.does: Detects white margins on PDF pages and fits the actual content to the window with Fit Width and Fit Height buttons. Adds page-by-page navigation and a button to cycle Zotero's single and spread layouts.
septyagu/zotero-margin-fit.pain: Large or uneven margins make text look small. This enlarges the content without cropping or changing the PDF. Built for Zotero 10 and replaces the Reset Zoom button while active.

mkant18/zotero_law.does: Saves Westlaw Advantage US cases through the Zotero Connector with structured metadata, and bundles a Bluebook Law Review citation style. Metadata covers court, date, dockets and reporter citations. Needs a Westlaw subscription.
mkant18/zotero_law.pain: Gives US legal researchers cleaner case records and citations than generic web saves. Marked beta, and it flags items whose metadata is missing or uncertain for review.

liuaustin/zotero-pdf-mem-cleanup.does: Releases the memory held by the PDF reader when you close a PDF tab, by cleaning up pdf.js resources and canvases. It runs silently and has no settings.
liuaustin/zotero-pdf-mem-cleanup.pain: Zotero's reader can keep growing in memory as PDFs are opened and closed. The author reports memory dropping back towards baseline after a tab closes. Written for Zotero 8 and later.

waterwoods-ai/clautero.does: Embeds Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or Pi as a chat side panel in Zotero's right pane and in the reader. It passes the selected paper or collection (metadata, abstract, PDF path, annotations) to the agent. Needs one of those command-line tools installed and signed in.
waterwoods-ai/clautero.pain: Using a coding-agent CLI on your papers normally means working in a terminal, away from the library. This puts the chat beside the paper, with multiple saved sessions.

eeeegoose/ocrflow.does: Runs OCR and AI workflows on documents from the right sidebar. It recognises PDFs and images with MinerU, PaddleOCR, Marker or an AI vision model, creates parent items, fills metadata, and writes summaries, translations and reader outlines. Mainly aimed at Chinese-language use. You supply your own OCR and AI services.
eeeegoose/ocrflow.pain: Scanned or unprocessed documents arrive in Zotero without text or metadata. This chains recognition, item creation, translation and summarising into one right-sidebar workflow.

vdcmathieu/zotero-ai-toolkit.does: Adds AI tools that use your own Claude or OpenAI key. They write structured paper summaries as child notes, recolour highlights into a fixed category scheme, suggest further reading and folders, and chat about one paper.
vdcmathieu/zotero-ai-toolkit.pain: Writing literature-review notes and sorting highlights by hand is slow. It also adds a journal-rank column (FT50, ABDC) and a citation-count column that need no key.

shuenhoy/zotero-break-pdf.does: Lets you select an area of a PDF in the Zotero reader for use with the Obsidian Broken PDF plugin. Early-stage, with known problems on tabs that were already open when Zotero started.
shuenhoy/zotero-break-pdf.pain: People who take PDF snippets into Obsidian need a way to mark the region from within Zotero. The author notes it is in an early state.

junyankang/paper-voice.does: Reads PDFs aloud in the Zotero reader with offline voices. It supports Chinese, English, Japanese and French, highlights the current sentence and shows a translation beside the original. The listing now points to its successor, Paper Loom.
junyankang/paper-voice.pain: Reading dense papers in a second language is tiring. Listening while following the text and translation helps you keep pace. Text-based PDFs only; scans need OCR first.

baijiyunze/zotero-chatgpt-sidebar.does: Embeds the web versions of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in Zotero's right sidebar. Selected PDF text, the full paper PDF, or an item's title and abstract can be sent to the open conversation. You log in with your own account.
baijiyunze/zotero-chatgpt-sidebar.pain: Using a chatbot on a paper usually means copy-pasting between browser and Zotero. This keeps the chat next to the paper and sends text with one click.

julianschelb/zotero-citation-graph.does: Draws the citation network of your own library as a force-directed graph or a timeline, and adds a Citations section to the item pane. Links come from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar reference lists; a Semantic Scholar key is optional.
julianschelb/zotero-citation-graph.pain: Zotero shows no relationships between the papers you hold. This shows which items in a collection cite which, and what a selected paper builds on.

situkangsayur/zotero-github-plugin.does: Backs up your whole library to a GitHub repository, public or private. Items become JSON and Markdown notes, with annotations and attachment files, and Git LFS handles large ones. Imports from GitHub to restore. Needs a GitHub personal access token.
situkangsayur/zotero-github-plugin.pain: Zotero sync is not a versioned backup. This gives you a readable, browsable history on GitHub that doubles as an Obsidian vault, without replacing Zotero's own sync.

chgwan/beaver-zotero-local.does: Runs the Beaver AI research agent inside Zotero on your own model provider. Chat about your library and the open paper, search OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar, with OpenAI-compatible endpoints (including Ollama, LM Studio) or Anthropic.
chgwan/beaver-zotero-local.pain: A fork of jlegewie/beaver-zotero that removes the Beaver account and servers. It drops write actions, persistent threads, citations and the MCP server. Early stage.

samuelyeewl/zot-nasa-ads.does: Updates an item's metadata from the NASA ADS database using its DOI or arXiv number, storing the bibcode and ADS URL in Extra. Can also download the publisher PDF. Needs a free NASA ADS API key.
samuelyeewl/zot-nasa-ads.pain: Astronomy papers added from arXiv carry preprint metadata. This swaps in the published version's details, though PDF download may fail on paywalls or captchas.

givemetarte/chat-with-paper.does: Adds a chat box for asking questions about the paper you are reading, answered by GPT-4o from relevant passages found by embedding the paper's text. Works in English and Korean. Needs an OpenAI API key.
givemetarte/chat-with-paper.pain: Lets you question a paper without leaving Zotero. Early project; it supports only GPT-4o and OpenAI, on Zotero 7.

dianzuan/zotron.does: Exposes Zotero's internal API to AI agents through a local command-line tool. Agents can search, read, annotate by quoted text, export citations, run OCR and search PDFs. Install the CLI and the plugin, plus Claude Code or Codex for agent use.
dianzuan/zotron.pain: Zotero's official API is read-only and MCP servers add overhead. This gives agents full read-write access with structured output.

meaning-infinite/zotero-color-keys.does: Adds keyboard shortcuts for text colour and highlight colour in Zotero notes, with eight colours and clear keys, acting on the selection or current paragraph. Also colours underline and highlight annotations in the PDF reader.
meaning-infinite/zotero-color-keys.pain: Colouring text in a note takes three clicks. Here you press one key, and pressing the same colour again removes it. Every key binding is customisable.

primuszp/lyz.does: Connects Zotero to LyX through the LyXServer pipe. Insert citations into LyX documents and keep the BibTeX database updated, with custom key formats, unique-key checks and translators. Needs LyX configured with a LyXServer pipe.
primuszp/lyz.pain: A fork of wshanks/lyz, modernised from Zotero 5/6 to Zotero 7 to 10. It adds a rebuilt settings pane, English, German and Hungarian text, and easier pipe setup.

janr383/zotero-qualified-references.does: Adds directed links between items with source and target pages, a five-point stance, a comment and an optional PDF anchor. Shows incoming links, a reference graph window, a list window, and optional item-list columns.
janr383/zotero-qualified-references.pain: Zotero's Related links are undirected and carry no meaning. This records which item supports or contradicts another, and where. The author says it was largely written with an AI model.

xzhang001/modern-zotero-themes.does: Restyles Zotero with colour themes such as Catppuccin, Nord and Solarized. It adds a rounded card layout, custom collection icons, a themed reader and a reading progress bar.
xzhang001/modern-zotero-themes.pain: Zotero's look is fixed and plain. This changes colours and spacing across the interface and reader while leaving item data and annotation colours alone. Zotero 8 or later recommended.

xfxf233/zotero-latex-math-tool.does: Adds a toolbar button to the PDF reader for placing LaTeX equations on a page, rendered with KaTeX and stored as free-text annotations. Double-click a formula to edit it. Targets Zotero 9 and later.
xfxf233/zotero-latex-math-tool.pain: Zotero has no way to write maths onto a PDF page. This lets you add typeset formulas, inline or display, beside the text.

sorinhostiuc/refdetect.does: Reports which reference manager made the citations in a Word or OpenDocument file. It recognises Zotero, EndNote, Mendeley, Paperpile, RefWorks, Citavi and others, and runs locally from the Tools menu.
sorinhostiuc/refdetect.pain: Before migrating or repairing a manuscript you need to know which tool its live citations came from. This tells you, with confidence notes.

myheart521/cli2openai.does: Translates a paper PDF into translated, bilingual and side-by-side PDFs through your signed-in Claude Code or Codex CLI and pdf2zh, with quality checks. The PaperBridge plugin runs it from Zotero, locally or over SSH. Mainly for Chinese output.
myheart521/cli2openai.pain: Translating papers normally needs a separate API key. This reuses an authenticated CLI instead. Needs Linux or WSL and Python.

he-chun/paper-library-checker.does: A Zotero companion for a Chrome or Edge extension that tells you whether the paper on a page, such as CNKI or MDPI, is already in your library. It shows Saved, Possible match or Not saved. The Zotero add-on only supplies an optional enhanced mode.
he-chun/paper-library-checker.pain: It's easy to save the same paper twice from a browser. This checks your local Zotero library first, without uploading it. Alpha software, Zotero 9 only.

siriyep/zotero-obsidian-linker.does: Creates or updates an Obsidian Markdown note for an item from the right-click menu, linking item, PDF and note, with an Obsidian Note attachment. Filenames follow a template. Includes a Claude Code skill that writes paper analyses.
siriyep/zotero-obsidian-linker.pain: Keeping literature notes in Obsidian linked to Zotero is manual. This generates the notes and keeps both sides connected.

memorushb/zotero-smart-highlighter.does: Highlights the most useful sentences in a PDF, for a selection or the whole paper. It ranks with local BM25 or TF-IDF, an optional on-device reranker on Apple Silicon, or an optional LLM with your own API key. Targets Zotero 8.
memorushb/zotero-smart-highlighter.pain: Highlighting a paper by hand takes time. This marks the claims, results and methods so you can skim, and works without any API key.

aaronkhodami/zotgit.does: Moves or copies imported attachments into a folder you choose and links them. It can sync settings and PDFs through a GitHub repository, with an on-demand remote PDF mode, and deletes linked files when you delete items. Needs a GitHub token for sync.
aaronkhodami/zotgit.pain: Built on ZotMoov, it keeps PDFs in your own folder and adds a GitHub copy for use across several computers.

yfengup/notion-item-opener-for-zotero.does: Opens a Zotero item when you click a link in a Notion literature database, using the item's native Item Key. It runs in Zotero, pairs a token on first use and uses Zotero's local connector server.
yfengup/notion-item-opener-for-zotero.pain: People tracking papers in Notion, for example through Notero, otherwise have to find the item in Zotero by hand. A click now brings it to the front.

sorinhostiuc/en2zotero.does: Converts EndNote Cite While You Write citations in a Word .docx into Zotero citations, matching by DOI and title and fetching missing references from Crossref. It writes a new document and keeps the original unless you enable overwrite.
sorinhostiuc/en2zotero.pain: Moving a manuscript from EndNote to Zotero would mean rebuilding every citation by hand. Plain-text citations without EndNote fields cannot be converted.

ouyangfeng2022/zotmd.does: Sends the PDF or Office file of selected items to MinerU for OCR and saves the result as a Markdown child attachment with images. Options cover model, language, formulas, tables and page ranges. Needs a MinerU API token.
ouyangfeng2022/zotmd.pain: Turns PDFs into editable Markdown inside the library for reading and later AI analysis. Files are uploaded to MinerU, and the token is stored in plain text.

zhanghm1995/zotarxiv.does: An arXiv helper: paste a link or ID above the item list to import with metadata and PDF. Adds columns for arXiv links, BibTeX, a one-line summary and an Unimportant tag, and fetches BibTeX from Google Scholar.
zhanghm1995/zotarxiv.pain: Collecting and triaging many arXiv preprints involves repeated copy-paste. This puts import, BibTeX and quick notes in one place. Mainly documented in Chinese.

alphainfix/alphainz.does: A research assistant that chats with your library using your own models and API keys. It builds a local semantic index of full texts and page images, answers cite the sentence, and Q&A can be kept in highlight comments. Optional Ollama and MCP server.
alphainfix/alphainz.pain: Zotero's search matches words only, not meaning. This finds passages and figures by meaning, with no account. Its front end is forked from Beaver.

cuny-ai-lab/zotero-autofill.does: Looks up missing metadata for books and articles from Open Library, Google Books and Crossref, then shows a review window before saving. It can also parse pasted bibliography text with AI (OpenRouter or CUNY AI Lab Gateway key) into items.
cuny-ai-lab/zotero-autofill.pain: Fixing incomplete records and typing references from a text list is slow. Changes are reviewed first, and a child note records the before and after values.

keiyuhin/zotero-obsidian-bridge.does: Starts from a Zotero item's right-click menu, passes its citation key to Obsidian, and saves an Obsidian Link in the Extra field. A paired Obsidian plugin calls Zotero Integration to create the literature note. Needs Better BibTeX.
keiyuhin/zotero-obsidian-bridge.pain: For people who keep one literature note per citation key in Obsidian, this links Zotero to the note and opens it in a new tab.

pandaaigc/zotero-duplicate-doctor.does: Audits duplicate groups and merges webpage records into journal articles that share the same DOI, moving merged items to the trash. It can also discard new imports with matching DOI or ISBN. Ambiguous cases are left for you.
pandaaigc/zotero-duplicate-doctor.pain: Bulk imports often leave a webpage copy beside the proper article, which Zotero's duplicate pane handles slowly. This cleans those conservatively.

cboulanger/zotero-language-categorizer.does: Detects the language of item titles and abstracts and fills the Language field with ISO 639-1 codes. It can also convert spelled-out names and three-letter codes. You review every change and press Apply.
cboulanger/zotero-language-categorizer.pain: Empty or inconsistent Language fields break citation styles that expect codes like de. This fixes a whole collection or library in one batch.

zpeters/zotero-random-read.does: Picks a random unread item from My Library with a dice button or Tools menu entry, files it in a ~In Progress~ collection, marks it To Read and selects it. You need a collection with exactly that name.
zpeters/zotero-random-read.pain: A library grows faster than you read it, and choosing the next paper is its own hurdle. This chooses for you.

erickpeirson/papermachines.does: Analyses and visualises a document collection for the digital humanities. It offers word clouds, phrase nets, maps of places mentioned, topic modelling and DBpedia annotation. Needs Java and an old Zotero.
erickpeirson/papermachines.pain: Lets historians and other researchers explore a large corpus without programming skills or heavy computing. Legacy plugin.

golden-pigeon/zotero-pdf-translate-plus-.does: A fork of Translate for Zotero that translates selected text with 20+ services such as DeepL, OpenAI and Google. It adds maths rendering in the reader popup, with streaming updates and better line breaks.
golden-pigeon/zotero-pdf-translate-plus-.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate, kept separately because the maths-rendering change was not merged upstream. Formulas appear correctly in translations.

haiyankong/zotero-md-note.does: Creates one local Markdown file per selected item from Tools > Create Markdown Note, named by year, first author and title. The note links back to the Zotero item and PDF, with Highlights and Notes headings.
haiyankong/zotero-md-note.pain: For people who keep one note file per paper outside Zotero, this creates them consistently. Existing files are never overwritten.

diraw/zotero-split-theme.does: Sets light or dark appearance separately for Zotero's main interface and for each PDF reader area. The areas are the top bar, left pane, reading area and right pane, each following Zotero, light or dark.
diraw/zotero-split-theme.pain: Zotero applies one theme everywhere. This allows a dark interface with a light reading page, or other mixes, which is common for long reading.

aguvener/ztldr.does: Fetches Semantic Scholar TL;DR summaries for items by DOI, falling back to title, and shows them in an item pane section. They are stored in the Extra field so they sync. Right-click and Tools menu actions refresh or clear them.
aguvener/ztldr.pain: Gives a one-sentence summary of each paper for triage without reading the abstract. Papers missing from Semantic Scholar get none.

rnicrosoft-studio/zot-plus-plus.does: Adds a ZotPP tags column with configurable emoji, and a right-click menu to apply tags such as star ratings, read or unread, flags and feelings. Also opens an item's attachment with a method other than the default.
rnicrosoft-studio/zot-plus-plus.pain: Zotero has no built-in way to rate or mark items visually in the list. This adds quick tag-based rating and status marks. Zotero 8 and 9.

brant-ruan/zotero-kentridge.does: Fetches bibliographic metadata by title from DBLP and applies it to selected items, with per-item candidate choice. You can replace existing metadata or only fill empty fields. Further providers are planned.
brant-ruan/zotero-kentridge.pain: Zotero's coverage of computer science conferences, such as USENIX venues, is patchy. This fills the gap from DBLP. Zotero 8 and 9.

tsmdt/zotero-tagwiz.does: Bulk-edits tags from the Tools menu or a collection's right-click menu. It changes case style, renames, merges, removes and finds duplicates at set strictness levels, with a preview, history and undo.
tsmdt/zotero-tagwiz.pain: Libraries accumulate tags like machine learning, Machine Learning and machine-learning. This tidies them in one pass. Every change applies library-wide.

kravornn/zotero-easygpt.does: Adds an AI side panel to the PDF reader for questions, summaries and Chinese-English translation. It also offers multi-turn chat, including across up to 10 selected papers. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service.
kravornn/zotero-easygpt.pain: Lets you question papers in Zotero with OpenAI, DeepSeek or similar, using different models for single and multiple papers to control cost.

hao-ianwy/zotero-retainpdf-plugin.does: Translates a paper's PDF from the right-click menu while keeping formulas and layout, then attaches translated-only and bilingual PDFs to the item. Scanned PDFs go through OCR. Needs its own Docker server and a model key. Documented in Chinese.
hao-ianwy/zotero-retainpdf-plugin.pain: Translation tools often break formulas and columns. This restores the layout and returns the files to the item without manual steps.

shamanstone/zotero_snapshot_reviver.does: Turns a webpage item or snapshot into a Journal Article using Crossref, with PubMed as fallback. It checks the title match and asks you to confirm first. It fills only empty fields unless overwrite is on.
shamanstone/zotero_snapshot_reviver.pain: Saving an article page often yields a Web Page item with poor metadata. This converts it into a proper article record.

sorinhostiuc/mc2zotero.does: Converts Mendeley Cite citations in a Word .docx into Zotero citations, matching by DOI and title and importing missing items through Crossref. It writes a separate document and supports field codes, bookmarks and ODF Reference Marks.
sorinhostiuc/mc2zotero.pain: Migrating a manuscript from Mendeley to Zotero would mean redoing each citation by hand.

shzhao27208/zotagent.does: Connects Codex CLI, Claude Code and OpenCode to the Zotero reader. Ask about a selection, full text or screenshot, compare papers, and archive each answer as a child note. Each agent needs its own installation and login.
shzhao27208/zotagent.pain: Lets you use agents already on your computer while reading, and keeps the discussion as notes. Supports Windows and WSL side by side.

waelitani/crop-to-margin.does: Adds a PDF reader toolbar button that measures where a document's text sits and crops the white margins, so the text fills the pane. It refits when sidebars or panes change and remembers each document.
waelitani/crop-to-margin.pain: Books are typeset for paper, and fit-to-width keeps their wide margins on screen. Cropping makes the type larger without changing zoom by hand.

anoopkcn/reference-map.does: Lets approved websites, such as a Reference Map web app, search your Zotero library and save items into it. Each site must be allowed in a Zotero dialog. The web app draws citation maps from Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex.
anoopkcn/reference-map.pain: Connects an in-browser citation exploration tool to your library, so you can add papers from a map straight into Zotero.

vincent929-cyber/survey-papers-to-zotero.does: A companion that attaches already-downloaded, validated local PDFs to existing items through a local endpoint, and audits which items lack a PDF. It pairs with a Codex skill and does not bypass paywalls. Documented in Chinese.
vincent929-cyber/survey-papers-to-zotero.pain: Supports a workflow where an agent finds papers by conference and topic, imports them, and then attaches legally obtained PDFs automatically.

sciencelivehub/zotero-nanopub-plugin.does: Creates, signs with your ORCID and publishes nanopublications from Zotero items using forms in a tab, with CiTO, AIDA and Rosetta templates. It also finds related nanopublications and attaches a note.
sciencelivehub/zotero-nanopub-plugin.pain: For researchers who publish machine-readable claims, this removes the need for external tools like Nanodash. Needs an ORCID account.

charlesapetersen/zotero-pdf-transfer.does: Sends the PDF attachments of selected items to a working folder, then returns the edited ones to Zotero in place. Each copy is hash-verified, and a dry-run preview and report show what a return would change.
charlesapetersen/zotero-pdf-transfer.pain: Editing a PDF outside Zotero normally means re-attaching it and losing the item key, tags or notes. This swaps the file in place so citations and links keep working.

hiyvri/pdf-fetcher.does: Fetches full-text PDFs through the JLSS (聚联医疗) document delivery service and attaches them to the selected item. A right-click command submits the query using DOI, PMID, title or URL, and tags items still being searched for by hand.
hiyvri/pdf-fetcher.pain: For researchers with an institutional JLSS account who otherwise request papers on the website and attach them by hand. You paste in your own website token, and the interface is in Chinese.

agents365-ai/zotero-cli-ai.does: Exposes Find Full Text, attachment renaming and local file import over Zotero's local HTTP server for the companion zot command-line tool. The zot CLI reads your library, searches it, and lets AI agents drive Zotero.
agents365-ai/zotero-cli-ai.pain: Lets Claude Code or another AI agent work with your library from a terminal, with no key needed for reads. Writes use the Zotero Web API and need a key.

weicheng14159/zotero-local-pdf-manager.does: Removes the local PDF copies of selected items, or of the whole library, while keeping the Zotero records and metadata. A completion dialog reports the disk space freed, and one failing item does not stop the batch.
weicheng14159/zotero-local-pdf-manager.pain: Large PDF collections fill your disk. This reclaims the space and lets Zotero's sync re-download files on demand, which helps before moving to Zotero cloud sync.

lineex/zotero-webai.does: Embeds DeepSeek Web, Z.ai Web and ChatGPT Web in a sidebar beside the library or PDF reader. Slash commands attach the PDF, run a web search or call local zotero-mcp tools, and you can save custom skills.
lineex/zotero-webai.pain: Lets you use those web chat services on the paper you are reading without an API key, signing in inside the sidebar instead of copying text out of Zotero.

fenzirong/zotero-zh-info.does: Adds Chinese title and Chinese abstract fields to the item pane and fills them in automatically by translation. Services are MyMemory, DeepL, Google or any OpenAI-compatible model, and results are stored in the Extra field.
fenzirong/zotero-zh-info.pain: For readers of English papers who want a Chinese title and abstract beside each item. Translations sync with the library, and bulk translation is available from the right-click menu.

nbtkmy/zoteroaddonforubb1.does: Checks whether the UB-UBB1 library at the University of Zurich holds selected books, by searching Alma through its SRU interface using the ISBN. The result goes into the Abstract field, and tags record the holding status.
nbtkmy/zoteroaddonforubb1.pain: Helps librarians and researchers in the Swiss SLSP network see which books a library already owns while building a collection. It is a modified Swissbib add-on and works only for items with a valid ISBN.

ginixstudy/zotero-browser.does: A small web browser inside Zotero's item pane, with an address bar, back, forward and reload buttons. You can drag its bottom edge to resize it.
ginixstudy/zotero-browser.pain: Lets you look something up online without leaving Zotero for another window. It has been tested only on Zotero 9.0.6.

windfollowingheart/deepseek-for-zotero.does: A chat panel for talking to DeepSeek about your PDFs, with file attachments, Markdown rendering, streaming replies and chat history. It needs a separate Windows backend program and a browser extension to connect.
windfollowingheart/deepseek-for-zotero.pain: Gives free access to DeepSeek from inside Zotero, using the web service rather than a paid API. At present it supports Windows only.

linxbxxh/retainpdf-zotero-plugin.does: Sends newly added PDFs to the RetainPDF desktop app's local service and attaches the Chinese translation to the item. It produces a translated PDF and an optional side-by-side English and Chinese version.
linxbxxh/retainpdf-zotero-plugin.pain: For readers who want a layout-preserving Chinese translation of each paper without exporting files by hand. You need RetainPDF installed with your own OCR token and model key.

panhaoyu/zotero-title.does: Shows translations of titles in the title column of the item list. It also lets you set a star rating from zero to five with the keyboard shortcuts Alt+Shift+0 to 5.
panhaoyu/zotero-title.pain: Helps you scan a library of foreign-language papers by their translated titles and rank items quickly. The author describes it as a personal tool shared for others to try.

zonezzc/zotero-xmnote.does: Sends Zotero items, notes and PDF annotations to the XMnote (纸间书摘) reading app's API import list. You can export everything, a selection or a collection, with options for reading position and estimated reading time.
zonezzc/zotero-xmnote.pain: For readers who keep books in Zotero and annotate in XMnote. Export is one way, and you must confirm each import inside the app.

gchapron/zoterothumblibrary.does: Replaces the library table with a grid of PDF thumbnails, EPUB covers and image previews. A toolbar button switches back to the list. It supports drag-and-drop tagging, keyboard selection and file import.
gchapron/zoterothumblibrary.pain: For people who recognise papers and books by how they look more than by a row of text. It is built for macOS and works with Zotero 9 and 10.

xiaoxuanli-a/zotero_agent_reader_plugin.does: A chat panel in the item pane that asks questions about the open paper using a local Codex or Claude Code command-line tool. Answers stream with Markdown and maths, and clickable page citations jump the reader to the passage.
xiaoxuanli-a/zotero_agent_reader_plugin.pain: Lets you question a paper with an AI agent you already use, with no API key to paste. You need Codex or Claude Code signed in, and poppler installed.

camiska/zotero-batchimport.does: Imports all the PDFs, EPUBs, HTML or other supported files from a folder into a new collection, optionally including subfolders as subcollections. It can trigger metadata retrieval and tag duplicates with batchimportdupe.
camiska/zotero-batchimport.pain: A replacement for the older folder import add-on for people with research files sitting in local folders. It runs on Zotero 7 and 8.

wakatime/zotero-wakatime.does: Sends time-tracking heartbeats to WakaTime while you read PDFs and EPUBs and add or annotate items, so your research time shows on your WakaTime dashboard. It needs your WakaTime API key and the wakatime-cli binary.
wakatime/zotero-wakatime.pain: For people who already track their coding time in WakaTime and want reading and writing time counted too. The plugin is described as early beta.

5ht2c/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up DOIs for selected items through the CrossRef API and fetches shortDOI names. It verifies stored DOIs, marks invalid ones, and strips prefixes such as doi: or publisher URLs from the DOI field.
5ht2c/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Keeps DOI fields clean and valid, and gives short DOIs that are easier to cite. Without it you check and tidy each DOI by hand.

retorquere/zotero-uid-column.does: Adds a column to the item list that shows each item's unique ID and its select link.
retorquere/zotero-uid-column.pain: For people who need to see or copy an item's identifier directly in the list. It is a Zotero 6 plugin.

zotero-cat/zotero-cat.does: An AI assistant in the item pane that chats about the selected item, summarises, critiques and explains methods, and can use selected PDF text. It can propose PDF annotations for you to review before Zotero writes them.
zotero-cat/zotero-cat.pain: Lets you discuss papers with the model provider of your choice, without a fixed vendor. You supply an OpenAI-compatible API address and key, and chat content goes to that provider.

myang-print/zotero-codex-bridge.does: A local, authenticated bridge on your own machine that lets the Codex AI agent import papers, build and merge collections, apply tags and attach PDFs. A companion Codex skill checks each plan and asks for confirmation before writing.
myang-print/zotero-codex-bridge.pain: Zotero's local API can read but not write, and the Web API needs cloud credentials. This lets an agent make safe writes without a Web API key. It is pre-1.0, so back up your data.

spgsu/zotero-focus-reader.does: Adds a locked single-page reading mode to Zotero's PDF reader. A review mode shows annotation comments as margin balloons with a map of every annotation, and Zotero 10's Reading Mode gets pages too.
spgsu/zotero-focus-reader.pain: Continuous scrolling makes dense papers harder to read than print. This restores page boundaries and shows comments beside the text. It relies on Zotero internals and was tested only on Windows.

fkallmer/zotero-orbit.does: Shows citation counts from five sources side by side, and graphs what a paper cites and what cites it. The sources are Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, INSPIRE and Google Scholar, in a column and an item pane section.
fkallmer/zotero-orbit.pain: Sources disagree about how often a paper is cited, and this shows them side by side with context such as references, open-access status and retractions. It needs Zotero 10 and is forked from Citation Tally.

shadww/zotero-split-view-reader.does: Shows two PDFs, or the same PDF twice, side by side in one reader tab. Set one pane as primary and the other follows its scrolling and zoom; clear the primary and each pane moves on its own.
shadww/zotero-split-view-reader.pain: Comparing two papers, or two places in one paper, otherwise means juggling tabs or windows. A fork of zerolfl/zotero-split-view-reader; its README doesn't say what it changes.

moonweave-research/zotero-vocab-flow.does: Turns PDF underlines into a note of candidate vocabulary terms to review, then saves the approved ones into a vocabulary note with Korean meanings. Optional translation aids use Google, OpenAI-compatible, Gemini or Claude services.
moonweave-research/zotero-vocab-flow.pain: Reading underlines mix key sentences with words to learn. The review step keeps vocabulary separate from reading marks, for learners reading papers in a second language.

janbaykara/zotero-youtube-transcripts.does: Fetches the captions of a YouTube item and stores them as an HTML attachment with clickable timestamps that you can open and annotate in Zotero's reader. You can also play the video with a follow-along transcript.
janbaykara/zotero-youtube-transcripts.pain: Lets you highlight and note spoken content from videos the way you do for web snapshots. You can choose the caption language, and YouTube sometimes blocks requests from VPNs.

informalgit/zotero-collection-nav.does: Shows the selected collection's full path as a clickable breadcrumb above the collections pane. Hovering any collection gives a tooltip with its full path. Group libraries show their name, and My Library is omitted.
informalgit/zotero-collection-nav.pain: In deeply nested collections it is easy to lose track of which level you are on and which collection is the parent. The interface is in Chinese.

weilr/zotero-scholium.does: Lets Claude Code, Codex or similar agents write highlights with comments, margin notes and reading notes into Zotero as native, editable annotations. On Zotero 10 it uses the official local API; Zotero 7 to 9 use a bundled bridge.
weilr/zotero-scholium.pain: Gets the results of an AI reading pass into the Zotero reader as normal annotations rather than loose text. It needs Python with PyMuPDF and an agent. It is alpha, and the PDF file is never changed.

wazeruan/zotero-translate-plugin.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader when you press a shortcut (Ctrl+T or Cmd+T) and shows the result in a draggable panel. It works with local Ollama, OpenAI-compatible APIs, DeepL and LibreTranslate.
wazeruan/zotero-translate-plugin.pain: Saves copying text into a translation site. You can point it at a local model or a hosted service, which needs your own key. It targets Zotero 7.

bapungiri/litmatrix.does: Builds a literature-review matrix: papers as rows, your highlight-colour meanings as columns. A second table lists every annotation to filter, tag, recolour and edit. It also keeps your own notes per paper.
bapungiri/litmatrix.pain: Zotero has no overview of what you have highlighted as questions, methods or results across many papers. This puts them side by side and exports Markdown notes. It was previously called Zotero Annotable.

sorinhostiuc/pp2zotero.does: Converts live Paperpile citations in a Word document into editable Zotero citations and rebuilds the bibliography. It matches references by DOI and title, can fetch missing ones from Crossref, and saves a separate converted file.
sorinhostiuc/pp2zotero.pain: For researchers moving from Paperpile to Zotero who would otherwise retype the citations in an existing manuscript. The original file is kept, and it supports Zotero 7 to 9.

zenanh/zotero-babeldoc.does: Translates a PDF attachment into Chinese with BabelDOC and saves the result as a child attachment, either Chinese only or original and Chinese side by side. It installs its own isolated BabelDOC environment.
zenanh/zotero-babeldoc.pain: Gives layout-preserving PDF translation from inside Zotero without touching the original file. You supply an OpenAI-compatible API address, key and model, and it needs Zotero 10.

iscopyman/zotero-bilingual-reader.does: Opens an English paper as a sentence-aligned bilingual page in Chinese and English, with side by side, stacked and single-language views. Translation uses an OpenAI-compatible API or a local agent command line, and MinerU is optional for formulas.
iscopyman/zotero-bilingual-reader.pain: Reading papers in a second language is slow with copy and paste. This keeps both languages aligned and links highlights to the PDF as Zotero annotations. It needs Zotero 10.

cczmd/zotero-deselect.does: Lets you click empty space in the item list to clear the selection, as in Finder or Windows File Explorer. Clicking blank space in the collections pane hides the collection highlight while the items stay shown.
cczmd/zotero-deselect.pain: Zotero keeps something selected after you click away, unlike most desktop file managers. Multi-select with Cmd, Ctrl and Shift is unchanged. Tested on Zotero 10 on macOS.

ching-chiang/zotero-elsevier-fulltext.does: Downloads PDFs you are entitled to from Elsevier's official Article Retrieval API and attaches them to items with a DOI. It checks the file is a real PDF and rejects first-page previews returned when you lack access.
ching-chiang/zotero-elsevier-fulltext.pain: Saves manual downloads from ScienceDirect for people with institutional access. You need your own Elsevier API key, and it does not get around paywalls.

wdoo02/zotero-gpt.does: A floating GPT chat window that asks about the open PDF or selected text, summarises items and searches your library. Command tags save prompts as one-click buttons. It needs an OpenAI API key.
wdoo02/zotero-gpt.pain: A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-gpt; its README doesn't say what it changes.

lixvqing01/zotero-literature-library.does: Converts PDFs to Markdown with MinerU and indexes them with embeddings. It offers layered search through a management window and an MCP server for AI agents. Embeddings run locally or through an API.
lixvqing01/zotero-literature-library.pain: For researchers who want agents to find evidence across their library by abstract first and full text second. You need a MinerU key.

groele/zotero-viewflow.does: Previews formatted references and in-text citations in the item pane. It uses your installed citation styles or Quick Copy settings, with buttons to copy them as plain or rich text.
groele/zotero-viewflow.pain: A fork of dcartertod/zotero-plugins. It lets you check how a citation will look while reading, without opening a word processor.

woniuzfb/zotero-voice-edge-plugin.does: Reads PDFs and EPUBs aloud in the reader. It uses a local Edge-TTS server through an OpenAI-compatible speech endpoint, and falls back to the browser's voices if none is running. It has speed and voice choices.
woniuzfb/zotero-voice-edge-plugin.pain: Lets you listen to papers instead of reading them. The server is optional, and the interface is in Chinese.

shengjiejin/pdftrim-for-llm.does: Detects where the references and appendix start in a PDF, lets you adjust the page numbers, and exports a trimmed PDF attached to the same item. The original PDF is untouched, and a button deletes the generated files.
shengjiejin/pdftrim-for-llm.pain: Sending a whole paper to an LLM wastes context on references and appendices. This cuts them off without manual exporting. Detection is a guess, so check the pages.

retorquere/zotero-erdos.does: Finds the shortest chain of co-authorship between given authors in your library.
retorquere/zotero-erdos.pain: For people curious how closely two authors are connected, in the manner of Erdos numbers. It is a Zotero 6 plugin.

shiyangzheng/zometaker.does: Cleans up items imported by the Zotero Connector. It checks metadata against CrossRef, OpenAlex and DataCite by DOI, normalises authors, journals, pages and DOIs to APA 7, and fills empty fields.
shiyangzheng/zometaker.pain: Connector imports arrive with inconsistent author names, capitalisation, DOI formats and missing volumes or pages. This fixes them in one step. It needs no API keys.

retorquere/zotero-cite-columns.does: Adds item list columns rendered from a CSL style. Each macro in a special style file you create becomes a column in the middle pane.
retorquere/zotero-cite-columns.pain: For people who want columns Zotero does not offer, such as formatted pieces of a citation. It needs a hand-built CSL style file and runs on Zotero 6.

edouardarmit/zotero-hover-abstract.does: Adds the abstract of the cited work to Zotero's citation hover popup in the PDF reader. It checks your library first, and can optionally fall back to Crossref and Semantic Scholar.
edouardarmit/zotero-hover-abstract.pain: Lets you judge a citation without leaving the paper. Online lookups are off by default, and a Semantic Scholar API key avoids rate limits.

musstafasnn/zotero-latin.does: Transliterates Arabic-script fields of selected items into Latin letters in DIA style. It follows ISNAD 2, and keeps the Arabic original in a note. It also turns Türâs book pages into complete book records.
musstafasnn/zotero-latin.pain: For Turkish-language Islamic studies, where Arabic titles and authors must be romanised for citations. It uses an AI service of your choice with your key, such as Gemini, OpenAI or a local Ollama. The interface is in Turkish.

reginalluna/zotero-reading-tracker.does: Adds a Reading Status column and a right-click menu to mark items To Read, Reading or Done. It can also record the current PDF page in the Extra field.
reginalluna/zotero-reading-tracker.pain: Gives Zotero a simple reading list and progress record. Status is stored as tags and progress as text in Extra, so both sync with your library.

el0808/zotfile-lite.does: Renames attachment files from item metadata using a rule such as author, year and title, and can move them into a folder you choose with rule-based subfolders. A preview shows the name for the selected item.
el0808/zotfile-lite.pain: A lighter ZotFile-style attachment manager for Zotero 7 to 10. It keeps files readable and in a synced folder instead of Zotero's key-named storage.

sorinhostiuc/zotdupe.does: Finds likely duplicates that exact matching misses, such as preprints and published versions, translations, different item types and incomplete records. You review each group, choose the master item and preview the merge.
sorinhostiuc/zotdupe.pain: Zotero's built-in duplicate detection misses records that differ in type or metadata. This catches them across the whole library or a collection, with strict, balanced or relaxed sensitivity.

benshen94/zotero-ask.does: A sidebar in the PDF reader for asking questions about the paper. It sends the extracted text, your selected passage and up to eight relevant page images to the Codex CLI on your computer, and keeps a chat per PDF.
benshen94/zotero-ask.pain: Lets you question papers, including figures and tables, using your signed-in Codex (ChatGPT) account with no API key. It is verified only on macOS with Zotero 9.

catcodeme/zotero-global-number.does: Gives each regular item in My Library a global, increasing number such as 00001, shown in an optional column. You set the width from 1 to 12 digits and can number all unnumbered items on demand.
catcodeme/zotero-global-number.pain: Gives every item a stable reference number that survives moving computers. The number is stored in the synced Extra field.

lojeunhou/zotero-notes-sync-zotero-plugi.does: Exports Zotero notes to Markdown files, one per note, with frontmatter for the Zotero key, parent item, authors, year, tags and a zotero:// link. It also writes an index file, and you choose the output folder.
lojeunhou/zotero-notes-sync-zotero-plugi.pain: For people who keep an Obsidian vault or other local knowledge base and want their Zotero notes there. It is one way and does not sync attachments.

ptigas/zotion.does: Sends notes on your papers from Zotero into a Notion database. You create a Notion integration, share a database template with it, and enter the secret key and database ID in the plugin's preferences.
ptigas/zotion.pain: People who keep their reading notes in Notion otherwise copy paper details across by hand.

retorquere/zotero-clear-journal-abbrev.does: Clears the journal abbreviation field on the items you have selected.
retorquere/zotero-clear-journal-abbrev.pain: Handy when imported or auto-filled abbreviations are wrong or unwanted and you would rather not blank the field item by item.

zhiborao/zotero-meta-refresh.does: Batch-refreshes item metadata from CrossRef, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and DBLP, showing a preview of old and new values to approve before anything is written. Works on selected items, a collection or the whole library.
zhiborao/zotero-meta-refresh.pain: Library metadata goes stale or stays incomplete, for example preprints that were later published. A field whitelist, preprint upgrade and an undo backup kept in Extra make bulk fixes safer. Needs Zotero 10; a Semantic Scholar key is optional.

kvarnelis/zotero-quiet-theme.does: Changes Zotero's colours, typography and spacing through a View menu. Choose Automatic, Light or Dark for the native appearance and switch an optional userChrome overlay on or off.
kvarnelis/zotero-quiet-theme.pain: For people who find stock Zotero visually busy. It targets macOS with Zotero 9 and 10, and the overlay may need adjusting after Zotero updates.

laiduo12345/arxiv_marker_ccf2026.does: Finds the published conference or journal version of arXiv preprints, checks the evidence, and lets you review proposed changes before writing them. Adds Venue and CCF 2026 ranking columns to the item list.
laiduo12345/arxiv_marker_ccf2026.pain: arXiv items keep preprint metadata long after publication, and CCF ranks need a manual lookup. It shows both in the list and saves an undo snapshot. Optional keys for Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and Brave Search add sources; written for Zotero 9 and 10.

thiagoelbert/collection-explorer-for-zot.does: Shows subcollections as folder-like rows at the top of the items list, like a file explorer. An optional navigation bar adds back, forward and up buttons, breadcrumbs and path editing.
thiagoelbert/collection-explorer-for-zot.pain: Zotero's tree makes deep collection hierarchies slow to move through. Folder rows let you click down into a collection from the items pane.

wu-lipeng/lexinote.does: Select a word in Zotero's PDF reader to see a definition popup, then save it to a vocabulary note under that item. Uses Baidu dictionary or translation APIs, or your own lookup service, with your own keys.
wu-lipeng/lexinote.pain: Readers of English papers who look up unfamiliar words otherwise lose them in a browser tab. This collects words with their sentences and page links in one note per paper. Mainly aimed at Chinese-speaking readers.

seanlawsonphd/zotero-add-missing-snapsho.does: Saves page snapshots for selected items that have a URL but no snapshot. A second command makes a clean reader-view copy of a snapshot as its own attachment.
seanlawsonphd/zotero-add-missing-snapsho.pain: Saving several items at once from the Zotero Connector skips snapshots, so these items end up with only a link. This backfills them afterwards and offers a clutter-free copy for reading.

sprooc/zotero-csvenue.does: Adds Venue and CCF columns to the item list, showing standard conference abbreviations and colour-coded CCF ranks A, B or C for computer science papers. Unrecognised papers can be looked up on DBLP.
sprooc/zotero-csvenue.pain: Computer science researchers judge papers by venue and CCF rank, which stock Zotero does not show. A built-in list of about 160 conferences matches most papers; you can also write a venue in the Extra field.

horbin-magician/zotero-ninja.does: A small toolbox that looks up the citation count of an item automatically and lets you give papers a rating. More features are planned.
horbin-magician/zotero-ninja.pain: Gives a quick view of how often a paper is cited and a way to record your own judgement. Early stage, with a short feature list.

observagp/adhd-lens.does: Draws a movable, resizable, translucent reading guide over the PDF reader to help you keep your place. It has colour presets, one- and two-column layout presets, keyboard shortcuts and per-PDF memory of its position.
observagp/adhd-lens.pain: Dense academic PDFs with small type and two columns are tiring to track, especially with ADHD or visual tracking fatigue. Described by its author as an experimental prototype for Zotero 9.

jpwang-ovo/openreview-fetcher.does: Fetches peer reviews, author responses and discussion comments from OpenReview for papers whose URL or DOI points there. Saves them as an HTML note or a Markdown attachment, with optional review statistics.
jpwang-ovo/openreview-fetcher.pain: Reading the reviews of a conference paper means leaving Zotero for the OpenReview page. This stores them with the item and handles several papers in one go.

shi-keke/vocab-for-zotero.does: Select an English word or phrase in the reader's text menu to add it to a vocabulary notebook with a Chinese definition, its source and the original selection. Reviews use spaced repetition, with statistics and CSV export.
shi-keke/vocab-for-zotero.pain: Helps Chinese-speaking readers learn vocabulary from the papers they read, and a click on the source jumps back to the passage. Definitions come from MyMemory, which receives only the selected words.

panwanke/zotero-attanger.does: Manages attachments: set a source folder and attachment type, and file PDFs into a folder tree using Zotero's renaming rules. Its documentation is in Chinese.
panwanke/zotero-attanger.pain: Keeps PDFs in readable, syncable folders instead of Zotero's opaque storage. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger; its README doesn't say what it changes.

crazyhalfday/ima-zotero-sync.does: Uploads the local attachments of selected items to a Tencent IMA knowledge base, in a chosen folder, from the right-click or Tools menu. A console window shows statistics and recent activity, and a dry run previews the sync.
crazyhalfday/ima-zotero-sync.pain: Lets people who use IMA as an AI knowledge base feed it from Zotero instead of uploading files by hand. It skips duplicates and tags synced items. Needs your own IMA Client ID and API key.

katayamalab/z-permalink.does: Adds a right-click command that copies a web link to an item or collection in a group library to the clipboard.
katayamalab/z-permalink.pain: Makes it easy to point colleagues to a specific item or collection in a shared group library. It does not work for items in your personal library.

yufeixia/zotero-claude-code.does: A chat in the item pane, or its own window, for talking to Claude about the paper you are reading. It runs the Claude Code CLI already on your computer, so you need it installed and signed in to a Claude account.
yufeixia/zotero-claude-code.pain: Lets you ask about a paper without copying text out of Zotero. Claude can read the PDF at your page, search your library, and save answers as notes. By default it can only read.

ossifiedsardine/zotero-feed-sort.does: Adds normal clickable column sorting to Zotero's RSS feed views, with newest first as the default.
ossifiedsardine/zotero-feed-sort.pain: Zotero's feed setting does not sort by publication date, so a long feed is hard to scan. This brings the usual column sorting to feeds. Needs Zotero 10.

zxing258974/zotero-knode-plugin.does: Syncs selected Zotero journal articles to the Knode personal knowledge center from a right-click command. You enter your Knode domain and API key in the preferences. Its instructions are in Chinese.
zxing258974/zotero-knode-plugin.pain: For Knode users who want to analyse and read their Zotero articles with its AI features without uploading each one again.

pcf566/zotero-kokoro-read-aloud-bridge.does: Routes Zotero 10's Read Aloud voices named Kokoro to a text-to-speech server running on your own computer. Text for those voices goes only to a local loopback address, and other voices behave as before.
pcf566/zotero-kokoro-read-aloud-bridge.pain: Read Aloud normally relies on Zotero's paid voices. This reads papers aloud with a local Kokoro model instead. You must run a compatible Kokoro server yourself.

josesiqueira/zotero-meta-data-repair.does: Right-click items to repair metadata from DOI, PMID, arXiv or ISBN lookups, with a guarded fuzzy title search as fallback. You approve each field in a diff, and nothing is blanked. A settings pane reports which core fields are missing.
josesiqueira/zotero-meta-data-repair.pain: Imported items often lack authors, dates, publishers or DOIs. This fills them while asking before any overwrite. It uses Crossref, and OpenAlex only if you add a free key.

shiwenber/zotero-paper-copilot.does: An AI chat sidebar for reading papers, using your own OpenAI, Claude or Gemini API key. The assistant can read PDF text, search your library, add notes and tags, create highlights, and run audit, auto-tag and metadata-sync actions.
shiwenber/zotero-paper-copilot.pain: Aims to give Zotero a Moonlight-style research assistant so you can question papers without leaving the reader.

luluyang928/zotero-paper-guide.does: Opens a window that sends the current PDF's extracted text to OpenAI or DeepSeek and answers your list of questions as a paper guide. Quotes are checked against the PDF pages and exported as a Markdown note, for example into Obsidian.
luluyang928/zotero-paper-guide.pain: Gives structured, checkable reading summaries from your own questions. You need your own API key and pay the provider, and scanned PDFs need OCR first. The interface is in Chinese.

wuguangheng/zotero-ragflow.does: Uploads a collection's attachments to a RAGFlow service to build a knowledge base, then answers questions about your papers with cited sources. Needs a RAGFlow API key and URL; the interface is in Chinese.
wuguangheng/zotero-ragflow.pain: For researchers who run RAGFlow, locally or hosted, and want question answering over their own literature without uploading files by hand.

aigraythorn/zoterosyncassistant.does: Syncs Zotero attachment files with Baidu Netdisk, with upload, download, preview, conflict checks and automatic sync. Needs a plugin account and Baidu authorisation; a paid licence follows a 3-day trial.
aigraythorn/zoterosyncassistant.pain: Gives Zotero users in China a way to sync attachments without Zotero Storage or WebDAV. Zotero's own sync still handles metadata. Its documentation is in Chinese.

wangzfof/gb-t-7714-2025-helper.does: Tidies references for the Chinese standard GB/T 7714-2025: normalises pinyin author names and marks online resources with Medium: OL, after a preview. Includes a matching CSL style.
