wangzfof/gb-t-7714-2025-helper.pain: Chinese-standard bibliographies need this fiddly clean-up, which is slow by hand across many items. It works offline, saves a snapshot before changes and can undo batches.

lyn6969/mineru-parse.does: Converts PDF attachments into structured Zotero notes using the MinerU cloud service, extracting text, formulas, tables and images. Can parse automatically, in batches, and send the result to an LLM for analysis.
lyn6969/mineru-parse.pain: Lets you read and search a paper's content, including equations and tables, as a note. Needs a MinerU API token and the Better Notes plugin; AI analysis needs an LLM key.

keshen-zhou/paperrouter.does: Right-click a paper to get a ranked list of the collections it probably belongs to, each with a confidence score, then pick the ones to file it in. Ranks by embedding similarity or an LLM, and learns from rejected suggestions.
keshen-zhou/paperrouter.pain: Filing each new PDF into the right collection is slow in a large library. Needs an API key for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Cohere or a compatible endpoint.

moonbowterfly/pop-fish.does: Adds item list columns for impact factor, JCR quartile and Chinese Academy of Sciences division, and flags journals on warning or predatory lists. Data comes from the Wenxian Paopao (BytesLink) journal API.
moonbowterfly/pop-fish.pain: Shows journal quality and risk next to each paper, mainly for Chinese-language research. It needs an API key from that service, and queries are billed by request, so it asks before bulk lookups.

huangyxi/zotero-alt-reader.does: Adds a right-click command to open PDFs in the other reader: the system viewer when Zotero is your default, or Zotero's reader when the system viewer is.
huangyxi/zotero-alt-reader.pain: Useful when you sometimes prefer another PDF app for a file but keep your library in Zotero. Needs Zotero 10.

josesiqueira/zotero-bibliometero.does: Adds an Insights panel with six interactive views of your library, including co-authorship networks, publications per year and top sources. Exports PNG or SVG.
josesiqueira/zotero-bibliometero.pain: Shows which groups, journals and years dominate your reading. Clicking a bar, slice or author selects those items. It runs inside Zotero with no account.

lanting-0119/zotero-bilingual-pdf.does: Batch-translates English papers into side-by-side English and Chinese PDFs and saves them as child attachments. It uses Doc2X for OCR and layout and DeepSeek for translation, through a local Python service. macOS only.
lanting-0119/zotero-bilingual-pdf.pain: Gives Chinese-speaking researchers a readable parallel copy that keeps figures, formulas and tables. You need your own Doc2X and DeepSeek keys and pay for the usage; it targets Zotero 9.

royenheart/zotero-proxy-gui.does: A settings interface for Zotero's network proxy. Save several HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5 presets, then switch or turn them off with one click or from a toolbar button.
royenheart/zotero-proxy-gui.pain: Changing proxies in Zotero otherwise means editing Firefox preferences by hand. Useful if you move between networks that need different proxies.

jimcsuen/zotero-reference-graph.does: Builds a local citation graph of the papers in your library, collection or visible list, shown in an embedded view in the main window. Menu buttons build the cache and open the graph.
jimcsuen/zotero-reference-graph.pain: Shows how the papers you collected cite one another. A modified version of Thrillcrazyer's plugin with the graph embedded in the main window.

kl3574/deep-research.does: A Zotero-side helper for Codex agent skills that run deep research and file the results in Zotero. It resolves exact collections and applies reviewed manifests as local transactions with limits on what they may do.
kl3574/deep-research.pain: For people who let AI agents add and correct library records and want those writes reviewed and constrained. Its documentation mainly describes the agent skills, not the plugin.

core-hn/readeck2zotero.does: Imports highlights and annotations from your Readeck server into a Zotero item, from a right-click command. Configure your Readeck server URL and API token under Tools.
core-hn/readeck2zotero.pain: Readeck users who read articles there otherwise copy highlights into Zotero by hand.

seanlawsonphd/readwise2zotero.does: Imports your Readwise library, including Reader documents, Kindle books, podcasts and tweets, into a Zotero collection with formatted highlight notes. Syncs incrementally and can enrich metadata.
seanlawsonphd/readwise2zotero.pain: Brings reading highlights from Readwise into your library without duplicates or overwriting your edits. Needs a Readwise token; enrichment can use Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or a local model.

mengqi-lei/texglot.does: Sends Zotero papers to a local TeXGlot app that translates arXiv or LaTeX sources with your own LLM API, keeping the translated PDFs as child attachments.
mengqi-lei/texglot.pain: Lets you read papers in your own language while keeping equations, citations and layout, and compare both PDFs side by side. You need the TeXGlot desktop app and a model API key or local model.

rahriver/z-daena.does: Summarises papers with OpenAI or Gemini for a selected item, several items, a collection or the whole library. It shows results in a chat-style popup and can save each summary as a child note with a tag.
rahriver/z-daena.pain: Gets quick overviews of many papers at once. It reads the attached PDF when there is one and handles rate limits. Needs your own OpenAI or Gemini API key.

andriwild/zotero-auto-export.does: Exports your library or one collection to a bibliography file automatically whenever items are added. Formats are BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, CSV, EndNote XML and CSL JSON, and it keeps a backup of the previous file.
andriwild/zotero-auto-export.pain: Keeps the .bib file used by LaTeX, Typst or Pandoc current without repeating File, Export each time.

jnsheff/zotero-hicite.does: Exports and auto-exports references as hicite definitions for the hicite legal-citation LaTeX package, with stable keys in the Citation Key field. Keys follow Better BibTeX's style with rules for cases and statutes.
jnsheff/zotero-hicite.pain: hicite does not read BibTeX, so legal writers need their own export. This keeps the .tex file updated as the library changes.

jiaojiaodubai/banyan.does: A citation backend that lets you write citation styles in JavaScript, with a built-in style editor and preview. It serves citations over local HTTP to companion add-ins for Microsoft Word and WPS Writer.
jiaojiaodubai/banyan.pain: Citation Style Language limits what styles can do. Styles as code allow full control over name abbreviation, ibid handling and multilingual dates, and AI-assisted style writing is offered.

0then0/margincarry.does: Transfers highlights and underlines from one PDF revision to another of the same item. You review each original passage against its proposed new location, then confirm. Comments, colours and tags carry over.
0then0/margincarry.pain: When a paper gets a new version, your marks stay on the old file. This moves them with exact text matching, an undo journal and nothing sent online. Zotero 10.0.5 or later; tested on macOS.

ayanya-0628/zotero-mcp.does: A local HTTP write API running inside Zotero. It lets the companion zotero-mcp server update item fields and creators, create items, add items by DOI or identifier, and search.
ayanya-0628/zotero-mcp.pain: Zotero's local API is read-only, so AI tools could not edit your library. This lets them write through Zotero's own save routine.

coro-afk/zotero-mouse-navigation.does: Makes your mouse's Back and Forward side buttons move through Zotero Reader history. It ignores them when the active tab is not a reader.
coro-afk/zotero-mouse-navigation.pain: After clicking a citation, equation or footnote link in a PDF, one button takes you back to your place. Supports Windows through Gecko AppCommand events; for Zotero 9 and 10.

ict-pr1nce/zotero-pdf-translate-codex.does: A fork of Translate for Zotero that adds a translation service using your local Codex CLI and its ChatGPT login, with model and reasoning settings. It adds a session cache and shows how long each translation took.
ict-pr1nce/zotero-pdf-translate-codex.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that translates through ChatGPT login instead of an API key. It is a personal trial build, mostly tested on Windows, with no automatic updates.

stem-sw/zotero-reader-tool-shortcuts.does: Adds configurable keyboard shortcuts for the PDF reader's note, text and area annotation tools, with Alt+3, Alt+4 and Alt+5 as defaults. Also sets default text colour, size and line width. Its documentation is in Korean.
stem-sw/zotero-reader-tool-shortcuts.pain: Saves reaching for the toolbar buttons while annotating. A shortcut only turns the tool on; you still click or drag on the page. For Zotero 9.

zjw11398925/zotero-retrieval-index.does: Builds a page-aware passage index of your library and serves it over Zotero's local HTTP server. AI agents fetch relevant passages with real page numbers, using BM25 plus optional bge-m3 vectors via Ollama.
zjw11398925/zotero-retrieval-index.pain: Lets agents and RAG tools pull a few passages instead of whole papers. Everything stays local and read-only, and it falls back to keyword search without Ollama.

barishnamazov/zotero-site-metadata.does: Fills in metadata for web pages that have no built-in translator, using patterns learned from the sites already in your library.
barishnamazov/zotero-site-metadata.pain: Saves typing titles, authors and dates by hand when you clip blog posts or personal websites.

allanchain/zotero-sort-by-color-tag.does: Sorts items by their coloured tags.
allanchain/zotero-sort-by-color-tag.pain: Lets you group items by tag colour in the item list. Its documentation is still the plugin template's and describes no further features.

zjj-low-key/zotero-word-learning.does: Collects unfamiliar English words and phrases while you read PDFs and saves them to a local wordbook. An optional LLM (DeepSeek by default, or OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic and others) fills in pronunciation, Chinese meaning and context. Review with cards, multiple-choice and spelling questions.
zjj-low-key/zotero-word-learning.pain: Learning academic English from papers usually means copying words into a separate vocabulary app. This keeps the word list and review practice inside Zotero, next to the paper where each word appeared.

xuzhiangdlut/zoterotldr.does: Generates structured AI summaries of PDF papers from the right-click menu, saving each PDF's summary as its own note. Works with Gemini, OpenAI-compatible services and MiMo, and needs your own API key for the provider you pick.
xuzhiangdlut/zoterotldr.pain: Skimming a pile of papers is slow. This writes a consistent summary note for each PDF, in batches, with prompts and PDF filename filters you can adjust. A fork of Zhang-ren/Zotero-AI-Summarizer; its README doesn't say what it changes.

last-diary/papertranslate-zotero-plugin.does: Translates PDFs into a reflowed text panel beside the Zotero reader. MinerU parses the paper and DeepSeek or another OpenAI-compatible model translates it. Handles formulas, tables and figures, and lets you edit the result. Needs a MinerU token and an LLM key.
last-diary/papertranslate-zotero-plugin.pain: Plain PDF translation breaks formulas and layout. This rebuilds the paper's structure first, so you can read a translated version next to the original, mainly aimed at Chinese-language readers of English papers.

wsxwj123/zotero-claudian.does: Puts a Claude Code chat panel in the Zotero reader sidebar or a full tab, running on the Claude Code CLI already installed on your computer. It passes the current paper, page and selected text to Claude and can save answers as notes.
wsxwj123/zotero-claudian.pain: Asking an AI about a paper normally means pasting text into another chat window. This keeps the conversation beside the PDF, uses your own Claude Code login and tools, and needs no separate API key.

katew11/zotero-imprint.does: Identifies papers by the DOI printed inside the PDF, using Crossref. It imports a folder of downloads, checks whether stored PDFs match their items, exports annotations in bulk, and compares a folder against your library.
katew11/zotero-imprint.pain: A paper filed under the wrong item looks normal in Zotero, and highlights live only in its database. Imprint finds mismatches and missing files, and writes annotations out as annotated PDFs or Markdown, text, CSV or HTML lists.

tenor-john/zotero-lit_ai_matrix.does: Builds a searchable, sortable literature matrix inside Zotero from item metadata plus structured fields parsed from your notes. Includes a usage heatmap, one-click opening of the PDF, cache rebuilds, and CSV or Markdown export.
tenor-john/zotero-lit_ai_matrix.pain: Comparing many papers across the same questions is awkward in a flat item list. This turns structured notes, such as those made with Zotero GPT, into a table for filtering and comparing.

kanhao100/zotero-tag-logic.does: Adds AND, OR and NOT logic to the Tag Selector, with an AND/OR toggle beside the filter box. Selected tags can be required, optional or excluded, for example (ECG OR EEG) AND FPGA AND NOT BCI.
kanhao100/zotero-tag-logic.pain: Zotero's Tag Selector only combines selected tags with AND, so searching across alternatives or excluding a tag needs a saved search. This does it in the tag pane without writing anything to the database.

bluesilveemperor/pdftranslate-zotero.does: Translates PDFs from within Zotero using PDF2zh or PDF2zh_next, keeping formulas and layout and producing bilingual or translated-only PDFs. Supports batch translation and several LLM services, and needs a companion translation server that runs on your computer.
bluesilveemperor/pdftranslate-zotero.pain: Translating a whole paper usually means uploading it to a web tool and losing the layout. This runs the translation engine locally and attaches the result to the item, aimed mainly at Chinese-speaking researchers. Based on zotero-pdf2zh by guaguastandup.

lnearfar/zotero-agentibility.does: Lets AI agents use your Zotero library through a command-line tool and local bridge. It offers semantic search and Markdown full text with line and page references. Needs Python, uv and Poppler; the current release is Linux only.
lnearfar/zotero-agentibility.pain: AI agents read PDFs badly, mangling formulas and losing citations. This gives them Markdown full text next to the PDF and grounded citations, with confirmation before anything is written.

retorquere/zotero-asreview.does: Shows ASReview rankings in Zotero. Add an attachment named asreview.csv to a collection and its rankings appear, sortable, matched to items by DOI only.
retorquere/zotero-asreview.pain: People screening papers for a systematic review with ASReview otherwise switch between its output and Zotero to see which items it ranks highest.

hdu-oranges/zotero-paper-chat.does: Adds a chat panel to the Zotero reader sidebar for asking questions about the open PDF, with page citations you can click to jump to. Works with any chat-completions API (DeepSeek by default, or a local server) and needs your own key unless the local server needs none.
hdu-oranges/zotero-paper-chat.pain: Questions about a paper usually mean copying text into a separate AI tool. This reads the PDF's text for you, keeps a separate conversation per paper and renders Markdown and LaTeX answers.

dawaltconley/zotero-plugin-pdf-filters.does: Adds Brightness and Contrast sliders to the PDF reader's Appearance panel. Settings are saved per document and restored when you reopen it, with default values set in the plugin preferences.
dawaltconley/zotero-plugin-pdf-filters.pain: Faint scans and washed-out PDFs are hard to read, and Zotero's reader has no brightness or contrast control. The filters also affect annotations, which the author notes can't currently be avoided.

edwardlewis35/zotero-translate.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader, looking single words up in your local MDX/MDD dictionaries first. Sentences and paragraphs go to an OpenAI-compatible model, and results can be saved as an underline annotation with the translation. Needs an API key for model translation.
edwardlewis35/zotero-translate.pain: Looking words up in a dictionary and pasting passages into a translator interrupts reading. This puts both in the selection popup and only calls the paid model when you ask. Its interface is in Chinese.

schulzedaniel/zoterocitationmaps.does: Draws an interactive citation network for a collection: papers are dots and citations are arrows. It suggests important papers you are missing using OpenAlex, searches for new work that cites yours, traces citation chains, and offers a timeline view.
schulzedaniel/zoterocitationmaps.pain: A flat list of papers hides which works your reading list rests on and what it lacks. This shows both, and adds a missing paper to your collection by DOI in one click. No account or key needed.

mappedinfo/local-zotero-bridge.does: Exposes Zotero collections, items, attachments and native note metadata to the companion Obsidian plugin Local Zotero Mirror over Zotero's localhost server. Also adds an Obsidian Search section in the item pane that opens matching Markdown notes.
mappedinfo/local-zotero-bridge.pain: For people who keep their reading notes in an Obsidian vault and want it mirrored from Zotero. It only works together with the Obsidian companion plugin.

kohirus/super-scholar.does: Exports Zotero PDF papers to an Obsidian vault from the item right-click menu. MinerU parses each PDF, and the plugin writes the Markdown beside a copied, hash-named PDF. Needs MinerU, either local or its cloud API with a key.
kohirus/super-scholar.pain: Moving papers into Obsidian as readable Markdown normally means converting and copying files by hand. This does it in one step for selected PDFs or items. Its menu text is in Chinese.

howtoexitvim/zotero-folder-import.does: Imports a whole folder tree of PDF and EPUB files, turning folders into nested collections and keeping filenames unchanged. A review screen shows counts and per-file status first. You choose Replace, Keep Both or Ignore for conflicts. Needs Zotero 10.
howtoexitvim/zotero-folder-import.pain: Zotero adds files one at a time, and a drive of PDFs sorted into folders over the years has to be re-sorted. No network calls, metadata lookup or renaming happen.

migueldlm/zotero-notebooklm.does: Connects Zotero collections to Google NotebookLM. Turn a collection into a notebook, add items from the right-click menu, sync missing items, and chat with your sources in a panel. Needs a Google account, Python 3.10 or later and a browser sign-in.
migueldlm/zotero-notebooklm.pain: Moving papers into NotebookLM by hand is tedious and drifts out of date. This keeps a notebook in step with a collection. An unofficial plugin, not affiliated with Google.

rg4sun/zotero-tab-manager.does: Groups open reader tabs into named, coloured, collapsible groups, much like tab groups in Edge. Drag tabs together to make a group, rename, recolour or dissolve it from a menu, and choose among several group appearances in the settings.
rg4sun/zotero-tab-manager.pain: With many PDFs open across several research tasks, Zotero's tab bar becomes a long, unordered row. Groups keep related papers together and remember them with the session.

christianfrisson/papermachines.does: Analyses and visualises a text collection for digital humanities research. It offers word clouds, phrase nets, topic models, maps of places mentioned and DBpedia annotation, run from the collection right-click menu. Needs Java.
christianfrisson/papermachines.pain: Gives historians and humanities researchers corpus analysis without programming or heavy computing. A legacy plugin for old Zotero versions, forked from papermachines/papermachines.

kvarnelis/zotero-compact-pane.does: Shows only selected metadata fields for each item type in the item pane, with a control to expand to the full list. Also adds Copy Attachment Path to the item right-click menu. Built and tested on macOS for Zotero 9 and 10.
kvarnelis/zotero-compact-pane.pain: Zotero's item pane lists many fields most items never use. A compact view keeps the useful ones in sight without removing any data.

mbradaschia/zotero-companion-launcher.does: Connects Zotero to a keyboard launcher for the Omarchy Linux desktop. The launcher offers fuzzy search of your library, notes, tags and journal rankings (ABS, ABDC, FT50, UTD24), citation copying, and chat about a paper with a model you choose. This is the local bridge it uses.
mbradaschia/zotero-companion-launcher.pain: Opening a paper normally means finding Zotero's window and clicking through it. This brings your library up with one shortcut, with nothing sent off your computer unless you pick a cloud model.

coderirse/zotero-fulltext-pdf-translate.does: Translates whole PDFs into bilingual PDFs that keep layout, formulas and tables, from the right-click menu, using your own LLM API key. Runs the pdf2zh engine locally, supports batch queues, and attaches the result to the item, side by side or stacked.
coderirse/zotero-fulltext-pdf-translate.pain: Whole-paper translation usually means a paid cloud service. This is an open-source, self-hosted alternative that works with any OpenAI-compatible model, and its interface is largely Chinese.

geshuangyang/zotero-hermes-ai-plugin.does: Adds a chat window for asking questions about the PDF you are reading, answered by the Hermes Agent running on your Mac. It sends selected text and metadata, shows its reasoning, and saves the conversation as a note on the item. Needs Hermes installed and set up.
geshuangyang/zotero-hermes-ai-plugin.pain: For people who already use the Hermes Agent and want it to answer about the current paper without switching apps, with a record kept in Zotero. Replies are in Chinese by default.

jderrfuss/zotero-narrative-citations.does: Adds a Narrative citation checkbox to the citation dialog in Word, producing Smith and Jones (2024) instead of (Smith & Jones, 2024). It follows APA 7's and/ampersand rule without modified style files. Pre-alpha, tested only on macOS with Word.
jderrfuss/zotero-narrative-citations.pain: Zotero has no narrative citations, so people use Omit Author and type names by hand, which go stale. Zotero is building this natively, but these citations won't convert, and edits without the plugin revert them.

yiyabo/zotero-reading-assistant.does: Adds an AI sidebar for chatting with the open paper, with follow-up questions, image input and comparison against other papers. It also provides Markdown sticky notes on PDF pages, a paper, method and dataset knowledge graph, and AI suggestions for tidying collections. Needs an API key.
yiyabo/zotero-reading-assistant.pain: Aimed at close reading rather than one-off summaries, keeping chat, page notes and a map of how your papers relate in Zotero. Collection changes are only applied after you confirm.

echo-lian/zotero-tts-plugin.does: Reads PDFs aloud in the reader with play, pause, speed and voice controls, using Microsoft Edge neural voices in English, Chinese or Japanese. Needs a local Python server running, and falls back to the browser's speech if it isn't. Includes an EPUB to MP3 converter script.
echo-lian/zotero-tts-plugin.pain: Listening to papers is useful when your eyes are tired or you're away from a screen. The default browser voices sound robotic, and this offers more natural ones.

akchan/zotero_write_api_plugin.does: Adds local write endpoints to Zotero's HTTP server. They import an item from a DOI, ISBN, arXiv ID or PMID, attach or update notes, add tags, attach files and import a PDF. Built as the back end for the zotero_mcp_server_write MCP server.
akchan/zotero_write_api_plugin.pain: Zotero's built-in local API is read-only, so an AI assistant can search but not add items or notes. A stripped-down fork of dzackgarza/zotero-local-write-api that keeps only the operations that server uses.

senyamiku1101/glossa.does: An open-source AI assistant in the item pane and a floating chat. It translates PDF selections (including with two models together), keeps a glossary and translation board, and records the passages sent with each answer. Needs your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic or compatible services.
senyamiku1101/glossa.pain: For people who want AI help on papers without a paid tier or closed code. Keys go only to the provider you pick, and chats are stored as local JSON files.

tantalus13a98b5f/make-it-fullscreen.does: An early-stage plugin that makes Zotero fullscreen. Its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
tantalus13a98b5f/make-it-fullscreen.pain: Someone who wants Zotero to fill the screen at startup or on demand. Adapted from the zotero/make-it-red sample plugin.

kromiii/paper-talk-zotero.does: Lets you hold a spoken conversation about the PDF you are reading, using the Gemini Live API with your microphone and voice replies. Open the Paper Talk tab in the reader sidebar and speak. Needs a Gemini API key; only the first 50,000 characters are sent.
kromiii/paper-talk-zotero.pain: Handy for hands-free review, practising English, or rehearsing a defence, since a custom system prompt can make the assistant a tutor or a strict reviewer.

text70/zotero_ai.does: A floating chat window for talking to a paper or your library through any OpenAI-compatible API (OpenRouter by default), with Markdown and LaTeX answers. Command tags summarise, translate, search your library with embeddings, or search the web. Needs an API key.
text70/zotero_ai.pain: Gives you a chat assistant that reads the selected item's PDF text without leaving Zotero, using whichever hosted or self-hosted model you choose.

kylekahraman/zotero-flat-export.does: Exports a collection and its subcollections into one flat folder from the collection right-click menu. It copies all PDFs under their original names, writes notes as Markdown files, and generates a BibTeX file whose file fields point to the copies.
kylekahraman/zotero-flat-export.pain: Zotero's own export nests files in subfolders. A flat, portable folder works better for LaTeX, Obsidian and editor workflows, including linked files such as those on Google Drive.

seifer08ms/zotero-repository-detector.does: Detects whether a paper has a public code repository on GitHub, Hugging Face or Gitee, using item metadata, web link attachments or title search. It stores the link in Extra, adds a Code Repo column and a tag, and can attach small repository snapshots.
seifer08ms/zotero-repository-detector.pain: Finding the code behind a paper is a manual search for each one. This checks many items at once, and lets you filter your library for papers that have code.

djebbkhaled/zoteropreview10.does: Adds a Preview tab that shows a citation preview for the selected item in a bibliographic style you choose. Updated to work with Zotero 10.
djebbkhaled/zoteropreview10.pain: Lets you check how an item will be cited without exporting a bibliography. A modified copy of the Zotero Preview plugin by Decartertod; its author describes it as a beginner's learning exercise.

hcf0526/zotwanglele.does: AI reading and PDF translation for Zotero 10. It writes deep-reading and quick-summary child notes, previews them in the item pane, and translates selected text with AI models, Google, DeepL or Baidu. You bring your own keys; the interface is mainly Chinese.
hcf0526/zotwanglele.pain: Combines summarising, translation and prompt management in one plugin, so you can compare translation services and keep their history.

saviotp/ufc-zotero-plugin.does: Installs a citation style for the Federal University of Ceara (UFC) reference guide, based on ABNT standards, plus fixes CSL can't express. Needs Zotero 8, and its documentation is in Portuguese.
saviotp/ufc-zotero-plugin.pain: Students and researchers at UFC must follow a strict ABNT-based reference format that stock Zotero styles don't match, so they otherwise fix references by hand.

dennis-huangm/zotero-ai-companion.does: A sidebar for chatting about the current paper: it reads the PDF, selection and annotations, translates paragraphs, analyses images and searches the web. Answers can go to notes or PDF annotations. Needs your own key for OpenAI, Anthropic or a compatible endpoint.
dennis-huangm/zotero-ai-companion.pain: Keeps AI reading help inside Zotero and switches to each paper's last conversation automatically. Includes WebDAV sync and backup of its own settings.

jin-taiyu/zotero-mark-reader.does: Parses PDFs with MinerU, online or via a local mineru-api, and draws paragraph boxes over the reader so you can click to copy or translate Markdown. Also translates whole papers with pause, resume, glossaries and cached versions.
jin-taiyu/zotero-mark-reader.pain: Selecting text in PDFs breaks formulas and paragraphs. Paragraph-level Markdown makes copying and translating cleaner. Its interface is in Chinese.

kvarnelis/zotero-praetor.does: Puts Codex or Claude Code beside your Zotero items in the item pane. Ask about the selected item, search indexed text, draft notes and review proposed metadata or collection changes. Uses the CLI and login already on your Mac, with no API key in the add-on.
kvarnelis/zotero-praetor.pain: For people who already use Codex or Claude Code and want it working on their library, with access levels from read-only to reorganising and an undo for applied proposals.

elbaro/zotero-redownloader.does: Scans your library and downloads missing attachments from their URLs, such as arXiv or OpenReview, not only PDFs.
elbaro/zotero-redownloader.pain: If most of your PDFs come from open-access sites, you can skip cloud storage for syncing files between computers and fetch them again when missing. Files behind authentication aren't supported.

williamwhite080808/zotero-structured-tag.does: Shows chosen Zotero tags as spreadsheet-style columns in the item list, which you can edit with a click. Fields can be single-choice, multiple-choice, numeric or text, and edited in batches. Values stay as native tags, with an SQLite mirror. Needs Zotero 10.
williamwhite080808/zotero-structured-tag.pain: Zotero tags are a flat list, which is awkward for rating, status or type. Structured columns let you annotate a literature table quickly, and everything still syncs as tags.

kazuma-yj/preprint-bridge.does: Finds the published conference or journal version of an arXiv preprint and updates your existing item after you review the changes. Also adds CCF 2026 ratings to Extra and tracks acceptance notes. Needs no API key and targets Zotero 10.
kazuma-yj/preprint-bridge.pain: Citing a preprint after it is published normally means re-entering details or replacing the item. This updates the record while keeping its annotations, notes, tags and collections.

endoretic/zontex-zotero-librarian.does: The Zotero side of Zontex, which lets Codex manage a Zotero 10 library: coloured tags, citation styles, tag and item merging, and experimental PDF annotations. This bridge adds what Zotero's local API lacks. Needs the Zontex Codex plugin.
endoretic/zontex-zotero-librarian.pain: For people who want an AI assistant to batch categorise, deduplicate and rate references, with confirmation rules before writes. Independent and not affiliated with Zotero or OpenAI.

boyi0/zotero-abs-ranker.does: Tags papers with their journal's ranking by matching publication titles against a built-in list: ABS (AJG) 2024, FT50 and UTD24. It adds coloured tags and a Ranking line in Extra, and can update your whole library from the right-click menu.
boyi0/zotero-abs-ranker.pain: Business and management researchers otherwise look up each journal's grade by hand. Matching works offline, with tolerant name comparison.

theocuc/zotero-arxiv-reader.does: Fetches an arXiv paper's HTML version as an attachment, hides distracting elements, fixes its styling and adds a translation after each paragraph. Translation uses an OpenAI-compatible API with your own key, and you can edit it in the reader.
theocuc/zotero-arxiv-reader.pain: Gives arXiv papers a clean, bilingual reading view inside Zotero instead of a PDF. Also opens Google Scholar for an item's title. Its interface is in Chinese.

wzh4464/zotero-conference-abbreviations.does: Shows conference abbreviations from the Extra field in Zotero's Journal Abbr column and sorts by them. With Green Frog installed, it also fills its CCF column from a built-in CCF 2026 catalogue of 681 conferences and journals.
wzh4464/zotero-conference-abbreviations.pain: Conference papers have no short-name column, so lists of ICLR, CVPR or AAAI papers are hard to scan and sort. No items or database are changed. Aimed at computer science researchers.

zhenyuanzhou/zotero-folder-watch.does: Watches one or more folders and imports new PDFs automatically, filing subfolders as nested collections. It waits until a file stops growing, skips duplicates by content hash, and can run Zotero's metadata recognizer. Deleted items return while their file stays in the folder.
zhenyuanzhou/zotero-folder-watch.pain: Adding downloads by hand is repetitive. This turns your downloads or an inbox folder into a feed, and keeps your library mirroring those folders.

liwind/zotero-fullcreator.does: Adds all authors' full names to the main item list column, shown as last name then first name. Written for Zotero 5, so it is a legacy plugin.
liwind/zotero-fullcreator.pain: Zotero's item list truncates long author lists, so you can't see everyone who wrote a paper at a glance.

unitian/zotero-memory-management.does: Reports Zotero 10 memory use and trims it. It unloads background PDF reader tabs while keeping tabs and reading positions, and unloads cached items of inactive feeds. Settings cover tab limits, idle time and memory thresholds.
unitian/zotero-memory-management.pain: Zotero can grow large with many PDF tabs and feeds open. This keeps memory down on long sessions without closing your tabs.

vic-c33/zotero-pdf-attachment-downloader.does: Downloads and attaches PDFs for selected items from IEEE Xplore and arXiv, from a toolbar button, right-click menu or keyboard shortcut. Items are matched by IEEE article number, DOI, arXiv ID or URL, and files are checked before being attached.
vic-c33/zotero-pdf-attachment-downloader.pain: Fetching PDFs one by one from publisher pages is tedious. This does it for a whole selection, skips items that already have a PDF, and never runs unless you start it; IEEE PDFs still need your own institutional access.

dawaltconley/zotero-vertical-toolbar.does: Moves the toolbar of Zotero's reader to the left or right edge of the window, switched from the View menu.
dawaltconley/zotero-vertical-toolbar.pain: A vertical toolbar frees up reading height and can be easier to reach on some devices, such as tablets or small screens.

quinn-zilly/zotero-wiki-citations.does: Makes author-year citations in the PDF reader clickable like wiki links. A matched citation opens the cited paper's PDF from your library in a new background tab. Numeric citation styles are not handled yet.
quinn-zilly/zotero-wiki-citations.pain: Following a citation normally means scrolling to the reference list and searching your library by hand. The author notes that the plugin is currently broken while bugs are worked out.

onlyls/docboxtrans.does: Translates selected text in Zotero's PDF reader using six engines: any OpenAI-compatible LLM, Google, Bing, Tencent, Youdao and CNKI. It also adds a translation history sidebar and context-enhanced translation that feeds earlier translations to the model for consistent terms.
onlyls/docboxtrans.pain: Keeps terminology consistent when translating a long paper, and stores history locally. Several engines are unofficial public interfaces; the repository also holds a separate Windows reader tool and is aimed at Chinese-language readers.

arjansiddhpura/zotchat.does: An AI chat panel in the reader's right-hand sidebar: select a passage, press Explain or Ask, and follow-ups continue in the same thread. Needs your own API key for DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
arjansiddhpura/zotchat.pain: Gets a quick explanation of a hard passage without leaving Zotero, and sends only the passage you selected with its source line, never your highlights, annotations or library. Chats are saved locally.

achuan-2/zotero-figure-extract.does: Extracts figures, tables and formulas from a PDF into a reader sidebar using Baidu's PaddleOCR-VL service. You can copy text or LaTeX, save crops as PNG, add image annotations or export Markdown or JSON. Needs an AI Studio or Baidu Cloud API key.
achuan-2/zotero-figure-extract.pain: Pulling charts, tables and equations out of papers for notes or slides is manual screenshotting. Selected pages are uploaded to the chosen service and use your account quota; the interface is in Chinese.

kvarnelis/zotero-page-view.does: Adds single-page reading, two-page spreads, fit-page controls and a focus mode to Zotero's PDF reader. Toolbar buttons, Tools menu entries and keyboard shortcuts toggle them, and pressing a shortcut again returns to continuous scrolling.
kvarnelis/zotero-page-view.pain: Zotero's reader only scrolls continuously, which suits scanned books and page-by-page reading poorly. Currently targets Zotero 9 and 10 on macOS.

janbaykara/zotero-photo-highlights.does: A wizard that turns photos of physical book pages into highlights on an item's PDF or EPUB. It runs OCR with Apple Vision, Windows OCR, PaddleOCR or Tesseract, finds the passages in the file, and lets you resolve duplicates and ambiguous matches.
janbaykara/zotero-photo-highlights.pain: People who read on paper otherwise retype passages or lose them. This carries marked-up print reading into Zotero as dated annotations, optionally keeping the photo.

fdamken/zotero-remarkable.does: Pushes PDF attachments from Zotero to a reMarkable tablet via the Tools menu, optionally into a chosen folder. Files are named by Better BibTeX citation key if installed, and an item can only be pushed once to avoid duplicates.
fdamken/zotero-remarkable.pain: Gets papers onto the reMarkable without manual upload. Setup needs a one-time code from your reMarkable account entered in the Config Editor, and the author describes it as work in progress and fragile.

acatechnic/zotero-scholar-search.does: Adds right-click search to the PDF reader: select text and search Google Scholar, Google, PubMed or your own custom search URLs. Results open in the browser you choose, such as Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge, on macOS, Windows or Linux.
acatechnic/zotero-scholar-search.pain: Looking up a phrase or a cited title normally means copying it into a browser tab by hand.

synesis-lang/zotero-synesis-export.does: Exports PDF annotations to Synesis (.syn) files for qualitative research: highlighted text as quotations, comments as memos and tags as codes. Works on selected items or the whole library, with field names you can rename.
synesis-lang/zotero-synesis-export.pain: Researchers coding texts in the Synesis language otherwise copy highlights and comments across by hand.

yufeixia/zotero-warm-theme.does: A colour theme that turns Zotero's white and grey surfaces ivory and beige with a burnt orange accent, plus a warm charcoal dark mode. It covers the library, item pane, settings, dialogs and the reader's toolbar and sidebar, and toggles from the Tools menu.
yufeixia/zotero-warm-theme.pain: A softer palette for long reading sessions. It changes colours only, leaves fonts and layout alone, and never touches the pages of your PDFs.

the-solipsist/zotero-wayback-autosave.does: Saves the URL of every new item to the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine, however it was added. It records the snapshot link in the Extra field with a tag, and a right-click command archives selected items on demand.
the-solipsist/zotero-wayback-autosave.pain: Web sources disappear or change, which breaks citations. This archives them as you collect them, retries failures, and accepts free archive.org keys for a higher save quota.

joao-fisio/colecoes-coloridas-zotero.does: Lets you give each collection its own colour and icon from the right-click menu, choosing from 14 colours, a custom colour and 136 icons. Several collections can be changed at once in Zotero 8 or later. The interface is in Portuguese and six other languages.
joao-fisio/colecoes-coloridas-zotero.pain: Stock Zotero shows every collection with the same folder icon, which makes a long collection tree hard to scan. Settings are stored locally and are not synced.

evelasko/zotero-citation-linker.does: Copies a Markdown citation link for an item from the right-click menu, and runs a local HTTP server so other apps can add items by URL, DOI or identifier. Includes duplicate detection and quality checks. An optional Perplexity API key enables AI extraction from URLs.
evelasko/zotero-citation-linker.pain: People writing in Markdown tools otherwise build citation links by hand or re-enter references. It also lets external apps send references into Zotero automatically.

kvarnelis/zotero-notebooklm-pane.does: Embeds Google NotebookLM in Zotero's item pane so you can chat and use its studio beside your items. A right-click command helps send a PDF to NotebookLM. You sign in with your own Google account.
kvarnelis/zotero-notebooklm-pane.pain: Saves switching between a browser and Zotero when working with NotebookLM. It is an embedded browser, not an official integration, and upload steps target macOS.

josesiqueira/zotero-stylero.does: Restyles the item list and collection tree with an unread dot column, clickable star ratings, a reformatted creator column and item-count badges. Also bolds unread items, tracks per-page reading time and adds a light and dark toggle.
josesiqueira/zotero-stylero.pain: Gives at-a-glance reading status, ratings and counts that stock Zotero lacks, in one plugin with a toggle per feature. Built and tested for Zotero 9.

yasu/zotero-washo-salvager.does: Rebuilds Japanese book records from ISBNs found in PDF file names, looking them up in openBD and the National Diet Library Search. It also suggests which collection to file unsorted items in. Both actions show a preview before changing anything.
yasu/zotero-washo-salvager.pain: Libraries of scanned Japanese books often hold bare PDFs with no metadata. This turns them into proper book items; only ISBNs are sent out, never your files. The interface is in Japanese.

chamomile93/zoteroautomaticreferenceextr.does: Imports the references cited by an article when you add it, using its DOI to query OpenCitations, Crossref and Semantic Scholar. An experimental fallback reads DOIs from the PDF. Also exports references to BibTeX and fetches abstracts and citation counts.
chamomile93/zoteroautomaticreferenceextr.pain: Building a library of a paper's sources means adding each reference by hand. This does it automatically for articles with DOIs and skips references you already have.

drownfish19/zoterofilemanager.does: Scans your library for linked attachments whose files are missing from disk and for duplicate files, matched by size and filename. It tags them with zotero_file_manager:missing or zotero_file_manager:duplicate so you can filter and review them.
drownfish19/zoterofilemanager.pain: Moved or deleted linked files and repeated downloads quietly accumulate. Tags make them easy to find; the plugin deletes nothing itself, and the oldest duplicate is left untagged.

canyi-chen/zoteroquicklookng-z7.does: Adds a Quick Look preview for Zotero items on macOS, for Zotero 7.
canyi-chen/zoteroquicklookng-z7.pain: Lets Mac users peek at a file without opening it in a full viewer.

hashmapw/hjfy-pdftranslate.does: Translates arXiv papers into Chinese through the hjfy.top service: right-click an item, and the translated PDF is attached as PDF-CN. If the item has no arXiv link, you can add one or upload its PDF. Signing in to hjfy.top is needed for new translations.
hashmapw/hjfy-pdftranslate.pain: Saves visiting the website, downloading and filing the result by hand, and shows progress in Zotero. Aimed at Chinese-speaking readers; an option removes the watermark link.

ildon/zotero-crawler.does: Downloads every article, with PDF and metadata, from a list of journals you follow into a Zotero collection, and on later runs fetches only new ones. It handles platforms such as Open Journal Systems, Digital Commons, WordPress, MDPI and OAI-PMH sites.
ildon/zotero-crawler.pain: Many open access journals have no feed or Zotero translator covering their archive, so keeping up means saving each article by hand. The interface is partly in Italian.

shaowen-ye/zotero-duplicate-merge-manage.does: Finds likely duplicate items from the right-click menu, scoring them by title, DOI, year, author and item type, and lists candidates in a window. After you confirm, it merges them into the item you keep or moves them to the trash.
shaowen-ye/zotero-duplicate-merge-manage.pain: Catches same-title duplicates that Zotero's own duplicate pane may miss, but never merges without confirmation and never deletes permanently. The interface is in Chinese.

ning703/zotero-excel-column-resize.does: Makes column resizing in the main library item list work like Excel. Dragging a divider resizes the column on its left, middle columns keep their widths, and the last resizable column absorbs the difference. Zotero 10.0.x only.
ning703/zotero-excel-column-resize.pain: Stock resizing shifts neighbouring columns as you drag, which makes tuning a wide item list fiddly. Disabling the plugin restores Zotero's behaviour.

hyunhwan-bcm/zotero-kindle-sync.does: Mirrors your Zotero PDFs into a Kindle-friendly folder by library and collection, and syncs them to a USB-connected Kindle using sync2kindle (s2k). Papers you delete on the Kindle are tagged in Zotero so they are not sent again. A Python command-line tool is included.
hyunhwan-bcm/zotero-kindle-sync.pain: Moving papers to a Kindle by hand is slow and loses track of what you removed. Needs a newer Kindle, and on macOS the libmtp library.

crushdemo01/zotero-pdf2md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown with Mistral OCR, translates the Markdown with an OpenAI-compatible LLM, and creates child notes from the result. Right-click commands run the whole chain or single steps. Needs a Mistral API key, an LLM API key and Python 3.10 or later.
crushdemo01/zotero-pdf2md.pain: Gives readable, translated text from scanned or English PDFs inside Zotero. Formulas may not render reliably in Zotero notes, so treat the Markdown as the source.

koenigderorangen/annosync.does: Turns each PDF annotation into a managed Zotero note built from an editable template, with native citations, internal links and mirrored tags. You choose which annotation colours sync, and a reader menu action resyncs on demand. Needs Zotero 8.
koenigderorangen/annosync.pain: Annotations live apart from notes and are awkward to cite or write from. This gives each highlight its own note, updated when the annotation changes; edits inside managed notes are overwritten.

openresearchtools/systematic-reviewer.does: Turns a Zotero collection into a workspace for systematic reviews, with harvesting, screening, data extraction, semantic search and report writing. It runs on local or hosted AI such as Ollama or LM Studio and can connect to MCP agent workflows. Research preview.
openresearchtools/systematic-reviewer.pain: Systematic reviews involve repetitive screening and extraction. This automates or assists those steps while you inspect and edit results; it also suits interviews and policy documents. Back up your library first.

harrywang/zotero-attachments-markdown.does: Converts web snapshots, EPUBs and Word (.docx) attachments into clean Markdown with YAML front matter, saved images and footnotes, as a new Markdown attachment. Works on selected items or the whole library, offline. PDFs are not supported. Needs Zotero 8.
harrywang/zotero-attachments-markdown.pain: Gives you plain text for Obsidian notes, AI tools or searching, from pages you have already saved. Snapshots go through Defuddle to strip menus and ads.

vecear/zotero-epub.does: Adds EPUB reader toolbar controls for font, image size and line spacing. It also switches between scrolling and paged mode and between single and two-page spreads. Settings persist across books and restarts. For Zotero 9.
vecear/zotero-epub.pain: The built-in EPUB reader offers few display controls. This brings it closer to PDF-style reading; bookmarks are left to Zotero's own annotations. The interface is in Traditional Chinese.

alanzeng423/zotero-paperlens.does: Reads a whole paper's text with an AI model first, then translates selected passages with an explanation grounded in the paper's methods and terminology. It adds located key passages as Zotero highlights. Needs an OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek or compatible API key.
alanzeng423/zotero-paperlens.pain: Translating a sentence alone loses its meaning in the paper. Full-paper reading sends the text to your provider and may incur charges. Works on text PDFs only.

seasideccm/zotero-translate-ant.does: Adds a menu button and right-click commands in Zotero for translation features, built for the Zotero 7 beta. The documentation gives only install steps and screenshots, so the specific features are not described.
seasideccm/zotero-translate-ant.pain: Probably aimed at Chinese-speaking users who want translation inside Zotero; the documentation is in Chinese and says no more.

vithrive/llm-for-zotero-sync.does: Syncs Markdown parsed by MinerU into a single maintained note under each item, rendered with contents, images and formulas. A reader button, right-click command and Tools command run it. Companion to the llm-for-zotero plugin.
vithrive/llm-for-zotero-sync.pain: Makes MinerU's PDF parsing results readable inside Zotero and updates the same note on each sync instead of creating duplicates. The MinerU output folder is set in the Config Editor; docs are in Chinese.

logan12l/pinyin-for-zotero.does: Fixes the pinyin sort order of Chinese author surnames that have several readings, so that Zeng (曾) sorts under Z rather than C. It applies to the Creator column in Zotero and to bibliography sorting in Word and WPS after a Refresh. Zotero 10 only.
logan12l/pinyin-for-zotero.pain: Zotero sorts such surnames by their common reading, putting authors in the wrong letter group. It changes only sort order, works offline, and can be switched off in the Config Editor.

yiiwang118/zotero-glossa.does: A research assistant in the item pane: chat with a paper, translate PDF selections, render LaTeX formulas and save answers as child notes. Uses your own API key, a local model such as Ollama, or the Codex, Claude Code or Grok command-line tools.
yiiwang118/zotero-glossa.pain: Questions about a paper normally mean copying text into a separate chat. Here the model reads metadata, annotations and your selection, shows what was sent, and sends nothing until you press Send.

lin-qingming/zotero-md-editor.does: Opens Markdown attachments in a Zotero tab for editing. Pasted screenshots and dropped images are saved beside the file so they sync with it, and you can link to items, PDF quotes and annotations. Needs Zotero 8 or later.
lin-qingming/zotero-md-editor.pain: Images pasted in Typora and similar editors point at paths on one computer, so other devices see broken links. Here images travel with the note through Zotero's file sync.

crowmane420/zotero-scientific-name-itali.does: Italicizes organism names in item titles, covering species, subspecies, varieties and genus names, including abbreviated genera such as B. cinerea. It matches against a local Catalogue of Life index you build, shows a preview, and can undo the last run. Needs Zotero 8.
crowmane420/zotero-scientific-name-itali.pain: Titles imported from databases often lack italics for scientific names, which journals expect. Matching is offline, and the setup needs a Catalogue of Life download and PowerShell scripts.

core-hn/hypothesis2zotero.does: Imports Hypothesis annotations into Zotero as a child note holding each quote, comment, tags, author and a public or private marker. It finds the page URL from the item's URL, snapshot or DOI. A Hypothesis API token is needed only for your private annotations.
core-hn/hypothesis2zotero.pain: Web annotations made in Hypothesis otherwise stay outside your library. This brings them next to the reference they belong to; only the first 200 per page are imported, and private group annotations are skipped.

dviralsh/plugins4zotero.does: A bundle of reader tools: Hebrew translation of selected text, local AI summaries through Ollama, and a Link instead of duplicate option for newly added items.
dviralsh/plugins4zotero.pain: Adds Hebrew translation and local summaries that stock Zotero lacks. For people who read in Hebrew or want summaries kept on their own machine.

offmor/titledrop.does: Renames PDF attachments and their files after the paper's title: automatically for new imports, or across your library or a selection on request. Uncertain titles go to a review list. Includes undo, a progress dashboard and a JSON report. Needs Zotero 10.0.x.
offmor/titledrop.pain: Downloaded PDFs keep names like synthetic-paper.pdf or a string of digits. This names them readably with local extraction and DOI or arXiv checks, with no AI account or API key.

zcjie1/zotero-ai.does: Reads PDF attachments with an AI model and writes a structured analysis as a Zotero note. It works over OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages APIs and can extract figures and tables and send them to vision models. Needs your API key.
zcjie1/zotero-ai.pain: Gets a first-pass summary note for many papers at once, with parallel jobs, retries and a progress window. Figure extraction installs a Python runtime, currently for Windows x64. The interface is in Chinese.

galapo/zotero-ai-referencing-plugin-rele.does: Processes saved ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini conversation snapshots. It extracts the conversation URL and your prompts, updates metadata, and creates a structured prompt note, for one item or a whole collection, all locally.
galapo/zotero-ai-referencing-plugin-rele.pain: Universities increasingly ask students to disclose AI use. This helps cite AI chats and supports acknowledgement sections, but it modifies item fields, converting Web Page items to Software.

oliverdudgeon/zotero-named-annotations.does: Lets you give names to Zotero's annotation colours in settings, such as Key claims, and shows them as tooltips in the reader's colour picker. For Zotero 7 or newer.
oliverdudgeon/zotero-named-annotations.pain: Colour-coded highlighting systems are easy to forget, since Zotero shows only swatches. Names keep the meaning of each colour visible while you annotate.

israfil-hossen/zotero-supplementary-down.does: Downloads supplementary files from publisher pages and attaches them to the selected items, titled with a [Suppl] prefix and tagged supplementary. Supports Elsevier, Springer Nature, Wiley, PLOS, PNAS, MDPI, ACS and others, and can copy files to a folder by author and year.
israfil-hossen/zotero-supplementary-down.pain: Supplementary data sits on publisher sites and is easy to miss or lose. Items need a URL or DOI, and access depends on your own institutional subscriptions.

zepadovani/zotobs-io.does: Exports Zotero annotations to Markdown for Obsidian and sends edits made there back as native Zotero annotations. Re-exports keep text you wrote between annotations. A companion zotobs command-line tool also works with AI agents.
zepadovani/zotobs-io.pain: Zotero keeps annotations in its database rather than in the PDF, so other tools cannot see them. This links them with Obsidian in both directions; detailed docs are in Portuguese.

frankkk1912/ai4s-literature-workbench.does: Adds Zotero columns for an editable priority rating and read-only AI summary, agent tags, article type, impact factor, JCR, CAS and citation metrics. Part of a workbench of agent skills for biomedical literature search, ranking, Zotero sync and evidence-based drafting.
frankkk1912/ai4s-literature-workbench.pain: Helps choose what to read next by showing journal metrics and your own priority beside each item. The wider workbench is meant for use with an AI agent.

wuzirui/paper-meta-update.does: Updates preprints in your library to their published conference metadata: press Shift-P, pick a conference, and the plugin matches your arXiv items. Lists CVPR 2013 to 2025, ICCV 2013 and 2023, and WACV 2020 to 2025, with more planned.
wuzirui/paper-meta-update.pain: Preprints keep their arXiv details after publication, so citations point to the wrong venue. This fixes them in bulk, mainly for computer vision papers.

mlava/scholar-sidekick-zotero.does: Checks a pasted bibliography or .bib or .ris file before import, flagging mismatched metadata, retractions and open access copies. You tick the rows to import, and canonical metadata is added with a note.
mlava/scholar-sidekick-zotero.pain: Reference lists from collaborators or AI tools can contain wrong or invented citations. This catches them before they become trusted items. Works without a key; a free Scholar Sidekick key raises rate limits.

newtontech/zotero-ai-newton.does: Chats with your selected items, PDFs or whole collections from a sidebar and right-click menu, using OpenAI, DeepSeek or another compatible API. Offers summaries, keyword extraction, related-reading ideas and grounded Q&A, with a choice of tone. You supply the API key and model.
newtontech/zotero-ai-newton.pain: Asking an AI about a paper normally means copying text out of Zotero. This keeps the conversation next to your selection and sends only the selected context to your chosen provider.

unitian/zotero-feed-management.does: Adds one Subscription Management window under Tools for Zotero's RSS feeds. Edit titles, URLs and retention periods, refresh feeds, and export them as OPML.
unitian/zotero-feed-management.pain: Zotero has no single place to review or bulk-edit feed settings, export feeds, or clear repeated entries. Made for Zotero 10, with a mostly Chinese description.

hanson-wang-chn/zotero-keep-reader-ready.does: Keeps rendered PDF pages and loaded PDF tabs from being discarded when you switch apps, desktops or tabs. Optionally pre-renders a whole paper and retains pages as you read, at the cost of more memory.
hanson-wang-chn/zotero-keep-reader-ready.pain: Returning to a paper in Zotero can force pages to redraw because the reader drops its canvases or unloads inactive tabs. This trades memory for a paper that is ready when you come back.

dragongong/zotero-math-patch.does: Repairs pasted maths in Zotero notes and Better Notes, turning broken formulas into proper LaTeX nodes. One command uses local rules only; the other sends text blocks to an OpenAI-compatible service you configure. Both run only when you invoke them.
dragongong/zotero-math-patch.pain: Formulas pasted from AI chats or PDFs often arrive as plain text with lost delimiters or split lines. This fixes them in place without watching your pastes or processing your library in the background.

josesiqueira/zotero-open-citations.does: Adds a sortable Citation column to your item list, filled from OpenAlex, Crossref and optionally Semantic Scholar. Update items, collections or the whole library from menus, with an optional once-a-day background refresh. A Semantic Scholar key is optional.
josesiqueira/zotero-open-citations.pain: Citation counters that scrape Google Scholar trigger captchas and blocks. This uses open citation APIs at a gentle pace. A rewrite of beloglazov/zotero-scholar-citations for Zotero 7 to 10.

qifu04/zotero-pdf-hand-catcher.does: Finds items in the selected collection that have no PDF and opens each in turn in an isolated Microsoft Edge window. When you download the PDF there, it is captured, attached to the item and the next one opens. Windows only.
qifu04/zotero-pdf-hand-catcher.pain: When Zotero's own PDF fetcher fails, you repeat a manual loop of finding the item, opening the page, downloading and re-attaching for every paper. This automates everything except clicking download. Edge keeps your institutional login.

volatile-static/zotero-reading-bridge.does: Gives AI assistants such as Claude Desktop and Codex read-only access to your Zotero library through a local endpoint. They can read the open paper, selection, notes, annotations and collections, and fetch publisher PDFs into temporary files using your institutional access.
volatile-static/zotero-reading-bridge.pain: AI chat apps cannot see the papers on your computer. This lets you ask about the paper you have open or search your library without uploading files. Any program on your computer can query the endpoint while Zotero runs.

bugbubbles/zoterocitationcountsmanager.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP and Semantic Scholar, on import or by right-click, and adds a sortable Citation Counts column. Google Scholar is not supported.
bugbubbles/zoterocitationcountsmanager.pain: Zotero shows no citation numbers of its own. A fork of FrLars21/ZoteroCitationCountsManager, itself based on Erik Schnetter's version, for Zotero 7; it adds concurrent retrieval, per-item error messages and refactored code.

altairwei/zutilore.does: A utility toolbox for Zotero 7 and 8: bulk tag copy, paste and removal, item relations, copyable links and paths, and book and section conversion. Also updates metadata from Crossref, PubMed or arXiv with a field-level merge dialog, and edits saved HTML snapshots.
altairwei/zutilore.pain: A successor to the Zutilo plugin, which does not run on Zotero 8. It covers the same power-user chores and avoids macOS clipboard permission problems.

crispstrobe/crispzotlib.does: Searches library catalogues from inside Zotero over SRU, OAI-PMH or IxTheo and imports the results. Endpoints include the German and French national libraries, K10plus, swisscovery and the Library of Congress. Can also resolve a DOI, PMID, ISBN or URL to a record.
crispstrobe/crispzotlib.pain: Zotero's own lookups lean on web translators and are weak for union catalogues and national libraries. This queries those catalogue protocols directly, with no Python or other external tool needed.

blanlak/docutranslate-zotero.does: Translates a PDF into Chinese from the right-click menu, using a DocuTranslate service running on your own computer. The translated PDF is saved next to the original and attached to the item. Needs DocuTranslate and a Python helper script in a conda environment.
blanlak/docutranslate-zotero.pain: For people reading English papers in Chinese who want a full translated PDF filed back under the item rather than copying text into a translator. Documented in Chinese only.

vithrive/llm-for-zotero-translator.does: Adds a button to the PDF reader toolbar that translates the MinerU-parsed Markdown of the open paper into Simplified Chinese, saving a .zh.md file beside it. Protects formulas, code and tables, skips references, and works with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Ollama and other providers.
vithrive/llm-for-zotero-translator.pain: A companion add-on for llm-for-zotero, for readers who parse papers with MinerU and want a Chinese version of the full text. It needs a provider key and the earlier MinerU parse.

ma-ji/miscite-zotero-connector.does: Syncs both ways between your miscite.review account and a miscite.review collection in Zotero. Moves items, files and folders, links existing items by DOI, syncs on a timer, and stores citation counts and FWCI in the Extra field. Needs a miscite API token.
ma-ji/miscite-zotero-connector.pain: Keeps a miscite library and Zotero in step without re-importing by hand, and it never touches items outside its own collection.

kinomotomio/zotero-agent-copilot.does: Creates a local workspace folder for each item, converts its PDF to Markdown through the MinerU API, and launches Claude Code or Codex in a terminal there. Saves workspace snapshots as ZIP attachments and restores them. Currently macOS only.
kinomotomio/zotero-agent-copilot.pain: Conversations with AI agents about a paper get scattered and are hard to resume. This gives each paper one persistent place for converted text, notes and agent output. Very early stage.

raideno/zotero-better-tags.does: Turns tags written as property:Name:Value into item list columns, one column per property name, showing the values. Prefix and value separator are configurable through preferences.
raideno/zotero-better-tags.pain: Stock Zotero tags are flat, so there is no way to show a status or priority as a column. This lets you sort and scan your library by properties like Status or Priority.

xamspanda/zotero-kokoro-tts.does: Manages custom pronunciation rules, such as C# read as C Sharp, for a local or self-hosted Kokoro TTS server used with Zotero Read Aloud. Adds a settings pane and reader menu actions, with audio preview and health check. Needs Zotero 10.
xamspanda/zotero-kokoro-tts.pain: Read Aloud mispronounces symbols and technical terms. This lets you fix them once on your own Kokoro server.

gshaikovski/zotero-quick-switcher.does: An Obsidian-style quick switcher: press Cmd+O from any tab, type a few words, and fuzzy-search your library by relevance. Enter opens the paper in a reader tab or switches to it if already open.
gshaikovski/zotero-quick-switcher.pain: Finding a paper normally means going back to the library tab and searching. This jumps straight to any paper from anywhere with the keyboard, and the shortcut is configurable.

jun0404/zotero-semantic-scholar-citation.does: Fetches citation counts from Semantic Scholar by DOI, arXiv ID or title and writes them to each item's Extra field. Run it from the right-click menu, the Tools menu or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+C, for selected items or the whole library. Requests are rate-limited.
jun0404/zotero-semantic-scholar-citation.pain: Zotero shows no citation numbers. This stores them in Extra so you can see how cited a paper is. For Zotero 8 and 9; use release 3.0.0 on Zotero 7.

longkou1988/zotero-submission-tracker.does: Tracks journal submissions of your manuscripts inside Zotero, from preparation to review, revision and acceptance or rejection. Offers a dashboard, status timelines, follow-up reminders, analytics, next-step suggestions and Chinese and English inquiry email templates.
longkou1988/zotero-submission-tracker.pain: Authors usually track submissions in spreadsheets outside their reference manager. This keeps the history and reminders next to the paper. Bilingual Chinese and English.

boan-anbo/zotero-title-without-articles.does: Generates sort titles without leading articles such as A, An and The and stores them in the Extra field as a title-without-articles CSL variable. Citation styles can then sort bibliographies by it. The list of articles is configurable.
boan-anbo/zotero-title-without-articles.pain: Bibliographies sort A Modest Proposal under A instead of M. This supplies the clean sort title, though you must edit the CSL style to use it; an example Chicago style is included.

carhojohn/doi2pdf.does: Extends Zotero's local API with endpoints to add items by DOI, ISBN or PMID, find full text for an item, and read the selected collection. New DOI items go into a collection you set in Settings.
carhojohn/doi2pdf.pain: Lets scripts and AI agents add papers with metadata and PDFs to Zotero without clicking through the interface. Based on GOKORURI007/zotero-api-plus and documented in Chinese.

openhistorymap/ohm-zotero.does: Manages Open History Map data descriptors, stored as ohm:* tags, on Zotero items for the openhistorymap data index.
openhistorymap/ohm-zotero.pain: For people cataloguing historical map data sources in Zotero for the Open History Map project. No further documentation is available.

tsekitsi/viszot.does: Renders a citation graph of a Zotero collection so you can see how its items connect.
tsekitsi/viszot.pain: For researchers who want a visual overview of a collection instead of a flat list. No further documentation is available.

buptweixin/zotero-hf-daily-papers.does: Browses Hugging Face Daily Papers by date and imports chosen ones as preprint items with arXiv metadata and optional PDFs. Tags them from AI keywords and upvotes, and files them into date and topic collections. Can sync recent papers at startup.
buptweixin/zotero-hf-daily-papers.pain: Following the daily paper feed means copying entries into Zotero by hand. This imports, de-duplicates and sorts them for you. Documented mainly in Chinese.

jiangshuguo/zotero-memory.does: Draws editable comment cards in the margins beside PDF pages, linked to their annotations by leader lines. Edits with basic formatting sync back to the annotation comment, with a toolbar toggle and export or import of annotation notes as JSON.
jiangshuguo/zotero-memory.pain: Annotation comments normally sit in the reader sidebar, away from the page. This puts them beside the text so you can review and revise without switching focus.

0xc1c4da/zotero7-datalab.does: Adds a Convert to Markdown right-click option that uploads a PDF to Datalab.to, converts it to Markdown and attaches the result to the item. Needs a Datalab API key, entered in Settings.
0xc1c4da/zotero7-datalab.pain: For people who want paper text as Markdown for notes or AI tools rather than as PDF.

gaiussheh/attanger-plus.does: Keeps linked-file folders matched one-to-one with your collections when used with Attanger. Items in several collections get a copy in each folder, and renames, moves and deletions follow on disk. Has a plugin trash, a changes window and a library check under Tools.
gaiussheh/attanger-plus.pain: Attanger files an attachment once and then stops, so folders drift from collections. This keeps them in step. Needs Attanger in linked mode, and is not affiliated with it.

cxrxhz/note-display.does: Adds a Key Content column to the item list showing the first 50 characters of one child note per item. Right-click an item to pick which child note is shown; by default the first is used. For Zotero 9.
cxrxhz/note-display.pain: Zotero's item list hides notes, so you must open each item to see your main takeaway. This puts a note excerpt in the list. Documented in Chinese.

liangliu-nlp/reference-guard.does: Makes clicking a citation link in the PDF reader jump to the exact reference using the PDF's own link annotations, with a temporary highlight. PDFs without internal links keep Zotero's normal behaviour.
liangliu-nlp/reference-guard.pain: Reference jumps in Zotero's reader sometimes land in the wrong place. This maps links to exact destinations instead of guessing from nearby text.

qiangqianglab/scansci-zotero.does: Adds a right-click item that runs the external scansci-pdf command-line tool on an item's DOI and attaches the downloaded PDF. Supports batch downloads with a pause between each, skipping items that already have a PDF, and an optional tag. You must install scansci-pdf.
qiangqianglab/scansci-zotero.pain: Automates fetching PDFs for items that have DOIs and reports successes, failures and skips. Where scansci-pdf gets papers is not stated. Documented in Chinese and English.

ariyanbe/science-lense.does: Select a word or phrase in the PDF reader and click Define · Wikipedia to see a short English Wikipedia definition with a thumbnail in a reader panel. Can offer other matching articles and disambiguation choices. No account or key needed. For Zotero 10.0.x.
ariyanbe/science-lense.pain: Looking up unfamiliar terms while reading means leaving Zotero for a browser. This gives a quick definition in place, without an AI service.

jackblack419/wenxian-yidu.does: Translates papers into Simplified Chinese: side-by-side split view, paragraph comparison, translate-on-select and a box for your own text. Uses free web engines, your own AI API or an optional offline engine. Windows and Zotero 10.
jackblack419/wenxian-yidu.pain: Reading English literature in Chinese otherwise means copying text out of the PDF. The translated PDF is saved as an attachment beside the original. Based on Z-Transplit.

arrancurran/zotag.does: Restyles tags in the item pane as rounded, shaded chips that wrap neatly, with hover highlights and a small colour dot for coloured tags. Follows light and dark themes. Has no settings and does not change your library.
arrancurran/zotag.pain: Zotero's plain tag list is hard to scan. This gives it a chip look inspired by the Papers app, and tag editing works as before.

tshippen/zotero-adobe-ocr-plugin.does: Runs OCR on selected PDF attachments through Adobe's PDF Services API. Choose language, searchable-image or exact output, and whether to replace the original or add a new attachment. Needs Adobe API credentials, and PDFs are uploaded to Adobe.
tshippen/zotero-adobe-ocr-plugin.pain: Scanned PDFs have no text layer, so Zotero cannot search them. This adds one using Adobe's cloud OCR, which has a free tier. Independent of Adobe.

zhikaiyici/zotero-inspire.does: Connects Zotero to the INSPIRE-HEP physics database for metadata, citation counts and BibTeX. Adds a panel of references, citations and related papers, plus a connections graph and academic family tree.
zhikaiyici/zotero-inspire.pain: A fork of fkguo/zotero-inspire; its README doesn't say what it changes, though it lists a BibTeX export API and the academic tree as new. High-energy physics researchers can browse literature without leaving Zotero.

damarals/zotero-page-count.does: Adds a sortable Page Count column to the item list showing each item's PDF page count, read from the full-text index Zotero already keeps. Items not yet indexed show blank. Needs full-text PDF indexing on.
damarals/zotero-page-count.pain: Zotero computes page counts but never shows them. This lets you sort by length when choosing what to read.

git-jiwon/zotero-pdf-metadata-refresh.does: Re-recognises metadata for PDFs already in your library using Zotero's recogniser, DOI and ISBN lookups, catalogues, web search or a local LM Studio model. Shows proposals field by field, applies chosen changes and keeps undo history.
git-jiwon/zotero-pdf-metadata-refresh.pain: Old library entries often have wrong or missing metadata. This lets you review and fix many at once without losing attachments, notes or annotations. Korean and English interface.

shiysent-ctrl/zotero-sideline.does: An AI chat sidebar in the PDF reader: summarise, explain selections, translate and ask questions, adding page text, notes or images as context. Uses an OpenAI-compatible API or local Codex, OpenCode or DeepSeek Harness, and saves answers as child notes. Windows and Zotero 10.
shiysent-ctrl/zotero-sideline.pain: Keeps one conversation per paper inside Zotero instead of a separate chat app. Selected text goes to your chosen provider. Documented in Chinese.

colefaraday/zotero-tex-fetch.does: Attaches a paper's arXiv LaTeX source as one flattened .tex file, automatically for new items or from right-click menus. Looks up missing arXiv IDs on INSPIRE and updates the file when arXiv has a newer version.
colefaraday/zotero-tex-fetch.pain: AI agents read LaTeX source far more reliably than PDFs. This puts it in Zotero. The author says it was largely AI-written and only skim-read.

techczech/zoterolm.does: Summarises PDFs with Google Gemini or OpenAI and saves the result as a Markdown-rendered child note. Also answers questions about an item, summarises collections, and manages prompt templates. An alpha reader panel adds an outline, glossary and tag suggestions. Needs your API key.
techczech/zoterolm.pain: Saves you from pasting papers into a chat window and copying summaries back, and keeps the notes in your library. Targets Zotero 8.

leobba/daxiang-zotero-tools.does: A personal toolbox for Zotero 10 that shows subcollection items in empty parent collections and adds to-read, reading and read status tags with a column. Also exports data packs and offers library checks and metadata clean-up.
leobba/daxiang-zotero-tools.pain: Zotero's recursive-collections switch is global and it has no reading status. This is more selective. Documented in Chinese, and the author calls it self-use.

bcs1037/synapse.does: Exports item metadata to Markdown notes for Obsidian. Uses custom templates with placeholders and filters, YAML frontmatter, filename templates and batch export, and adds a link attachment to the generated file. For Zotero 8.
bcs1037/synapse.pain: A successor to Mdnotes, which stopped after Zotero 7, for people keeping literature notes in Obsidian. Back up before installing.

jsglazer/zotero-audit.does: Opens a spreadsheet-style table of every item with content type, citation ID, title, short title, author, year and month. Edit cells inline, sort columns and see missing values in red. Citation ID needs Better BibTeX. Opens from Tools or Alt+Cmd+A.
jsglazer/zotero-audit.pain: Finding and fixing missing metadata item by item is slow. This shows the whole library at once and saves edits back to Zotero.

terrywen2023/zotero-c1life.does: Embeds the Google Gemini web interface in the PDF reader sidebar, so you can ask about a paper beside it. Sign in with a Google account; no API key is needed. For Zotero 9.0.3 or later.
terrywen2023/zotero-c1life.pain: Reading, translating and summarising with a free Gemini account normally means switching windows, avoiding API fees. Selected text is not sent automatically.

kdmsnr/zotero-metadata-updater.does: Updates metadata on selected items from their DOI using Zotero's own DOI lookup, overwriting bibliographic fields. Keeps Extra, tags, collections, related items, notes and attachments. Run it from the right-click menu. Zotero 9 only.
kdmsnr/zotero-metadata-updater.pain: Stock Zotero cannot refresh an existing item from its DOI. This avoids deleting and re-adding it, which would lose your notes and attachments.

zhanyuanium/zotero-pdf-noir.does: Improves figures in the PDF reader's dark themes: white backgrounds become transparent and near-black ink turns light, while colours stay. Has sliders for threshold, band width and sensitivity. Affects only raster images. Needs Zotero 10.
zhanyuanium/zotero-pdf-noir.pain: In dark mode, embedded figures with white backgrounds still glare. This fixes them.

jaehho/zotero-tray.does: Hides Zotero to a system tray icon on Linux when you close the window, instead of quitting. Click the icon to show or hide it, and Quit still quits. Needs Python with PyGObject and a StatusNotifierItem tray.
jaehho/zotero-tray.pain: Zotero has no tray on Linux, so closing it ends the session and reopening is slow.

fanyc22/arch-note.does: Generates paper reading guides for computer-architecture papers with DeepSeek, saving them as child notes. Runs automatically on new papers or from Tools menu actions for selected papers, collections or the library, optionally using a local arch-note CLI. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
fanyc22/arch-note.pain: For architecture reading groups and PhD students who want a structured, critical note for every paper. Jobs run one at a time to avoid API bursts.

rapharomero/zotero-fullscreen.does: Binds Ctrl+Cmd+F to toggle fullscreen on the Zotero main window on macOS.
rapharomero/zotero-fullscreen.pain: Zotero has no working fullscreen on macOS, since the green window button and menu item do nothing. This adds a shortcut.
