zhuzihan728/zotero-paperlink.does: When the Zotero Connector saves a paper, looks in your Downloads or other folders for a PDF you already have and links it instead of keeping a second copy. Then checks for duplicate items and offers to merge. Also runs from the right-click menu.
zhuzihan728/zotero-paperlink.pain: Saving a paper through the Connector can leave two copies of the PDF and duplicate entries, with your annotations in the original. This links the file you have. Documented in Chinese.

starlitsky27/zotero-renameattachments.does: Renames PDF attachments to the pattern Author (Year)_ProcessedTitle.pdf and sets each attachment's title to "PDF". It uses the Short Title when present, shortens long titles with abbreviations, and runs on several items at once from the right-click menu.
starlitsky27/zotero-renameattachments.pain: Publisher-supplied PDF names are long and inconsistent. This gives every file a short, predictable name; the built-in abbreviations lean towards psychology and mental-health terms.

chrisyangqn/zotero-zhutero.does: Generates a navigable reading outline for a PDF or EPUB with Claude or GPT, shown as a tree in the item pane. Clicking a node jumps the reader there, and your highlights attach to the matching section. Needs an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible API key.
chrisyangqn/zotero-zhutero.pain: Long books and papers are hard to hold in your head. The outline lives as a synced Zotero note, so structure, highlights and your own notes stay together.

legojeon/zotero2notion.does: Syncs items from My Library into a Notion database, one page per item, built from Markdown templates you edit in Zotero settings. Templates can differ by collection or tag, and Zotero notes can be included. Connects with your own Notion personal access token.
legojeon/zotero2notion.pain: People who study in Notion otherwise copy references in by hand. Metadata updates keep the notes you write on each Notion page.

faibk/zotlit-notifier.does: Tells the ZotLit add-on for Obsidian when you switch reader tabs or change annotations, so its annotation pane refreshes.
faibk/zotlit-notifier.pain: The original ZotLit notifier is not adapted for newer Zotero versions. This is a minimal personal fix covering only the refresh, not the original's other features.

mcburton/zotero-clavicularius.does: Generates citation keys for new items from a token template, such as author, year and the first few title words. Offers a live preview in preferences and bulk actions to backfill missing keys or rebuild all of them.
mcburton/zotero-clavicularius.pain: Zotero has no built-in citation key field to fill automatically. This creates consistent keys without overwriting existing ones unless you ask for a rebuild.

stilljosh/zotero-semantic-scholar.does: Fetches citation counts and metadata from Semantic Scholar and shows them in library columns and an item pane section. Can fetch automatically for new items or in batches, matching by DOI, arXiv ID, PubMed ID or title.
stilljosh/zotero-semantic-scholar.pain: Zotero shows no citation counts. This puts citation and influential-citation numbers beside each paper so you can sort by them.

generalpawz/zotero-tts-byok.does: Routes Zotero's built-in Read Aloud through your own text-to-speech API key. Supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints, ElevenLabs, Speechify, Azure, Google Gemini or a custom one, with reader skip rules and per-document voice settings.
generalpawz/zotero-tts-byok.pain: Read Aloud otherwise spends Zotero's metered voice minutes or falls back to basic local voices. Requires a signed-in Zotero account.

anka-afk/paperbridge.does: Lets you ask Codex or DeepSeek about text selected in the PDF or HTML reader, and syncs reading notes both ways between Zotero and Obsidian. Windows only, for Zotero 10. A Chinese-language tool; Codex needs a local login, DeepSeek an API key.
anka-afk/paperbridge.pain: Reading, asking an AI and keeping Obsidian notes usually means three apps. This keeps one paired note per paper in step on both sides.

mengzeovo/zotero-agent-bridge.does: Adds a chat assistant to the item and reader sidebars that answers questions about the current paper using the Pi CLI. It can save answers as notes and build a running notes summary. Windows only; needs Pi CLI with a model configured.
mengzeovo/zotero-agent-bridge.pain: Discussing a paper with an AI normally means moving between Zotero and a terminal. This keeps per-paper conversations and saved answers inside Zotero.

oliverdudgeon/zotero-arxiv-html.does: Saves the arXiv HTML version of a paper as an offline snapshot. Adds an Attach arXiv HTML item menu entry; you read and annotate the result in Zotero.
oliverdudgeon/zotero-arxiv-html.pain: The Zotero Connector saves the arXiv PDF and abstract page but not the HTML version, which reflows better on small screens and can be annotated like any snapshot.

lzy248/zotero-cs-venues.does: Recognises computer science conferences and journals offline and shows labels like ACL 2026 in an item list column. Can fill the Extra and Journal Abbr fields, with manual overrides. Chinese and English interface, no API key.
lzy248/zotero-cs-venues.pain: Conference and journal names arrive in many spellings. This gives consistent short labels for sorting and citation without any online lookup.

cz-hit/zotero-markdown-notes.does: Opens Markdown attachments in a Zotero tab with a Cherry Markdown editor and preview, including formulas and Mermaid diagrams. Adds links between Markdown notes, a manager for orphaned links, and a menu to create new Markdown attachments.
cz-hit/zotero-markdown-notes.pain: Zotero's own notes are not Markdown. This lets you read and write .md files inside Zotero instead of switching to an external editor.

ilker-golcuk/zotero-plugins.does: Adds Export PDFs to Folder to the item menu, copying the PDFs of selected items into a folder you choose and keeping their filenames. The same repository holds a second plugin, ref-verifier, which checks metadata against Crossref and OpenAlex.
ilker-golcuk/zotero-plugins.pain: Zotero hides each PDF in a folder named by internal key, so collecting the files for 40 references is awkward. This gathers them in one step.

dillemon/zotero-shortdoi-8-update.does: Looks up full DOIs or shortDOIs for selected items through Crossref and the shortDOI service, and checks stored DOIs, marking invalid ones. Also strips prefixes such as doi: and publisher URLs from the DOI field.
dillemon/zotero-shortdoi-8-update.pain: Items often lack a DOI or carry a malformed one. A fork of bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi; its README doesn't say what it changes.

groele/zoteropreview.does: A citation preview pane for Zotero 7, maintained as a compatibility and interface fix of the original ZoteroPreview7. It documents goals rather than specific features.
groele/zoteropreview.pain: Keeps an older preview plugin working on newer Zotero versions. A fork of dcartertod/zotero-plugins; its README doesn't say what it changes.

mrbell/copy-item-uri-zotero-plugin.does: Adds Copy Item URI to the item right-click menu, putting a zotero://select link for the selected item on the clipboard. Works for personal and group libraries.
mrbell/copy-item-uri-zotero-plugin.pain: Linking to a specific Zotero item from notes or other apps otherwise needs the link built by hand. Pasting the link opens and selects the item.

junyankang/paper-nexus.does: Previews a paper when you hover a citation in the PDF reader, with translated abstracts, a read-later list and an author network from your library. Now merged into Paper Loom, which this version installs. Chinese interface.
junyankang/paper-nexus.pain: Following a citation or an author normally means leaving Zotero to search. Citation lookups and the author network need no account; translation can use your own model API.

howarddong711/paperpet.does: Shows a draggable pet in Zotero that changes state as you read, and builds local reading reports with heatmaps and trends. Supports character packs and backups. Everything runs locally.
howarddong711/paperpet.pain: For readers who want a record of how much and when they read, without an efficiency score or any upload. It is for self-review, not goals or rankings.

coekfung/zotero-extra.does: Fetches short conference names from Semantic Scholar for items with a DOI and saves them in the Extra field as shortConferenceName. An optional Semantic Scholar API key speeds requests up.
coekfung/zotero-extra.pain: Conference papers often lack a short venue name, which citation styles or the Linter plugin may need. This fills it in automatically.

loonghfut/zotero-siyuan.does: Sends a PDF annotation and its comment to SiYuan with one click, as quote and note blocks with a link back to Zotero. Targets your daily note, a chosen document or one document per paper.
loonghfut/zotero-siyuan.pain: Moving highlights from Zotero into SiYuan by hand loses the source link. This keeps a jump-back link and avoids sending the same annotation twice by accident. Chinese interface.

migueldlm/author-harvester.does: Imports an author's complete publication list from OpenAlex into your library through a three-step wizard, skipping items you already have. Can download PDFs with rate limiting and produces a report with retry links, exportable to CSV or HTML.
migueldlm/author-harvester.pain: Building a library of one author's works by hand is slow and creates duplicates. Re-running later adds only new publications. Bulk downloading can get your IP blocked by publishers.

victor-levindo/nuvem-palavras-z.does: Builds word clouds from the text of PDFs, from author keywords inside them, or from manual tags, for one item or a whole collection. Also counts a chosen word or phrase per article and exports images or CSV. Mainly Portuguese, with seven interface languages.
victor-levindo/nuvem-palavras-z.pain: Gives a quick view of the vocabulary across a set of papers and where a term appears, without exporting text to another tool.

arrancurran/zostats.does: Adds a Metrics section to the item pane with a citations-by-year chart and up to 100 citing articles, from Semantic Scholar. Shows total and influential counts; an API key is optional.
arrancurran/zostats.pain: Zotero shows no citation history. This sends only the item's DOI, PMID, arXiv ID or title to Semantic Scholar to see how a paper is being cited.

kjamison/zoterename.does: A file renaming utility for Zotero. The project says only that it adds a few helpful features and points to a website, so specifics are unknown.
kjamison/zoterename.pain: Probably for people who want attachment files renamed from item data. Legacy plugin, it runs only on older Zotero versions.

acavalkyrie/zotero-handwritten-notes.does: Creates blank, ruled or grid A4 PDFs attached to an item, or standalone, for handwriting on a tablet. Adds or deletes trailing pages without disturbing annotations. Japanese interface; for Zotero 10 desktop.
acavalkyrie/zotero-handwritten-notes.pain: Lets you write notes by hand on an iPad with Apple Pencil while reading on the computer, with ink synced as normal Zotero annotations.

teamlilysai/zotero-readray.does: Adds Read with Readray to the item menu, opening the item's PDF in Chrome where the Readray extension starts summarising it. Needs Chrome and the Readray extension with file access allowed. Verified on macOS only.
teamlilysai/zotero-readray.pain: Lets you hand a paper from Zotero to Readray in one click instead of locating and opening the file yourself.

septyagu/zotero-theme-toggle.does: Adds a toolbar button next to Sync that cycles Zotero between system, light and dark appearance modes with one click, using Zotero's own setting.
septyagu/zotero-theme-toggle.pain: Changing appearance normally means opening Settings. This makes it a single click while you work in the library or reader.

paolovolterra/zotpush.does: Exports selected items to standalone Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, notes, annotations and annotation images, from the Tools or right-click menu. Read-only toward Zotero. Works with Obsidian or any Markdown tool. Italian interface.
paolovolterra/zotpush.pain: For people who keep reading notes in Markdown. It copies one way only, and re-exports keep what you wrote below the generated block.

zgdd12345/aipaperanalysis.does: Analyses selected papers with an AI model from the right-click menu, using editable prompts, and saves the result as a tagged child note. Supports OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Doubao or a custom endpoint, with your own API key.
zgdd12345/aipaperanalysis.pain: Gets a structured first read of many papers in one batch, covering summary, methods, novelty and limitations. The planned chart dashboard is not built yet.

jyluo1994/paper-acquisition-zotero.does: Gets PDFs for selected items through a local helper service that uses a browser, with login or captcha steps confirmed by you. Offers a queue, optional automatic fetching of new items, institutional profiles, proxy settings and an optional Camoufox browser.
jyluo1994/paper-acquisition-zotero.pain: For papers that Zotero's own Find Full Text cannot fetch behind publisher logins. Needs the helper service running locally; it works around publisher anti-bot checks.

zjysnow/paperpilot.does: An AI research assistant in the reader or a standalone window. Chat with the open PDF, figures and your library, save answers as notes or Markdown, and run multi-step Agent Mode tasks with approval cards. Works with local models such as Ollama or any compatible endpoint.
zjysnow/paperpilot.pain: Keeps AI reading help inside Zotero and lets you run it entirely on a local model. Agent Mode needs a model that supports tool calling.

mcburton/vinculum-zotero.does: Adds Copy Zotero Link to the item and collection right-click menus, putting a zotero://select link on the clipboard. Item links keep the collection you are viewing.
mcburton/vinculum-zotero.pain: Gives you a link to paste into notes or documents that opens the exact item or collection in Zotero.

jnsheff/zotero-legal-translators.does: Installs web translators for legal sites. The Zotero Connector can then save cases, statutes, regulations, articles and treatises from Westlaw, Lexis+, Cornell LII, the Federal Register, Bloomberg Law and LegiScan.
jnsheff/zotero-legal-translators.pain: Zotero has no translators for these legal databases, so saves arrive incomplete. Westlaw and Lexis+ need your own subscription, and the author has tested them on saved pages, not yet a live session.

nexdep/zotero-npdfpages.does: Adds a sortable PDF Pages column to the item list and a PDF Pages condition to Advanced Search, based on Zotero's indexed page totals. Parent items show the sum across their PDFs.
nexdep/zotero-npdfpages.pain: Zotero can't sort or search by length. This helps you find short papers to read or filter long documents.

srmateos/zotero-pinakes.does: Lists the references of the selected paper or open PDF in the item pane, in the paper's own order, and imports any cited work with one click. Uses Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, DBLP and Crossref, with a PDF fallback. Finds published versions of preprints.
srmateos/zotero-pinakes.pain: Following a paper's bibliography normally means copying DOIs by hand. This shows which references are already in your library and imports the rest, singly or in batches.

dvanoni/zotero-plugin-sandbox.does: A sandbox for testing Zotero plugins, with no documented features of its own.
dvanoni/zotero-plugin-sandbox.pain: Probably a developer's test project rather than a plugin for everyday use.

aderavi/zotero-scrape-update-report.does: Looks up selected papers in DBLP, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex, updates standard fields, adds keyword tags, and writes a child note reporting what it found. A mismatch in title, date or DOI opens a prompt before any change. An optional Semantic Scholar key raises rate limits.
aderavi/zotero-scrape-update-report.pain: Cleans metadata in one click without silent overwrites. A fork of Creling/Zotero-Metadata-Scraper; its README doesn't say what it changes.

louis1642/zotero-trackpad-navigation.does: Maps two-finger swipes on a Mac trackpad to Back and Forward through your location history in Zotero's PDF and EPUB reader. Works in tabs and split views and makes no network requests.
louis1642/zotero-trackpad-navigation.pain: Lets you return to where you were after following an internal link, with the swipe gesture familiar from browsers. macOS only.

dingzy53/mineru-for-zotero.does: Sends PDFs to the MinerU service, online or on your own server, and shows the parsed text, table and formula boxes in the reader for copying. Includes a task manager and export to Markdown and BibTeX. Needs a MinerU API key for the online service.
dingzy53/mineru-for-zotero.pain: Copying formulas and tables out of PDFs is error-prone. A fork of Asianfleet/mineru-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

iciriceciecr/zotero-literature-analizer.does: Generates a ten-section HTML interpretation report from a PDF, saved as a Zotero child note, using the DeepSeek API. A manual mode extracts text and figures for another chatbot. Needs Python and PyMuPDF; Chinese and English.
iciriceciecr/zotero-literature-analizer.pain: Gives a structured read of a paper, covering design, results, limitations and writing templates, with figures embedded in the note.

weicheng14159/zotero_paper2speech.does: Reads the selected paper's PDF aloud with Apple's built-in macOS voices, from a Play button beside the search box or in the reader toolbar. Voice and speed are set in preferences. Local only, no API key.
weicheng14159/zotero_paper2speech.pain: Lets you listen to papers instead of reading them. There is no pause, and scanned PDFs need OCR first.

luxun-spec/zotero-papercompare.does: Builds comparison tables of experiments across papers, with several experiments per paper. Each cell holds your summary and saved PDF highlights, and a quote opens the original annotation. Exports Markdown and CSV, with JSON backups. No API key.
luxun-spec/zotero-papercompare.pain: Comparing results across papers usually happens in a spreadsheet that loses the source. This keeps each value linked to its evidence.

zhanglinqi-07/zotero-pdf2zh-body-only.does: Translates PDFs into Chinese bilingual versions, optionally skipping references and appendices. Adds a reader chat sidebar and deep-reading notes saved as child notes. Needs a local backend from the release package, plus a model API or free service.
zhanglinqi-07/zotero-pdf2zh-body-only.pain: Reading papers in a second language is slow. It builds on the PDF2zh translator and adds checks for untranslated text; the interface is Chinese-language.

aaaarjimedes/zotero-pdf2zh-companion.does: Adds a Server button that starts a local PDF2zh Server and opens its page in Zotero. Also adds translation checks, contents rebuilding and layout checks. Needs the official PDF2zh plugin and a Python setup; Chinese interface.
aaaarjimedes/zotero-pdf2zh-companion.pain: Makes the PDF2zh translation setup easier to run on Windows and improves its output. It does not replace the main plugin.

windingwind/zotero-spotlight-search.does: Indexes your Zotero library and groups into macOS Spotlight, so items appear in Spotlight results even when Zotero is not running. A helper app, ZotLight, is installed automatically. You can choose which fields are indexed.
windingwind/zotero-spotlight-search.pain: Finding a reference normally means opening Zotero first. This lets you search your library from the Mac's own search.

cpsimpson/zotero-todoist-bridge.does: Adds a Send To Todoist right-click submenu with one entry per template, creating tasks from selected papers. Templates use Todoist quick-add syntax and placeholders such as title, year and URL. Needs a Todoist personal API token.
cpsimpson/zotero-todoist-bridge.pain: Turns a reading list into Todoist tasks with a link back to the paper, without retyping titles.

xinxzk/zotero-wakatime.does: Sends WakaTime heartbeats while a reader tab is active, so PDF reading time appears in your WakaTime dashboard. Uses the first collection as the project name and can send item titles or anonymised IDs. Needs your WakaTime API key.
xinxzk/zotero-wakatime.pain: For people who already log coding time in WakaTime and want reading time tracked alongside it.

zhuhu00/obsitero.does: Syncs each Zotero parent item into one Obsidian Markdown file, appending its Zotero notes and keeping your own notes. Generates a Zotero.base file for Obsidian Bases. Auto-syncs monitored collections. One-way, Zotero to Obsidian.
zhuhu00/obsitero.pain: Keeps an Obsidian literature folder in step with Zotero in the style of Notero. Fields you edit in Obsidian are preserved when you sync again.

dreamperday/paperlens-zotero.does: An AI sidebar in the PDF reader for asking about selected text or boxed figures. Also gives paragraph annotations, overviews and claim checking. Needs your own OpenAI-compatible provider and key, or a local model; Chinese interface.
dreamperday/paperlens-zotero.pain: Keeps AI reading help beside the PDF, with evidence checking to see whether the paper supports a claim.

eginez/zotero-ai-reply.does: Answers commented PDF annotations for one selected paper with a single OpenAI-compatible request, writing each answer into the annotation as an AI Reply block. You set the endpoint and model; a key is optional, and a local server works.
eginez/zotero-ai-reply.pain: Lets you put questions in annotations while reading and get answers later in the same place. Rerunning replaces earlier replies.

aramosalv/zotero-apa7-uoc.does: Adds an APA 7th edition citation style adapted to the Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) rules. It puts the author's full first name in square brackets after the initials, drops the Oxford comma and the 'Retrieved from' phrase, and picks the final conjunction by language (Spanish, Catalan, Occitan, English, German).
aramosalv/zotero-apa7-uoc.pain: UOC students must follow a variant of APA 7 that stock Zotero styles don't produce, so bibliographies otherwise need hand editing. Bracketed names depend on full first names being stored in your library.

junhwan26/zotero-margin-notes.does: Shows the comments on your PDF highlights, underlines and note annotations as cards in the page margin of Zotero's reader. Comments render as Markdown, can be edited in place, and sit on the left or right depending on where the annotation is.
junhwan26/zotero-margin-notes.pain: Annotation comments normally live only in the sidebar, away from the text they refer to. This keeps them beside the passage, including in two-column papers. The interface is in English or Korean.

weicheng14159/zotero-md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown files with Python and attaches the result to the same item. It runs on import, from a right-click menu, or on the whole library from the Tools menu. Needs Python 3 with docling or pymupdf4llm installed.
weicheng14159/zotero-md.pain: Machine-readable text from papers is useful for LLM workflows and for note tools such as Obsidian or Logseq, and Zotero has no built-in PDF to Markdown export.

luciferer/zotero-open-router.does: Controls what happens when you double-click items and attachments. It opens the main article PDF ahead of supplementary files, previews Markdown, CSV, JSON, text and zip files in Zotero tabs, and sends files to apps you choose with Option + double-click.
luciferer/zotero-open-router.pain: Double-clicking a parent item can open a supplementary PDF, and other file types fall through to whatever app your system picks. This gives you predictable routing without changing Zotero's global reader settings.

akirk20-code/zotero-spellcheck-plugin.does: Adds spell check suggestions and dictionary options to the right-click menu in Zotero's note editor and in annotation comments.
akirk20-code/zotero-spellcheck-plugin.pain: Zotero's note and annotation fields underline misspellings but don't offer corrections in the context menu, so fixing typos means retyping the word. Early-stage: its documentation is still the plugin template's.

leauny/zoterotransnator.does: Translates PDFs into bilingual notes. It runs OCR with Baidu PaddleOCR-VL, translates with DeepL or an OpenAI-compatible model, and can explain formulas with an LLM. Shows a cost estimate first and handles batches. Needs an OCR token and a DeepL or OpenAI key.
leauny/zoterotransnator.pain: Translating a whole paper by hand means copying text, losing tables and formulas along the way. This produces a note with original and translation side by side. Alpha release; it currently translates only into one pair of languages as configured.

siyuanj/zotero-author-profiles.does: Adds a Corresponding Author row to the item pane that shows a generated profile of the paper's corresponding author, written in Chinese. It finds candidates from PMC XML, PDF text and OpenAlex, adds Semantic Scholar data, and caches the result as a child note.
siyuanj/zotero-author-profiles.pain: For readers who want to know who the corresponding author is and what they work on without searching elsewhere. Generating profiles uses the API address, key and model set in the separate AIdea plugin.

ausanx/zotero-card-library.does: Opens a separate card-style view of your library in its own window, with a cover image taken from each paper's main figure. Browse by collection or tag, search, sort, and mark items unread, reading or read. Details open in a second window. Nothing is uploaded.
ausanx/zotero-card-library.pain: The standard item list is dense text. A card view makes a large library easier to scan visually. Reading status and colours are stored in the plugin only, and the interface is mainly in Simplified Chinese.

jaehho/zotero-citegraph.does: Draws the citation relationships between the items in a collection or selection as a force-directed graph. Hover for details, size and colour nodes by field, and add a Citations section to the item pane. Works offline, with OpenAlex data fetched only on request.
jaehho/zotero-citegraph.pain: Zotero has no way to see which papers in your library cite each other. This shows how a set of papers builds on one another without exporting to another tool.

oroites/ccf-for-zotero.does: Shows CCF (A/B/C and T1/T2/T3) and Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) zone 1 to 4 ranking badges in two item list columns. It matches by DOI, ISSN or venue name from built-in offline data, with manual overrides and an Extra field hint for venues. Mainly for Chinese computing research.
oroites/ccf-for-zotero.pain: Looking up a venue's CCF or CAS rank by hand for every paper is slow. A fork of nyaru177/ccf-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

juandodyk/my-zotero-ocr.does: Replaces the old invisible OCR layer in scanned PDFs using OCRmyPDF, without re-rendering visible pages, and can detect and remove common watermarks. It swaps the file behind the existing attachment, so annotations are kept, and can store the original as a backup.
juandodyk/my-zotero-ocr.pain: Downloads such as JSTOR scans often carry a poor text layer that breaks search and copying. This redoes the text layer and keeps your annotations and links intact.

zhang-dut/zotero-file.does: A ZotFile-style attachment manager for Zotero 7 that renames, moves and attaches PDFs and other files to items. The project itself tells users to use Zotero Attanger by MuiseDestiny instead.
zhang-dut/zotero-file.pain: A fork of daidaishengweinan/zotero-file; its README doesn't say what it changes.

gronuj/zotero-paper-buddy.does: Lets you ask an AI model about passages you highlight in the PDF reader, with answers in a sidebar thread and a Q&A child note on the item. Works with Claude through the Anthropic API or any OpenAI-compatible API such as Ollama. Needs your own API key.
gronuj/zotero-paper-buddy.pain: Asking an AI about a paper usually means copying text into a separate chat. Here you ask where you read, can include figures or the whole paper as context, and the Q&A is saved with the item.

douxy1994/zotero_paper_download.does: Adds a right-click action that downloads full text for items with a DOI and imports the PDF as an attachment. It calls local tools, Paper-fetch first and then ScanSci, and checks the file matches the item. Needs those tools installed; tested on macOS only.
douxy1994/zotero_paper_download.pain: Find Full Text often fails behind paywalls. This chains several download routes, including an interactive publisher or institutional login, before falling back to Zotero's own open access lookup.

lumiazure/zotero-pdf-copy.does: Finds the PDF file for a Zotero item and copies it out of the library.
lumiazure/zotero-pdf-copy.pain: For people who need the actual PDF file from an item, for example to send or move it, rather than opening it in Zotero. No further documentation is available.

p1aintiff/zotero-rule-outline.does: Generates a bookmark outline for a PDF using local rules based on font size and numbered headings, then writes it into the PDF. You review and edit the detected headings and page numbers first. Runs entirely on your machine with no API key.
p1aintiff/zotero-rule-outline.pain: Papers and books without bookmarks are hard to navigate. This builds a table of contents and writes it into the original file, keeping the attachment and its annotations. The interface is in Chinese.

nova-meteor/zotero-sentence-hover.does: Translates the English sentence under your mouse in the PDF reader into Chinese, with no selection needed. Matching words are highlighted in the original and the translation as you move, and a button can pre-translate the full paper. Needs an API address, model name and key.
nova-meteor/zotero-sentence-hover.pain: Reading English papers in Chinese usually means selecting text and waiting for a translation each time. Hovering shows the sentence translation at once and caches it for later reading.

icychlorine/paper-connections.does: Adds a graph workspace where you drag papers in as nodes, draw connection edges between them, and group them into topics. Selection syncs with the item list, double-click opens the PDF, and a graph can be exported as an SVG image.
icychlorine/paper-connections.pain: Zotero collections can't show how individual papers relate to each other. This gives you a visual map of a topic that you build by hand.

woif-sha/reference-for-zotro.does: Adds a reader sidebar that lists a paper's references and the papers that cite it, using OpenCitations, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar for details and abstracts. Can suggest what to read first with an AI model. Needs MinerU Markdown of the PDF; AI needs a key or Codex sign-in.
woif-sha/reference-for-zotro.pain: Following a reference means copying the title, searching elsewhere and checking it is the right paper. This keeps references, citing papers and abstracts in the reader. Interface text is mainly Chinese.

derican/zotero-annotes.does: Automatically creates notes from your PDF annotations.
derican/zotero-annotes.pain: An early-stage plugin for turning annotations into notes; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.

windfollowingheart/zotero-claw.does: A chat panel for talking to an AI assistant about your PDFs. It needs a separate backend program (zotero-claw.exe) that you download and configure with your LLM. Supports file uploads, streaming Markdown answers and saved history. Windows only.
windfollowingheart/zotero-claw.pain: Lets you discuss the PDF you are reading with an OpenClaw-based assistant without leaving Zotero. You must run the backend service yourself.

toustifer/zotero-dsh.does: Embeds a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) chat panel in the Zotero item pane and adds Send to DSH and Ask DSH buttons to the text selection popup in the reader. A companion plugin lets DSH search, read, annotate and organise your library. Needs DSH installed.
toustifer/zotero-dsh.pain: Connects Zotero and the DeepSeek Harness agent both ways, so you can quote a passage into an AI session or let the agent work on your papers. Documentation is mainly in Chinese.

nebula0/zotero-llm-wiki.does: Paper Chat adds an Ask Claude panel to the PDF reader: answers quote the paper, each quote is highlighted in the PDF, and page links jump there. The Q&A is saved as a note. Needs Claude Code or an Anthropic API key. The repo also has Claude Code skills and an Obsidian wiki.
nebula0/zotero-llm-wiki.pain: Asking about a paper in a chat window loses the link to the exact passage. Here every quoted passage is highlighted in the PDF, so you can check it.

zbhou2002/iris-zotero.does: An AI reading assistant in the reader sidebar. Ask about a selected passage, translate text in place, dictate questions with local Whisper speech to text, and highlight a paper's contributions and evidence. Connect a Codex account sign-in or your own API endpoint and key.
zbhou2002/iris-zotero.pain: Understanding a paper often means copying passages into a separate chat app. Iris keeps questions, translation and voice input next to the PDF.

kianmax0/zotero-chatgpt.does: Reads papers with ChatGPT and a Codex agent. Chat mode opens the official ChatGPT page with the paper's context prepared. Agent mode uses Codex to explain, write highlights, mark figures, and find, fetch and organise items. Agent needs a separate Codex sign-in.
kianmax0/zotero-chatgpt.pain: Moving between a PDF and ChatGPT means copying text and metadata by hand. This prepares the context for you, and agent edits are previewed for approval except explicitly requested highlights.

nakamuratakumu/zotero-gemini-pdf.does: Adds an LLM chat panel to the PDF reader. It uploads the item's PDFs to Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic when chat starts, lets you ask about selected text from the context menu, and stores chat history on the item. Renders Markdown and KaTeX. Needs an API key for your provider.
nakamuratakumu/zotero-gemini-pdf.pain: Lets you question the paper you are reading without leaving Zotero. Note that PDFs are sent to the provider you choose, and the plugin is still under active development.

dawaltconley/zotero-paged-snapshots.does: Adds page buttons for moving through web page snapshots in the Zotero reader.
dawaltconley/zotero-paged-snapshots.pain: Scrolling through long snapshots is awkward on some devices, such as e-ink readers. Page buttons make navigation easier.

grainrainandy/zotero-storage-cleaner.does: Finds folders in Zotero's storage directory that no item in the database refers to and moves them to a recoverable quarantine folder after you confirm. A Tools menu entry opens the quarantine or empties it for good. Supports Zotero 8 and 9.
grainrainandy/zotero-storage-cleaner.pain: Failed imports and interrupted operations can leave orphaned attachment folders that waste disk space. This removes them with a way back before anything is deleted. Documentation is in Chinese.

alfredhw/zotero-to-voyant.does: Sends the PDF, text and HTML attachments of selected items to Voyant Tools for text analysis. It uploads them, creates a corpus and opens it in your browser, from the right-click menu or the Tools menu. Needs an internet connection.
alfredhw/zotero-to-voyant.pain: Text analysis of a set of papers in Voyant normally means exporting and uploading files by hand. This does it from the items you select, which suits digital humanities work.

liyang-tju/ai-web-for-zotero.does: Opens AI chat websites (ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Studio, DeepSeek, Kimi, Zhipu Qingyan, or a custom address) in a panel beside the reader. Upload the current PDF or several attachments, bookmark conversations per item, and export chats as a note, HTML or Markdown.
liyang-tju/ai-web-for-zotero.pain: Uses your logged-in website account instead of an API key, so you can discuss papers with an AI without setting up keys. Documentation is mainly in Chinese.

ttungx/easyread-zotero-sync.does: Syncs full paper translations finished in the EasyRead app into Zotero as offline-readable HTML attachments. Right-click to sync up to 20 items at a time. Needs the EasyRead local service running.
ttungx/easyread-zotero-sync.pain: Lets you read translated papers on a phone through Zotero's normal file sync. It warns before overwriting an attachment that has annotations. A candidate build, with Android testing still pending.

kcodea516/zotero-ai-reader.does: A reader sidebar for asking an OpenAI-compatible model about the open PDF. Answers link to source pages, and it can search other papers in your library, take image questions, generate images and add highlights with comments you can undo. English or Chinese; needs your own API.
kcodea516/zotero-ai-reader.pain: Keeps AI questions beside the paper instead of in a browser chat, and can mark relevant passages on the PDF for later reading.

shaexys/zotero-auto-relate.does: Adds Related Items links between a new paper and the references and citing works already in your library, using OpenAlex citation data. It runs when items are added or from a right-click command, and needs papers to have DOIs. Setting an email address gives faster OpenAlex limits.
shaexys/zotero-auto-relate.pain: Citation links between papers in your library otherwise have to be added by hand. The relations can be exported to note tools such as Obsidian through Better BibTeX.

visserle/zotero-google-this.does: Adds a Google this entry to the reader's right-click menu for selected text in PDFs and EPUBs, opening a Google search in your browser.
visserle/zotero-google-this.pain: Looking up an unfamiliar term otherwise means copying it and switching to a browser. Requires Zotero 8 or later.

dawaltconley/zotero-grayscale-ui.does: Provides partial support for grayscale interface options in Zotero.
dawaltconley/zotero-grayscale-ui.pain: Aims to make Zotero more usable on e-ink devices, which have no colour display.

linjiangxian110/zotero-local-academic-tt.does: Reads selected English text in the PDF reader aloud. A Local TTS Read button in the selection popup sends text to a local Kokoro speech server on your machine and plays the audio in Zotero, with a floating pause button. Windows only, with Python 3.12 needed.
linjiangxian110/zotero-local-academic-tt.pain: Zotero's own Read Aloud is not an option here; this gives a local, offline text to speech for academic passages, so selected text is not sent to a cloud service.

zhongyangchuwu/zotero-neo.does: A Neovim-inspired keyboard layer for Zotero's main window, reader and notes. It adds Vim-style navigation, keyboard text selection, link hints, a fuzzy picker, a command palette, tag actions and configurable keymaps. Targets Zotero 10.
zhongyangchuwu/zotero-neo.pain: For people who prefer to work from the keyboard rather than the mouse, across the library, PDF reading, tagging and note editing.

commanderpho/zotero-plugin-noduplicates.does: Detects when an item being added or imported duplicates an existing one, blocks it and warns you.
commanderpho/zotero-plugin-noduplicates.pain: Prevents duplicates from entering the library, instead of cleaning them up afterwards. Early-stage for Zotero 9; its documentation is still the plugin template's and describes no features yet.

lzhmarkk/zotero-relationgraph.does: Reads references from the PDFs of selected items, then shows a paper citation graph, an author relation graph and a tag graph from buttons at the top.
lzhmarkk/zotero-relationgraph.pain: Gives a visual overview of how the papers, authors and tags in your library connect. References come from PDF parsing only, so results depend on the file.

karwanoa/zoterocitationcountsmanager.does: Fetches citation counts from Google Scholar, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar or INSPIRE-HEP, or a best count across them. Counts go in the Extra field and a sortable item list column. Supports Zotero 7 to 10.
karwanoa/zoterocitationcountsmanager.pain: Shows how often each paper is cited without looking it up elsewhere, and lets you sort your library by it. An enhanced fork-style update of earlier Citation Counts Manager plugins.

raykr/better-sync.does: A file sync solution for using your library across several devices.
raykr/better-sync.pain: An early-stage plugin for syncing files between devices; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.

partlyjadedyouth/marktero.does: Creates a Markdown literature note in your Obsidian vault for each new Zotero item, automatically or from a right-click or Tools menu command. Notes use Better BibTeX citation keys, PDF links, and a template you can change. One way only: it never writes back to Zotero.
partlyjadedyouth/marktero.pain: Keeps an Obsidian literature note folder in step with Zotero without copying metadata by hand, and never overwrites or deletes existing files.

kadzo/zotero-attachment-formats.does: Adds an item list column showing the file extensions of each item's attachments, for example PDF (2), JPG or DOCX. The column label is translated into 17 languages. Display only; it changes no library data. Built for Zotero 10.
kadzo/zotero-attachment-formats.pain: In a large library, a title doesn't tell you whether an item has a PDF, an image, a Word file or nothing attached. This shows it at a glance.

leisongju/zotero-hjfy-split-reader-cn.does: Fetches the Chinese translation PDF of an arXiv paper from hjfy.top and opens it beside the original in a split-view reader. Supports batch download, arXiv ID detection from DOI, URL or title, and optional auto fetch for new items. A login cookie may be needed.
leisongju/zotero-hjfy-split-reader-cn.pain: For Chinese readers who want an arXiv paper and its translation side by side. It only works for papers with an arXiv version. Documentation is in Chinese.

sameggleton/zotero-organiser.does: Suggests tags for your papers from a taxonomy you define, with a sidebar to accept, dismiss or override each one. Includes 25 discipline profiles based on Australian Fields of Research and runs local embedding models, with an optional Python command line tool and daemon.
sameggleton/zotero-organiser.pain: Keeps tagging consistent across a large library. Human tags are never removed, nothing is uploaded, and PDFs are not read.

forguse/zotero-paper-companion.does: A reader sidebar with ongoing AI question answering, translation of selected text, Markdown notes and a vocabulary list with review. Uses your own DeepSeek API key, a ChatGPT authorisation, or the ChatGPT website. Interface in Chinese.
forguse/zotero-paper-companion.pain: Keeps questions, translations, notes and new words for each paper in one place. Questions and selected text go to the model service you choose.

beichenzhao/zotero-remind-me.does: Shows a small card when you hover over an item, with your Brief, Novelty and Limitation notes for the paper. Write them yourself or have an AI draft them from the abstract and PDF, one item or in batches. Notes are saved in the Extra field. AI needs your own key or Ollama.
beichenzhao/zotero-remind-me.pain: In a library of hundreds of papers, titles blur together and abstracts are too long to skim. This keeps a one-glance summary on each item.

lsx-uniwue/bibsonomy-zotero-sync.does: Syncs items from Zotero to your BibSonomy account, including PDF attachments, and updates or deletes them in BibSonomy when they change in Zotero. Syncs automatically or manually and can copy a share URL for a publication. Needs a BibSonomy username and API token.
lsx-uniwue/bibsonomy-zotero-sync.pain: Keeps a BibSonomy publication list in step with Zotero without entering references twice.

minhhaduong/search-works-for-zotero.does: An experimental add-on that prepares Zotero 10's structured-text caches in the background, one attachment at a time, with an on and off switch. The repo is also a workshop on semantic search for Zotero.
minhhaduong/search-works-for-zotero.pain: Aimed at people exploring semantic retrieval in Zotero, a feature not yet available in stock Zotero. It is experimental, so check its known bugs before installing.

greycatproductions/sentai.does: Adds semantic search to a Zotero 9 library: it indexes your PDFs as embeddings in a local SQLite database and finds passages by meaning. A chat tab answers questions with citations to your papers. Embeddings use a default server, Azure or Ollama; chat uses Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible or Ollama.
greycatproductions/sentai.pain: Keyword search misses papers that use different wording. Searching by meaning helps you find the right passage. Indexed data stays on your device.

jlupini/zotero-avo-toolkit-dist.does: Turns a collection's PDF annotations into a Word-ready reference list. Each annotation becomes a line with a live citekey link that opens the PDF at that annotation, as a Zotero note or a .docx file.
jlupini/zotero-avo-toolkit-dist.pain: Pulling highlights from many PDFs into a document by hand means copy-paste and footnote clean-up. This produces the list in one click, with links back to the source.

muisedestiny/zotero-claudero.does: An AI research assistant pane in Zotero that answers questions about selected papers, annotations and figures, with clickable links back to the source passages. Needs Node.js and a Claude Code, Codex or DeepSeek Harness install.
muisedestiny/zotero-claudero.pain: Asking an AI about your papers usually means copying text out of Zotero. This keeps the conversation, evidence and notes inside Zotero, using the AI tool you already have.

elsevoid/zotero-close-to-tray.does: Hides the Zotero window to the Windows notification area when you close it, instead of quitting. Click the tray icon to bring it back, or right-click it for Show Zotero and Quit Zotero.
elsevoid/zotero-close-to-tray.pain: Closing Zotero stops the browser connector and word processor plugins from working. Keeping it running in the tray avoids restarting it each time.

grantzachary/zotero-highlighter.does: Renames the highlight colours in the Zotero reader so each means something to you, such as Yellow to Key finding. The names show in the colour picker, the annotation sidebar and the item pane.
grantzachary/zotero-highlighter.pain: Zotero's highlight colours have no meaning until you remember them. Labels make a colour scheme readable, and the change is display-only, so your annotations stay untouched.

ltzyl/zotero-paper-companion.does: Supports Chinese-language reading of English papers: bilingual side-by-side windows, translated titles and abstracts, and local summaries via Ollama. It also fetches missing PDFs and draws in-library citation graphs.
ltzyl/zotero-paper-companion.pain: For Chinese readers, English papers mean constant switching to translation tools. This sets up the models and pages locally on Apple Silicon Macs, though translation goes through Bing.

nexdep/zotero-ntags.does: Adds a sortable Tag Number column to the item list, showing how many tags each item has. The column is hidden until you enable it from the column picker.
nexdep/zotero-ntags.pain: Zotero can't sort items by how many tags they carry. This helps you find untagged or heavily tagged items.

kinetic27/zotero_paper_translate.does: Translates PDF papers page by page in the Zotero reader, keeping maths, figures and tables as the original PDF image. Saves translations locally and can translate a whole document using Google, Bing, DeepLX, Claude, Gemini or ChatGPT.
kinetic27/zotero_paper_translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate. It adds page-based PDF translation that preserves equations and tables, and signing in with a ChatGPT account instead of an API key.

gchapron/zoterothumbfile.does: Shows a PDF as a contact sheet of page thumbnails, like Preview on macOS, with an adjustable thumbnail size. Click a page to open it in Zotero's normal reader.
gchapron/zoterothumbfile.pain: Zotero's reader only scrolls through pages one after another. A grid makes it quick to scan a long document and jump to a figure or section.

thanejoss/ccfa.does: Adds a CCFA column to the item list that shows the short name of a CCF A-class journal or conference, such as CVPR or TPAMI. It uses the 2026 seventh-edition catalogue and works offline.
thanejoss/ccfa.pain: Computer science researchers in China need to know which publications are CCF A-class. This shows it in the library without manual tagging.

shamus-li/zotero-citation-cards.does: Click an in-text citation in Zotero's PDF reader to see the cited paper's title, authors, abstract and links in a card styled like Google Scholar's. It uses Google Scholar when you sign in, otherwise OpenAlex.
shamus-li/zotero-citation-cards.pain: Checking a reference normally means leaving the PDF to search for it. The card shows the cited paper right where you read.

anemone95/zotero-copy-pdf-path.does: Adds Copy PDF Path to the item right-click menu. It copies the file path of selected PDF attachments, or of the PDFs under selected items, one path per line.
anemone95/zotero-copy-pdf-path.pain: Zotero hides where attachments live on disk. This gives you the paths for scripts, other apps or file managers.

solitern/zotero-inbox-organizer.does: Sorts items in a 00-Inbox collection into topic subcollections under AI Organized, using an OpenAI-compatible model. It shows a preview before changing anything and leaves low-confidence items in the Inbox. Needs an API key.
solitern/zotero-inbox-organizer.pain: New papers pile up unsorted in an inbox. This files them for you while you confirm the result. Titles, abstracts, creators and tags are sent to your provider, not PDFs.

februarysea/zotero-paper-lens.does: Translates selected PDF text in Zotero using Codex models through your ChatGPT account. Translations appear in the selection popup and reading pane, can be saved as notes, and are cached locally.
februarysea/zotero-paper-lens.pain: Reading papers in another language means pasting passages into a translator. This translates in place and needs a ChatGPT plan, not an API key.

dawaltconley/zotero-pdf-content-flow.does: Makes PDF paging in the Zotero reader zoom to and step through the page's content column by column. You can set one to four columns, draw a content area and choose page or continuous stepping.
dawaltconley/zotero-pdf-content-flow.pain: Scrolling is awkward on e-ink screens and other devices where scrolling is slow. This steps through each column so text stays large and readable.

korhonenaleksi/zotero-research-radar.does: Fetches new articles from journals you follow and ranks them High, Possible or Rest against your keyword rules and watched authors. Matches go into a Radar collection via Crossref, each with a note on why. AI ranking is optional.
korhonenaleksi/zotero-research-radar.pain: Keeping up with new papers in your journals means checking feeds by hand. Radar filters them against your interests inside Zotero. It adds items to your library, so back it up first.

hegghammer/zotero-settings-key.does: Adds a configurable keyboard shortcut that toggles the Zotero Settings window. The default is Alt+S, and you change it in its own settings pane.
hegghammer/zotero-settings-key.pain: Zotero has no quick shortcut for opening its settings. This gives you one.

liotou/zotero-toc.does: Generates a missing table of contents for PDFs and EPUBs and writes it into the file, so the reader's Sommaire pane works. It detects headings from layout, with optional help from a local or remote model.
liotou/zotero-toc.pain: Many PDFs have no bookmarks, so the outline pane stays empty. The generated outline also works in other PDF readers. The interface is in French.

seancomeon/zotero7_json_importer_checker.does: Batch-imports references from JSON returned by a large language model, with title, introduction and DOI, and lets you visually check titles for hallucinations.
seancomeon/zotero7_json_importer_checker.pain: AI models invent plausible papers. This imports the real ones by DOI and shows whether the returned title matches. Its instructions are in Chinese.

thalloerupt/fusion_reader_for_zotero.does: Adds a toolbar button and right-click menu entry that open the selected Zotero PDF in the Fusion Reader app. Needs Fusion Reader installed.
thalloerupt/fusion_reader_for_zotero.pain: Gives Fusion Reader's document translation a one-click path from Zotero, so you skip finding and opening the file yourself.

lockfaiz/paper-notion-flow.does: Syncs Zotero papers into a Notion database and has a local AI tool (Codex CLI or Claude Code) write a reading guide under each paper's page. Needs a Notion integration token and a Python workspace.
lockfaiz/paper-notion-flow.pain: People who read in Notion otherwise add each paper and write summaries by hand. This automates the row and the guide from your Zotero metadata and PDFs.

hopeleeee/readerc.does: Underlines unfamiliar English words in Zotero PDFs and shows a Chinese meaning when you hover, chosen from the sentence by your own model API. Press Delete or Backspace to mark a word as known.
hopeleeee/readerc.pain: For Chinese readers of English papers, looking up words breaks reading flow. This gives context-based meanings in place and remembers the words you know.

leonezz/tasks-timeline-zotero.does: Adds a sidebar timeline for planning reading and research tasks stored as Zotero notes. It can add child task notes to items, repeat recurring tasks, and offers an AI assistant and an optional MCP server.
leonezz/tasks-timeline-zotero.pain: Zotero has no way to schedule reading. This puts to-dos on a timeline while keeping them as ordinary notes in your library.

wegene38/zotero-auto-sort.does: Scans a library or collection and suggests topic categories computed locally from titles, abstracts and tags. Tick the ones you want and it files items into subcollections under Auto-Sorted, leaving existing collections alone.
wegene38/zotero-auto-sort.pain: Sorting a large unorganised library by hand takes a long time. This proposes a structure without sending anything over the network.

p1aintiff/zotero-close-to-tray.does: Hides Zotero to the Windows system tray when you click the main window's close button, and keeps it running. Click the tray icon to restore it, or use its menu to quit.
p1aintiff/zotero-close-to-tray.pain: Closing Zotero normally quits it. This keeps it available in the background for Windows users on Zotero 10.

justushenke/zotero-copy-path.does: Adds right-click items that copy the file paths of PDF attachments, or the DOI or URL, of selected items to the clipboard. The menu is available in English and German.
justushenke/zotero-copy-path.pain: Getting a PDF's location or a DOI link out of Zotero takes several clicks. This does it in one step.

pengtb/zotero-custom-columns.does: Adds any custom columns to the item list, defined in a JSON file with a settings pane. Columns can take a field, a regular-expression match from it, or values like collections, note count and reading status.
pengtb/zotero-custom-columns.pain: Zotero columns only come from item fields, so things kept in Extra, like ratings, can't get their own column. This makes them sortable columns. Its interface is in Chinese and English.

fanyingfx/zotero-excerpt.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
fanyingfx/zotero-excerpt.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

qdryougi/zotero-mcp-tags.does: Runs a small local MCP server that lets AI agents batch add, remove or set tags on Zotero items by item key. It reports the before and after tags for each item.
qdryougi/zotero-mcp-tags.pain: A companion to zotero-mcp for agents that search your library. Keeping tag writing in a separate server gives agents a narrower write surface.

sjc88661/zotero-nature-reader.does: Shows a paper's full text as paragraph-by-paragraph English and Chinese, with figures side by side and questions answered by DeepSeek Harness. Saves annotations and discussions to an Obsidian literature note. Built for Windows.
sjc88661/zotero-nature-reader.pain: Reading English papers and keeping notes means moving between several tools. This keeps reading, translation and archiving in one flow. Needs DeepSeek Harness, Obsidian, Node.js and Python.

gucarpenter/zotmcp.does: An MCP server inside Zotero 10 that lets any MCP client search, read, annotate and edit your library through fourteen tools. These cover search, import, notes, annotations and page images.
gucarpenter/zotmcp.pain: Gives AI assistants direct access to your library and open PDFs. Writes are not gated, so any local program that can reach Zotero's HTTP server can change your library.

swfc/zutilo.does: Adds editing shortcuts that stock Zotero lacks. You can copy, paste and remove tag sets, relate several items at once and copy items in several formats, with keyboard shortcuts for editing and moving around the interface.
swfc/zutilo.pain: Fills small gaps in Zotero's menus, and each menu item can be switched off. A fork of wshanks/Zutilo for the older Zotero versions.

robert-stackflow/better-rss-for-zotero.does: Extracts the full article text from RSS feed items using Readability and saves it as a note or HTML snapshot. Right-click one or many feed items; tags and a folder path template are optional.
robert-stackflow/better-rss-for-zotero.pain: Feed items often hold only a teaser. This pulls the whole article into your library, with its source link. Its interface is in English and Chinese.

yedadasd/scholar-published-bibtex.does: Fetches the current Google Scholar BibTeX for selected items, preferring the published journal or conference version over preprints, and copies it. It also stores the result in an item field.
yedadasd/scholar-published-bibtex.pain: Scholar and old Zotero entries often return arXiv BibTeX for papers that have since been published. This finds the formal record. It may hit Scholar rate limits on large batches.

techczech/writeflex-app.does: Saves highlights made in the Reading Room of WriteFlex, a Markdown writing app for macOS and Windows, into your Zotero library while Zotero is open.
techczech/writeflex-app.pain: For people who write in WriteFlex and read sources there, highlights land in Zotero without retyping. WriteFlex itself is a separate Markdown writing app.

zhang-ren/zotero-ai-summarizer.does: Summarises selected items with an LLM through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, reading PDF or HTML attachments, and saves the result as a child note. Needs an API endpoint and key, or a local model.
zhang-ren/zotero-ai-summarizer.pain: Writing structured notes for many papers is slow. Run on a whole library, a local model can summarise overnight.

toby-shi-cloud/zotero-auto-ccf-tag-plugi.does: Automatically tags new items as CCF-A, CCF-B or CCF-C by matching the conference or journal name, adding the venue's short name for A-class. A settings button tags the whole library.
toby-shi-cloud/zotero-auto-ccf-tag-plugi.pain: Computer science researchers in China need to know a venue's CCF rank. An optional AI check suggests missing fields and tags, and needs your own key.

mohui666/zotero-chatgpt-sidebar.does: Embeds the ChatGPT web page as a sidebar in the Zotero reader, with Ask ChatGPT on selected text and a summary request filled in from the PDF's text. An optional Chrome extension reuses your ChatGPT login.
mohui666/zotero-chatgpt-sidebar.pain: Lets you use your own ChatGPT account next to the paper with no API key. Nothing is sent automatically; you review the message first. Needs Zotero 10.

makashibata02/zotero-local-bilingual.does: Translates PDFs into side-by-side bilingual or translation-only PDFs, keeping layout, images and formulas. Uses a local engine with free Bing or Tencent translation, or your own DeepSeek or OpenAI-compatible API.
makashibata02/zotero-local-bilingual.pain: Reading English papers and lecture notes often loses the layout when translated. Windows and Apple Silicon Mac are verified, and text goes to the chosen translation service.

shice951229-oss/easy-translate.does: Translates PDFs in the Zotero reader over the original layout and exports a translated PDF that keeps images, headers and columns. Needs Translate for Zotero configured.
shice951229-oss/easy-translate.pain: Makes foreign-language papers easier to read in their original form. The author calls it a personal demo, not for formal publishing.

11zhouxuan/vibe-zotero-translate.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader in a popup, using a page screenshot as context. It saves every lookup to a wordbook that exports to Anki, using AWS Bedrock or an OpenAI-compatible API. Needs an API key.
11zhouxuan/vibe-zotero-translate.pain: Terms in papers are hard to translate without context. This translates to any language your model supports and builds a vocabulary list as you read.

auince/zotero-assistant.does: A research agent for Zotero with a local collection knowledge base, using DeepSeek. It has no documentation, so its features aren't described further.
auince/zotero-assistant.pain: Probably for asking an AI questions about the papers in a collection. It is marked as removed.

atlasfield92/zotero-bulk-importer-plugin.does: Imports references in bulk from a text file with one URL per line, fetching metadata through Zotero translators. Saves the page as is when no translator matches.
atlasfield92/zotero-bulk-importer-plugin.pain: Adding many sources one by one in the browser is slow. This works through a list with a configurable delay, a progress bar and a stop button.

loveychen/zotero-chat.does: An AI chat pane for the PDF reader. A ReAct agent answers questions about the open paper using an OpenAI-compatible API, with source locations in answers. Needs an API key.
loveychen/zotero-chat.pain: Helps you grasp a paper's contributions and methods by asking questions. Works with OpenAI and compatible APIs.

jwow-schneider/zotero-shortdoi.does: Converts long DOIs to short ones and back, and verifies and cleans existing DOIs, from the Manage DOIs right-click menu. It can fetch DOIs for new items automatically.
jwow-schneider/zotero-shortdoi.pain: A fork of the zotero-shortdoi plugin that adds Zotero 9 support to the Zotero 7 and 8 rewrite, as the original is not actively maintained.

mugpeng/zotlink.does: Supplementary file management that works with ZotFile: after ZotFile moves a PDF, the item's supplementary files are moved along and relinked to the new path. Zotero 6 only.
mugpeng/zotlink.pain: Keeps supplementary files with their paper in a folder organised by ZotFile. The author calls it an early learning project.

jinhao-luo/anytero.does: Syncs PDF annotations into an Anytype space, one object per annotated item, with deep links that open each annotation in the Zotero reader. Syncs in real time or on demand. Needs the Anytype desktop app and an API key.
jinhao-luo/anytero.pain: Anytype users otherwise copy highlights across by hand. Inspired by Notero, this keeps annotation notes in Anytype linked to your Zotero library.

gdinh/citekey-url.does: Lets you link to a Zotero item by its BibTeX citation key with zotero://citekey/select/ URLs. It adds a right-click item to copy the link. Meant for use with Better BibTeX.
gdinh/citekey-url.pain: Item keys are opaque, but citekeys are stable and readable. The author notes it was written quickly, with no guarantees.

ebryg/ganglion-app.does: Reading help for Zotero papers: select text to see what a claim rests on, explain or translate it, or check a citation. Also explains figures and tables and shows brief summaries beside each paper.
ebryg/ganglion-app.pain: Its page only hosts downloads and a Windows installer for the Ganglion research assistant, so its other details aren't documented.

yu-tingsun/litgap.does: Finds papers you haven't read that are cited by several items in a collection, using Semantic Scholar, and writes Markdown and HTML reports. A second feature maps your research field with AI.
yu-tingsun/litgap.pain: Spotting gaps in a literature collection by hand is hard. The map feature needs your own Anthropic, OpenAI or Google key, or a custom endpoint.

mightytonylun/obsidian-zotlit-forzotero8.does: The Zotero side of ZotLit, which links Zotero to Obsidian, for Zotero 8 and 9. It works with the Obsidian ZotLit plugin so you can use Zotero literature in Obsidian.
mightytonylun/obsidian-zotlit-forzotero8.pain: A fork of aidenlx/zotlit that adds Zotero 8 and 9 compatibility. Back up your data first, since third-party plugins can break after updates.

phobrla/wikipedia-to-zotero.does: Imports your Wikipedia Saved reading lists into Zotero as Encyclopedia Article items, with list names as tags and the original saved dates as Date Added. Works from a live sign-in or a saved CSV or JSON export, and offers optional deletion of the originals afterwards.
phobrla/wikipedia-to-zotero.pain: Years of saved Wikipedia articles sit outside your reference library. This moves them in with their timestamps intact, backs up first and can resume if interrupted. Needs Zotero 10.

virchow-zhang/wmu-journal-tags.does: Tags items with their grade in the Wenzhou Medical University journal list, such as WMU:T1 or WMU:Q2. It also adds a colour badge column to the item list.
virchow-zhang/wmu-journal-tags.pain: Researchers at Wenzhou Medical University otherwise look up each journal's grade by hand. The list is built in and works offline, with no API key, tagging new items automatically or in bulk.

kianmax0/zotero-chatgpt-web.does: Opens the official ChatGPT website in a sidebar beside the PDF in Zotero Reader, and sends selected text or the paper's details to it.
kianmax0/zotero-chatgpt-web.pain: Discussing a paper with ChatGPT usually means switching windows and pasting text. This keeps the chat next to the PDF and uses your own ChatGPT sign-in, with no API key. PDF body text is never sent automatically.

qilinn-robotics/zotero-paperchat.does: An AI chat sidebar in the Zotero reader that talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. It can use up to five PDFs plus selected text as context and keeps separate named conversations. You supply an API key, endpoint and model.
qilinn-robotics/zotero-paperchat.pain: For asking questions about one or several papers without leaving Zotero. Its developer says it has only been tested on Zotero 8.

ice-cream-cpu/zotero-plugin-paper-readin.does: A full-text, multi-paper AI reading assistant in its own window. It pins up to 12 papers, retrieves relevant pages with page citations and renders answers with Markdown and formulas. Works with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Claude, Qwen or a custom endpoint, and needs an API key.
ice-cream-cpu/zotero-plugin-paper-readin.pain: Chatting about papers usually sees only titles and abstracts. This reads the indexed PDF text page by page, so answers can cite pages, and handles figures and tables by sending the relevant pages. Built for Zotero 9.

jmiba/zotero-redisearch-rag.does: An Obsidian plugin that imports Zotero items into your vault and answers questions about their PDFs. It extracts text with OCR when needed, indexes it in Redis 8 and cites the source chunk.
jmiba/zotero-redisearch-rag.pain: For people who keep their thinking in Obsidian and want to ask questions across their Zotero PDFs there, with local embeddings and chat. It also syncs metadata and annotations back and forth.

suwueng/zotero-reference-marker-fix.does: Fixes the misplaced reference marker in Zotero's citation hover popups, so the dot sits at the first line of the reference it points to.
suwueng/zotero-reference-marker-fix.pain: A temporary workaround for a Zotero 10.0.5 bug where the marker is shifted down and to the right in the preview. Its developer says it was tested on macOS and should be disabled once Zotero fixes the bug.

oliverdudgeon/zotero-tab-fix.does: Makes Ctrl+Tab toggle between your two most recently used Zotero tabs, as Firefox does, instead of cycling through the tab strip. Ctrl+Shift+Tab behaves the same way.
oliverdudgeon/zotero-tab-fix.pain: Zotero's default tab cycling gets slow when many readers are open and you only want to flip between two. This restores the Firefox habit. Works on Zotero 9 and 10.

zcyisiee/zotero-tts-reader.does: Reads selected PDF text aloud using the OpenAI text-to-speech API, with six voices, speed from 0.25x to 4x and standard or HD models. A side panel has play, pause, stop and a progress bar. Needs an OpenAI API key.
zcyisiee/zotero-tts-reader.pain: Listening to a paper instead of reading it is useful for tired eyes or language learning. It can skip bracketed numbers and author-year citations so they are not read out, and caches audio for repeated text.

shalom-lab/deepread.does: An AI reading assistant in the item pane that chats about PDF or Word attachments using Google Gemini. It has preset prompts and saves replies as notes. Needs a Gemini API key.
shalom-lab/deepread.pain: Lets you discuss whole papers, books or a paper with its supplements without leaving Zotero. When a PDF is open in the reader it automatically uses that PDF as context.

chengyue-lu/literature-mind.does: The Zotero companion for LiteratureMind, a separate Windows desktop research app. It sends selected items or PDF selections to a LiteratureMind project through the right-click menu or Ctrl+Shift+M, connecting only to a local port.
chengyue-lu/literature-mind.pain: For people who organise research in LiteratureMind and want to send papers and highlights over without retyping. It needs the Windows app installed, and it never writes to Zotero. Built for Zotero 9.

sparklemuff1n/zotero-author-search.does: Searches your library for other works by the author of a selected item, from the right-click menu or Ctrl+Shift+A (Cmd+Shift+A on macOS). Items with several authors show a list to pick from.
sparklemuff1n/zotero-author-search.pain: Finding everything you hold by one author normally means typing their name into the search bar and switching modes. This does it in one step across the whole library.

earnest-zhang/zotero-component-datasheet.does: Saves component datasheets from LCSC (立创商城) product pages via the Zotero Connector. You get a Document item with the PDF and a note of parameters, and a blank date is filled from the PDF's first page.
earnest-zhang/zotero-component-datasheet.pain: Component datasheets and specifications are otherwise saved by hand with inconsistent metadata. Aimed at electronics engineers using the Chinese parts shop LCSC, on Zotero 9.

dawsonmv/zotero-moment-o7.does: Archives web pages to prevent link rot, automatically when you save through the Browser Connector or from the right-click menu. Supports Internet Archive, Archive.today, Perma.cc, UK Web Archive and Arquivo.pt, and stores the archive link in Extra with a note and tag.
dawsonmv/zotero-moment-o7.pain: A Zotero 7 port of the old Zotero Memento plugin. Cited web pages vanish or change, so this saves a permanent copy and a link to it. Perma.cc needs a free API key. Its developer calls it alpha.

zpeters/zotero-page-count.does: Adds a #Pages column to the item list, taking the count from the Pages field, the numPages field or the page count Zotero stores for the item's PDF.
zpeters/zotero-page-count.pain: Zotero shows titles, authors and dates but not how long a paper is. This lets you see and sort by length at a glance.

dcondrey/zotero-validate.does: Checks references against up to 14 scholarly databases, including Crossref, OpenAlex and PubMed. Each is marked verified, verified with corrections or flagged, with suggested fixes. An optional LLM step uses OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini keys.
dcondrey/zotero-validate.pain: Imported references often contain wrong or invented details. This cross-checks them against several sources so you can spot bad entries before citing them.

zrqworkmail-cloud/zotero-vocab-review.does: Records English words you highlight in Zotero PDFs and syncs them to Anki through AnkiConnect. Cards get a Youdao definition, examples and a sentence from the paper, and repeat captures raise a word's priority.
zrqworkmail-cloud/zotero-vocab-review.pain: For learners reading English papers who want vocabulary cards made as they read. Only the highlighted word is sent to Youdao. A companion Anki add-on captures text from other Windows apps. Built for Zotero 10.

techyangj/zotero-voice.does: Adds a Pronounce button to the reader's selection toolbar that speaks the selected word or sentence. It uses a local OpenAI-compatible text-to-speech server.
techyangj/zotero-voice.pain: Checking how an English word sounds normally means leaving the PDF. No API key is needed, but you must set up and run a local server such as Kokoro-FastAPI yourself.

nbtkmy/zoteroaddonforaoi.does: Checks whether the UZH Asia-Orient Library holds the books in your library, using the ISBN. It writes the holding result into the Abstract field and adds tags for owned, online or nearby-library copies.
nbtkmy/zoteroaddonforaoi.pain: Helps librarians and researchers at the University of Zurich decide what to acquire, without searching the catalogue book by book. A modified version of an earlier Swiss library add-on.

zt0214/bibgenie.does: An AI research agent in the Zotero sidebar. You add items, PDFs, notes, snapshots, images or collections as context, ask questions, search the library and save results as notes. A local Zotero MCP server is built in.
zt0214/bibgenie.pain: A fork of BaiRuic/BibGenie; its README doesn't say what it changes. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and others by key, or Ollama and LM Studio locally. Paid plans add web search.

aadi219/defn.does: Lets you mark a definition in a PDF, then underlines every other occurrence of that term so hovering shows the definition. Offers pinned definitions in a side panel and a searchable glossary. Also runs as a web app.
aadi219/defn.pain: Textbooks and papers reuse terms defined chapters earlier, and finding the definition means scrolling or searching. Definitions are also saved as Zotero highlights. Its developer notes it was built with AI assistance.

lateshift/iwutoolbox.does: Adds a copy citation button to the Zotero toolbar, using the citation style chosen in the Quick Copy preferences.
lateshift/iwutoolbox.pain: Saves going through the menus to copy a formatted citation. Its developer calls it an early work in progress.

cube-lover/paperloom.does: Shows a translation beside the original in the Zotero PDF reader, translating the text paragraph by paragraph. It also recognises text in figures and tables with local OCR, and lets you box-select missed areas to translate them. You bring an OpenAI-compatible or DeepL service.
cube-lover/paperloom.pain: Reading papers in another language usually means exporting a translated PDF or switching windows. It keeps a glossary, supports manual corrections, saves bilingual notes and can generate AI summaries.

merc-hecl/zota.does: Chat with an AI about your PDFs in a Zotero sidebar or floating window. You attach the whole PDF or chosen paragraphs, and get streaming replies, image upload and per-document history. Needs a provider API key.
merc-hecl/zota.pain: Lets you ask questions about a paper without copying text into a separate chat site. Chats can be exported as notes.

lendle-king/zotero-bibtex-copy.does: Copies the BibTeX for the selected items to the clipboard from the right-click menu or Ctrl+Shift+B (Cmd+Shift+B on macOS).
lendle-king/zotero-bibtex-copy.pain: Getting a BibTeX entry into a LaTeX file normally means exporting to a file or a dialog first. This takes one step.

mrpsharp/zotero-extra-columns.does: Shows values stored as key and value lines in an item's Extra field as columns in the item list, which you can sort as text, dates or numbers. You define each column in the settings.
mrpsharp/zotero-extra-columns.pain: Custom data such as a finished-reading date, a rating or a project name is kept in Extra but invisible in the list. This makes it visible and sortable next to the title.

korhonenaleksi/zotero-fix-caps.does: Fixes casing on selected items from the right-click menu. It turns ALL-CAPS and sentence-case titles into title case, strips SAGE's EXPRESS: label and corrects ALL-CAPS author names. A dialog previews every change first.
korhonenaleksi/zotero-fix-caps.pain: Imports from databases like Web of Science often arrive in capitals. Changes are logged to a CSV in the Zotero data folder so they can be reverted. Works on Zotero 9 and 10.

authentic3096/zotero-kb.does: Turns your library into a local knowledge base for AI, slicing papers into page-referenced chunks for search and serving them through an MCP server. A sidebar and admin panel inside Zotero show each paper in layers.
authentic3096/zotero-kb.pain: AI tools struggle to find and cite exact pages in large PDF collections. Search and models run locally, and the plugin can also fetch new papers into Zotero. It needs Python and a separate runtime package.

squirrelrao/zotero-lingocloud.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader using Caiyun Xiaoyi (彩云小译), with its academic or general models and its public or personal glossaries. Needs your Caiyun account ID.
squirrelrao/zotero-lingocloud.pain: For people who read papers with Chinese translation from Caiyun. Personal glossaries need a Caiyun membership. Works on Zotero 6 and 7.

111112200/zotero-pdf-ai-translate.does: Translates a whole PDF and exports a side-by-side bilingual PDF, with the original on one side and the same layout with translated text on the other. Figures and formulas stay in place. Works with any OpenAI-compatible service and needs an API key.
111112200/zotero-pdf-ai-translate.pain: Reading papers in another language otherwise means copy-pasting or losing the layout. Supports a glossary, page ranges and resumable translation. Defaults to translating into Simplified Chinese. Built for Zotero 10.

wuxinxin27/zotero-reading-room.does: A sidebar for the paper open in Zotero's PDF reader, with an AI summary, chat, notes and reading-status tags (unread to on hold). Works with OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or Ollama models, and answers link to pages.
wuxinxin27/zotero-reading-room.pain: Helps you read one paper at a time with checkable evidence, calling the model only when you ask. Its developer calls it experimental, and it is built for Zotero 10.

korhonenaleksi/zotero-reference-check.does: Prepares selected items for a journal's reference list. It removes database and proxy links, database names and accession numbers, and fixes odd page and volume fields. A second command fills missing details from Crossref.
korhonenaleksi/zotero-reference-check.pain: Imports often leave EBSCO or ProQuest links and database names that end up printed in APA references. Both commands list changes for confirmation and log them to a CSV. Formerly Zotero Clean URLs.

sentient-codebot/zotero-remarkable-usb.does: Sends PDFs to a reMarkable tablet over USB, optionally cropped or split into columns. Highlights and handwriting come back as Zotero annotations.
sentient-codebot/zotero-remarkable-usb.pain: Syncs with a reMarkable without its cloud or a subscription. A fork of fbkarsdorp/zotero-remarkable with annotation import adapted from another plugin. Needs firmware 3.9 or later and Zotero 8 to 10.

ljeagle/papersgpt-for-zotero.does: An AI plugin for chatting with papers across your Zotero library, with indexing done locally and cited answers that jump to the source paper. Connects to built-in local models, Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
ljeagle/papersgpt-for-zotero.pain: A fork of papersgpt/papersgpt-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes. Aimed at large libraries and private, offline use.

anaxonda/uttermux-zotero.does: Connects Zotero's Read Aloud feature to the UtterMux voice broker on Linux, so UtterMux voices can prepare upcoming sentences while the current one plays. It keeps sentence highlighting and transport controls.
