anaxonda/uttermux-zotero.pain: Reading aloud through system voices pauses between sentences when a model is slow to start. Needs UtterMux for Linux running with its Zotero bridge, and Zotero 9 or 10.

1281300805/zotero-inline-translate.does: Translates selected PDF text into Simplified Chinese with DeepSeek and draws the translation over the original in the reader. You can keep several separate regions, click to toggle the original, and annotations follow the translated sentences. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
1281300805/zotero-inline-translate.pain: Translation appears right where the text is, without changing the PDF. Also accepts any OpenAI-compatible service. Needs a text layer, so scanned PDFs need OCR first. Built for Zotero 8 and 9.

koabula/zotero-margin.does: An AI reading companion in the reader's sidebar that explains selected passages, searches the PDF and your annotations, and proposes notes to save. Answers link to cited pages. Needs a Chat Completions API with tool calling.
koabula/zotero-margin.pain: Lets you ask follow-up questions while reading and return to the source text. The assistant can only read inside Zotero. Its developer says it is tested on Windows with Zotero 10.

zhuzihan728/zotero-minimise-tray.does: Sends Zotero to the Windows system tray when you close the main window, so syncing and the Zotero Connector keep running. Click the tray icon to restore it, or right-click to exit.
zhuzihan728/zotero-minimise-tray.pain: Closing Zotero normally quits it, which stops the Connector for browser saves. Windows only.

yuukibarns/zotero-page-tools.does: Copies the current PDF page as an image or a one-page PDF file, and saves chosen page ranges as a new PDF. Works from the reader toolbar or right-click menu.
yuukibarns/zotero-page-tools.pain: Pulling a page or a few pages out of a paper normally needs another PDF tool. It leaves the original untouched. Its developer says it relies on Zotero 10 internals and is limited to that version.

northword/zotero-plugin-test.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own, labelled by its author as only for testing.
northword/zotero-plugin-test.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

migueldlm/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up DOIs and shortDOIs for selected items and marks invalid ones. It can also fetch full metadata from Crossref, filling gaps from OpenAlex, and clean prefixes such as doi: from the DOI field.
migueldlm/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Fixes missing, wrong or messy DOIs in bulk. A fork of JuliusBairaktaris/zotero-shortdoi that adds the full-metadata function using Crossref and OpenAlex.

max101johnston/embeddingzotero.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants can search and read your library. Semantic search uses embeddings from a cloud or local service.
max101johnston/embeddingzotero.pain: A modified fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp that checks embedding dimensions, re-embeds mismatched items and cleans index entries for deleted items. Indexing can incur provider charges.

utkubilendemir/kanzi.does: Imports Kindle highlights from My Clippings.txt into Zotero as native annotations, matching titles to items and letting you fix mismatches in a manager window. Codes like [o] set the colour.
utkubilendemir/kanzi.pain: Gets Kindle highlights onto the books and papers in your library. Needs Python 3.11 or newer, and Poppler for PDFs. Its developer notes it was heavily vibecoded.

mejistus/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research agent in the reader: ask about the PDF, selected text or figures, compare papers and save notes to Zotero or Obsidian folders. Agent Mode can search, tag and organise the library.
mejistus/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes. Works with API keys, local models, ChatGPT WebChat, Codex App Server, Claude Code or OpenCode.

flemington8/lumina.does: Chat with your papers in the Zotero item pane or a global chat window, using the paper's metadata, abstract and full text as context. Supports many providers (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and others) and local Ollama or vLLM.
flemington8/lumina.pain: Lets you question papers without leaving Zotero. Features include @ references to other papers, saving replies as notes and comparing several papers. Cloud providers need your own key.

janbaykara/zotero-annas-archive.does: Downloads PDFs for items with a DOI from Anna's Archive SciDB, from the right-click menu, Find Full Text or automatically for new items. It tries several mirrors and can use an Anna's Archive membership key.
janbaykara/zotero-annas-archive.pain: Fetches papers that publishers and open-access sources don't supply. Note that Anna's Archive distributes copyrighted material without permission, which is illegal in many jurisdictions.

yuukibarns/zotero-compact-menu.does: Hides Zotero's top menu row on Linux and Windows and moves the window controls beside the tabs. A hamburger button opens the original menus.
yuukibarns/zotero-compact-menu.pain: Frees a row of vertical space on small screens. macOS is left unchanged, and disabling the plugin restores the usual menus. Built for Zotero 10.

traviszhan/zotero-hermes-reader.does: Adds a Hermes AI chat to the Zotero 9 item pane, with a separate conversation per paper and an Ask Hermes option for selected PDF text or highlights. Quick actions include a guided read, parameter extraction and drafts for Obsidian.
traviszhan/zotero-hermes-reader.pain: For users of the Hermes assistant who want it tied to the open paper. It needs a Hermes server, reached through a relay you set up. Obsidian drafts are written only after you confirm.

thexeos/zotero-memento.does: Archives saved web pages and articles to the Internet Archive, automatically when you save through the Browser Connector or from the right-click menu. The archive link goes into Extra with a note and tag. Includes five export translators.
thexeos/zotero-memento.pain: Guards against link rot in your references. A fork of leonkt/zotero-memento that runs on Zotero 7 and later.

441837297/zotero-mineru-plugin.does: Converts a PDF attachment to Markdown through a right-click command using a local MinerU install, and saves the Markdown as an attachment on the parent item.
441837297/zotero-mineru-plugin.pain: Markdown keeps formulas, tables and image positions better than PDF text for AI reading. You must install MinerU with a GPU and edit paths in the plugin's script, then repackage it.

nian1147/zotero-pdf-translate-medical.does: Translates selected text, titles, abstracts and annotations into Chinese with a medical translation service built on DeepSeek. It injects a built-in glossary of about 4,000 medical terms and abbreviations, plus your own term list, into the prompt.
nian1147/zotero-pdf-translate-medical.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate for medical papers, where general translators render abbreviations and terms inconsistently. Needs a DeepSeek API key.

nico-zck/zotero-scholar-citations-forked.does: Fetches the number of citations for your items from Google Scholar and stores it in the Extra field so you can sort by it. Adds a random delay between batch requests and better handling of reCAPTCHA.
nico-zck/zotero-scholar-citations-forked.pain: A fork of MaxKuehn/zotero-scholar-citations aimed at making it work better in China: it fixes a URL error with special characters in titles and reduces Google Scholar blocking. Legacy, Zotero 6 only.

cameron-utils/zotero_semantic_scholar_pl.does: Adds a right-click menu item that opens a Semantic Scholar search for the selected paper in your browser. Works on Zotero 7 only.
cameron-utils/zotero_semantic_scholar_pl.pain: Saves copying a title into Semantic Scholar by hand when you want to find related or citing work.

aykutcayir34/zotero-smart-organizer.does: Files new items from an inbox collection into your existing collection tree, locally with no API key. It compares titles, abstracts and tags with collection names and previews each suggestion with its score; uncertain matches go to a Needs Review collection.
aykutcayir34/zotero-smart-organizer.pain: Large libraries pile up uncategorised papers. This files them using your own taxonomy, never deletes anything, and is manual by default. Its developer calls it an early beta for Zotero 10.

fdossi/attach-finder.does: Attaches PDFs from a local folder to selected items by matching the DOI found in file names and metadata. Caches the folder scan, lets you set the root folder and scan depth, and shows a summary of what was attached.
fdossi/attach-finder.pain: If your PDFs already sit in folders on disk, linking them to the right items one by one is slow. This matches them by DOI in a single batch.

liufangshuo666/dsh-for-zotero.does: Runs the DeepSeek Harness agent inside Zotero 10. The agent reads your papers and annotations, answers questions, searches your library, edits tags and notes, and finds papers through Crossref and DataCite. Deleting or creating items always needs your confirmation.
liufangshuo666/dsh-for-zotero.pain: Chatting with a model and pasting answers back loses context. This gives the agent tools to work on your library directly. Needs the DeepSeek Harness desktop app installed locally.

un-seen/hedwigai-zotero.does: Checks selected items or a whole collection against Crossref and reports each as found, found with a different year or authors, not found, or retracted. The check runs on the hedwigai website, free with no account, up to 25 references at a time.
un-seen/hedwigai-zotero.pain: Catches wrong details and retracted papers in your reference list before you submit. Its developer says the plugin itself sends nothing; it opens the checker page with your list in the URL.

molaison/llm-for-zotero-papers.does: An AI research assistant in the Zotero reader that chats about your papers. This edition adds a ChatGPT Web based service that keeps one fixed remote conversation per paper, and keeps the upstream agent mode, notes and library chat.
molaison/llm-for-zotero-papers.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that adds a papers service channel with its own auto-updates. Its developer says remote history sync needs a server component that is not yet live.

cnteng/onedict.does: Looks up words in online dictionaries (Youdao, Cambridge, Collins, Oxford) and adds them as Anki cards through AnkiConnect. Builds as a Zotero plugin as well as Chrome and Firefox extensions.
cnteng/onedict.pain: For readers learning English from papers who want to turn unfamiliar words into flashcards without leaving the page. Needs Anki with AnkiConnect.

woif-sha/paper-translate-for-zotero.does: Translates reader selections into Chinese using the paper's own context. It draws sections, a glossary and background from the MinerU Markdown that llm-for-zotero produces, reads text from figures, and still translates plain text without Markdown.
woif-sha/paper-translate-for-zotero.pain: Selection-only translation can't tell what a term like cell means in a given paper. This adds paper context. Needs llm-for-zotero, plus Codex CLI sign-in or an OpenAI-compatible API key.

dragonliu2018/zotcard-8plus.does: Card-based note-taking: templates for concept, quote, character and review cards, plus tools to batch-edit, sort, print, randomly review and chart your cards. Adapted to run on Zotero 8 and 9.
dragonliu2018/zotcard-8plus.pain: A fork of 018/zotcard 3.3.0 that updates it for newer Zotero versions, for people who want Zettelkasten-style cards with structure.

nkbaim/zotero-ai-note.does: Summarises selected PDFs with DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu GLM or Xiaomi MiMo into a structured child note. It covers the question, methods, findings, limitations and keywords, using Zotero's own text extraction and sending text, not the file.
nkbaim/zotero-ai-note.pain: Writing a first-pass summary for every paper is slow. This creates one note per paper in one go. Needs an API key for the chosen service; the notes are in Chinese-oriented layouts.

llpetro/zotero-collection-relations.does: Draws the papers in a collection as an interactive citation graph or timeline. Pick starting papers, then use OpenAlex to find references, citing papers and recommended related research.
llpetro/zotero-collection-relations.pain: Helps map a topic or prepare a literature review by showing how your papers connect and what to read next. Its developer calls it a development build for Zotero 9.

dahliasan/zotero-doi-manager.does: Looks up DOIs and shortDOIs for selected items through Crossref, verifies stored DOIs, strips prefixes from the DOI field and tags invalid ones. It only ever writes the DOI field.
dahliasan/zotero-doi-manager.pain: A fork of the DOI Manager updated for Zotero 10. Missing or malformed DOIs break lookups and citations, and this cleans them in bulk.

kimstitute/zotero-obsidian-connector.does: Creates one Markdown literature note per Zotero item in an Obsidian vault, keeps it updated, and builds a dashboard of titles. You can also edit the note in a Zotero tab. Optionally translates abstracts into Korean.
kimstitute/zotero-obsidian-connector.pain: For people who keep references in Zotero and thinking in Obsidian and don't want to rebuild notes by hand. Korean translation needs ChatGPT sign-in or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the core needs no key.

pendulating/zotero-opendata-cite.does: Saves datasets from Socrata and CKAN open data portals as Dataset items from a pasted URL. The agency becomes the author, the portal the repository, and a child note lists API links and columns; metadata can be refreshed later.
pendulating/zotero-opendata-cite.pain: Zotero's browser connector handles open data portals poorly. This gives datasets proper citable records instead of web pages.

nbtkmy/zotero-price-checker.does: Looks up the price of Japanese books by ISBN through the OpenBD API and writes it to the Extra field. Adds tags when an ISBN is missing, unlisted or has no price, and sums prices for items with several ISBNs.
nbtkmy/zotero-price-checker.pain: Useful for tracking what a Japanese book collection costs without checking each title by hand. Legacy, Zotero 6 only.

fbkarsdorp/zotero-remarkable.does: Sends PDF and EPUB attachments to a reMarkable tablet over its USB web interface, then pulls annotated versions back as new attachments. Can sync automatically whenever the tablet is connected.
fbkarsdorp/zotero-remarkable.pain: Gets papers onto an e-ink tablet and your handwriting back without the reMarkable cloud or SSH. Its developer says the unofficial USB interface may change between firmware versions.

lxx006/zotero-rich-annotation.does: Lets you write PDF annotations in Markdown, LaTeX, restricted HTML, images and code blocks, with source and live preview side by side. Includes formula templates, managed images, and multiple annotation windows. Zotero 10 only.
lxx006/zotero-rich-annotation.pain: Zotero's plain-text annotations can't hold formulas or figures. This is built on the Annotation Markdown plugin and replaces it.

mars-robotics-star/local-immersive-trans.does: Translates whole PDFs while keeping their layout, using a local BabelDOC backend, and saves the translated PDF back to Zotero. Includes a task manager and keyboard shortcuts. You supply a model API address, name and key.
mars-robotics-star/local-immersive-trans.pain: Layout-preserving translation of full papers, with the PDF processing done on your own machine. Mainly aimed at Chinese-language users.

kuchinashiyume/memorive.does: Connects selected items and annotations to the Memorive Windows research app, which retrieves evidence and writes research results back to Zotero. Needs the Memorive desktop app installed.
kuchinashiyume/memorive.pain: For people already using Memorive to ask questions across papers with checkable citations who want it linked to their Zotero library.

yebuqiu/paper-pilot.does: An AI literature assistant for Zotero 7 to 10. It offers reader translation and chat, bilingual side-by-side PDF translation, Chinese metadata, journal ranks and citation counts, scheduled reports and an agent with library tools.
yebuqiu/paper-pilot.pain: A bundle of Chinese-language literature management helpers in one plugin. It has been removed, so it is probably no longer available.

sumno-app/sumno-zotero.does: Pulls your sumno library into a Sumno collection in Zotero, keeping title, authors, year, DOI, abstract, Open Access link and OpenAlex ID. One-way and read-only, with duplicates skipped.
sumno-app/sumno-zotero.pain: For people who collect papers in sumno and want them in Zotero too. Needs a sumno account API token; its developer calls it a beta.

dariusada/zotero-reading-guide.does: Adds a transparent highlighter line to the PDF reader that follows your mouse, with a mode for two-column papers, colour choices and keyboard shortcuts.
dariusada/zotero-reading-guide.pain: Helps you keep your place on long papers. Its developer marks the two-column mode as beta.

generalpawz/zotero-researcher.does: Finds papers for a collection in scholarly databases, from a boolean query or an AI-written one, and runs PRISMA-style screening. Also links citing papers, fetches PDFs, repairs sparse metadata and can use a small local model.
generalpawz/zotero-researcher.pain: Builds and screens a literature collection without leaving Zotero, with search runs that can be logged for reproducibility. AI providers are optional and use your own keys.

yunxop/zotero-superior-intelligence.does: An AI sidebar for the PDF reader: chat with a paper and auto-highlight conclusions, methods and gaps in colours. It also extracts reusable English phrasing and evidence into a writing knowledge base. Needs an LLM API; Voyage AI and MinerU are optional.
yunxop/zotero-superior-intelligence.pain: Speeds up reading and builds a store of sentences and findings for later writing. The plugin is free, but model services may charge; local OpenAI-compatible models work.

sorinhostiuc/zotero-zotcloud.does: Syncs library metadata, attachments, notes and PDF annotations to WebDAV, Google Drive, Dropbox or pCloud. Offers optional AES-256 encryption, set intervals and file naming patterns, and a browser of synced files and devices.
sorinhostiuc/zotero-zotcloud.pain: For people who want to sync Zotero to cloud storage they already have. Needs your own WebDAV login or a sign-in to a provider.

fkkzz/aiagent.does: Sends PDFs to a local Python agent that calls an LLM to write a summary and keywords, saved in the item. Runs from the right-click menu, on import, or in batch, and only handles Journal Article items.
fkkzz/aiagent.pain: Gives imported papers a quick summary and tags automatically. Needs the Python agent running and an LLM API key; its developer says there are no plans to fix known issues.

joydddd/colorful-bionic.does: Bionic reading in the Zotero reader: bolds word beginnings and colours verbs, nouns and conjunctions differently. It uses the compromise package to spot parts of speech.
joydddd/colorful-bionic.pain: A fork of DrUsagi/Colorful-Bionic that adds part-of-speech colouring. Its developer uses it to help with ADHD and says verb detection is not perfectly accurate.

tcxm/llm-for-zotero-ui.does: An interface-focused edition of llm-for-zotero with a quieter, denser chat panel in the reader sidebar. You can add or explain selected text directly and quote replies into the next prompt. It uses the original add-on ID.
tcxm/llm-for-zotero-ui.pain: For users of llm-for-zotero who want a cleaner chat layout. It replaces an installed upstream copy; features and setup follow the upstream project.

antonalia/paperbridge.does: Lets Codex read your Zotero PDFs through a built-in local MCP bridge and create native highlights, comments and tags. It also imports annotations into Obsidian notes by collection. Windows, personal libraries only.
antonalia/paperbridge.pain: Moves from reading a paper with an AI to a structured note in Obsidian without copying by hand. Needs Codex and an Obsidian vault.

lllateron/zotero-focus-columns.does: Adds item list columns for journal rank, hash tags, status and short remarks, plus item pane rows, named column layouts, and optional sync across computers. Journal rank lookups can use an EasyScholar key. Zotero 10 only.
lllateron/zotero-focus-columns.pain: Zotero has no columns for journal tier or personal status. This keeps them visible in the list; the interface is Chinese.

k-ghoshal/zotero-pdf-to-md.does: Converts the PDFs of selected items to Markdown files in a folder using pymupdf4llm, with OCR for scans if Tesseract is installed. Scores each result and puts doubtful ones in a needs-review folder.
k-ghoshal/zotero-pdf-to-md.pain: Prepares papers for note-taking apps or LLMs, locally with nothing uploaded. Tested on macOS only; needs uv or Python 3.

macvirii/zotero-publication-rankings.does: Shows journal and conference rankings in a sortable Ranking column: SJR, JCR, CORE, ABS, ABDC, Qualis CAPES, SPELL, SciELO and FT50. Matches by ISSN or title, shows match details and lets you override rankings.
macvirii/zotero-publication-rankings.pain: A fork of ben-AI-cybersec/zotero-publication-rankings that adds more ranking sources, especially Brazilian CAPES ones, plus Zotero 10 compatibility and speed work.

vbcnft59/zotero-quicklex.does: Double-click an English word in a PDF to see its Chinese definition, phonetics and base form in Zotero's popup, using the offline ECDICT dictionary. No network or API key. Windows and macOS, Zotero 10.
vbcnft59/zotero-quicklex.pain: Quick lookups for Chinese readers of English papers, without sending words or text anywhere. A Russian edition lives on a separate branch.

maxccess/zotero-vocab.does: Select a foreign-language word in the reader and add it to a vocabulary list with one click, saving the context sentence and source. A Chinese meaning is filled in through Baidu Translate. Includes search, quiz mode and export to CSV, Markdown, Anki or JSON.
maxccess/zotero-vocab.pain: Recurring terms in papers get looked up and forgotten. Counting how often you save a word shows which ones matter in your field.

zhenwanli/zotero-worldlib-pdf.does: Submits a DOI request to the Worldlib (世图) literature service, waits for the result and attaches the PDF to your item. Has a task panel with retry and stop. Needs a Worldlib account with consultation access.
zhenwanli/zotero-worldlib-pdf.pain: Automates a manual request-and-download routine for papers you can't open. Its developer calls it a test version and says not every paper can be fetched.

unfound77/fidoic.does: A docked reading companion for the open PDF: select a passage and ask, and it answers with short verbatim quotes, streams replies, and saves answers as notes. Works with the Gemini API free tier or Claude using your own key.
unfound77/fidoic.pain: Made for close reading of dense texts where you need to check actual wording, and separates what the text says from outside context. It is a reading aid, not a writing tool.

steven-jianhao-li/zotero-ai-butler-fang.does: Reads new PDFs automatically and writes a Markdown summary note. Also offers a detailed multi-round reading, mind maps, multi-paper reviews, a one-image poster summary and a follow-up sidebar. Works with OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, OpenRouter and others.
steven-jianhao-li/zotero-ai-butler-fang.pain: Saved papers pile up unread and long ones are hard to retain. This produces notes without sending files one by one. Needs your own model API key; prompts are editable.

shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-color-menu-.does: Adds a right-click menu to collections that gives them a background colour in the left tree: red, gold, green, blue or purple. Colours are stored locally and can be cleared.
shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-color-menu-.pain: Makes deep or numerous collection trees easier to scan. Colours don't sync and don't change your items.

maedayoshiaki/zotero-mcp.does: Runs a local MCP server inside Zotero with about 20 tools, so AI assistants can search items, read PDF text and outlines, and create highlights from text. They can also create or update notes, tags, collections and attachments.
maedayoshiaki/zotero-mcp.pain: A fork of stephenstubbs/zotero-mcp that bundles pdf.js, so tools like Claude Code can annotate papers without a Python proxy. Works with Zotero 7 and 9.

nightwatcher314/zotero-mcp.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI clients such as Claude can search your library, read PDF text and annotations, and browse collections. They can also do semantic search and write notes, tags and metadata.
nightwatcher314/zotero-mcp.pain: A fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp; its README doesn't say what it changes. For people who want an AI assistant to work with their library.

np-atcw/zotero-open-archive.does: Opens the file whose path is stored in an item's Archive field.
np-atcw/zotero-open-archive.pain: Useful if you keep the location of an external file in Archive and want to open it from Zotero. It documents no other features.

haoknight/zotero.quicklook.does: Press Space on an item to preview its attachments with the QuickLook app, and use the arrow keys to move between attachments. You can set the QuickLook.exe path. Windows only; QuickLook must be installed.
haoknight/zotero.quicklook.pain: Gives a quick look at PDFs and images without opening the reader, in the style of macOS QuickLook.

yyu-ang/zotero-skill-task-mcp.does: Turns items into a task queue for external AI agents. You define skills with a SKILL.md, and an AI claims tasks over MCP, then submits results that are saved as notes or attached files on the item.
yyu-ang/zotero-skill-task-mcp.pain: For running repeatable AI jobs across a library, such as summaries. The plugin includes no AI of its own and never starts one.

sukui10/zotero-split-screen.does: A comparison workbench in the main window that shows two to four PDFs side by side with synchronised pages. Adds structured A/B comparison notes, labelled links between passages, and term highlighting across papers. Local analysis.
sukui10/zotero-split-screen.pain: Comparing methods and results across papers means flipping tabs and noting things by hand. This keeps them together. Zotero 7 to 9.

yaolimumu/zoteroquicklook.does: Previews attachments with QuickLook on macOS, Gloobus-Preview on Linux, or a QuickLook tool of your choice on Windows, from within Zotero.
yaolimumu/zoteroquicklook.pain: A fork of mronkko/ZoteroQuickLook. Its developer says it is not actively maintained and may not work with current Zotero versions.

archechef/iacr-tools.does: For cryptographers: fixes Springer conference papers into Conference Paper items, fills metadata from CryptoBib, and finds IACR ePrint versions with PDFs. Also finds duplicate versions, adds papers from lists and links a LaTeX folder.
archechef/iacr-tools.pain: Springer proceedings and ePrint papers arrive with wrong types and messy metadata. This keeps cryptography references consistent with CryptoBib. Zotero 8 to 10.

aknahin/kozosync.does: Reads highlight files that KOReader uploads to a WebDAV server and adds them to the matching PDF in Zotero as native annotations with notes and colours. One-way only: it never writes to the server.
aknahin/kozosync.pain: Gets highlights from your e-reader into Zotero without retyping. Needs WebDAV sign-in and KOReader's highlight sync plugin; only tested with Koofr.

veale/metadata-filler-for-zotero.does: Fills missing fields by sending text from the first PDF pages to an AI model, with OpenAlex and Crossref shortcuts when a DOI is found. Shows every proposed change for approval before writing anything.
veale/metadata-filler-for-zotero.pain: Fixes sparse metadata on imported PDFs in bulk. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Apple Intelligence or a local model such as Ollama.

nkbaim/pubmed-importer.does: Searches PubMed from inside Zotero and imports the records you tick into the current library or a chosen collection. Results page through with abstracts, skip PMIDs you already have, and trigger Find Available PDF after import.
nkbaim/pubmed-importer.pain: Getting PubMed hits into Zotero normally means switching to the website and saving records one search at a time. This keeps the search, selection and duplicate check in one window.

666666lyc/zotero-codex-translate.does: Translates English text-layer PDFs into Chinese through your local Codex CLI. The translation opens beside the original in the reader as a new attachment.
666666lyc/zotero-codex-translate.pain: For people who read English papers in Chinese and already use Codex. Its developer says it is a development preview, downloads about 600 MB of tools on first run, and does not handle scanned PDFs.

situkangsayur/zotero-graphanalysis-plugi.does: Maps how the works in a collection cite each other using OpenAlex data. The interactive report shows clusters, central works, a main path and shared references you don't have yet. No AI is involved.
situkangsayur/zotero-graphanalysis-plugi.pain: Seeing the structure of a reading list normally needs a separate bibliometrics tool. This builds the network from a collection and also exports JSON, CSV and GraphML for Gephi or VOSviewer.

jeff-jw-wang/zotero-llm-assistant.does: Chat with the PDF open in the reader, with answers drawn from the most relevant chunks and citations that jump to the source page. Also searches your library by metadata and works with Ollama, Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic or any compatible endpoint.
jeff-jw-wang/zotero-llm-assistant.pain: Asking an AI about a paper otherwise means pasting text into a chat site. Cloud sharing is off by default and individual items can be marked so they are never sent.

agentsmith29/zotero-mcp-plugin.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so an agent such as Claude Code can manage your library. It can search, cite, edit items, organise collections, add by DOI or ISBN, and find duplicates. It also works with Better BibTeX and exports attachment files to a folder tree that follows your collections.
agentsmith29/zotero-mcp-plugin.pain: Lets an AI agent maintain your library directly, with a preview and confirmation step before bulk changes. Needs Zotero 10 and Better BibTeX, and covers My Library only.

zotero-flow/zotero-quick-highlight.does: Replaces the PDF selection popup with a compact menu that highlights or underlines in your last-used colour, with Zotero's eight colours on hover. Keeps translation results below it.
zotero-flow/zotero-quick-highlight.pain: Zotero's native popup repeats a colour strip and tool toggle. This cuts it to one click per annotation, and stops Translate for Zotero popups from appending earlier selections.

alice1323/zotero-research-workbench.does: A Chinese-language research panel for Zotero 8 and 9. It finds papers through OpenAlex, Crossref and Unpaywall, lets you review candidates before import, and has an OpenAI-compatible model summarise papers into notes. Needs your own API key.
alice1323/zotero-research-workbench.pain: Aimed at researchers in China who want literature discovery and AI-assisted reading notes in one place. Nothing is written to Zotero until you confirm. Its developer describes the first release as deliberately narrow.

orbital188/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up DOIs and shortDOIs for selected items using Crossref and shortdoi.org. It also verifies stored DOIs, marks invalid ones and strips prefixes such as doi: or publisher URLs.
orbital188/zotero-shortdoi.pain: A fork of bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi that adds Zotero 8 and 9 compatibility. Cleans messy DOI fields in bulk instead of editing them one at a time.

qc3455/zotero-toggle-bars--schinese.does: Adds View menu items and shortcuts to toggle the tab bar (Ctrl+T), the annotation toolbar (Ctrl+Y) and the sidebar (Ctrl+B).
qc3455/zotero-toggle-bars--schinese.pain: A fork of wmstack/Zotero-Toggle-Bars that adapts the labels to Simplified Chinese, because the original showed mixed Chinese and English. Frees screen space when reading.

jerryzhongj/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research agent in Zotero: chat with the open PDF, selected text or figures, and compare papers. Agent Mode adds library-wide search, tagging and note editing. Works with API keys, local models, ChatGPT WebChat, Codex or Claude Code.
jerryzhongj/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes. Keeps paper questions, answers with source citations and notes inside Zotero, with Markdown export to Obsidian or Logseq.

guotuanwang/wenxianbianhao.does: Numbers the items in a selected collection with a start number, prefix and zero padding, and translates English titles into Chinese with DeepSeek. Adds two item-list columns for the number and the translation.
guotuanwang/wenxianbianhao.pain: Chinese-language reviewers who keep numbered reading lists otherwise number items by hand. Title translation needs a DeepSeek API key, and the original title is left unchanged.

cookjohn/wohoo.does: A floating GPT chat window with modes for chat, writing, outlining, review and summary, plus tools to analyse and summarise papers and keep a task history. You supply your own API key.
cookjohn/wohoo.pain: Meant for researchers who want writing and reading help from a GPT model without leaving Zotero. Its interface supports Chinese and English.

liuchzzyy/zot-simplificado.does: Adds an Item Key column, editable Short Note and Translated Title rows, and bilingual translation in the Zotero 10 reader. Translation uses Google or an OpenAI-compatible API.
liuchzzyy/zot-simplificado.pain: A fork of roderickvella/Zotero-Item-Key-Column that adds notes, title translation and immersive translated reading in the reader's reading mode.

auince/zotero-agent.does: Indexes a collection into a local knowledge base, then lets a DeepSeek or other OpenAI-compatible model answer questions about it in a sidebar. Embeddings come from SiliconFlow. Keeps a local Markdown note per conversation.
auince/zotero-agent.pain: For researchers who want retrieval-based answers across a whole collection. Needs a chat-model API key, and indexed text is sent to SiliconFlow for embedding. Marked as a prototype.

verandathu/zotero-ai.does: A chat panel in the item pane and reader sidebar that answers questions about the open paper, optionally using its full text. It also searches your library for papers you mention and works with any OpenAI-compatible API.
verandathu/zotero-ai.pain: Asking questions about a paper normally means copying text into a separate chat. It adds prompt presets, searchable conversation history and a meter showing context usage. Needs an API key or a local model.

chocay/zotero-latex-fix.does: Fixes LaTeX pasted into Zotero notes by converting the \( \) and \[ \] delimiters to the $ and $$ forms the editor renders. Unrendered $...$ text also becomes math.
chocay/zotero-latex-fix.pain: Formulas copied from PDFs or websites show up as raw LaTeX in Zotero notes because the editor only recognises dollar-sign delimiters. This fixes them on paste with no setup.

dyingjie/zotero-livereload.does: Previews a remote LaTeX-compiled PDF in Zotero's own reader and refreshes it on demand or automatically when the file changes on the server.
dyingjie/zotero-livereload.pain: For people compiling LaTeX on a server who want to watch the result without leaving Zotero. Auto-refresh polls the PDF address and is off by default. Built and tested on Windows.

soft-defoliation/zotero-smart-translate.does: Translates selected text and item titles and abstracts through an OpenAI-compatible service, with style presets, a glossary and failover between engines. Also summarises papers, extracts innovations, and saves reading notes. Needs your own API key.
soft-defoliation/zotero-smart-translate.pain: Built for reading technical papers in Chinese, with a seed glossary for ferroelectric and high-pressure terms and a bilingual Markdown export. Batch translation writes results back to each item.

meekflyer/zoterokindlenotes.does: Imports highlights and notes from a Kindle's My Clippings.txt into Zotero through a five-step wizard. Books are matched to existing items or created from Google Books and Open Library.
meekflyer/zoterokindlenotes.pain: Kindle highlights sit in one text file outside your library. This files them as child notes under the right book and skips ones already imported.

xiao-chenguang/zotmeta-cs.does: Updates the metadata of articles by DOI and books by ISBN.
xiao-chenguang/zotmeta-cs.pain: A fork of RoadToDream/ZotMeta, extended for computer science conference papers according to its title; it documents little else.

seigwen/dualtran-zotero.does: Translates an item's title and abstract into a child note, a replacement, an appended block or a translated copy. Selected reader text becomes an annotation or note. Uses Google Translate or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
seigwen/dualtran-zotero.pain: Keeps the original beside the translation instead of overwriting it. Google needs no key; AI services need your own key. Defaults to Simplified Chinese, and settings live in the Config Editor.

khakiakhaki/keepzot.does: Minimises Zotero to the taskbar or tray, with custom shortcuts for minimising and closing.
khakiakhaki/keepzot.pain: Keeps Zotero running in the background instead of quitting it. Its developer describes it as almost the same as KeepZotero with configurable shortcuts, which are off by default.

ivorpad/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research agent in Zotero: chat with the open PDF, selected text or figures, and compare papers. Agent Mode adds library-wide search, tagging and note editing. Works with API keys, local models, WebChat, Codex or Claude Code.
ivorpad/llm-for-zotero.pain: Keeps paper questions, source-linked citations and notes inside Zotero, and can save notes to Obsidian or Logseq folders. Optional MinerU parsing handles tables and equations.

dennisklappe/zotero-ai-summarizer.does: Adds an AI icon to the item sidebar that summarises a PDF with OpenAI as a short summary, bullet points, an academic abstract or key quotes. Needs your own OpenAI API key.
dennisklappe/zotero-ai-summarizer.pain: Quick summaries of a paper without leaving Zotero or copying text elsewhere. The key is entered through the Config Editor.

joaocarlos/zotero-gemini.does: A Google Gemini chat in the reader sidebar that streams answers, can attach the current PDF as context, and lists the available Gemini models. Needs a Google AI Studio API key.
joaocarlos/zotero-gemini.pain: A fork of kazgu/zotero-chatgpt rebuilt for Gemini. Lets you ask Gemini about the paper you are reading without uploading it by hand.

as-zdq/zotero-institutional-pdf-bridge.does: Adds an institutional proxy to Find Available PDF so Zotero can fetch full text through a university or company gateway. Supports Sangfor-compatible WebVPN and URL-template proxies, and can look up PDFs for new items.
as-zdq/zotero-institutional-pdf-bridge.pain: Off-campus access normally means logging in through the browser and downloading by hand. Sign-in happens on your institution's own page, and credentials are held in Zotero's Password Manager.

b1ue-e/zotero-llm-wiki.does: Turns selected papers into structured wiki pages through an OpenAI-compatible API. Includes a wiki browser, concept and entity pages, an agent chat and a multi-step deep research command. Needs an API key.
b1ue-e/zotero-llm-wiki.pain: Follows Karpathy's LLM-Wiki idea: instead of re-reading papers, you build a linked knowledge base from your library that you can browse and edit. Interface in Chinese and English.

philippyang21/zotero-pdf-helper.does: Adds an invisible text layer to scanned PDFs using PaddleOCR and tidies highlighted quotations. It converts punctuation, removes stray spaces and fills in book details from the copyright page. OCR needs a PaddleOCR token and local Python.
philippyang21/zotero-pdf-helper.pain: Aimed at Chinese-language readers whose scanned books cannot be searched or highlighted, and whose CNKI papers copy out with English punctuation and extra spaces.

jkroes/zotero-tana.does: Syncs Zotero items into Tana as #zotero nodes through Tana's Local API, updating them in place when items change. Includes PDF annotations as highlight, comment and image nodes. Needs a Tana access token.
jkroes/zotero-tana.pain: A fork of Notero with the Notion side replaced by Tana. Keeps a Tana reference graph in step with Zotero without re-entering references.

tangent-owl/zotero_temporary_ink.does: Draws pen strokes and rectangles over a PDF in the Zotero reader that fade away on their own, without creating annotations or changing the file.
tangent-owl/zotero_temporary_ink.pain: Useful for pointing at something while reading or presenting without cluttering the PDF. Works only on PDFs in Zotero 9, and drawing is cleared when you scroll or zoom.

grayxu/zotero6-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader, annotations, notes and item titles, with a dictionary for single words and a standalone window comparing engines. Defaults to Google Translate.
grayxu/zotero6-pdf-translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate for Zotero 6. Puts translation next to the text instead of in a separate translation site.

const7/llm-for-zotero-lite.does: Chat with the current paper in Zotero's side panel using API, Codex, GitHub Copilot or WebChat providers. Includes selected-text context, prompt presets and a timeline for jumping between questions.
const7/llm-for-zotero-lite.pain: A lean fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that removes Agent workflows, standalone windows and note export to keep paper chat fast. Its author calls it a personal fork.

brian-j-griffith/storscan.does: Audits linked attachments, moves misplaced files into author folders, renames them from Zotero's template, removes broken links and merges duplicate files. Can also find open-access full text by DOI.
brian-j-griffith/storscan.pain: Large libraries of linked PDFs drift out of order and leave dead links. This checks every attachment and previews changes before moving or renaming anything.

ustc-iontrap/zotero-author-search.does: Right-click an item to find other items in your library by the same authors, using flexible, strict or surname matching. Results can be copied, saved as a child note or filed into per-author collections.
ustc-iontrap/zotero-author-search.pain: Zotero has no quick way to see what else you hold by an item's authors. Affiliations are read from the Extra field when present.

gmf3/zotero-bookmark-editor.does: A reader sidebar panel to add, rename, nest, reorder and delete PDF bookmarks. It writes them into the PDF's own outline, so any standards-compliant reader shows them.
gmf3/zotero-bookmark-editor.pain: A minimal fork of Jasminum with only its bookmark module and a Spanish and English interface. Long PDFs without a table of contents become navigable, in stored or linked files.

adoream/zotero-citation-count.does: Fetches citation counts by DOI through api.rua.dev and saves them in the Extra field. Adds item-list columns for the count and update date, and updates new items automatically.
adoream/zotero-citation-count.pain: Zotero shows no citation numbers. This stores them in your library without an API key, and they stay readable after the plugin is removed.

purushka/zotero-concept-explorer.does: Select a term or passage in the PDF reader to get an AI explanation, then follow sub-concepts and ask follow-up questions. Conversations are saved as a local knowledge tree. Needs your own model service and API key.
purushka/zotero-concept-explorer.pain: For readers meeting unfamiliar concepts in a paper who want to chase them down without losing their place. The full text is sent only when you ask for a full-text explanation. Mainly Chinese interface.

kongyan66/zotero-paper-radar.does: Recommends new arXiv papers based on interest profiles built from your library, explaining why each matched. Offers optional Chinese AI summaries and one-click saving of paper and PDF. Needs an embedding service key.
kongyan66/zotero-paper-radar.pain: Finding new papers otherwise means browsing arXiv by hand. Profiles are editable and you choose the topics and date range. Beta, for Zotero 9, with a Chinese interface.

bulletproof-system/zotero-paralens.does: Translates whole PDFs through a local BabelDOC backend and your own API key. The translation imports as a new attachment and opens beside the original, with hover highlighting between matching paragraphs.
bulletproof-system/zotero-paralens.pain: Reading a translated paper usually loses the link to the original wording. Its developer calls this a technical prototype, tested on Windows with Zotero 10; it needs uv installed and may cost API fees.

leewin0531/zotero-pdf-compress.does: Right-click a PDF attachment to shrink it with a bundled Ghostscript, at 150 or 100 DPI for embedded images, keeping annotations when it replaces the file. Runs offline on Windows.
leewin0531/zotero-pdf-compress.pain: Large paper PDFs are slow to open and sync. It skips encrypted or damaged files and keeps the original if savings are small; replacing in place cannot be undone. Chinese interface, Zotero 9.

ppavlidis/zotero-pdf-sethorizontal.does: Sets default PDF view options in Zotero 7 to 10: scroll mode, zoom, page layout and the hand tool. They apply when an item is added or a tab opens.
ppavlidis/zotero-pdf-sethorizontal.pain: A fork of qiwei-ma/zotero-pdf-setHorizontal that adds Zotero 9 and 10 support, a page layout option and fixes for stale preferences and a blank settings pane.

lemos1235/zotero-putongdoc.does: Sends selected PDFs to the PutongDoc online service for translation and imports bilingual or translation-only PDFs as attachments. Needs a PutongDoc API token and uses your account's quota.
lemos1235/zotero-putongdoc.pain: Translating a whole paper by hand means uploading and downloading files. This queues one or many PDFs from Zotero and attaches the results, with MinerU, Zhipu or built-in parsing. Chinese interface.

useroption3/zotero-relation-graph.does: Draws the Related links between items as an interactive graph you can pan, zoom, search and limit to a collection. Nodes are coloured by item type. Runs locally with no network requests.
useroption3/zotero-relation-graph.pain: Zotero shows related items only one at a time. This shows clusters, hubs and stray links across the whole library at once.

x-t-e-r/zotero-resource-search-mcp.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI clients can search academic sources, patents and the web. They can also look up DOI, PMID, arXiv or ISBN, add results to collections and fetch PDFs.
x-t-e-r/zotero-resource-search-mcp.pain: Lets an AI agent search and save into your library without manual copy-paste. You connect clients such as Claude Code or Cursor, and install search sources separately from a provider repository.

lovelynewlife/zoteroofmine.does: Keeps a reading history of opened PDFs in the left sidebar and copies items as structured AI context from the right-click menu. Includes a separate command-line tool, zcli, for querying the local library.
lovelynewlife/zoteroofmine.pain: A personal toolkit that lets AI assistants read your library metadata without API keys. Its developer says Zotero 8 and 9 behaviour still needs checking on real builds.

migueldlm/zotlit.does: The Zotero side of ZotLit, which connects Zotero to Obsidian so notes and library data can be used from the Obsidian plugin.
migueldlm/zotlit.pain: For people who keep literature notes in Obsidian. Its developer warns it is third-party, may break after updates, and advises backing up your data first.

wgcyeo/aitero.does: A chat panel in the item pane and reader sidebar that answers questions about the selected PDF through your local Codex CLI. Citations open the cited PDF page. Needs Zotero 10.
wgcyeo/aitero.pain: Ask about a paper without copying text elsewhere. It is read-only: it never changes your items, notes or database. Validated on macOS only.

saona-raimundo/hellozotero.does: A hello-world example of a Zotero plug-in with no real features, for people writing their first plugin.
saona-raimundo/hellozotero.pain: A starting point showing the file layout and packaging of a legacy Zotero 6 plugin.

xiaohemo9178/paper-classifier.does: Sorts selected papers into two-level collections by their role in a research topic you type, using the title and abstract with DeepSeek. Creates folders as needed and moves items or keeps their old collections. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
xiaohemo9178/paper-classifier.pain: Sorting a pile of papers for one project by hand is slow. It uses a fixed theme pool to avoid scattered folders. Chinese and English versions are available.

reborker/reta-ai-chat.does: Adds an AI chat area to the item pane that answers questions about the selected item's metadata, abstract, tags and notes. It can optionally send the PDF's indexed full text. Needs your own API key for an OpenAI-compatible service such as DeepSeek.
reborker/reta-ai-chat.pain: Asking an AI about a paper otherwise means copying text out of Zotero. This keeps the chat beside the item, and its developer says nothing goes to a server of the author's.

cuzimnero/zitatlotse.does: Searches your PDFs' full text for original quotations and reviews supporting and opposing evidence with AI. Saves chosen passages as quotations or citations. Runs on Windows with a bundled Python runtime; models can be OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek or local Ollama.
cuzimnero/zitatlotse.pain: Finding the exact passage that backs or contradicts a claim means re-reading many PDFs. This searches your own library and jumps to the highlighted passage. Its developer calls it experimental.

matt-v50/zotero-arxiv-workflow.does: Merges an arXiv preprint item with its published version into one item. Also searches online for published versions, downloads the latest PDF, and lets you choose which PDF opens by default.
matt-v50/zotero-arxiv-workflow.pain: A fork of AllanChain/zotero-arxiv-workflow; its README doesn't say what it changes. Zotero can't merge items of different types, so a preprint and its journal version stay separate and lose the data other plugins attach to the item.

normanify/zotero-attach-size.does: Adds a sortable Size column to the item list showing the total file size of each item's attachments, or the file's own size for an attachment. Sizes appear in B, K, M or G units. Built for Zotero 9.
normanify/zotero-attach-size.pain: Zotero doesn't show how large your attachments are, so finding the heavy PDFs that fill storage means checking files by hand.

yileme/zotero-chapterize.does: Previews and splits a book PDF into chapters by its bookmarks or page ranges you enter. Each chapter becomes a linked Book Section item with its own PDF, with DOIs and authors filled from Crossref.
yileme/zotero-chapterize.pain: Citing or reading one chapter of an edited book otherwise means cutting the PDF yourself and typing the chapter's metadata. This does the split and fills in details, with a preview before anything is written.

mug-chen/zotero-context-translator.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader into a persistent card showing original, translation and notes. It sends the title, abstract, section path and nearby text to your own OpenAI-compatible API, and only when you click Translate. Windows and Zotero 9 only.
mug-chen/zotero-context-translator.pain: Plain selection translation loses the paper's context, so technical terms come out wrong. This gives the model the surrounding text and makes no request until you ask. It doesn't work on scanned PDFs.

oddish3/zotero-custom-plugins.does: A personal set of Zotero 10 add-ons: Semantic Scholar TLDR summaries for items, and a Supplement PDF tool. Published with update metadata and source files. The TLDR plugin derives from syt2/Zotero-TLDR.
oddish3/zotero-custom-plugins.pain: Aimed at one person's own workflow: cleaning duplicates, filling in missing summaries and keeping the add-ons compatible with Zotero 10.

young-bo-i/zotero-enterscholar-journal.does: Shows journal details for the selected item in the item pane, including JCR impact factor, SJR, H-index and Chinese Academy of Sciences (中科院) tier. Also shows review time and APC fees from sources such as Crossref, OpenAlex, DOAJ and Scimago. Needs an EnterScholar (恩特学术) account.
young-bo-i/zotero-enterscholar-journal.pain: Checking a journal's ranking and fees means searching several sites for each paper. This shows them where you read the reference, mainly useful to Chinese-language researchers.

vitaminac/zotero-github-star-count.does: Links a paper to a GitHub repository and fetches its star count, storing the number in the Extra field so you can show and sort by it in the item list.
vitaminac/zotero-github-star-count.pain: For papers that come with code, repository popularity is a quick signal that stock Zotero has no way to show or sort by.

dlestarjette/zotero-key-reveal.does: Shows each item's 8-character key in a sortable Item Key column and in an Item Key row in the item pane. A right-click Copy Item Key command puts the key, or several keys one per line, on the clipboard.
dlestarjette/zotero-key-reveal.pain: Item keys are needed for the Zotero web API, zotero://select links and scripts, but Zotero shows them nowhere.

attr0/zotero-pdf-background.does: Adds a toolbar eye button to the PDF reader that switches between background colours, including a green one, to ease eye strain. Based on a Zotero night-mode framework.
attr0/zotero-pdf-background.pain: A fork of wangqian06/zotero-pdf-background. It adds a brighter night mode and fixes missing background colour in spread mode, where several pages sit in one row. Zotero 6 only.

raphaelstevens/zotero-pdf-to-md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown from a right-click menu, saving the .md file next to the PDF or in a folder you choose. Needs Python 3.8 or newer with Microsoft's MarkItDown package installed.
raphaelstevens/zotero-pdf-to-md.pain: Zotero can't turn papers into Markdown, which people want for notes, search tools or feeding text to AI. This does it for several items at once.

itofrrr/zotero-reading-order.does: Adds an Order column to the item list for a numeric reading priority. Set it from the right-click menu, or number a selection in the order shown in the list. The value is kept in the Extra field, so it syncs.
itofrrr/zotero-reading-order.pain: Zotero has no field for the order in which to read papers. This lets you rank a reading list and sort by it.

kai-yhg/zotero-research-link-manager.does: Mirrors your collections as a folder tree on Windows. Each stored PDF gets a hard or symbolic link named by title, year and attachment key, and PDFs are never copied. Built for Zotero 9.
kai-yhg/zotero-research-link-manager.pain: Zotero keeps PDFs in opaque storage folders. This gives other programs a readable folder view of your collections without duplicating files. It handles only stored PDFs, not linked files or group libraries.

saxena224pawan/zotero-scholar-assistant.does: Imports paper lists from CSV or TSV, finds open-access PDFs, and uses local Ollama or Google Gemini to make highlights, study notes and quizzes. A dashboard shows each paper's progress. Gemini needs a Google AI Studio API key.
saxena224pawan/zotero-scholar-assistant.pain: Reading and summarising many papers is slow. This batches the work and rejects incomplete AI output instead of saving broken notes. Built for Zotero 10.

scaltagi/zotero-show-keys.does: Shows Zotero's internal 8-character keys in a sortable column and a read-only field in the item pane. Right-click commands copy an item's key or a collection's key to the clipboard.
scaltagi/zotero-show-keys.pain: Keys are useful for scripting and the web API, but Zotero hides them. This makes them visible and copyable.

oneoneliu/zotero-tag-graph.does: Draws the papers and tags of the selected collection as an interactive network graph you can drag, zoom and search. A side panel filters tags, and a right-click menu changes a tag's colour or hides it.
oneoneliu/zotero-tag-graph.pain: Seeing which topics dominate a project or journal folder is hard from a flat tag list. The graph shows tag counts and links at a glance. Its developer advises against opening it on a whole large library.

li-kangling/zotero-watch-folder-multiroo.does: Keeps several local PDF folders in two-way step with Zotero collections. Each watched folder binds to a top-level collection, subfolders map to subcollections, and renames, moves and deletions follow both ways. PDFs import as linked files. Built for Zotero 10.
li-kangling/zotero-watch-folder-multiroo.pain: A derivative of Zotero Watch Folder 2.8.6, which watches only one folder. Its developer says mirroring and deletion sync change files on disk, so back up first.

qianrenli/fastlinkinzotero.does: Adds Obsidian-style note linking to the note editor. Typing [[ opens a search popup of your notes, and Ctrl+N finds or creates a note and inserts a native zotero://note link. Works without Better Notes.
qianrenli/fastlinkinzotero.pain: Linking one Zotero note to another normally means copying note links by hand. This makes it as quick as wiki-style linking in Obsidian.

leike0813/mineru-cli-zotero.does: Runs the MinerU command-line tool on PDF attachments from a right-click menu and attaches the resulting Markdown file to the parent item as a linked attachment. Handles several items at once. Needs MinerU installed and a MinerU API key.
leike0813/mineru-cli-zotero.pain: Gets structured Markdown, with images extracted, out of scientific PDFs without leaving Zotero, and skips PDFs that already have a Markdown file.

wzq-come-on/paper-chat-for-zotero.does: Chat with papers, translate selected text, search literature and make notes or slides, using a sidebar or floating window. This fork adds a Codex Switch local proxy for model discovery, streaming chat, translation and voice input. You can use your own OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or DeepSeek key.
wzq-come-on/paper-chat-for-zotero.pain: A fork of syt2/paper-chat-for-zotero that adds Codex Switch support and turns off the original's automatic updates. For people who run Codex through a local proxy.

olekd21/translate-bridge-for-zotero.does: Connects Chrome's built-in Google Translate to Zotero. Select a translated Chinese sentence on a paper's web page and it finds the matching English text in your Zotero PDF, then creates a native highlight with the Chinese translation and your note. Needs a Chrome extension and Chrome 138 or newer.
olekd21/translate-bridge-for-zotero.pain: Reading a paper in machine translation and then finding and annotating the original passage is slow work. This does it in one step, with no translation API key.

cantikapf/zotero-ai-agent.does: An early scaffold for an AI assistant in the PDF reader that would chat about the open paper through an LLM gateway. Plans include a read-only local bridge for external agents and export to Obsidian via ZotLit.
cantikapf/zotero-ai-agent.pain: Its developer says it is not yet a working plugin. It is aimed at people who want a lightweight AI reading assistant with Obsidian notes.

shunzi-work/zotero-bibtex-to-clipboard.does: Adds a toolbar button that copies the selected items as BibTeX, ready to paste into a .bib file. Converts accented and special characters to LaTeX and generates unique citation keys when none exist.
shunzi-work/zotero-bibtex-to-clipboard.pain: Getting clean BibTeX out of Zotero normally means an export dialog or a larger plugin. This is one click, with LaTeX escaping done for you.

jiang-111/zotero-codex-chat.does: Embeds a Codex chat panel in Zotero 9 for asking about the selected item, collection or PDF selection, and writes replies into child notes. Asks you to confirm before any Zotero MCP read or write. Needs Codex CLI with app-server support and Node.js.
jiang-111/zotero-codex-chat.pain: Lets people who use Codex for reading and note drafting stay inside Zotero. The confirmation step exists because heavy MCP reads can freeze Zotero.

shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-location-me.does: Adds a right-click Folders submenu listing every collection that holds the selected item. From it you can jump to a collection, remove the item from one, or keep only one. A batch manager window handles many items at once.
shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-location-me.pain: One item can sit in several collections, and Zotero makes it hard to see where or to tidy those memberships. It never deletes the item, attachments or notes.

wadaxiyang/zotero-collection-sorter.does: Lets you set how each collection orders its direct child collections: Zotero default, name A to Z, or name Z to A. Choose it from a right-click menu on the parent. Rules are per parent, display only and stay in your local profile.
wadaxiyang/zotero-collection-sorter.pain: Zotero sorts the collection tree one way for everything, so a folder of conference years can't run newest first while venues run alphabetically. Built for Zotero 9.

ravenhogwarts/zotero_csl_visual_editor_r.does: A step-by-step visual editor for CSL citation styles. Pick a starting style, reorder fields, set name rules and punctuation, compare previews, then export and install it. Built for Chinese-language academic writing.
ravenhogwarts/zotero_csl_visual_editor_r.pain: Editing a citation style normally means writing CSL XML by hand. This lets Chinese-language researchers adjust a style to a journal's rules without that.

huanongfish/zotero-doc2x-tag.does: Automatically adds a circled-M tag to an item when the Doc2X plugin adds a converted Markdown child note to it. A Tools menu command tags items converted earlier. Needs the Doc2X Zotero plugin.
huanongfish/zotero-doc2x-tag.pain: Once you give the tag a colour, converted papers show a coloured marker in the item list, so you can see which have been through Doc2X.

thegadflyandmontalleni/zotero_download_f.does: Removes the Zotero version from the User-Agent sent to Sci-Hub hosts, which Cloudflare otherwise blocks with HTTP 403. This lets Sci-Hub PDF resolvers work on Zotero 9; you still add the resolvers yourself.
thegadflyandmontalleni/zotero_download_f.pain: Find Available PDF fails silently against Sci-Hub mirrors on Zotero 9 without this. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

homomorph1sm/zotero-draft-pdf-watch.does: Watches a local folder for new versions of your manuscript PDF and updates a fixed Zotero item, by telling you or replacing the old attachment automatically. Matches files by name pattern and checks content first. Built for Zotero 10.
homomorph1sm/zotero-draft-pdf-watch.pain: Authors who keep re-exporting a draft otherwise re-attach each version by hand. The old PDF and its annotations go to the Zotero trash and the source file is never deleted.

sigmoid-bar/zotero-file.does: A Zotero 7 port of ZotFile that automatically renames and moves attachments, and reads your existing ZotFile settings. Tablet sync is not included.
sigmoid-bar/zotero-file.pain: ZotFile never moved to Zotero 7. This carries over its core renaming and moving so you can keep using a familiar workflow.

yuchen-06/zotero-html-style.does: Adds a reader toolbar button for switching the colour theme of HTML pages opened in Zotero, with light, dark, beige, green and lilac options. You can set your own colours as JSON variables in preferences.
yuchen-06/zotero-html-style.pain: Saved web pages open as a plain white page. This lets you read them in a gentler theme.

jrjfonseca/zotero_merge_supplementary_pl.does: Appends a supplementary PDF to the main paper PDF on an item with exactly two PDF attachments, from a right-click command. Annotations on both are kept, and a backup of the original is saved. Finds the supplement by keywords in its title or filename.
jrjfonseca/zotero_merge_supplementary_pl.pain: Papers and their supporting information often live as two files. This puts them in one PDF so you read and annotate once.

lubinxtu/zotero-paper-translator.does: Translates a whole English PDF paper into Chinese, block by block, keeping LaTeX formulas and tables intact. Saves an HTML child attachment you can print to PDF. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service.
lubinxtu/zotero-paper-translator.pain: Selection translators work on fragments. This produces a full structured Chinese version of a paper with a terminology list, aimed at computer vision and robotics.

q1351998764/zotero-pdf2zh-community.does: Translates PDFs into bilingual PDFs through a local Python backend, from a selection in Zotero. You need the backend running and your own translation service, model and API key. Windows is the documented setup.
q1351998764/zotero-pdf2zh-community.pain: A community fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh. It handles more API response formats, pins dependencies, fixes model downloads and improves error reports.

kazusa3e/zotero-progress.does: Tracks reading progress for PDFs and EPUBs by table-of-contents chapter. An item pane panel has a progress bar and checkable chapters, and a Progress column shows counts like 3/7. Clicking a chapter jumps to it in the reader.
kazusa3e/zotero-progress.pain: Zotero doesn't record how far through a long book or report you are. This keeps chapter-level progress, stored in the Extra field. Built for Zotero 8.

lukas7766/zotero-tag-viewer.does: Adds a sortable Tags column to the item list showing each item's tags, comma-separated. A setting chooses manual tags, automatic tags or both.
lukas7766/zotero-tag-viewer.pain: Seeing tags normally means selecting each item or using the tag selector. This shows them in the list beside titles and authors.

nkbaim/zotero-wechat-importer.does: Takes a WeChat official account article link, extracts the text, and uses DeepSeek to find the papers it mentions. Each is checked against PubMed and Crossref, then imported to Zotero. Needs your own DeepSeek API key.
nkbaim/zotero-wechat-importer.pain: Chinese-language science posts mention studies without full citations. This turns them into verified Zotero records without searching for each, and only checked records are imported.

delinqu/ipec-paper-group.does: Downloads PDFs from arXiv for selected items or a whole collection from the right-click menu. It reads the arXiv ID from the URL, DOI or Extra field, skips items that have a PDF, and replaces broken ones.
delinqu/ipec-paper-group.pain: Saves attaching arXiv papers one by one when you have imported many references without their files.

xvhaor/paper-translation-master.does: Runs OCR on a paper's PDF in Zotero and shows it as an editable HTML page you can correct, then translates it with an OpenAI-compatible model. Both are saved as attachments, with side-by-side PDF reading and export to HTML, Markdown, LaTeX and Excel. Windows installers for GPU and CPU OCR.
xvhaor/paper-translation-master.pain: Scanned or awkwardly formatted papers are hard to read and translate. This keeps formulas and tables and saves results so they are not redone, in a Chinese-language interface.

jiwannian/zhanhtran.does: Translates PDFs, scans and images using a model provider you configure, with local Python parsing and OCR. Output keeps the source layout, as a translated file or a side-by-side bilingual one. Needs Python 3.10 or newer and your own provider and API key.
jiwannian/zhanhtran.pain: Most translators lose a document's layout. This puts the translation back into the original areas of the page. Extracted text goes to your provider.

arrancurran/zometa.does: Updates the metadata of selected items in bulk: journal articles from DOI records, books from ISBN records and preprints from arXiv IDs. It can find identifiers in the PDF text and create parent items for loose PDFs. Tags failed and skipped items.
arrancurran/zometa.pain: A fork of RoadToDream/ZotMeta; its README doesn't say what it changes. Imports often leave thin metadata, and fixing many items one at a time is slow.

evanbrooks01/zotero-ai-reading-studio.does: An AI reading workspace in the PDF reader: chat with a paper, translate selected text in a separate panel, and open online paper briefs for arXiv items. Conversations are saved per paper as child notes. Uses your own OpenAI Responses-compatible API URL and key.
evanbrooks01/zotero-ai-reading-studio.pain: Keeps AI questions, translation and long-running paper discussions in one place, with a separate model for each. For researchers who build up context on a paper over time.

reginalluna/zotero-ciation-preview.does: Adds a Citation Preview section to the item pane showing the in-text citation and bibliography entry for the selected item, in your Quick Copy style. A separate legacy build covers Zotero 4 to 6.
reginalluna/zotero-ciation-preview.pain: Checking how an item will look in a given citation style normally means pasting it into a document. This shows it as you browse.

ccwss-maker/zotero-edge-tts.does: Reads text you select in the PDF reader aloud using Microsoft Edge text-to-speech, with a toolbar toggle and a choice of voices in several languages. Needs edge-tts and the mpv player installed. Tested on Linux only.
ccwss-maker/zotero-edge-tts.pain: Lets you listen to a paper as you follow it, which helps with long texts or reading in a second language.

practiceearnestly/zotero-fulltext-flow.does: Finds missing full-text PDFs for the collections you choose, trying Zotero's own retrieval and the JLSS (聚联) service in an order you set. Downloaded files are checked against the item's DOI and title before attaching. A JLSS account is needed for that route.
practiceearnestly/zotero-fulltext-flow.pain: Filling in missing PDFs for a whole project folder is slow by hand. This queues the work and flags uncertain matches for review. Its developer calls it a preview.

fjonasalice/zotero-inspire.does: Updates selected items or collections from the INSPIRE-HEP database, filling in published metadata and citation counts with and without self-citations. Falls back to Crossref counts for papers outside INSPIRE. Can run automatically on new items.
fjonasalice/zotero-inspire.pain: A fork of fkguo/zotero-inspire; its README doesn't say what it changes. For high energy physics researchers whose arXiv items later get published.

kalenjosifovski/zotero-integration-agent.does: A local bridge that tags new items status/to-read and ai/pending. A separate local worker then writes Obsidian literature notes and proposes tags from a controlled list. Needs that worker and OMP set up.
kalenjosifovski/zotero-integration-agent.pain: For one person's pipeline from Zotero to an Obsidian wiki, with automatic tagging and notes. It is not a stand-alone plugin.

ethanwanghaven/zotero-math-inline-fixer.does: Fixes maths that fails to render when AI text is pasted into Zotero notes, turning stray $...$ and $$...$$ into real formula nodes. A floating toolbar has a converter window that rewrites Markdown and LaTeX for Better Notes, and a tool that wraps bare letters as formulas.
ethanwanghaven/zotero-math-inline-fixer.pain: Pasting from ChatGPT, DeepSeek and similar tools into Better Notes often leaves raw dollar signs instead of formulas. This repairs them in one step.

yikuyoo/zotero-page-images.does: Places images on PDF pages in the Zotero reader, with captions you can edit, and exports a new PDF containing the images and your native annotations. Images can be pasted from the clipboard or loaded from PNG, JPEG or WebP files, then moved, resized, hidden or backed up as JSON.
yikuyoo/zotero-page-images.pain: Zotero can't put a figure or screenshot beside a paragraph in a PDF. Its developer says this is a beta tested only on Windows with Zotero 10.0.3, and Zotero's own export or print leaves the images out.

phlya/zotero-paper-import.does: Imports papers from pasted text, skipping ones already in your library. Paste chat messages, e-mails or reference lists and it finds links, DOIs, arXiv and PubMed IDs. A companion plugin watches a Microsoft Teams channel through a Power Automate flow.
phlya/zotero-paper-import.pain: Colleagues share papers as links in chat threads, and adding each one by hand is slow. This turns a pasted block of messages into library items, with each reference reported as added, duplicate or failed.

wintus/zotero-remove-space-ja.does: Adds a Remove Space button to each annotation in the reader sidebar that deletes stray spaces between Japanese characters (Kanji, Hiragana, Katakana). Spaces next to Latin letters or digits are kept.
wintus/zotero-remove-space-ja.pain: Highlighting Japanese text in a PDF often puts spaces between characters, which Japanese doesn't use. This cleans an annotation in one click.

adamsghaier/zotero-replace-pdf.does: Adds Add PDF and Replace PDF to the item right-click menu. Replace PDF writes the new file into the existing attachment's file, so the name and attachment stay the same, then reindexes it and clears the picked file from Downloads.
adamsghaier/zotero-replace-pdf.pain: Deleting and re-adding a PDF creates a new file with the same name, which synced folders such as iCloud can show as a duplicate like Name (1).pdf. Writing in place syncs as an ordinary edit and keeps tags, notes and links.

anfang886/zotero-selection-search.does: Searches your whole library for text you have selected in the item pane. Select text in an editable field, right-click and choose Search for the selection, and Zotero jumps to My Library and runs the quick search.
anfang886/zotero-selection-search.pain: Looking up a phrase from an item's metadata normally means copying it, going to My Library and pasting it into the search box. This does it in one step.

luckyfulong/zotlite.does: An AI reading assistant: chat about a paper with DeepSeek, OpenAI or Google Gemini. It parses PDFs into Markdown through the MinerU service and jumps from answers to the original text. Adds impact factor and citation count columns and updates metadata from Crossref and Semantic Scholar.
luckyfulong/zotlite.pain: Reading, checking journal metrics and tidying metadata normally means switching between windows. Needs an API key for the chat provider, and MinerU, Semantic Scholar and Tavily need their own keys.

4-dimethylamino-78-dihydroxyflavone/zsyn.does: Exports a Zotero collection into a Typst project folder. It writes items and every annotation (text, comment, colour, page) as JSON, a BibLaTeX bibliography with citation keys, and copies of the annotated PDFs. Exports run automatically when highlights or comments change.
4-dimethylamino-78-dihydroxyflavone/zsyn.pain: Writers using Typst otherwise copy quotes and references out of Zotero by hand. The files stay in step with the collection, so typst watch picks up new highlights and devices without Zotero can still compile.

zeyu42/breeze.does: Summarises your research interests from your library's titles, abstracts and collections using an LLM, then hides RSS feed articles that don't match them. A Breeze Filter button in the feed toolbar toggles the filtering, and results are cached.
zeyu42/breeze.pain: Journal RSS feeds are mostly articles you don't care about. This filters them against your own library. Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible service.

lilynaux/citepulse.does: Fetches citation counts from OpenAlex by DOI and shows them in a sortable OpenAlex Citations column. Right-click selected items to update them in a batch; counts are stored in each item's Extra field.
lilynaux/citepulse.pain: Zotero has no citation count column. This lets you sort a library by how often papers are cited, with no account or API key, and keeps your other Extra content intact.

a1exhorst/llm-for-zotero-themes-companio.does: Restyles the LLM for Zotero plugin with 20+ colour themes and live previews. A custom CSS editor applies to its sidebar, standalone chat, dialogs and menus. Needs the original LLM for Zotero plugin installed as well.
a1exhorst/llm-for-zotero-themes-companio.pain: For people who use LLM for Zotero and want its chat windows to match their taste. Disabling the companion restores the original look.

dinnercooker/minimize-zotero-to-tray-plu.does: Hides Zotero in the Windows system tray when you close the window, with a tray menu to show, hide, open preferences or quit Zotero. Options include a global hotkey and starting silently. Needs Windows 10 or 11 and the built-in PowerShell.
dinnercooker/minimize-zotero-to-tray-plu.pain: A fork of B3000Kcn/minimize-zotero-to-tray, rewritten for Zotero 8 to 10. The original's tray menu had no Quit entry, which left Zotero hidden with no way to exit.

crowcosmos/stashlibrary.does: A companion for StashLibrary, a tool for collecting references first and organising them in Zotero later.
crowcosmos/stashlibrary.pain: Probably for people who gather sources quickly and sort them afterwards; little else is documented.

chan-developer/zotero-bilingual-reader.does: Translates PDF pages or selected text between English and Simplified Chinese, shown beside the original. It handles the current page, a range or the whole PDF, and saves the pair as a child note. Also lets you ask an AI about a page or passage.
chan-developer/zotero-bilingual-reader.pain: Reading papers across English and Chinese means pasting into a translator and losing the layout. Needs an API key for DeepSeek, MiniMax or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint; some local services need none.

git-jiwon/zotero-context-search.does: Searches metadata and indexed PDF text from the existing search box. Results show matching excerpts with PDF page numbers you can click to open. Also adds star favourites and configurable citation copying.
git-jiwon/zotero-context-search.pain: Zotero's search shows which items match but not why. This shows the passage and page, and needs no AI service or separate index. Korean and English interface.

jeremyliew7/zotero-dual-reader-releases.does: Side-by-side translation preview for academic PDFs in Zotero. This repository only hosts the plugin's release files and update feed.
jeremyliew7/zotero-dual-reader-releases.pain: For readers who want a paper and its translation on screen together; its source is kept elsewhere and the repository documents nothing more.

pencilheart/zotero-google-scholar-citati.does: Fetches Google Scholar citation counts into a sortable column. You can choose a mirror URL, and counts are fetched automatically when an item is added. Also formats chemical formulas in titles and renames Chinese authors.
pencilheart/zotero-google-scholar-citati.pain: A fork of justinribeiro/zotero-google-scholar-citation-count. Mirror URLs avoid Google's robot checks and the random waits, and it adds auto-fetch, a redesigned settings pane and better Chinese localisation.

lenbour1/zotero-gpt-pro.does: An AI research assistant for Zotero with annotations, outlines and advanced prompts. Can use an OpenAI-compatible key.
lenbour1/zotero-gpt-pro.pain: For people who want to put GPT-style assistance inside Zotero; little else is documented.

xpropel/zotero-mcp.does: Lets AI clients manage your Zotero library through a local MCP server and a bridge plugin that writes locally. Tools cover items, attachments, notes, collections, tags, BibTeX export and OCR of PDFs, with no Zotero cloud key.
xpropel/zotero-mcp.pain: Zotero's built-in local API can read but not write items. This plugin adds those write endpoints so an AI assistant can organise a library without direct database edits.

nicrael/zotero-pdf-region-export.does: Exports a selected region of a PDF page as a PNG or JPG at a chosen DPI, with aspect ratio locks and a filename built from the item. Also adds a LaTeX cite button to the text selection popup that copies the quote as a citation.
