nicrael/zotero-pdf-region-export.pain: Zotero can't crop a figure from a PDF at high resolution. This saves it directly, and the LaTeX button gives a paste-ready quote with a Better BibTeX key.

parsam110/zotero-reading-list.does: Lets you define your own item list columns with preset values, then set a value for one or several items from the right-click menu. Originally built to track whether you have read items.
parsam110/zotero-reading-list.pain: A fork of Dominic-DallOsto/zotero-reading-list; it generalises read status into custom columns for statuses such as read or to-read.

grahmgaydos/zotero-reading-partner.does: A dialogue partner in the PDF reader's side pane that reads the paper with your highlights, comments and notes. Pin points from the conversation onto passages as highlight comments, save replies as notes, and compare against other papers. Works with Anthropic, OpenAI or Ollama.
grahmgaydos/zotero-reading-partner.pain: Made for thinking a paper through like a supervision, not for summarising or automating a literature review. Each paper keeps its own conversation.

reycn/zotero-super-search.does: Searches your library by meaning as well as keywords. It indexes titles, creators, tags, abstracts and notes, and searches PDF text with local embeddings, jumping to the matched page. Needs Zotero 9; PDF search needs Python 3.12.
reycn/zotero-super-search.pain: Zotero search misses a paper if your words differ from its text. This finds related passages and keeps PDF text, queries and indexes on your computer.

guzhiling/lolping_zotero.does: A League of Legends-style ping wheel for the PDF reader: hold a key, press the page and drag to a ping, and its icon and sound appear. Repeat the ping in the same spot to save it as a coloured note annotation with a tag.
guzhiling/lolping_zotero.pain: A playful way to flag spots on a page quickly. Saved pings sync like annotations and go into exported PDFs as ordinary sticky notes. A Zotero port of lolPing.

dsmoz/scholar-companion.does: An AI research companion for Zotero with chat, semantic search, a similarity graph and discovery of related work. This repository only hosts the built plugin and its update feed.
dsmoz/scholar-companion.pain: For readers who want AI help exploring their library; the source is private and the repository documents nothing more.

kumiko-kmk/translator-for-zotero.does: Translates titles, abstracts and selected text in the PDF reader into Simplified Chinese. The translation overlays the original layout and can be selected and copied. Translations are cached locally.
kumiko-kmk/translator-for-zotero.pain: Reading English papers means copying text into a translator and losing the page. Uses Qwen, DeepSeek or Gemini with an API key, or keyless Bing, Tencent Transmart or CNKI. Needs Zotero 9 and a PDF with a text layer.

zhiqing0205/zotero-ai-butler.does: Sends new papers to an AI model and saves a structured Markdown summary as a note. It can generate a one-image poster, a mind map and multi-paper reviews, and has a sidebar for questions while reading. You supply an API key.
zhiqing0205/zotero-ai-butler.pain: Papers pile up unread. This summarises them in the background or on right-click. A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jwingnut/zotero-batch-open.does: Opens or searches many selected items in your browser at once, using the item's URL, DOI or a Google Scholar or web search. Also moves files saved by the Zotero Connector onto the original item and trashes the duplicate.
jwingnut/zotero-batch-open.pain: Gathering PDFs for dozens of items means opening each by hand. Its developer built it for library access that needs a browser session, so it never downloads files itself.

jasperhu95/zotero-better-notes.does: Note management: note links, templates, two-way sync with Markdown files and export to Markdown, Word, PDF and mind maps. Adds an outline and command palette to the note editor, and note headings built from a PDF's bookmarks.
jasperhu95/zotero-better-notes.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-better-notes. Its added feature is turning a PDF's chapter outline into note headings in one click.

talos-1/zotero-citationcounts.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP, Semantic Scholar and NASA/ADS, by right-click or when items are added, and stores them in Extra. Adds a sortable Citations column. NASA/ADS needs a free token.
talos-1/zotero-citationcounts.pain: Zotero has no field for citation counts. This is a rewrite of eschnett/zotero-citationcounts for Zotero 8 and later; Google Scholar is left out because it forbids automated access.

shaowen-ye/zotero-doi-dedup-import-plugi.does: Extends Add Item by Identifier to take pasted DOI lists or text containing DOIs, reusing items already in your library instead of duplicating them. Reused items are marked, and relevance groups become tags.
shaowen-ye/zotero-doi-dedup-import-plugi.pain: Bulk DOI imports from AI tools or database exports create duplicates. A fork of huanongfish/zotero-doi-dedup-import-plugin that adds whole-library DOI and title matching, relevance tags and cautious skipping.

useroption3/zotero-extra-columns.does: Shows key: value pairs from an item's Extra field as sortable columns in the item list. You list the keys in settings, and they are matched case-insensitively.
useroption3/zotero-extra-columns.pain: People who keep status or memo lines in Extra can't otherwise sort or scan them in the list.

ifeitao/zotero-finance.does: Saves Eastmoney (东方财富网) company announcements and broker research reports into Zotero. It captures title, date, analyst, stock code, rating, target price and the PDF. A userscript helps with Robo reports.
ifeitao/zotero-finance.pain: Chinese financial reports are hard to cite from Zotero. This lets the browser connector capture them. Made for Chinese-language financial research.

sciencemaverick/zotero-getcitation.does: Fetches citation counts for selected items from Semantic Scholar, falling back to Crossref and then INSPIRE-HEP, and stores the number in Extra. Adds a Citations column and an Update Citation Counts command; a Semantic Scholar key is optional.
sciencemaverick/zotero-getcitation.pain: Its developer wanted a smaller citation-count plugin that is easier to trust and debug. It can export a support log from settings.

yuukibarns/zotero-latex-suite.does: Renders LaTeX in PDF annotation comments as you type. It also brings Obsidian Latex Suite snippets to annotations and notes: auto-fractions, tabstops, matrix shortcuts and bracket sizing. About 220 default snippets can be edited.
yuukibarns/zotero-latex-suite.pain: Zotero shows equations in notes but not in annotation comments. A fork of ievlevpn/zotero-latex-suite; its manifest adds TikZ-CD diagrams, note and PDF page export and annotation backlinks.

tulingli/zotero-literature-review.does: Generates a structured summary of one item, or a literature review across several, using an LLM, and saves it as a child note. Long texts are split into chunks and merged. Works with OpenAI-compatible APIs such as OpenAI, DeepSeek and Ollama.
tulingli/zotero-literature-review.pain: Writing a review means reading and condensing many papers. Settings cover API address, key, model, temperature and timeout. Chinese and English interface.

pipme/zotero-markdb-connect.does: Scans a folder of Markdown notes from Obsidian, logseq or Zettlr and tags the Zotero items they match, by Better BibTeX citekey or item key. A context menu entry opens the linked note.
pipme/zotero-markdb-connect.pain: Shows which papers you've already written notes on and jumps to them. A fork of daeh/zotero-markdb-connect that runs only on Zotero 6.

cloneorcopy/zotero-mcp-plus.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants such as Claude can use your library. They can search it, read PDF text, notes and annotations, create notes and tags, update metadata and export BibTeX. Includes semantic search by embeddings.
cloneorcopy/zotero-mcp-plus.pain: Lets an AI client work with your local library without a separate server process. A fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jinshijiming/zotero-pdf-translate-z6.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader, annotations, notes, item titles and abstracts, showing results in a popup and sidebar. Includes a dictionary for single words, sentence-by-sentence translation and a standalone comparison window.
jinshijiming/zotero-pdf-translate-z6.pain: Copying text into a translation site interrupts reading. Google Translate is the default, and engines such as Microsoft, Baidu, Tencent, DeepL and GPT need their own keys.

tabris-trees/zotero-plugin-dropdown.does: Adds a dropdown menu for switching collections while the collection sidebar is hidden.
tabris-trees/zotero-plugin-dropdown.pain: Zotero can't switch collections with the sidebar off, and the developer wanted to keep it off to give item lists more room.

zhidongmiao/zotero-split-viewer.does: Reads two attachments side by side in one Zotero tab, across PDF, EPUB, saved web page and Markdown files, with optional synchronised scrolling and zoom. Markdown files render in a built-in viewer.
zhidongmiao/zotero-split-viewer.pain: Zotero has no split view or Markdown reader. Inspired by zerolfl/zotero-split-view-reader, which handles only PDFs; this is a separate rewrite for more formats.

luociqvq/zotero-unified-translator.does: Instant and full-document translation for Zotero.
luociqvq/zotero-unified-translator.pain: For readers of papers in another language; little else is documented.

liuaoran/zotero-veil.does: A theme that recolours Zotero with Material colours generated from a seed colour you pick, plus frosted glass on Apple Silicon Macs. Covers the library, item pane and reader toolbar, in light, dark or system mode.
liuaoran/zotero-veil.pain: Gives Zotero a custom look. Made for macOS and Zotero 10; native glass is tested only on Apple Silicon, and disabling the plugin restores the original interface.

hannislee/zotero-word-books.does: Adds a menu entry to the PDF reader to save a selected word into a word book, ignoring case duplicates. Words can be listed and deleted in settings and exported to a text file, one per line, sorted alphabetically.
hannislee/zotero-word-books.pain: Keeps a vocabulary list from papers without leaving Zotero. Words are stored in a JSON file you can place anywhere.

zhstark/zotero9_gpt_plugin.does: Translates text selected in the PDF reader into Chinese using OpenAI, with nearby text sent as context. The result shows in a draggable panel opened by shortcut or the Tools menu. Needs an OpenAI access token; the default model is gpt-4o-mini.
zhstark/zotero9_gpt_plugin.pain: Copying sentences into a web translator interrupts reading and loses context. Translations aren't saved to notes or annotations.

tim-vdl/zotextend.does: Widens PDF pages to add blank margin space, so there is room for handwritten notes in Zotero's iPad reader. Run it from the right-click menu or automatically on import, choose the side and amount, and reset a PDF to its original size.
tim-vdl/zotextend.pain: Zotero's iPad reader gives little room to write beside the text. This edits the stored PDF so the wider file syncs to your iPad, overwriting it in place, so keep a backup.

grayxu/zotfile.does: The classic attachment manager: renames and moves PDFs, attaches files, sends PDFs to a tablet and back, and extracts annotations.
grayxu/zotfile.pain: A fork of jlegewie/zotfile; its README doesn't say what it changes. It runs on Zotero 6 and earlier only.

jan-grp/zotvim.does: Vim-style keys for Zotero's library and PDF reader: j and k to move, gg and G to jump, counts such as 5j, search with slash, and :12 to go to a PDF page. There is no insert mode, so text fields type normally.
jan-grp/zotvim.pain: For keyboard users who want to browse items and read PDFs without the mouse. Needs Zotero 8 or later; tested on Zotero 9.0.6 on Linux.

leobba/litflow.does: Links a PDF to its translated bilingual copy and colours item tags. Translation goes through the LitFlow service, with a local script as a fallback.
leobba/litflow.pain: For people who read translated papers and want the original and translation connected in Zotero.

ravenhogwarts/obsidian-zotlit.does: Connects Zotero to Obsidian. It is the Zotero side of ZotLit, a set of community plugins for both applications.
ravenhogwarts/obsidian-zotlit.pain: A fork of aidenlx/zotlit for people who take notes in Obsidian and keep references in Zotero.

aykutpurde/pdf-kucult.does: Shrinks the PDF attachments of selected items or a whole library, keeping text readable, using a PDF Küçült app that must be installed on Mac or Windows. The original goes to the Trash and the file is replaced in place. The interface is in Turkish.
aykutpurde/pdf-kucult.pain: Large scanned PDFs fill storage and sync slowly. A KB per page column flags bloated files, and automatic compression of new PDFs is off by default.

qiuyin616/pdf2zh.does: Translates a whole PDF into Chinese and attaches the rendered translated PDF to the item. It parses with MinerU, translates in chunks through an OpenAI-compatible API, and also exports Markdown or HTML. Needs a MinerU token or local MinerU, a translation API key and a separately started local render service (Node.js, Pandoc, XeLaTeX).
qiuyin616/pdf2zh.pain: Full-text translation that keeps figures and equations in a readable PDF otherwise means external tools. A fork of LuckYang1/PDF-to-md; its developer calls it experimental and says formulas need checking by hand.

zwmjohn-cool/showmarkdown.does: Adds MinerU Markdown files to Zotero items and, in the PDF reader sidebar, draws MinerU's layout boxes over the page and fills them with translated text. Translation uses a local OpenAI-compatible model server that you configure.
zwmjohn-cool/showmarkdown.pain: For people who parse papers with MinerU and want the Markdown and a page-aligned translation inside Zotero instead of in separate files.

15674852801/twinlens-zotero.does: Sends PDF attachments to MinerU for parsing, translates the result with DeepSeek, and shows source and translated blocks side by side in a Zotero panel. Selected reader text jumps to the nearest translated block. Needs a MinerU token and a DeepSeek token.
15674852801/twinlens-zotero.pain: Reading papers in another language usually means switching between the PDF and a translator. This keeps the original structure and the translation together while you read.

mnkhprre/zotero-better-notes.does: Note management inside Zotero, with note links, templates and a better note editor. It adds a main-note button, an outline, a command palette, two-way Markdown sync (such as Obsidian) and export to Markdown, Word, PDF and mind maps. Its AI chat pane needs Zotero-GPT.
mnkhprre/zotero-better-notes.pain: Zotero's notes are plain and isolated, so linking, templating and syncing them with other tools is hard. A fork of windingwind/zotero-better-notes that adds Turkish placeholder cleaning to the note editor.

lllateron/zotero-bilingual-outline.does: Adds Chinese translations beside the existing table of contents of a PDF in the reader, keeping the English, hierarchy and click-to-jump. Translates with a DeepSeek API key, sends only the title and outline, and syncs translations between computers through Zotero notes.
lllateron/zotero-bilingual-outline.pain: Reading English papers with a Chinese outline helps navigation, but translating headings by hand is slow. It is built for Windows with Zotero 10, and for personal libraries.

shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-structure-m.does: Opens a manager window that lists every collection as a tree, with search by name or path, jump to a collection, favourites and recents. It shows item counts, finds empty folders, exports the structure as Markdown or CSV, and moves or merges collections with a preview and undo for moves.
shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-structure-m.pain: Large libraries with deep folder trees are slow to navigate and reorganise in the left pane. This gives one place to find, count, move and merge collections without touching the items themselves.

lostwildland/zotero-extra-columns.does: Turns fields written in an item's Extra box (such as arXiv or titleTranslation) into native item-list columns and a key-value section in the item pane. DOI, URL and arXiv values become clickable, and a menu cleans a chosen Extra field from selected or all items.
lostwildland/zotero-extra-columns.pain: Extra is a single text box, so structured values stored there can't be sorted or scanned in the list. This surfaces them as columns and lets you strip a field in bulk.

notoootori/zotero-feed-filter.does: Filters RSS feed items with a regular expression you set per feed from the feed's right-click menu. It runs in the background when feeds update and removes items that don't match.
notoootori/zotero-feed-filter.pain: Feeds such as arXiv mix new papers with cross-lists and updates. A pattern like 'Announce Type: new' keeps only the new ones.

jsrdcht/zotero-github-stars.does: Finds the GitHub star count of each selected paper's repository and writes it to Extra, with a read-only GitHub Stars column in the item list. A right-click command updates many items at once, with a progress window you can cancel.
jsrdcht/zotero-github-stars.pain: Papers with code are easier to judge when you can see how much attention the repository has. Without this you would look each one up on GitHub by hand.

asuka123456789/zotero-mcp-plus.does: Extends the Zotero MCP server with tools to recognise standalone PDFs, queue persistent tasks, merge duplicates and check library health. Writes are off by default and use a preview, then a confirmed run. Semantic indexing is off by default.
asuka123456789/zotero-mcp-plus.pain: AI clients connected to Zotero need safe, reviewable ways to repair a library. It is based on cookjohn/zotero-mcp and keeps writes behind explicit confirmation.

zhanghangjia/zotero-note-preview-column.does: Adds a Note Preview column to the item list that shows the plain text of a parent item's child notes, a standalone note, or a standalone PDF's own note. You choose whether to combine all notes, the first or the latest, plus length and separator.
zhanghangjia/zotero-note-preview-column.pain: Zotero shows only a note count, so reading a note means expanding the item. This lets you scan notes straight from the list, including for PDFs that have no metadata yet. For Zotero 10.

iuliaturc/zotero-notebooklm.does: Syncs Zotero collections with Google NotebookLM: sends PDFs, notes and metadata as notebooks, and imports source guides, sources and notes back. Free or Pro accounts use a Chrome extension bridge; Enterprise uses the official API with a Google Cloud project.
iuliaturc/zotero-notebooklm.pain: Getting a reading list into NotebookLM otherwise means uploading files one by one. This sends whole collections, and can pull NotebookLM's summaries back into Zotero.

tcpsoftware/zotero-open-pdf.does: Adds a right-click option to open a PDF with the opposite of your default (system viewer or Zotero's reader) and lets you add your own viewers. Each is defined by a config key holding a command line with @pdf for the file, for PDFs, snapshots or EPUBs.
tcpsoftware/zotero-open-pdf.pain: Zotero lets you pick only one default viewer. This gives quick access to Preview, Skim, Edge or another tool as needed. A fork of retorquere/zotero-open-pdf.

hanbinhsh/zotero-pdf2zh-bilingual.does: Translates PDF attachments with a local PDFMathTranslate install and imports a translated or bilingual PDF. It uses Ollama or another OpenAI-compatible model you run. Bilingual output can be alternating pages or side by side. Batches run in Zotero's task queue.
hanbinhsh/zotero-pdf2zh-bilingual.pain: Translating papers locally keeps the text on your machine and preserves formulas. You must install PDFMathTranslate yourself; for Zotero 9.

kouichi-c-nakamura/zotero-relate-selecte.does: Relates every selected item to every other one with one right-click command, with a matching command to remove relations within the selection. The menu shows when two or more regular items are selected.
kouichi-c-nakamura/zotero-relate-selecte.pain: Linking five papers in Zotero's Related tab means ten separate steps. Its developer notes Zotero 8 now has a Relate Items command, with unrelate expected later.

peihenglu/zotero-synced-collections.does: Creates synchronised copies of a collection, in the same library or another. Adding, removing or restoring an item in one copy updates the others, and subcollection changes can be mirrored too. Synced folders get a teal icon, and the link between copies travels through Zotero sync in a note.
peihenglu/zotero-synced-collections.pain: Zotero collections can't stay in step with each other, so keeping the same papers in two places means doing every change twice. For Zotero 8 to 10.

hyfaust/zotero-tab-enhance.does: A vertical tab sidebar with colour-coded groups, search and multi-select, plus a button that gathers all open tabs into a timestamped group and closes them. Tab context menus gain Show in File Manager, Reload Tab and Copy Reference. Features are off until enabled in settings.
hyfaust/zotero-tab-enhance.pain: Many open papers make the horizontal tab bar hard to manage. For Zotero 8 and later; a fork of Rphone/zotero-tab-enhance.

lllateron/zotero-tag-editor.does: Opens an editor with Ctrl+T to add, remove or rename tags across one or many selected items at once. Changes stay as a draft until you save, and you can undo the last save in that session. Other tags are kept.
lllateron/zotero-tag-editor.pain: Zotero's tag selector is clumsy for batch changes on several items. This gives one dialog for bulk tag edits. Built for Windows and Zotero 10.

trifullkim/zotero-to-capacities-pdf.does: Sends PDF annotations (highlights, underlines, notes) from Zotero items to Capacities as pages with author, date, DOI and tags. Highlight colours become emojis and page numbers link back to the annotation in Zotero. Optional auto-sync. Needs a Capacities API token and Space ID.
trifullkim/zotero-to-capacities-pdf.pain: People who keep notes in Capacities otherwise copy highlights over by hand. Capacities can't take PDF uploads, so links use the item's DOI or URL. A fork of the Zotero plugin template.

rbialoz/zotrekey.does: Renames attachment files to URL-safe names, converting umlauts and removing special characters, and appends the Zotero storage folder key to keep names unique. Run from the item menu or Tools menu on one item or a whole collection.
rbialoz/zotrekey.pain: Filenames with spaces, umlauts or punctuation break web links, and similar titles collide. This makes them predictable. Its developer calls it intentionally minimal and says the first version was written with ChatGPT.

einheriar/zotseek-u.does: Semantic search over your Zotero library, indexing metadata, notes and PDF text with local embeddings. It adds hybrid search and a built-in MCP server, and handles Chinese, Japanese, Korean and other languages, and can use a cloud embedding API key if you bring one.
einheriar/zotseek-u.pain: Finding a paper you remember only by its idea is hard with keyword search. A fork of introfini/ZotSeek that replaces it with the same add-on ID, with better token counting for non-English text.

524892804/batch-obsidian-export.does: Sends selected Zotero items to Obsidian in one batch through ZotLit, in skip or overwrite mode. It writes note status back to Extra and adds an Obsidian Note column. Needs an enhanced ZotLit build in your Obsidian vault.
524892804/batch-obsidian-export.pain: Exporting literature notes to Obsidian one item at a time is slow. This sends a whole selection at once and shows which items already have notes.

jinkeguo/paperloop.does: A reading notebook that pairs a browser extension, built on Zotero Connector, with a Zotero plugin. Collect text and webpage images while reading, write alongside the paper, and save references and notes to a Zotero child note.
jinkeguo/paperloop.pain: Reading online and writing notes means juggling a browser, a note app and Zotero. This keeps the paper, your excerpts and your draft in one side panel. It is an independent modified Zotero Connector.

jianguo99/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads papers with an AI model and saves a Markdown summary as a note on each item. It can scan new PDFs automatically, queue old ones, make mind maps and a poster-style one-image summary, write multi-paper reviews, and chat in a sidebar. Needs your own API key for OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic or a compatible service.
jianguo99/zotero-ai-butler.pain: Too many papers to read and little retention. A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler; its README doesn't say what it changes.

yuukibarns/zotero-annotation-backlinks.does: Finds saved Zotero notes that reference a selected annotation, from a Find Referencing Notes command in the PDF reader. Results open in a popup, and annotations without identifiers can show as possible matches. It is read-only and sends nothing to any service.
yuukibarns/zotero-annotation-backlinks.pain: After quoting a highlight in several notes you can't tell where. This traces it back. Its developer calls it a beta for Zotero 10.

lin-qingming/zotero-attachment-type-icon.does: Gives Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Markdown and XMind attachments their own icons in the item list and attachment rows, with link variants for linked files. It recognises files by content type or extension and changes icons only, not how files open.
lin-qingming/zotero-attachment-type-icon.pain: Zotero shows every non-PDF file as a blank page, so Word and Excel files look identical. This tells them apart at a glance.

erbiaoger/zotero-better-authors.does: Adds item-list columns for the first author, the second author (often the corresponding author) and a customisable authors list. You choose how many authors show, separators, a symbol for the second author, and name order.
erbiaoger/zotero-better-authors.pain: Zotero's creator column is limited. A fork of github-young/zotero-better-authors; its README doesn't say what it changes.

alh63/zotero-bibfix.does: Improves bibliographic metadata using K10plus, the German National Library (DNB) and Crossref. Optional Claude AI features, such as short-title generation, need an Anthropic API key. For Zotero 8.
alh63/zotero-bibfix.pain: For people whose items carry incomplete or inconsistent catalogue data, such as German-language libraries. Little more is documented about how it works.

sahanarajan18/zotero-focus-reader.does: A focus-reading mode for the PDF reader that highlights the current word, line or sentence and moves forward automatically at a set speed. Optional spotlight dimming, click to jump, auto-scroll and keyboard shortcuts.
sahanarajan18/zotero-focus-reader.pain: Staying with long academic text is hard. A moving highlight paces your reading and keeps you from losing your place.

situkangsayur/zotero-generalgit-plugin.does: Backs up your whole Zotero library to a Git repository on any host (GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Bitbucket, your own server) using the git on your computer. Items become JSON and Markdown notes, files can go through Git LFS, and Import from Git restores a library. Needs git installed.
situkangsayur/zotero-generalgit-plugin.pain: Zotero sync isn't a versioned backup you control. Its developer says it is an early release and not a replacement for Zotero sync.

sciencemaverick/zotero-getjournalabbr.does: Fills empty Journal Abbr fields without overwriting existing ones. It uses an abbreviation already used consistently in your library, a bundled journal table, or Crossref's short title for items with a DOI, and shows a preview before writing.
sciencemaverick/zotero-getjournalabbr.pain: Citation styles that need abbreviated journal names mean looking each up by hand.

shaowen-ye/zotero-item-column-layout-plu.does: Adjusts the item list columns with title-first presets: widen the title, maximise it, compact, or balanced. Presets can hide rarely used columns, re-apply when you change folders or resize, and you can save, restore or reset layouts. Only display preferences change.
shaowen-ye/zotero-item-column-layout-plu.pain: In large libraries the title column is often too narrow while side columns waste space. For Zotero 7 to 9.

puzan/zotero-links.does: Copies zotero:// links for collections from a right-click menu. It also has an automatic collection-assignment feature that calls Anthropic's Claude and needs your own API key.
puzan/zotero-links.pain: For people who want to link to a collection from notes or other apps. Little more is documented about how it works.

voldythecorn/zotero_multifetcher.does: Fills in missing DOIs through Crossref and downloads PDFs from several sources in a set order: OpenAlex, Sci-Hub, Anna's Archive, LibGen or your own JavaScript. Books are searched by title and author. Optional SOCKS5 proxy. Some sources distribute copyrighted works without permission.
voldythecorn/zotero_multifetcher.pain: Finding a free PDF means trying sources by hand. A fork of syt2/zotero-scipdf that adds DOI lookup, OpenAlex, Anna's Archive, LibGen and a proxy; using Sci-Hub and similar sources is illegal in many places.

programmerayaka/zotero_paper_summary.does: Summarises a paper from its PDF with DeepSeek or Google Gemini and saves the Chinese summary as a child note. Choose truncated, full-text or chunked mode. Needs your own API key; the key is stored locally.
programmerayaka/zotero_paper_summary.pain: Getting the gist of a paper otherwise means copying text into a chatbot. This does it from the right-click menu. For Zotero 7.

pl0ver/zotero-pdf-exporter.does: Exports selected PDFs, or whole collections with subfolders, as independent copies or as macOS symbolic links. Files are named Author - Year - Title.pdf by default, with prompts when a name already exists.
pl0ver/zotero-pdf-exporter.pain: Sharing PDFs out of Zotero's key-named storage folders is awkward. This produces a tidy folder tree. Symlinks work on macOS only; for Zotero 10.

keepgogogo/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text in the PDF, EPUB or web reader, plus titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services. It adds Zhipu (GLM) models and has been tested only on Zotero 7.0.32.
keepgogogo/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that keeps Zotero 7 working and adds Zhipu GLM models, including free ones, as a translation service.

zebin426-wq/zotero-semantic-scholar-assi.does: Recommends and imports papers using Semantic Scholar: from a collection, related papers for an item, keyword search, and search of a local reading database. Imports go to a Recommended by Semantic Scholar subcollection. A key is optional; without one it shows demo data only.
zebin426-wq/zotero-semantic-scholar-assi.pain: Finding new papers related to your reading means leaving Zotero to search. For Zotero 8 and 9.

kdmsnr/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up full DOIs through Crossref and shortDOIs, checks stored DOIs and flags invalid ones, and cleans prefixes like doi: or a publisher URL from the field. Runs on selected items.
kdmsnr/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Wrong or messy DOIs break lookups and links. A fork of bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi that makes it work on Zotero 9; tested on 9.0.1.

plastik-punk/zotero-show-tags.does: Adds a Tags column to the item list so you can see each item's tags without opening it. Turn it on from the column header menu.
plastik-punk/zotero-show-tags.pain: Zotero shows tags only in the item pane or tag selector, so you can't scan them across items.

alanhuang99/zotero-watch-folder.does: Watches a folder and imports new PDFs into Zotero with metadata lookup and a clean filename, skipping duplicates by content hash. Can mirror subfolders as collections, apply rules and store files in Zotero or link them. Deletion is opt-in and goes to a recoverable trash.
alanhuang99/zotero-watch-folder.pain: Importing PDFs by dragging is repetitive. A fork of josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder that repackages it to declare Zotero 10 compatibility; its runtime code is unchanged.

couldfulrial/zoterocopycitationkey.does: Makes Cmd/Ctrl+C in the item list copy the selected items' citation keys, comma-separated for several, with a brief popup. It reads the citationKey field, then Extra, then the item key. In the PDF reader, use a right-click Copy Citation Key command.
couldfulrial/zoterocopycitationkey.pain: Getting a citation key into a document otherwise means opening each item. This makes copying a key a normal shortcut.

jr-xing/2026-10-24-zotero-rich-comment-p.does: Adds colour swatches and action buttons to the floating annotation popup. You can change colour, convert highlight and underline, edit the page number, delete, add to note, or use commands from other plugins. Changes use Zotero's native commands, with undo.
jr-xing/2026-10-24-zotero-rich-comment-p.pain: Editing an annotation otherwise means opening the More menu. Its developer says it targets Zotero 10.0 and was tested on Windows only.

yangchenguang94/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research assistant in the reader sidebar that chats with your papers. It supports OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and others, with agent mode, skills, Markdown file notes and MinerU PDF parsing. This fork improves chat across collections. Needs an API key.
yangchenguang94/llm-for-zotero.pain: Chatting with papers otherwise means uploading PDFs to a website. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that lets the model read across collections from the side panel.

zxc-heu/mineru-zotero-reader.does: A Zotero bridge for Codex that parses PDFs with MinerU into Markdown and links the files to items as attachments. Menu actions make quick-read, deep-read or writing-level notes. Needs Codex CLI, the skill and a MinerU token.
zxc-heu/mineru-zotero-reader.pain: Reading papers with an AI agent works better from clean Markdown. This keeps Zotero as the library and stores the Markdown beside your PDFs.

fanqing203/openclaw-for-zotero.does: A sidebar chat for the selected reference, which knows its title, authors and abstract and keeps a conversation per paper. It talks to an OpenClaw Gateway (local or remote) with models such as GLM-5 or DeepSeek, and needs the Gateway's API key.
fanqing203/openclaw-for-zotero.pain: Asking questions about a paper without leaving Zotero. For people already running OpenClaw.

l41036406-del/retainpdf-zotero.does: Translates PDF attachments through a local RetainPDF engine and writes a translated or bilingual PDF back to the item, from the right-click menu. It downloads a Windows engine of about 165 MB. Needs a Paddle OCR token and an OpenAI-compatible translation API key.
l41036406-del/retainpdf-zotero.pain: Translating a whole paper while keeping the layout needs several tools. This runs OCR, translation and rendering for you. For Windows with Zotero 9.

frostime/sy-f-misc.does: Provides local HTTP bridge endpoints so the SiYuan notes app can read your current Zotero selection and library. SiYuan's f-misc plugin uses them to cite papers and import notes.
frostime/sy-f-misc.pain: People who write in SiYuan can cite Zotero papers there. It is the Zotero side of a personal plugin, and its developer gives no stability guarantees.

kasc0206/tst.does: Scans your libraries for items whose linked attachment files are missing on disk and puts them in a Missing Attachments collection. A second Tools command removes items from it once their files return.
kasc0206/tst.pain: Zotero shows an attachment even when the file has gone, so broken ones are hard to find. This lists them. Items with only URL links are not counted.

iduoduo1002/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads papers with an AI model and saves a Markdown summary as a note. Also does deeper reading, mind maps, one-image summaries, multi-paper reviews and a chat sidebar. Needs an API key, or a local Codex CLI login.
iduoduo1002/zotero-ai-butler.pain: Too many papers to read and little retention. A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler; its README doesn't say what it changes. Extracted text goes to the model you pick.

callioper/zotero-aireader.does: An AI assistant in the PDF reader sidebar with six skills: summaries, concept explanations, argument analysis, people tracking, quotes and a reading guide. AI quotations become PDF highlights you can click to jump to the source. It builds a local search index and works with OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama or LM Studio, so you need an API key or a local model. Written for Zotero 9 and Chinese-language use, with English replies available.
callioper/zotero-aireader.pain: Reading a dense paper means switching to a chatbot and pasting text. This keeps the conversation beside the PDF and ties each answer back to highlighted passages.

udiboy1209/zotero-annot-copy.does: Adds right-click options to copy an annotation as an Obsidian callout block with a link back to its page. Another option copies just the zotero:// link.
udiboy1209/zotero-annot-copy.pain: Moving highlights into Obsidian by hand loses the colour and the way back to the page. The callout type follows the annotation type and colour, and a bundled CSS snippet styles them in your vault.

bkbrooklyn/zotero-citation-auto-collecti.does: Keeps a Zotero collection in step with the references cited in a Microsoft Word document. Items are added when you insert or edit a citation and removed after you delete one and click Refresh.
bkbrooklyn/zotero-citation-auto-collecti.pain: Without it you collect the sources of a manuscript by hand. Removing an item from the collection never deletes it from your library. Only Word is supported, not LibreOffice or Google Docs.

sparklemuff1n/zotero-collection-colors.does: Lets you assign colours to collection folders in Zotero's left pane.
sparklemuff1n/zotero-collection-colors.pain: A long collection tree looks uniform. Colour coding makes the folders you use most easier to spot.

dsuess/zotero-collection-selector.does: Adds two endpoints to Zotero's local connector server: one lists all collections as JSON and one switches the selected collection by id.
dsuess/zotero-collection-selector.pain: Zotero offers no way for outside tools to change the active collection, so saving web pages from a script or Alfred workflow meant switching windows by hand. Legacy plugin for Zotero 6 and Firefox.

lllateron/zotero-comment-expand.does: Adds a reader sidebar button that shows every annotation comment or translation in full. A second click restores Zotero's shortened display.
lllateron/zotero-comment-expand.pain: Long annotation comments are truncated in the sidebar until you select them. This lets you read them all at once without changing the annotation text. Written for Zotero 10, with Chinese and English prompts.

virchow-zhang/zotero-doi-metadata-fill.does: Fills missing metadata for items that have a DOI: authors, journal, year, volume, pages, ISSN, publisher and abstract. Run it from the right-click menu for selected items or from the Tools menu for the whole library.
virchow-zhang/zotero-doi-metadata-fill.pain: Imports through the browser connector often arrive incomplete. This fills only empty fields and never overwrites yours, and it upgrades web page or preprint items to journal articles when the DOI says so. No API key is needed.

lassiterdc/zotero-email-intake.does: Turns an email dropped onto a collection into a proper item. Drag an .eml file or an Outlook .msg file in and it creates the parent item with sender, subject and date.
lassiterdc/zotero-email-intake.pain: Dropped emails otherwise land as bare attachments with no metadata. It also catches duplicates and works alongside ZotMoov by offering to add eml and msg to its allowed file types.

yunoinsky/zotero-folder-import.does: Imports a whole folder of files into Zotero, recreating the folder structure as a collection hierarchy. Adds a PDF Watch mode that monitors a folder and imports new PDFs automatically.
yunoinsky/zotero-folder-import.pain: A fork of retorquere/zotero-folder-import. It makes the collection optional, selects all file types by default, stores copies instead of links, and recognises metadata for imported PDFs.

kiiilin/zotero-fulltext-translate.does: Translates a whole paper paragraph by paragraph and saves it as a Zotero note. Translations show on the PDF as movable, resizable cards linked to the source text, toggled with Alt+T.
kiiilin/zotero-fulltext-translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate, built for full-paper translation that survives restarts and syncs to another computer. It replaces the original plugin and sends paper text to the translation service you configure.

wilhenry777/zotero-gpt-literature-summar.does: Opens ChatGPT in Chrome from the Zotero reader, attaches the current PDF to the conversation and sends a structured summary prompt written in Chinese.
wilhenry777/zotero-gpt-literature-summar.pain: Saves uploading each paper to ChatGPT by hand. It needs a ChatGPT account signed in to Chrome and a companion Chrome extension, but no OpenAI API key. Its developer calls it experimental and built for a personal workflow.

imczxx/zotero-hjfy.does: Opens the HJFY translation of an arXiv paper from a Zotero item.
imczxx/zotero-hjfy.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template; its README is still the template's and documents no features beyond what its manifest says.

liuyujie0136/zotero-journalabbr.does: Replaces journal titles with standard abbreviations from a right-click menu entry. The bundled list is built from JabRef and the Woodward Library list.
liuyujie0136/zotero-journalabbr.pain: Reference lists often require abbreviated journal names, and typing them is slow. This fork of zoushucai/zotero-journalabbr is for Zotero 6 only and, its developer says, for personal use.

desperadoccy/zotero-metadata-scraper.does: Searches DBLP and Semantic Scholar by title and updates an item's metadata from the match you pick. An optional Semantic Scholar API key raises rate limits.
desperadoccy/zotero-metadata-scraper.pain: Papers saved from preprint servers keep incomplete or outdated publication details. A fork of Creling/Zotero-Metadata-Scraper, with English and Chinese interfaces.

futuresxy/zotero-mineru-translator.does: Translates a whole PDF paper into a Zotero note. It sends the PDF to MinerU for parsing, translates the text in chunks with an OpenAI-compatible model such as DeepSeek, and writes the result to a child note as it goes.
futuresxy/zotero-mineru-translator.pain: Needs a MinerU token and an LLM API key. It skips images, tables, formula blocks and references to cut translation cost, which suits readers who want a full Chinese translation inside Zotero.

wangergouaaaa/zotero-note-batch-exporter.does: Exports the notes in the selected collection, optionally with subcollections, or the notes of selected items to Markdown files. Invalid and duplicate filenames are handled automatically.
wangergouaaaa/zotero-note-batch-exporter.pain: Zotero has no bulk note export. This lets you take your reading notes into other Markdown tools in one step. Written for Zotero 8.

ubombar/zotero-obsidian-plugin.does: Adds a local endpoint to Zotero that returns the currently selected items.
ubombar/zotero-obsidian-plugin.pain: Lets tools such as Obsidian read your selection from the running Zotero without using the Zotero web API.

molaison/zotero-onekey-annotations.does: Adds single-key annotation shortcuts to the PDF reader. Q, W, E, R, T, Y, G and F make highlights in eight colours, Z, X, C and V place notes, M draws an area, D deletes.
molaison/zotero-onekey-annotations.pain: Zotero's colour picker takes extra clicks for every highlight. The keys work with Chinese input methods, and Alt+H and Alt+S hide and show all annotations. Its developer notes it was not tested on a live Zotero 10.

xin-yi6/zotero-paper-updater.does: Detects newer arXiv versions and journal-published versions of papers in your library and attaches the updated PDF next to the original. Scan from a toolbar button, the right-click menu or the Tools menu.
xin-yi6/zotero-paper-updater.pain: Preprints change after you save them. This notices new versions and publication, updates the metadata when a published version is found, and never deletes anything. A scheduled scan runs every 24 hours by default.

fukangz/zotero-pdf-to-markdown.does: Converts a Zotero item's PDF into a Markdown attachment stored under the same item. It uses a parsing service of your choice: Zhiyi PDF, MinerU or GLM-OCR, each needing its own key or token.
fukangz/zotero-pdf-to-markdown.pain: PDFs are hard for language models, search tools and note apps to read. Markdown keeps headings, tables and formulas. Images can be uploaded through PicGo or saved as local files. Written for Zotero 9.

shininvvs/zotero-plugin.does: Copies the bibliography entry, in-text citation or link of selected items to the clipboard for pasting into Hangul (HWP), with italics and hyperlinks kept. Also corrects Korean particles such as 와/과 in the output.
shininvvs/zotero-plugin.pain: Zotero supports only Word and LibreOffice, so Hangul users retyped references by hand. It also warns about incomplete fields and ships a Korean author-year citation style.

nbtkmy/zotero-price-lookup.does: Looks up the retail price of selected books by ISBN through the OpenBD service and writes it to the Price line of the Extra field. No API key is needed.
nbtkmy/zotero-price-lookup.pain: Useful for tracking what books cost. OpenBD covers Japanese books only, so other titles are reported as not found. Written for Zotero 8.

aprilgrimoire/zotero-reader-stack.does: Gives each reader attachment a persistent tree of reading positions. Push Position, Pop Position and Forward Branch commands under the Go menu, and a keyboard-navigable tree selector, let you branch and return.
aprilgrimoire/zotero-reader-stack.pain: Zotero's navigation history is linear, which is awkward when you jump around a paper or book. Shortcuts are configurable and none are set by default. Needs Zotero 9.0.4 or newer.

scaddleloong/zotero_reading_record-per-y.does: Tracks how long each item is open and shows a yearly reading heatmap, daily statistics, a trend chart and a per-day log. Data is stored in a synced Zotero note.
scaddleloong/zotero_reading_record-per-y.pain: Shows how much you actually read. An optional AI analysis gives a nine-field summary of an article and needs your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, key and model. The interface comes in ten languages.

zouyonghao/zotero-semantic-coloring.does: Adds semantic colouring of PDF annotations in Zotero.
zouyonghao/zotero-semantic-coloring.pain: Its developer gives no further detail, so little more can be said. Probably for readers who want annotation colours to carry meaning.

connorb/zotero-shortdoi.does: Looks up full DOIs through Crossref and shortDOIs for selected items, checks that stored DOIs are valid and marks the invalid ones. It also strips prefixes such as doi: and publisher URLs from the DOI field.
connorb/zotero-shortdoi.pain: Citations with missing or malformed DOIs are hard to follow up. A fork of bwiernik/zotero-shortdoi, updated for Zotero 8 and 9.

pgauding/zotero-smart-import.does: Imports a .bib file without creating duplicates. Each entry is matched against your library by DOI or fuzzy title, author and year, then everything goes into a new collection with new items tagged smart-import:new.
pgauding/zotero-smart-import.pain: Zotero's own BibTeX import adds every entry again, so references from a collaborator or a LaTeX project pile up as duplicates. The tag shows which items still need PDFs. Its developer calls it alpha.

asuka123456789/zotero-topic-explorer.does: A workbench for research topic ideas. From selected items and your own constraints, four AI roles (explorer, literature reviewer, feasibility assessor, lead) discuss in six fixed requests and produce editable topic cards that you can export to Markdown.
asuka123456789/zotero-topic-explorer.pain: Needs an API key for an OpenAI-compatible model of your choice. Nothing is sent until you confirm a preview of what will go out, and it never writes to your Zotero library. Built for Zotero 9.0.6.

lvansnippenburg/zotero-utils.does: Translates annotations and summarises PDFs with the Gemini API. Also exports annotations or notes to Markdown, copies an annotation with its reference, and tags new items /unread.
lvansnippenburg/zotero-utils.pain: Bundles several annotation and tagging helpers in one plugin. The AI features need a Gemini API key, and the annotation colour labels are in Dutch.

daniel-addae/zotero-vertical-tab-groups.does: Turns Zotero's tab bar into a vertical sidebar with Edge-style tab groups. Groups are named, colour-coded and collapsible, and the collections pane stays pinned beside them while you read.
daniel-addae/zotero-vertical-tab-groups.pain: With many PDFs open, horizontal tabs become unreadable and the collection tree disappears in the reader. Groups and assignments persist across restarts. Needs Zotero 8 or 9.

matfu-pixel/zotero-vim-note.does: Adds Vim-style modal editing to the Zotero note editor, with normal, insert and visual modes, motions, operators such as dd, cw and yy, counts, and undo.
matfu-pixel/zotero-vim-note.pain: For people who edit in Vim and want the same keys in notes. Keys match physical positions, so they work on non-Latin layouts. It works only on Zotero 10 and omits text objects, search and macros.

lfan0103/zotero-wordbook.does: Exports vocabulary from PDF highlights of one colour, with definitions and original sentences. Output is a Bubeidanci-format text file or a CSV with fields you pick, suitable for Anki.
lfan0103/zotero-wordbook.pain: Turns words you highlight while reading into a word list. It relies on the Translate for Zotero plugin to supply definitions. Aimed at Chinese-speaking English learners.

38260/zotero-wysiwyg-pdf-export.does: Exports the PDF open in the reader with its annotations as they look on screen. One command makes an image-based PDF at 300 DPI, the other keeps selectable text and editable annotations.
38260/zotero-wysiwyg-pdf-export.pain: Zotero's own export can turn Chinese fixed-text annotations into boxes and change fonts and line breaks. This keeps the reader's appearance. Nothing is uploaded and the original is untouched.

yongwoo-lee-ccl/zoterocrop.does: Crops the margins that are blank on every page of a PDF and adds the result as a new attachment. You set the margin to keep, and it can copy annotations and trash the original.
yongwoo-lee-ccl/zoterocrop.pain: Wide margins waste space on phones and tablets. Works on macOS and needs Python 3.10 or later with PyMuPDF and Pillow installed locally. Its developer says it is beta and was written entirely with OpenAI Codex.

hdchen27/zoteromindmap.does: Turns a paper's PDF into an interactive mind map in its own window. Nodes cover innovations, methods and conclusions, each with its source passage. Needs a MinerU API key and an LLM API key.
hdchen27/zoteromindmap.pain: Gives a quick structural overview of a paper before you read it. Output is in Simplified Chinese. Parse results and maps are cached locally. Built for Zotero 9.

izjxnxn/zoteromineru.does: Bridges Zotero to a companion Windows program that turns paper PDFs into Markdown through MinerU. Markdown, AI summary cards and bilingual PDFs come back as child attachments of the item.
izjxnxn/zoteromineru.pain: Prepares your library so AI agents can find and read relevant papers without parsing every PDF again. Needs your own MinerU token and an LLM service. Also offers category reviews and tracking of new papers.

nerdneilsfield/zotpass.does: Sends a saved browser Cookie with Zotero 10's file downloads for sites you configure, so Find Available File can fetch PDFs behind a publisher login. Other URLs use Zotero's normal downloader.
nerdneilsfield/zotpass.pain: Some PDFs open in your browser but fail in Zotero because of authentication. It does not find papers or bypass access rights, and Cookies are stored as plain text in Zotero preferences.

zotero-flow/zotseek.does: Semantic search that finds papers by meaning using embedding models running locally. A built-in MCP server lets AI agents such as Claude Code search and cite your library.
zotero-flow/zotseek.pain: A fork of introfini/ZotSeek that adds an EmbeddingGemma 2 multilingual model and optional Mac GPU indexing. Keyword search misses papers that use different words; nothing leaves your machine.

georghildebrand/zutilo.does: Adds extra editing functions through menu items and keyboard shortcuts. Copy, paste and remove sets of tags, relate several items, copy items in several formats, and focus or hide parts of the interface.
georghildebrand/zutilo.pain: A fork of wshanks/Zutilo. Its developers say some features, mainly keyboard shortcuts, stopped working as of Zotero 7, and the original maintainer has little time for it.

pigggggggggg/better-tags-for-zotero.does: Replaces the tag selector in the bottom-left corner with a panel of nested tag groups and coloured chips with item counts. Filter by tags with All or ANY logic while keeping Zotero's own item list and search.
pigggggggggg/better-tags-for-zotero.pain: Zotero's tag pane is flat and cramped, so tags can't replace folders. This adds groups, bulk tagging with undo, saved filter combinations and automatic tagging from item titles. Built for Zotero 10 with a Chinese interface.

juanzhio/chartero.does: Records reading pages, time and progress, and shows them as a reading progress column, reader sidebar charts and library overview pages. Supports Zotero 9 to 10.1.
juanzhio/chartero.pain: A fork of volatile-static/Chartero. Zotero does not track how much of each paper you have read, and this charts it.

zycyjun/keepzotero-windows.does: Keeps Zotero 10 running in the Windows system tray when you close the main window. Double-click the tray icon to reopen it and right-click to quit. Optionally starts Zotero hidden at login.
zycyjun/keepzotero-windows.pain: Closing Zotero normally quits it, so reopening is slow. Inspired by yhmtsai/KeepZotero, this version works on Windows x64 only and loads a native DLL inside Zotero.

linn60/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research agent that works from your Zotero library.
linn60/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that, its developer says, lets custom prompts override the system prompt.

aykutpurde/metadata-duzelt.does: Fixes common metadata errors, especially in Turkish records: garbled characters, all-caps titles, academic titles in author names and wrong language fields. Every change is previewed and can be undone.
aykutpurde/metadata-duzelt.pain: Items imported from PDFs or DOIs often arrive broken for Turkish text. Fixing happens locally. Only the optional verify button contacts Crossref and the item's DergiPark page.

ed359/mineru-for-zotero.does: Sends PDFs to the MinerU API for parsing and shows its layout boxes in the PDF reader. Click a box to copy a paragraph, table, formula or caption, or copy several in reading order. Needs a MinerU API key.
ed359/mineru-for-zotero.pain: A fork of Asianfleet/mineru-for-zotero. Copying clean text, tables and formulas out of a PDF is awkward, and parsed Markdown can also be read by local tools through a local query API.

andrewmkahn/nihongo-zotero.does: Adds an item pane section for storing romanised titles, names, publishers and English translations of Japanese sources, saved in the Extra field. Bundled Chicago styles cite the romanised values.
andrewmkahn/nihongo-zotero.pain: Standard fields and citation styles handle Japanese sources poorly. An optional button sends item metadata to Anthropic's Claude to draft romanisation and needs an API key. It also migrates data from Jurism.

windfollowingheart/openclaw-zotero-chann.does: A chat panel in Zotero for talking to an AI assistant about your PDFs through OpenClaw. You can reference the open PDF, attach files and read Markdown-formatted replies.
windfollowingheart/openclaw-zotero-chann.pain: For people who use OpenClaw and want its assistant inside Zotero. It requires installing a companion OpenClaw plugin from the repository.

y1-fan/re-kubikatia.does: Imports Kubikat catalogue records into a new collection from a pasted search-results URL, record link or document id, mapping the MARC data directly. It makes one request every 10 seconds and imports at most 50 items.
y1-fan/re-kubikatia.pain: Exporting Kubikat records through RIS loses much of their detail. This keeps creator roles, item types and extra fields. Its developer says it is for personal, non-commercial use and not an official tool.

tacmon/tacmon-trans.does: Looks up an English word double-clicked in the PDF reader with the local wd dictionary command. Saves it with definition, page and full sentence to an Obsidian vocabulary note.
tacmon/tacmon-trans.pain: Builds a word list with context as you read papers, in a format the Obsidian Spaced Repetition plugin can review. Its developer says it is built first for one Linux machine and needs wd installed.

theciteshop/the-cite-shop-client-sync.does: Installs and updates the custom citation styles you bought from The Cite Shop. Enter your purchase email and licence key, then install each style from the settings pane.
theciteshop/the-cite-shop-client-sync.pain: Needs a paid subscription and a signed-in Zotero account. Styles are removed if the subscription ends or no licence check succeeds for three days. Your own styles are left alone.

chenglinbo/zotero-ai-sider.does: Adds a permanent AI sidebar to Zotero with Gemini and ChatGPT loaded side by side. Select text in the PDF reader to insert it into the chat with your own prompts, ask for a term to be explained, or send the current PDF. You log in to both services yourself.
chenglinbo/zotero-ai-sider.pain: Asking an AI about a paper usually means copying text between Zotero and a browser tab. This keeps both chats beside the PDF, with shortcuts to switch between them.

chancezhangcr/zotero-bilingual-reader.does: Translates a whole English paper into Chinese beside the original in the PDF reader. Exports a Chinese-only PDF and a bilingual PDF, using four free engines (Tencent, Youdao, MyMemory, Google) with no API key.
chancezhangcr/zotero-bilingual-reader.pain: Reading English papers in Chinese usually means pasting passages into a translator one at a time. Its developer says it needs Zotero 9 on Windows and has been tested only there.

jerryzhongj/zotero-ccf-info.does: Looks up the CCF rank of a paper's conference or journal and shows it as a coloured badge in a custom item list column. Fetch it from the right-click menu or automatically when new items are added.
jerryzhongj/zotero-ccf-info.pain: Computer science researchers who need to know whether a venue is CCF A, B or C otherwise check the catalogue by hand. A fork of TimeTrapzz/zotero-ccf-info; the rank data is the CCF 7th edition (2026).

karlinin/zotero-citationcounts.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, Inspire HEP, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex or Google Scholar. Stores them in the Extra field, tagged with the date. The Google Scholar source needs a SerpAPI key.
karlinin/zotero-citationcounts.pain: Zotero has no field for citation counts, so checking how often a paper is cited means visiting each source by hand. A fork of eschnett/zotero-citationcounts; its README doesn't say what it changes.

apple5089/zotero-easyread.does: Sends a PDF to the EasyRead reader with a right-click. Syncs your reading notes, highlights and saved AI answers back into a child note on the item. Needs EasyRead installed on the same computer.
apple5089/zotero-easyread.pain: People who read papers in EasyRead and manage them in Zotero otherwise copy notes between the two by hand. Its developer says it is an independent community project, tested only on Windows.

xhy200606/zotero-full-translate.does: Translates a whole PDF from the reader through a Cloud service you run yourself. Shows task progress, imports the translated PDF and offers side-by-side reading with linked scrolling.
xhy200606/zotero-full-translate.pain: Full-paper translation normally needs several translation services set up locally. Here the accounts and API quotas live on the Cloud server, which you deploy with Docker and connect to with an account key.

hdusiaocbawa/zotero-gpt-binder-update-ch.does: A local bridge for engineering evidence kept as Markdown files and attachments. This repository holds the update metadata and release hashes for the add-on, which ships with write access switched off.
hdusiaocbawa/zotero-gpt-binder-update-ch.pain: Probably for people connecting Zotero to an outside workflow of evidence notes. The available description is thin and doesn't say more about who it suits.

lalalaladam/zotero-item-tree-expand-coll.does: Adds a toolbar button that expands or collapses every child row in the item list. Covers attachments, notes and annotations, and its icon shows whether rows are collapsed, partly or fully expanded.
lalalaladam/zotero-item-tree-expand-coll.pain: Zotero makes you open parent items one at a time to see their children. This does it in one click and remembers the expanded state separately for each collection, library and saved search.

mathcals/zotero-logseqserver.does: Exposes extra HTTP endpoints from Zotero for the Zotero extension for Logseq to use. Requires Better BibTeX (version 6.7.136 or later).
mathcals/zotero-logseqserver.pain: Lets Logseq users pull references from their Zotero library into their graph. It was originally based on the ZotServer extension.

eric-sly/zotero-mcp-manager.does: Runs a local MCP server inside Zotero, on 127.0.0.1 only, so AI clients can search items, read abstracts, notes and annotations, and manage collections. Tools that write notes, tags or metadata are off until you enable them.
eric-sly/zotero-mcp-manager.pain: Lets Claude Code or other MCP clients work with your library without export steps. A slimmed fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp focused on metadata management, updated for Zotero 10.

edd-gao/zotero-mdnotes.does: Exports item metadata and notes as Markdown files from the right-click menu. Also creates a file for your own notes and batch-exports everything. Works best with ZotFile and Better BibTeX installed.
edd-gao/zotero-mdnotes.pain: Useful for keeping Zotero notes in Markdown tools such as Obsidian. A fork of argenos/zotero-mdnotes, and its developer tested it only on Zotero 5.

djluigipremium-byte/zotero-merge-all-dup.does: Merges every duplicate set in the selected library at once after a single confirmation. It keeps the most complete record, fills its empty fields from the others and moves the merged-away items to the trash.
djluigipremium-byte/zotero-merge-all-dup.pain: Zotero's duplicate pane merges one set at a time, which is slow for big libraries. Its developer advises backing up your data directory first, since conflicting fields are not chosen by hand.

yanyucai/zotero-pdf-auto-bookmarks.does: Generates a bookmark outline for PDFs from their content, using the contents page, headings, font sizes and numbering, and writes it into the PDF. Tuned for medical and life-science papers. Optional AI cleanup uses an OpenAI-compatible API you configure.
yanyucai/zotero-pdf-auto-bookmarks.pain: Long PDFs without bookmarks are hard to navigate in Zotero's reader. It makes a timestamped backup before editing, and scanned PDFs need OCR first.

grahmgaydos/zotero-pdf-summarizer.does: Writes an abstract into the Abstract field when you add a PDF, using a local model (Ollama or LM Studio) or Anthropic, OpenAI or OpenRouter. It can also write a source page per paper into an Obsidian vault.
grahmgaydos/zotero-pdf-summarizer.pain: Items imported without an abstract are hard to skim. This fills one in automatically, asks before overwriting an existing abstract, and can re-run from the right-click menu.

sasaju/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader, plus titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services and a dictionary for single words. Has a standalone window for comparing services.
sasaju/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading papers in a second language means copying text into a translator. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes.

wqe134/zotero-pdf-translate-custom.does: Translates selected text, titles, abstracts, annotations and notes with 20+ services. Compared with the original it makes Ctrl-select the default for joining selections, and adds a switch for double-click copy in the popup.
wqe134/zotero-pdf-translate-custom.pain: A community fork of windingwind's Translate for Zotero. It uses its own plugin ID and settings names, so it can be installed alongside the original without conflicts.

geyuuu/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates PDFs into Chinese with PDF2zh or PDF2zh_next from the right-click menu. This fork starts and stops the Python translation server for you, bundles the server in the plugin, and adds a toolbar button that opens a progress page. Needs uv or Python installed.
geyuuu/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: The original needs you to run a server script in a terminal before translating. This fork removes that step.

zotero-flow/zotero-read-tracker.does: Shows a private activity page inside Zotero with a year-long calendar of reading, notes and saved papers. Also gives totals, reading time, completed papers and a timeline, filterable by collection. Nothing is uploaded.
zotero-flow/zotero-read-tracker.pain: Zotero doesn't show how much you read or when. A fork of Zotero Read Tracker; its developer tested only Zotero 10 on macOS, and reading time is counted only from installation.

anzhaohao/zotero-research-database.does: Adds a database-style table view of your items, switched with one toolbar button. It has sortable and groupable columns, PDF thumbnails and custom research fields filled by hand or by an external agent such as Codex CLI, Claude Code or Ollama.
anzhaohao/zotero-research-database.pain: Comparing many papers on research question, value and results is cramped in Zotero's list. This gives a Notion-like table over the same library, with optional MinerU conversion of PDFs.

hyfaust/zotero-roam.does: Opens a random item from the current collection, search results or library, and jumps to a random page in the open PDF. Use the toolbar buttons or the Tools menu entries.
hyfaust/zotero-roam.pain: For rediscovering papers you saved and forgot, or sampling a long PDF, without picking one by hand.

joshfbvsantos/zotero-rsvp.does: Adds speed reading to the PDF reader: words appear one at a time between 150 and 900 words per minute, with a highlighted focus letter. Start from the current page or from selected text, with keyboard controls.
joshfbvsantos/zotero-rsvp.pain: For skimming long papers faster without moving your eyes. A fork of Amogh-Joshi/zotero-rsvp; its README doesn't say what it changes. Free for noncommercial use only.

wengu4765-lang/zotero-scholar-suite.does: Combines Better Notes and Translate for Zotero in one plugin. It adds full-text PDF translation to bilingual HTML that keeps figures and translates text inside images, and a manager for switching between several language model and translation services.
wengu4765-lang/zotero-scholar-suite.pain: Saves installing the two plugins separately and adds multi-model switching. It needs Zotero 8 or later, and the original plugins must be removed first.

paopaoovo/zotero-selection-notes.does: Lets you select text in the PDF reader and write a note anchored to it, with Markdown, LaTeX and highlighted code rendered when you click the highlight. Exports the paper with a rendered notes appendix, plus HTML and Markdown copies.
paopaoovo/zotero-selection-notes.pain: Annotation comments in Zotero are plain text, so formulas and code are unreadable. Its developer tested it only on Zotero 9 with macOS.

alexgoodenbour/zotero-sort-by-annotation.does: Adds two item list columns: Last Annotated, showing when you most recently highlighted or annotated a paper, and Annotations, showing how many it has. Sort by either to see recent reading.
alexgoodenbour/zotero-sort-by-annotation.pain: Zotero can't show which papers you recently worked on in the PDF reader. These columns bring them to the top of your library.

utf8-coding/zotero-theme-switcher.does: Adds a button to the left of Zotero's tab bar that switches between dark and light themes when double-clicked. No restart is needed.
utf8-coding/zotero-theme-switcher.pain: Zotero 8's theme setting is buried in Advanced Settings. This puts it one double-click away.

holly1226/zotero-venue-tagger.does: Recognises journal and conference venues in a collection and tags items from built-in Zhejiang University Design and CCF lists or your own CSV lists. Shows badges in an HCI Lists column and exports results.
holly1226/zotero-venue-tagger.pain: Made for HCI and design researchers who check venue rankings by hand. It previews changes before writing and needs no API key or cloud service.

piskuliche/zotero-yorklib-exporter.does: Exports selected items as Yorklib-style BibTeX files with matching PDFs, sorted into complete, needs-attention and misc folders. Also writes combined bibliography files, with keys like Last_Journal_Year_vVolume_pPage.
piskuliche/zotero-yorklib-exporter.pain: Built for one research group's bibliography format, and its developer says it isn't worthwhile to anyone outside the York group.

ichirowt/zotero-zotadata.does: Fills in missing metadata from Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, OpenLibrary, Google Books and DBLP, and finds missing DOIs and ISBNs. Downloads PDFs from open-access sources, Library Genesis and Sci-Hub, and removes broken attachment links.
ichirowt/zotero-zotadata.pain: Saves checking each item by hand. Sci-Hub and Library Genesis distribute copyrighted papers without permission, which is illegal in many places. A fork of ydeng11/zotero-zotadata; its README doesn't say what it changes.

grayxu/zotero6-metadata-search-plugin.does: Searches CrossRef and DBLP by title and authors from the right-click menu, pulls DBLP BibTeX results, and updates the fields you choose on the selected item.
grayxu/zotero6-metadata-search-plugin.pain: Fixes incomplete or wrong metadata on computer science papers without retyping it. A fork of ajdavis/zotero-metadata-search-plugin for Zotero 6 only.

gty0709/zoteroagy.does: An AI research assistant in the reader sidebar or a pinned floating window, driven by your local Antigravity CLI (agy) rather than an API key. Add PDF selections or annotation cards to the chat, fill annotation comments from replies, and save answers to notes.
gty0709/zoteroagy.pain: Lets you use the models behind Antigravity while reading, with Obsidian-style formatting, LaTeX and Mermaid diagrams, instead of copying text into another chat tool.

joshgao22/zoterocitationcountsmanager.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, INSPIRE-HEP and Semantic Scholar for new items or from the right-click menu. Adds a sortable Citation count column. No API key needed.
joshgao22/zoterocitationcountsmanager.pain: Zotero has no field for citation counts. A maintained fork of FrLars21's plugin that adds Zotero 7 to 9 support, a compact progress window and bug fixes.

g-steven037/zoterosci.does: Translates PDFs, EPUBs, webpages, metadata, annotations and notes with 20+ services. It adds Chinese title translation into a separate field and journal rank, SCI quartile and impact factor lookups through EasyScholar, which needs your EasyScholar SecretKey.
g-steven037/zoterosci.pain: Mainly for Chinese-language research that needs translated titles and journal rankings next to each item. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate.

domiden/zotfile.does: Renames, moves and attaches PDFs and other files to items, syncs PDFs to a tablet or mobile reader, and extracts PDF annotations into notes.
domiden/zotfile.pain: An attachment manager from before Zotero had its own reader and renaming. A fork of jlegewie/zotfile for Zotero 4 and 5 only. Its developer says it is no longer actively maintained.

piece-of-schmidt/caitation.does: Finds papers similar to one in your library, runs semantic search over your library and checks whether citations support a claim. It connects to the separate Caitation app running locally.
piece-of-schmidt/caitation.pain: For finding related papers and verifying references by meaning rather than keywords. Written from a short German description, as there is no documentation.

xiangweiw/deepread.does: Adds an AI chat sidebar to the PDF reader and an Ask DeepRead button for selected text. Right-click a collection to chat across all its papers with retrieval. Needs your own Anthropic Claude or Google Gemini API key.
xiangweiw/deepread.pain: Lets you question papers and whole collections without leaving Zotero. It can also be exposed as an MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex CLI. Its developer calls it a working MVP tested on macOS.

utsmok/endnote-date-fixer.does: Corrects the Date Added and Date Modified fields of items imported from EndNote, using dates stored in notes. Run Fix EndNote Import Dates from the Tools menu. Works with the companion endnote-exporter app.
utsmok/endnote-date-fixer.pain: An EndNote XML import gives every item the import date, which loses the library's history. This restores the original dates.

andychase/epa-zotero-plugin.does: Disables Zotero's built-in cloud sync features. It exists so the software can be used at the US Environmental Protection Agency, and it supports Zotero 7 only.
andychase/epa-zotero-plugin.pain: For organisations that can't allow Zotero's cloud sync. A fork of USEPA/epa-zotero-plugin; its README doesn't say what it changes.

alvaroaguado3/journal-ranking-zotero-plu.does: Looks up a journal's 2-year mean citedness (close to impact factor), H-index and citation count from OpenAlex, with Crossref as fallback. Appends them to the Extra field from the right-click or Tools menu.
alvaroaguado3/journal-ranking-zotero-plu.pain: Checking journal metrics by hand for each reference is slow. This stores the figures with the item and caches results. Only journal names are sent to OpenAlex and Crossref.

qingmu-aoki/mktero-community-3.16.does: Converts selected PDFs to Markdown in batches through MinerU or Mistral, with status in a Markdown column. Imports local MinerU results and saves outputs as snapshots. Needs a MinerU API token.
qingmu-aoki/mktero-community-3.16.pain: Turning many PDFs into readable Markdown one at a time is tedious. A community fork of Mktero that adds batch conversion, local import and automatic snapshots.

mmmaurer/obsidian-zot.does: Creates and updates an Obsidian note for each item as you add, edit or annotate it, with metadata, child notes and PDF highlights by colour and page. Uses a customisable template and keeps what you write in Obsidian.
mmmaurer/obsidian-zot.pain: Keeping reading notes in Obsidian otherwise means copying metadata and highlights by hand. Its developer calls it a personal vibe-coded project with rough edges.

saimlau/rhapsode.does: Turns paper PDFs into narrated audio with read-along sentence highlighting, using a local Kokoro text-to-speech model and a local server. Adds Listen with Rhapsode to the item menu and a collection menu entry that builds a playlist.
saimlau/rhapsode.pain: Lets you listen to papers instead of reading them, with everything running on your own machine. It needs the separate Rhapsode program, and Linux is its best-tested platform.

jinshijiming/tara-0.06-fix.does: Backs up and restores Zotero preferences, installed plugins, citation styles, translators and locate engines. Toolbar buttons create a backup, export it and restore it elsewhere. Sync account details and some paths are excluded.
jinshijiming/tara-0.06-fix.pain: Zotero sync doesn't carry settings or plugins. A fix of Tara's backup and restore problems for the legacy Zotero 6 version.

arrancurran/zolast.does: Creates and maintains a Recently Added smart collection in My Library that lists items added within a number of days, 30 by default, newest first. Set the window from 1 to 3,650 days in settings.
arrancurran/zolast.pain: Zotero has no built-in view of recently added items. This adds one without making network requests or sending library data.

adno/zot-anlp.does: Adds metadata to PDFs of papers from Japan's ANLP annual meeting (Association for Natural Language Processing). It matches the paper ID such as B2-3, fetches details from the programme and bibliography pages, and fills a conference paper item with title, authors, abstract and pages.
adno/zot-anlp.pain: ANLP PDFs import with no metadata, so entering it by hand is slow. It can run automatically on new PDFs; its developer says the results should be checked.

chr-wei/zotero-annotation-finder.does: Finds all your Zotero annotations in one place.
chr-wei/zotero-annotation-finder.pain: For people whose highlights and comments are spread across many PDFs. Written from a one-line description, as there is no documentation.

denubis/zotero-api-plus.does: Adds endpoints to Zotero's local API for scripts and tools. They add items by DOI, ISBN or PMID with PDF lookup, target groups and collections, open a PDF at a page, and add notes and highlights.
denubis/zotero-api-plus.pain: For scripts and tools that need to drive Zotero from outside. A Zotero 10 fork of GOKORURI007/zotero-api-plus; on Zotero 10, write requests need an API key you authorise.

haoq1nyuan/zotero-better-popups.does: Shows the reader's hover popups for references and sections only while you hold a trigger key, which can be Shift, Option, Control or Command. Click popups such as image zoom keep their normal behaviour.
haoq1nyuan/zotero-better-popups.pain: Selecting text to translate or annotate often triggers hover popups by accident. This stops that unless you ask for them.

gw19ddd/zotero-better-viewer.does: Wraps text in chosen item list columns and row types instead of cutting it off. Dragging a column width moves the columns to its right in proportion, and Auto Fit resizes columns or shrinks text to fit.
gw19ddd/zotero-better-viewer.pain: Zotero truncates long titles and makes column resizing awkward. Based on northword/zotero-itemtree-expand; remove Expand Item Tree first if you have it.

meridianmcp/zotero-bridge-updates.does: Imports BibTeX into a chosen collection with duplicate checks, and attaches PDFs from a folder by BibTeX key. It runs only from Zotero menus, with no server, network or watchers. This repository holds its Mozilla-signed releases and update file.
meridianmcp/zotero-bridge-updates.pain: For people who collect BibTeX and PDFs outside Zotero and want them in a collection without duplicates or manual attaching.

liuaoran/zotero-capsules-status-tag.does: Adds a Status column of clickable capsules for New, To Read, Reading, Finished and UnRead, stored as ordinary tags. You can add custom statuses and colours, and choose a light, dark or system theme.
liuaoran/zotero-capsules-status-tag.pain: Tracking what you've read usually means typing tags by hand. Its developer built it for Zotero 10 and tested it only on macOS.

physicslog/zotero-clock.does: Shows the current time inside the Zotero window.
physicslog/zotero-clock.pain: For people who work in Zotero full screen and want the time in view without switching to another window.

wyfnwpu/zotero-copy-anything.does: Copies local attachment files to the system clipboard so you can paste them into a file manager, chat app or anything that accepts files.
