It works from the item right-click menu, the PDF tab menu, the reader menu or a custom shortcut, for one or several attachments.
wyfnwpu/zotero-copy-anything.pain: Zotero has no way to put a PDF on the clipboard for pasting elsewhere. A fork of windfollowingheart/zotero-copy-anything that adds Zotero 10 compatibility. It downloads a small helper program on first run.

distinguish-dot/zotero-doi-order.does: Keeps a reference list's order in a separate column, so items appear in the order of your DOI list. It restores the order from a pasted list, keeps gaps for missing papers and lets you drag items into place.
distinguish-dot/zotero-doi-order.pain: Papers imported from a reference list land in Zotero in an arbitrary order that no longer matches the manuscript. This preserves the original numbering. Developed for Zotero 9 and aimed at Chinese-language users.

sickerine/zotero-edtechhub-release-test.does: Adds right-click tools for citing in Google Docs and sharing citations, saves item IDs and metadata to notes, and keeps field values in a note when items merge. Built for the EdTech Hub team.
sickerine/zotero-edtechhub-release-test.pain: Helps a research team keep citations consistent across Google Docs, Slack and email. A fork of edtechhub/zotero-edtechhub; its README doesn't say what it changes.

ebawak-fekede/zotero-ferry.does: Temporarily turns linked attachments into stored files so they sync to Zotero's mobile app, then returns them to their original linked paths. Works from the right-click menu on attachments or parent items, and annotations carry over.
ebawak-fekede/zotero-ferry.pain: Keeping large books as linked files saves space, but Zotero's mobile app only reads stored files and its free storage fills up. Ferry lets you store just the books you are reading on mobile.

austrust/zotero-guide-helper.does: Runs a small local API inside Zotero that attaches a verified literature guide PDF to an existing item as a stored attachment, with a set title and tags. Meant to be called by outside automation scripts.
austrust/zotero-guide-helper.pain: Replaces a fragile debug-bridge step in the author's own literature-guide workflow. Its developer's notes say it is an early draft not yet installed or verified in Zotero.

invincible-dhh/zotero-image-uploader.does: Uploads PDF image and area annotations to your image host through PicList or PicGo and writes the Markdown image link into the annotation comment. Works automatically or from a right-click menu.
invincible-dhh/zotero-image-uploader.pain: Image annotations stay inside Zotero, which makes them awkward to reuse in Markdown notes. Needs PicList or PicGo running locally with an image host set up there; the plugin itself needs no keys.

sorinhostiuc/zotero-instant-cite-wordcra.does: Opens the Instant Cite search, add and cite dialog when you choose Add/Edit Citation in the WordCraft word processor. Searches your library and online sources, adds the paper to Zotero and cites it in one step.
sorinhostiuc/zotero-instant-cite-wordcra.pain: Citing a paper you don't yet have normally means leaving the document to import it first. This does it in one dialog and adds a keyboard shortcut for WordCraft on Windows.

yellow-queer/zotero-llm_summerize.does: Right-click a paper or its PDF to have an OpenAI-compatible language model summarise it with a prompt template you choose, saved as a child note. Works with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Kimi, Ollama or LM Studio.
yellow-queer/zotero-llm_summerize.pain: Gets a first-pass summary of a paper into Zotero without copying text into a chat window. You supply the API address and key, or a local model; output language and templates are configurable.

dzp62442/zotero-mcp.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Cherry Studio or Cursor can search your library and read item details. Filters by tags, creators and year, and finds items by DOI or ISBN.
dzp62442/zotero-mcp.pain: Lets an AI client work with your own references for literature reviews and citation tasks without a separate server. A fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp; its README doesn't say what it changes.

zhoas/zotero-md-annotations.does: Renders Markdown in PDF annotation comments, including headings, lists, bold and italics, with a preview and source toggle. Also renders LaTeX maths written between double dollar signs.
zhoas/zotero-md-annotations.pain: Zotero shows annotation comments as plain text, so formatting and equations stay unrendered. Its developer says it may not be actively maintained.

corvo007/zotero-mdnotes.does: Exports item metadata and notes as Markdown files from the right-click menu, creates a file for your own notes and batch-exports everything. File names follow a configurable convention.
corvo007/zotero-mdnotes.pain: Moves reading notes into Markdown tools such as Obsidian. It only works on older Zotero versions, and its developer no longer maintains it and suggests the Zotero Integration plugin for Obsidian instead.

mqjinwon/zotero-paper-ai.does: An AI co-reader for the PDF reader: translates selections, explains text or figures as sticky notes, answers questions about the paper and writes summaries. It can also auto-highlight claims and methods. Needs a Grok or Codex login, or a Grok API key.
mqjinwon/zotero-paper-ai.pain: Keeps paper questions, translation and summaries next to the PDF. Chats and summaries are saved as child notes, so they sync with your library.

hibikiyuki/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text in the PDF, EPUB or web reader using more than 20 services. Also translates item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, and has a dictionary for single words.
hibikiyuki/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading in a second language otherwise means copying text into a translation site. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes.

benature/zotero-plugin-generate-parent-i.does: Creates a parent item for a standalone PDF attachment by asking an AI model for the metadata, starting from the filename and reading page text only if needed. You preview and accept or refine it before saving. Needs an API key.
benature/zotero-plugin-generate-parent-i.pain: PDFs dragged into Zotero without metadata end up as loose attachments. This builds proper bibliographic records in batches. Works with OpenAI, Gemini or Claude style APIs.

20bytes/zotero-plugin-hjfy.does: Downloads a Chinese translation of an arXiv paper from hjfy.top (幻觉翻译), which translates from the LaTeX source, and attaches it to the item. It finds the arXiv ID from the DOI, URL or Extra field and handles several items at once.
20bytes/zotero-plugin-hjfy.pain: Chinese-language readers get a translated PDF with the original layout instead of translating by hand. A fork of ANGJustinl/zotero-plugin-hjfy; its README doesn't say what it changes.

hzx0211/zotero-quick-read-note.does: Right-click a paper to create a child note with an AI-written quick read, built from its metadata and indexed PDF text, or the abstract when there is no PDF. Prompt, research context and note template are editable. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
hzx0211/zotero-quick-read-note.pain: Gives you a structured first look at a paper before deciding to read it fully. Text goes to the service you configure and long papers are cut off after 80,000 characters.

zzt-flash/zotero-reader-note-tweaks.does: Hides the small sticky-note badge Zotero draws on annotations with comments and enlarges the annotation popup and its text in the PDF reader. It changes display only, not your annotations.
zzt-flash/zotero-reader-note-tweaks.pain: Zotero offers no setting for either. This works as a plugin, so it survives Zotero updates.

yamaizumiminoru/zotero-ris-linker.does: Imports every RIS file in a folder and attaches the PDF with the same filename. It skips PDFs already linked to an item and saves a report of imported, skipped and failed files. Runs from the Tools menu.
yamaizumiminoru/zotero-ris-linker.pain: Bulk-importing records and matching PDFs by hand is slow. Everything is processed locally. Its developer tested it on Zotero 7 on Windows.

nathancashion/zotero-scipdf.does: Registers Sci-Hub mirrors as a PDF resolver so Find Full Text and automatic downloads fetch papers from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI. You can add or remove mirror sites in settings.
nathancashion/zotero-scipdf.pain: A fork of syt2/zotero-scipdf that moves to Zotero 8 to 10, adopts the newer menu API and fixes preference handling. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many places.

wuc9521/zotero-search.does: Speeds up Find in Document by preparing a PDF's text in the background and caching it for later sessions. The page your search needs is prepared first, so you can search while it works.
wuc9521/zotero-search.pain: Searching long PDFs and books in the reader can be slow. The cache is limited to 256 MiB. Its developer says it was tested only on Zotero 10.0.5 on macOS and uses private reader internals.

qingshu-wsy/zoteroquicklook-7-10.does: Previews local attachments with your system's quick look tool when you press Space or choose Quick Look from the menu. Uses QuickLook on Windows, qlmanage on macOS or gloobus-preview on Linux, or a custom program.
qingshu-wsy/zoteroquicklook-7-10.pain: Opening each PDF just to check it is slow. Its developer tested it only on Windows 11 with Zotero 10; Windows needs QuickLook running.

kiastien/zotodo.does: Creates Todoist tasks for papers as they are imported into Zotero, or for existing papers on request. Task text, comments, labels, sections and due dates come from templates, and tasks go into a Todoist project matching the collection. Needs a Todoist API token.
kiastien/zotodo.pain: Keeps a reading to-do list in Todoist without retyping titles and links. Tasks can include Zotero select or PDF links. A fork of cpsimpson/zotodo.

daniel-eder/zotseek.does: Semantic search for your library: find papers similar in meaning from the right-click menu, from selected PDF text or from a plain-language query. Embeddings are built and searched locally with a bundled model, and it can combine them with keyword search.
daniel-eder/zotseek.pain: Zotero's search only matches words, so related papers using different terms are missed. A fork of introfini/ZotSeek for Zotero 8; its README doesn't say what it changes.

woyekun-cell/ask-for-gpt.does: Translates PDF pages inside the Zotero reader and shows original and translation side by side, with a companion Mac or Windows app. Also provides word lookup, questions about selected text and Chrome page translation. AI features use your ChatGPT login through Codex.
woyekun-cell/ask-for-gpt.pain: Reading papers in another language usually means juggling windows. Layout-preserving translation keeps figures in place, and notes and annotations stay in Zotero. Needs the separate Ask for GPT app installed.

mindbreaker81/autotag_zotero_plugin.does: Suggests tags for selected items with a language model, then shows them per paper for you to edit before they are added. Works with OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter or local models through Ollama, and can include full PDF text. Needs an API key unless local.
mindbreaker81/autotag_zotero_plugin.pain: Manual tagging doesn't scale and drifts over time as similar papers get different tags. A fork of LilyKun064/Autotag_zotero_plugin; its README doesn't say what it changes.

6forwater29/citation-dialogue.does: Shows an interactive citation graph from OpenAlex for selected papers or a collection, with ranked candidates you don't yet have. Saves notes to Obsidian or Notion, and a local MCP server lets Claude or Codex work with the same graph.
6forwater29/citation-dialogue.pain: Zotero shows no citation links between papers. This helps find highly cited work missing from your library without downloading anything. The interface comes in 20 languages.

mspet1995/evidenceguide.does: Adds a Grade button to the reader toolbar that opens a guided questionnaire for grading medical or psychiatric articles. It has explanatory help and a live score gauge, and answers are saved locally per attachment.
mspet1995/evidenceguide.pain: Gives a consistent way to appraise the strength of clinical evidence while reading. It follows a published grading method but is independent of its author. Its developer tested it on Zotero 10 on Linux.

dcy456/kokoro-reader.does: Reads selected PDF text aloud with the Kokoro text-to-speech model running inside Zotero, with a player bar, speed and voice choices. It can keep reading from the selected sentence to the end of the paper.
dcy456/kokoro-reader.pain: Lets you listen to papers instead of reading on screen. It skips citations and repairs hyphenated words. The voice model, 163 MB by default, downloads on first use; after that it works offline.

uscabayaosj/llm-for-zotero_hack.does: An AI assistant in the Zotero reader: chat with a PDF or EPUB, selected text or figures. Answers carry citations that jump to the source passage, notes can be saved, and an agent mode can search, tag and organise your library.
uscabayaosj/llm-for-zotero_hack.pain: Questions about a paper can be asked without leaving Zotero. It works with API keys, local models, ChatGPT WebChat, Codex or Claude Code. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that adds security hardening and EPUB support.

jensen-zheng-cmd/recto-plugin.does: Adds an editable quick note below the authors in Zotero's Info pane. It is the Zotero companion to Recto for Obsidian, which can copy the note in when it imports the paper.
jensen-zheng-cmd/recto-plugin.pain: Lets you jot a thought on a paper in Zotero before it moves into Obsidian, where Recto converts PDFs to Markdown and shows translations alongside. It targets Zotero 10.

suppakoko/research_helper.does: A planned plugin for literature search and summaries. It would build collections from PubMed, Europe PMC, Crossref, Semantic Scholar and arXiv, summarise with an LLM, and read a trends report aloud. No code is written yet.
suppakoko/research_helper.pain: Aims to turn a literature search into a collection and report in one place. Its developer says the repository holds specification documents only for now.

samlothen/zotbag.does: Imports saved articles from Wallabag into Zotero, one entry at a time or by automatic sync at an interval you set. Articles go into a Wallabag collection with title, URL, date, authors and tags, and files can be attached as PDF, EPUB or other formats.
samlothen/zotbag.pain: Keeps articles saved for later reading in Wallabag in step with your reference library. Needs a Wallabag account with API client credentials. Its developer says it was written with AI tools.

ki-chi/zotbind.does: Links a Zotero collection to a folder on disk and keeps symbolic links to its primary PDFs in sync, named by citation key or item key. Right-click a collection to choose the folder.
ki-chi/zotbind.pain: Gives scripts and other tools a plain folder of readable PDF names that follows your collection. Its developer tested it only on macOS; Windows needs permission to create symbolic links.

keqiye/zotero-ai-classifier.does: Sorts papers into collection folders by sending titles, abstracts and keywords to a language model with a confidence threshold. Also exports titles or abstracts to JSON, saves and restores the folder structure and imports a hierarchy from a text file. Needs an API key.
keqiye/zotero-ai-classifier.pain: Filing a large library into folders by hand is slow. Works with SiliconFlow by default or other OpenAI-style services, and you can stop a run at any time.

xjf17/zotero-ai-extension.does: AI reading help from three buttons in the right-hand bar. It saves a structured reading note, finds library papers related to a claim you type, answers questions in your notes and explains figures. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key, OpenRouter by default.
xjf17/zotero-ai-extension.pain: Gets reading notes and relevant citations from your own library without leaving Zotero. Three buttons in the right-hand bar start the actions, and costs depend on the model you pick.

mondyue1001-alt/zotero-ai-reader.does: Adds an AI sidebar tab to the PDF reader. Key sentences highlight in the PDF as you hover, with figure-by-figure explanations, a structured summary and Q&A on the full text. Needs an OpenAI, DeepSeek, Anthropic or compatible API key.
mondyue1001-alt/zotero-ai-reader.pain: Gives a quick map of a paper in the language you read in, with highlights that land on the exact sentences. Nothing is written to your library unless you ask.

shuyao998/zotero-citation-radar.does: Builds a citation graph for a paper from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar. An LLM report then labels it seminal, mainstream, follow-up, fringe or review. Needs an OpenAlex key and a DeepSeek key.
shuyao998/zotero-citation-radar.pain: Zotero shows only a citation count, not where a paper sits in its field or whose work it builds on. The report is in Chinese and the paper needs a DOI.

pasiooooo/zotero-figure.does: Detects and extracts figures, tables and formulae from PDFs locally, with a reader sidebar to copy, save, caption-edit and add them to notes. Also has a library view for comparing figures across papers. Formula LaTeX recognition optionally uses SiliconFlow.
pasiooooo/zotero-figure.pain: Pulling a figure or table out of a paper normally means screenshots. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-figure that adds a figure library, batch analysis and formula recognition.

pbilodeau94/zotero-figure-extract.does: Extracts figures and tables from a paper's PDF and files them under the item as child attachments titled from their captions. Adds a figures-extracted tag and can store the captions as JSON. Needs a separate extractor service, run locally with Docker.
pbilodeau94/zotero-figure-extract.pain: Gets every figure and table as a ready image without screenshots. Several items can be processed in one go, and a bundled alternative backend gives better crops than pdffigures2.

lordhoth/zotero-hide-citation-highlights.does: Hides the blue boxes the PDF reader draws over detected citations and cross-reference links. Links stay clickable and their hover popups still work; only the painted box goes.
lordhoth/zotero-hide-citation-highlights.pain: The boxes clutter pages of LaTeX papers and Zotero has no setting to turn them off. A fork of jkroes/zotero-hide-citation-highlights that works on Zotero 7 to 10.

kud3n013/zotero-hide-titlebar.does: Hides Zotero's built-in titlebar to give more room on screen.
kud3n013/zotero-hide-titlebar.pain: For people who want a little extra vertical space in the Zotero window.

thatguo/zotero-import-preprocessor.does: Cleans records before they enter Zotero, from CSV, XLSX, BibTeX, RIS and CSL JSON files or article and search-result links. It normalises identifiers, merges exact duplicates and flags probable ones for review.
thatguo/zotero-import-preprocessor.pain: Bulk imports from spreadsheets and search pages arrive messy and duplicated. You can pause or resume a run and optionally fill missing DOIs from Crossref. Built for Zotero 9.

liongkj/zotero-library-bridge-skills.does: Runs a local-only HTTP server so scripts and LLM tools can work with your library. They can import, search and organise items, read attachment text, add notes and tags, and format citations. Comes with companion Claude skills.
liongkj/zotero-library-bridge-skills.pain: Lets AI workflows talk to your library through simple local requests. It does not generate summaries by itself; the companion skills do that after import.

situkangsayur/zotero-llm-analysis-plugin.does: Ask a language model about a collection or selected items: summaries, themes, research gaps, reading order or a literature review draft. Answers cite your items, and each citation is checked against what was sent. Works with Gemini, OpenAI-compatible APIs or Ollama.
situkangsayur/zotero-llm-analysis-plugin.pain: Gives a research overview of a collection without pasting references into a chat. You see what will be sent first, and answers can be saved as a note. Its developer calls it an early 0.1.0 version.

seehowli/zotero-localchat.does: Adds a sidebar chat that sends your paper questions through the ChatGPT desktop app already signed in on your computer, with streamed replies. Each paper keeps its own conversation in a ChatGPT project you pick. Windows only, Zotero 10 only, and it needs Node.js.
seehowli/zotero-localchat.pain: Lets you use an existing ChatGPT account for paper questions without an API key. Its developer calls it an independent experiment that may break when the desktop app updates.

unlastingr/zotero-mcp.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero so AI clients such as Claude Desktop or Cursor can use your library. They can search, read PDF text and notes, analyse annotations, browse collections, create notes and edit tags and metadata.
unlastingr/zotero-mcp.pain: Lets an AI assistant work with your own references for reviews and citation tasks. A fork of cookjohn/zotero-mcp; its README doesn't say what it changes.

brigealong/zotero-mcp-enhanced.does: Zotero side of an MCP setup: it writes item, note, attachment and annotation changes to a local queue. The repository adds a Python MCP service and agent skills for metadata lookup and note writeback. Needs Python and an MCP client.
brigealong/zotero-mcp-enhanced.pain: Lets AI agents make changes to your library through a controlled queue. OCR tools such as Tesseract are optional and installed separately. Installs by hand and targets Zotero 7.

kaiwen-wang/zotero-open-items-plugin.does: Opens the URLs of selected items in your browser with Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+U or a right-click entry. It uses the URL field, falls back to the DOI and checks the parent item for attachments and notes.
kaiwen-wang/zotero-open-items-plugin.pain: Saves copying a link out of the item pane when you want to look at a paper online. Works on several items at once.

yrhoo/zotero-paperlens.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader into Simplified Chinese inside Zotero's selection popup, streamed as it arrives. Cleans up broken line breaks and keeps formulas, units and reference numbers. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
yrhoo/zotero-paperlens.pain: Gives a quick translation without leaving the page you are reading. Several API profiles can be saved, with a glossary and a fast mode that sends only the selected text.

liuning12921/zotero-pdf-fulltext-search.does: Adds a PDF full-text search box to the main Zotero window that shows matching snippets from Zotero's indexed PDF text. Hits are highlighted, with previous and next navigation, and you can locate the item, open the PDF or copy a snippet.
liuning12921/zotero-pdf-fulltext-search.pain: Zotero's full-text search returns whole items, not the passages that matched. This shows the matching text in place. Scanned PDFs need to be indexed first, since it relies on Zotero's own index.

longdeng1/zotero-pdf-translate-popup-lat.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader using 20+ services and renders formulas in the popup with KaTeX. It also translates titles, abstracts, annotations and notes. Click a rendered translation to view and copy its LaTeX or Markdown source.
longdeng1/zotero-pdf-translate-popup-lat.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that adds KaTeX formula rendering to the selection popup, so translated maths displays as formulas instead of raw markup.

xiegaoxiao/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates PDFs inside Zotero with PDF2zh and PDF2zh_next, keeping formulas and layout. Offers bilingual side-by-side output, cropped reading, batch translation and many LLM services. Needs a local Python server and a model service you configure.
xiegaoxiao/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: A fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh that adds translation-failure handling, PDF layout and font fixes, consistent bold text, glossary JSON handling and a switch for translating author names.

xujinsheng/zotero-pdf2zh-next.does: Sends PDFs from Zotero to a local pdf2zh_next server for translation and imports the result as a Chinese PDF, a bilingual PDF or both. Includes a task manager with progress, cancel and retry, and a settings page for your model service.
xujinsheng/zotero-pdf2zh-next.pain: A fork of NightWatcher314/zotero-pdf2zh-next, trimmed down to the Zotero plugin and one local server. It aims for less setup, with the server installed through uv or run in Docker.

notandia/zotero-plugin.does: Identifies MDPI publications in your library and finds verified MDPI references while you read a PDF or saved HTML article. Adds an MDPI column, a tag, scan commands and an MDPI References panel in the reader that highlights matching citations.
notandia/zotero-plugin.pain: For researchers who want to know how much of a paper's reading list comes from one publisher. For PubMed Central papers it uses Europe PMC data so references can be matched reliably.

lyk7539511/zotero-plugin-template.does: An early-stage plugin apparently meant for GPT translation over a websocket; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
lyk7539511/zotero-plugin-template.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template. Probably a starting point for a translation plugin that hasn't been written yet.

leven-comeon/zotero-plugins.does: A pair of plugins in one repository: DOI Manager fetches and validates DOIs and short DOIs for items, and Sync Autofill fills in missing PDFs after a sync. DOI Manager is for Zotero 8 and 9.
leven-comeon/zotero-plugins.pain: Missing or wrong DOIs break lookups and citations, and synced libraries can arrive without their PDFs. These fill both gaps without manual work.

miaameen/zotero-reading-list.does: Sets a read status on items (New, To Read, In Progress, Read, Not Reading, or your own), shown in a sortable column. Change it from the right-click menu or Alt+1 to Alt+5, label new items automatically, and update status when a PDF is opened.
miaameen/zotero-reading-list.pain: A fork of Dominic-DallOsto/zotero-reading-list. Zotero has no built-in way to track what you have read, so people fall back on tags or notes. This adds status and emoji labels.

shanxiao-studio/zotero-redfrog.does: Fills in missing bibliographic metadata and updates journal metrics such as partition, impact factor and citation count from easyScholar. Adds item list columns for publisher or conference, partition, citation count (including Google Scholar) and a rating.
shanxiao-studio/zotero-redfrog.pain: A fork of redleafnew/zotero-updateifsE. Aimed at Chinese-language research, where journal partitions and impact factors are checked by hand and Zotero has no columns for them.

ubvu/zotero-refsense.does: Extracts bibliographic metadata from a PDF's text with AI, using OpenAI or a local Ollama model, and creates or updates the parent item. Starts from a reader button, a shortcut or the right-click menu, with a field-by-field comparison when a parent exists.
ubvu/zotero-refsense.pain: PDFs imported without metadata sit as bare attachments. This reads the paper and builds the record, with a choice between OpenAI (your own key) and local processing. A fork of jikhanjung/zotero-refsense.

z-jjj-y/zotero-research-bridge.does: Exposes your Zotero library to MCP clients such as Codex over a local, token-protected connection. Covers search, PDF access, adding papers, and reviewable edits, trashing and restoring. Includes a Codex skill that writes a map.json analysis per paper.
z-jjj-y/zotero-research-bridge.pain: Lets an AI agent work on your library without desktop automation or loose credentials. Every write is off by default and goes through a plan then apply step. Embedding providers other than Ollama need a key.

jackdhch/zotero-research-companion.does: Shows in the item sidebar, in Chinese, what a paper is about and how it relates to your research and improvement plans. Imports a literature-survey list as collections and tags, attaches local PDFs and adds a translation-status column. Needs Zotero 10.
jackdhch/zotero-research-companion.pain: For researchers running a structured literature survey in Chinese, who otherwise keep notes on relevance outside Zotero. It reads a data file you generate from your own paper and improvement lists.

seifer08ms/zotero-review-studio.does: A beta workspace for writing literature reviews from selected papers. It extracts evidence from their PDFs, builds an editable cross-paper evidence matrix, reviews potential research gaps and generates a traceable draft. Also searches your library and OpenAlex for related studies.
seifer08ms/zotero-review-studio.pain: Writing a literature review means tracking claims and quotes across many PDFs by hand. This keeps evidence tied to source passages. It sends paper content to the model service you configure, so test with non-sensitive papers first.

ineffab1e-vista/zotero-url-import.does: Extends the zotero:// URL scheme so a link can import an item from a BibTeX string or from identifiers such as ISBN, DOI and arXiv IDs. Multiple identifiers can be comma-separated.
ineffab1e-vista/zotero-url-import.pain: Lets web pages, scripts and launchers add items to Zotero with one link, using the same identifiers as File, Add by Identifier. Parameters must be URI-encoded.

rj0508/zoteroassistant.does: A chat assistant in the item pane and a floating window for asking about papers. Quick actions cover summaries, key points, methods, findings and comparison, with citation copying and image input from uploads, paste or a captured PDF page.
rj0508/zoteroassistant.pain: Works with GitHub Copilot models (needs a Copilot subscription) or local models in LM Studio or Ollama, with per-task model overrides, so you can ask questions about a paper without leaving Zotero.

gchapron/zoteromultiplelibraries.does: Adds several personal libraries side by side in the collection tree, each working like My Library. Each has its own collections, searches, tags, trash and duplicates. Drag items between them. Extra libraries can stay local or sync as a private group. Needs Zotero 10.
gchapron/zoteromultiplelibraries.pain: A Zotero account has one personal library, so separating work, teaching and personal reading means group libraries or a second profile. This gives you separate libraries in one window.

fdossi/zotread.does: Adds a Reading status column to the item list with coloured dots: red for unread, green for read, and green with yellow for read and annotated. Opening an attachment marks the item read, and you can mark items manually. Needs Zotero 10.
fdossi/zotread.pain: Zotero doesn't show at a glance which papers you have opened or annotated. This marks it automatically, with a sortable column that works in group libraries too.

colobas/zotxt.does: Exposes your Zotero library through a local API so plain-text tools can look up items and citations. Works with pandoc through the pandoc-zotxt.lua filter and Better BibTeX citation keys, and with Emacs through zotxt-emacs.
colobas/zotxt.pain: A fork of egh/zotxt. People writing in Markdown, reStructuredText or LaTeX otherwise export bibliographies by hand. This lets pandoc pull citations from a running Zotero.

sinoftj/bottom.does: Improves Zotero's tag selector with a top search button and a first-letter filter. It supports filtering in several steps and clears all selected tags with one click. Works for Chinese and English tags.
sinoftj/bottom.pain: In libraries with many tags, the stock tag pane is slow to scan and clear. Its developer says it was tested only on macOS with Zotero 8.

eureka39/cars-zotero-plugin.does: Builds a research matrix of problems against methods from selected PDFs, showing covered areas and gaps. It first extracts structured details such as method, innovations, blind spots and datasets. Matrices open in a Zotero window and export as images. Needs a Gemini or Anthropic-compatible API key.
eureka39/cars-zotero-plugin.pain: Spotting research gaps across many papers is slow when done by hand. This turns a reading set into a problem-by-method grid and explains why empty cells may be empty. It is the Zotero version of the CARS method, originally a Claude Code skill.

cyberlaboratory/chartero.does: Records the pages and times you read and charts them. Adds a reading-progress column, item summaries, an overview tab, a reader scrollbar showing read pages and annotations, and a sidebar of all images in the document. Recent documents appear in the File menu.
cyberlaboratory/chartero.pain: A fork of volatile-static/Chartero. Zotero doesn't show how far you have got in a paper or how you spend your reading time. This keeps and displays that history.

yehongyu1234/chatpapers.does: Chat with the PDF in a sidebar panel, summarise it, compare up to 8 papers, and save replies as child notes. Also has a voice lecture mode that reads a paper aloud section by section with highlighting in the PDF, and an explain-and-read option for selected text.
yehongyu1234/chatpapers.pain: Needs Zotero 9. Works with Ollama, LM Studio, OpenRouter, OpenAI, DeepSeek, SiliconFlow or a custom endpoint; cloud services need your own key. Lets you question and listen to papers without leaving Zotero.

sparklemuff1n/cjk-date-convert.does: Converts Japanese dates in the Date field, including era years such as Reiwa and Heisei, to Western formats like 2025.03.14. Run it from the right-click menu or the Tools menu on selected items and pick an output format.
sparklemuff1n/cjk-date-convert.pain: Japanese sources record dates by era, which sort and format badly in citations. This rewrites them in one step and skips items without a recognisable Japanese date.

fangchenghao/codex-bilingual-reader.does: Turns a PDF into a layout-preserving English and Chinese bilingual PDF, added as a child attachment while the original stays untouched. Uses a local Codex CLI or an OpenAI-compatible API such as DeepSeek, with batch queues, progress, token and cost tracking.
fangchenghao/codex-bilingual-reader.pain: Reading English papers alongside a Chinese translation usually loses figures and equations. This keeps the page layout. It installs PDFMathTranslate-next, and paper text goes to your chosen service. A maintained fork of Mengqi97's plugin.

xuchaoemail1996-silence/collectioncitati.does: Lets you mark items as cited or uncited separately in each collection, shown in a Citation status column. Mark one or several items from the right-click menu, or clear the mark. Marks stay on your computer and don't sync. Built for Zotero 10.
xuchaoemail1996-silence/collectioncitati.pain: The same paper can be cited in one chapter and not another, and Zotero has no per-collection record of that. This keeps the two statuses apart. It is manual and doesn't read your Word or LibreOffice documents.

ycjian04/llm-for-zotero.does: Brings LLMs into the Zotero reader to ask about the current PDF, selected text or figures. Answers carry citations that jump to the source passage, and notes save to Zotero or Markdown folders. Agent Mode can search, tag, import and edit your library.
ycjian04/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes. Works with API keys, local models, WebChat, Codex App Server or Claude Code.

rockthevegetablemechanics/llm-for-zotero.does: Adds a batch queue to llm-for-zotero: select several papers, apply one prompt to each in turn, and save each result in that paper's own chat session. Prompts include Summarize, Key Points, Methodology and Limitations. Needs a Codex App Server login.
rockthevegetablemechanics/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero for running the same question over many papers unattended, then reading each result later. The queue pauses, stops or retries failed items. Its developer tested it on Windows with Zotero 7.

mo-qc/mo-qc-zotero-wpsnote-sync.does: Syncs items, notes, PDF links and annotations to WPS Notes through its MCP endpoint, by right-click or automatically when a chosen tag is added. Converts Markdown and LaTeX, skips unchanged items, asks on conflicts and uses title and body templates. Needs a WPS Notes MCP API key.
mo-qc/mo-qc-zotero-wpsnote-sync.pain: People who keep reading notes in WPS Notes otherwise copy them over by hand. This keeps them updated from Zotero and avoids duplicates.

tsiangsun/promote-bib.does: Promotes selected items into a master BibTeX file and optionally creates a Markdown reference note from your template. Shows a dry-run preview, reuses existing entries, detects duplicate citation keys and updates the item's citation key in Zotero.
tsiangsun/promote-bib.pain: For writers who keep a project .bib file and a Markdown literature vault alongside Zotero, and want one step to keep the three in sync without editing files by hand.

ruali-dev/qingyi-translator.does: Select text in the Zotero PDF reader, right-click Translate Selected Text, and a card shows the translation with formula rendering. Sends the text to an OpenAI-compatible service you choose, including Ollama, through a small Windows desktop app. Needs Zotero 10 on Windows.
ruali-dev/qingyi-translator.pain: A light alternative to full dictionary or browser tools for reading papers in another language. Only the selected text is sent, and you pick the model and provider.

ashwin-pothen/zocitally.does: Fetches citation counts from OpenAlex for items with a DOI and shows them in a sortable Citations column. Update from the right-click or Tools menu for selected items. A free OpenAlex key is optional and raises the daily allowance.
ashwin-pothen/zocitally.pain: Zotero shows no citation counts, so ranking a reading list means looking each paper up. Counts come from OpenAlex, not Google Scholar, and will differ from other sources.

gavin-zcx/zot-link.does: Converts imported PDF attachments into linked files in a fixed folder per item (_items/ITEM_KEY/). Roles are main PDF, translation PDF or supplement, with matching titles and tags. Checks each copy before erasing the original and keeps annotations and notes.
gavin-zcx/zot-link.pain: For people who keep a file-based paper archive and want attachments to point to predictable files, not duplicates inside Zotero storage. Back up first, as its developer notes it is an early release.

huqilin0504/zotero-academic-translator.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader with streaming output and formula rendering. Adds an AI sidebar for questions about the paper, and translates whole PDFs through an external pdf2zh into Chinese or bilingual copies. Engines include DeepSeek, Gemini, a local agy CLI and Ollama.
huqilin0504/zotero-academic-translator.pain: Gives translation and paper Q&A in one place for Chinese readers. DeepSeek and Gemini need your own API key, and full-text translation needs pdf2zh installed separately.

orange4664/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads new PDFs with an LLM and saves a structured Markdown note under each item. Also offers deep reading, mind maps, poster-style one-image summaries, multi-paper reviews and a reading sidebar. Needs an API key from your chosen model provider.
orange4664/zotero-ai-butler.pain: A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler, adding a cleaner interface and security fixes such as filtering untrusted HTML and exporting settings without keys. Saves you reading backlogs paper by paper.

yidong72/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads new PDFs with an LLM and saves a structured Markdown note under each item. Also offers mind maps, poster-style one-image summaries, multi-paper reviews and a reading sidebar. Runs from the right-click menu, automatically, or as a batch over old papers. Needs your own API key.
yidong72/zotero-ai-butler.pain: A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler; its README doesn't say what it changes. Helps with a backlog of papers you never get round to reading.

practiceearnestly/zotero-ai-literature-w.does: Queues a Figure and Table review through the llm-for-zotero Agent API when an item's rating reaches five stars, and saves it as a child note. The repository also holds prompts, scripts and a patched AI Butler for a three-level (L1 to L3) summary workflow.
practiceearnestly/zotero-ai-literature-w.pain: Automates deeper reading for the papers you rate highest, so the effort goes where it matters. The queue is local to one device, you need llm-for-zotero set up, and updates are manual.

guanjunz432-ctrl/zotero-bilingual-reader.does: Generates a layout-preserving English and Chinese side-by-side PDF and attaches it to the item. It translates body text, captions and labels inside figures. Windows only, using your own Codex account. Needs Zotero 9, Python and Node.js.
guanjunz432-ctrl/zotero-bilingual-reader.pain: Plain translation loses figure text and page structure. This translates axis labels and legends in place. Its developer notes dense or tilted labels need checking. It is a preview.

hlx0509/zotero-bilingual-translator.does: Builds a bilingual PDF where each original page is followed by its Simplified Chinese translation. Images, standalone formulas and tables are cropped in from the source page. Sends only text to DeepSeek and saves the result as a linked attachment. Needs a DeepSeek API key and Zotero 10.
hlx0509/zotero-bilingual-translator.pain: Gives page-by-page comparison while the original pages stay intact. Scanned or password-protected PDFs aren't supported, and text inside images and tables isn't translated.

chengrain0424/zotero-chatgpt-bridge.does: Adds a reader toolbar button that opens a new ChatGPT conversation in Safari and attaches the paper's PDF and supporting files. It has an editable review prompt. It never presses Send. Imports a returned ZIP or Markdown as a child note with Better Notes.
chengrain0424/zotero-chatgpt-bridge.pain: Uses your existing signed-in ChatGPT session, not the OpenAI API, so no key is needed. It is a beta for macOS with Safari, needs several system permissions and depends on ChatGPT's page layout.

barrierfly/zotero-citation-tally.does: Fetches citation counts from Crossref, Semantic Scholar, INSPIRE and OpenAlex and shows them in sortable Citations, FWCI and average citations per year columns. Updates new items automatically or on a schedule, with per-source updates in the right-click menu.
barrierfly/zotero-citation-tally.pain: A fork of daeh/zotero-citation-tally that adds the average-per-year column and OpenAlex FWCI. Without it, citation counts mean looking papers up one by one. Data is stored in the Extra field.

berumotto-mk/zotero-codex-local-api.does: Adds automation endpoints to Zotero's local connector server. They provide a health check, collection creation and adding existing items to a collection by key. Requests must be JSON and come from the local machine.
berumotto-mk/zotero-codex-local-api.pain: Lets scripts or Codex organise a library into collections without desktop automation, using only Zotero's built-in local server and no new network port.

kongbai55/zotero-codex-reader.does: A chat sidebar in the PDF reader driven by your installed Codex CLI, for reading, summarising, translating and discussing papers. Add PDF excerpts as numbered annotations, and drop in files or paste screenshots. Reuses your Codex login, so no separate API key.
kongbai55/zotero-codex-reader.pain: Lets Codex users talk to a paper without leaving Zotero. Tested by its developer on Windows with Zotero 10; there is no automatic update server.

seanlawsonphd/zotero-coding-templates.does: Installs 37 Better Notes templates for qualitative coding of highlights tagged with codes. They build a code overview, codebook, code matrix, code and memo reports, theme document and theme map. Notes can be refreshed after more coding. Needs Better Notes.
seanlawsonphd/zotero-coding-templates.pain: Turns Zotero into a simple coding tool for class projects: highlight passages, tag each with a code, and the templates collect the bookkeeping without a separate qualitative analysis program.

manu-gibst/zotero-color-shortcuts.does: Highlights selected text in the reader with Ctrl+Shift+1 to 8 (Cmd+Shift on Mac), one key per default annotation colour. No colour popup is needed. The colours are fixed for now.
manu-gibst/zotero-color-shortcuts.pain: Choosing a colour by mouse after every selection slows down heavy annotating. Its developer says a remapping pane is planned, and the live selection path still needs a manual check.

shjdgwj/zotero-copy-anything.does: Copies the selected items' attachment files to the system clipboard so you can paste them into a file manager or another app. Register your own shortcut; it handles several attachments and formats. Downloads a helper binary on first use; Linux needs xclip and wl-clipboard.
shjdgwj/zotero-copy-anything.pain: A fork of windfollowingheart/zotero-copy-anything; its README doesn't say what it changes. Zotero can't copy an attachment as a file, so sharing a PDF means finding it on disk.

knhn1004/zotero-copy-author.does: Copies short author names such as Smith & Jones, or a LaTeX \cite{key} command using Better BibTeX keys. Use Ctrl or Cmd+Shift+A and L, or the right-click menu.
knhn1004/zotero-copy-author.pain: Saves retyping author lists and citation keys when writing emails, notes or LaTeX. Without Better BibTeX it builds keys from author name and year.

37-yami/zotero-dedup.does: Scans the selected collection, or the collection of the selected item, for duplicates by DOI, title with author and year, title only, or PDF content hash. A window lets you keep one, delete all or skip each group, and removals go to the trash.
37-yami/zotero-dedup.pain: Catches duplicates that metadata misses, such as identical PDFs under different titles, and duplicate PDFs within one item. Deleted items stay in the trash so they can be restored.

migueldlm/zotero-filters.does: Adds a search box under each column header in the item list, so you can filter by typing in any column. Filters apply as you type and combine across columns, with a clear button on each box. For Zotero 7 to 10.
migueldlm/zotero-filters.pain: Zotero's single search bar can't narrow by a given column, such as one author and one year together. This works like spreadsheet filters.

lineex/zotero-fmrs.does: Looks up an item's DOI or PMID on FMRS, attaches a PDF from its download channels, and sends a full-text request by email if that fails. Can poll your mailbox by POP3 or the agently-cli and attach PDFs that arrive. Needs an FMRS login session.
lineex/zotero-fmrs.pain: Gets full texts for people who use FMRS for access, saving the manual search, request and attach steps. Built for Chinese-language users of that service.

jain-arham-hsr/zotero-harvester.does: Rolls highlights, area-box figures and comments into a Markdown bundle, then sends it to your open chat box through a companion Chrome extension. Adds three right-click items. Needs no API key and never calls a model itself.
jain-arham-hsr/zotero-harvester.pain: Pasting highlights into a chat model loses diagrams and blurs your own comments into the author's text. This sends quotations, your notes, images and page numbers separately.

raythere/zotero-infinity.does: A chat panel that answers questions about the open paper using a local Ollama model. It also compares several papers, searches your library by full text, and suggests tags or groups of similar papers for you to review.
raythere/zotero-infinity.pain: Cloud AI assistants need API keys and send your papers off your machine. This keeps everything local, at the cost of needing Ollama and a model of about 700 MB (llama3.2:1b).

pengtb/zotero-litfetch.does: Adds a right-click command that fetches missing PDFs for selected items by DOI, arXiv ID or PMID and attaches them. It calls a separate lit-fetch Python backend on your computer, which tries open-access sources first, then a real browser.
pengtb/zotero-litfetch.pain: Collecting full texts one by one is slow. This batches it, shows progress per item, and skips items that already have a PDF. It does not bypass paywalls; institutional IP or VPN access is used where you have it.

charliegarfield/zotero-llm-extraction.does: Extracts bibliographic metadata from PDFs with an LLM and fills in the item's fields. It supports Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as Ollama, sends page images for scanned PDFs, and checks DOIs against CrossRef.
charliegarfield/zotero-llm-extraction.pain: Zotero's own metadata lookup often fails for preprints, theses, scans and foreign-language documents. You review each extracted field side by side before anything is written. Needs an API key unless you use a local model.

rxy0424/zotero-mdnotes.does: Exports item metadata and notes as markdown files. It also creates a file for your own notes on an item and can batch-export everything at once, all from the right-click menu.
rxy0424/zotero-mdnotes.pain: Moves Zotero notes and references into markdown-based note apps. A fork of argenos/zotero-mdnotes; its README doesn't say what it changes. Its developer says it was tested on Zotero 5 and works best with ZotFile and Better BibTeX.

fanyingfx/zotero-odh.does: Brings the Online Dictionary Helper (ODH) to Zotero, so you can look up words and send them to Anki through AnkiConnect. It supports ODH system scripts; Anki Web and user-defined scripts are not yet implemented.
fanyingfx/zotero-odh.pain: Language learners reading papers in Zotero can build Anki vocabulary cards without leaving the reader. A fork of 1ywan/zotero-odh; its README doesn't say what it changes.

weekendp/zotero-paper-chat.does: Adds a Paper Chat panel to the right sidebar for asking questions about a PDF using Google's Gemini models. Includes quick actions for summary, methodology and key findings, multi-paper comparison and clickable page references.
weekendp/zotero-paper-chat.pain: Lets you question papers without copying text into a separate chatbot. Needs a free Google Gemini API key from Google AI Studio; the newest model has strict rate limits, so you can switch models.

yangjay2004/zotero-paper-markdown.does: Converts a paper's PDF attachment into Markdown with the MinerU API and saves it as a child attachment on the same item. Needs a MinerU token.
yangjay2004/zotero-paper-markdown.pain: Raw PDFs lose section structure, formulas and tables when read by AI agents and text tools. A Markdown copy next to each PDF gives agents and note-taking tools cleaner text to work from.

azhar-rafiq/zotero-pdf-background.does: Changes the PDF reader's background colour to ease eye strain. It has several preset backgrounds, a custom colour in settings and an eye button on the toolbar to switch modes. Follows system dark mode and works in split view.
azhar-rafiq/zotero-pdf-background.pain: Long reading sessions on a white page tire the eyes. A fork of wangqian06/zotero-pdf-background; its README doesn't say what it changes.

ccsouljump/zotero-pdf-deduplicator.does: Detects duplicate PDF attachments that are byte-identical by SHA-256 hash and moves the extra copy to the trash after you confirm. Checks new PDFs as they arrive and scans older ones from Tools, Scan Existing PDFs.
ccsouljump/zotero-pdf-deduplicator.pain: Zotero's duplicate pane compares metadata, not files, so the same PDF can sit in a library many times. This finds true file duplicates only; re-saved or OCR-processed copies are not matched. A Zotero 10 compatibility fork of heimi98/zotero-deduplicator.

code-thx/zotero-pdf-translate-v0.9.8-noc.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader. It also handles annotations, notes, item titles and abstracts, with a dictionary for single words and sentence-by-sentence mode. The default engine is Google Translate.
code-thx/zotero-pdf-translate-v0.9.8-noc.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate version 0.9.8 that removes the CNKI advert. Its developer says translations come without the abc marker so you can edit them freely, and titles show in the short title field for note templates.

albresky/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates whole PDFs with PDF2zh or PDF2zh_next, keeping the layout and producing bilingual versions. It connects Zotero to a local Python server you install with uv or conda. Works with Zotero 7 and 8.
albresky/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: Full-document translation normally means exporting the PDF and using a separate tool. This runs it from within Zotero. A fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh; its README doesn't say what it changes.

nathancashion/zotero-quicklook.does: Previews attachments with macOS QuickLook when you press Space on an item, like in Finder. Shift+Space previews notes, and Option+Space shows a PDF as a contact sheet of page thumbnails.
nathancashion/zotero-quicklook.pain: Checking what a file is normally means opening it in a tab or app. This gives the quick peek Mac users know from Finder. Works on macOS only. A fork of gchapron/ZoteroQuickLookMac, updated for newer Zotero.

samdowrickstr/zotero-reading-list.does: Adds a Read Status column with labels such as New, To Read, In Progress, Read and Not Reading, set from the right-click menu or Alt+1 to Alt+5. It can label new items and update status when you open a PDF. Also tracks per-item reading tasks.
samdowrickstr/zotero-reading-list.pain: Zotero has no built-in way to mark what you have read. A fork of Dominic-DallOsto/zotero-reading-list that adds recording reading tasks such as chapters or pages with their own statuses and progress.

ytong24/zotero-reading-list.does: Adds a Read Status column with labels such as New, To Read, In Progress, Read and Not Reading, set from the right-click menu or Alt+1 to Alt+5. It can label new items and update status when you open a PDF.
ytong24/zotero-reading-list.pain: Zotero has no built-in way to mark what you have read. A fork of Dominic-DallOsto/zotero-reading-list; its README doesn't say what it changes.

dcrizz/zotero-research-canvas.does: Local freeform canvases and mind maps where you arrange Zotero notes, annotations and references as cards that stay linked to their sources. Add frames and labelled connectors, and export to SVG, PNG, PDF, JSON or Obsidian Canvas.
dcrizz/zotero-research-canvas.pain: Zotero has no visual space for laying out evidence and ideas. Its developer says it is tested only on Zotero 10.0.6 on macOS and advises backing up first. Optional AI suggestions need a provider.

wcg0726/zotero-researchhub.does: A sidebar toolbox for researchers. It has a check-in tracker, Pomodoro timer, AI writing polish, translation, email templates, LaTeX snippets and plotting tips. AI features use an OpenAI-compatible API you configure.
wcg0726/zotero-researchhub.pain: Bundles small daily research aids into one place, mostly for Chinese-speaking researchers. Includes a submission checklist and AI journal suggestions, plus lighter extras such as water and meal tracking.

yuyichao/zotero-tray.does: Keeps Zotero running in the Linux system tray. Closing the main window hides it instead of quitting, and clicking the tray icon shows or hides it, with a menu to show, hide or quit Zotero.
yuyichao/zotero-tray.pain: Linux users otherwise lose the app, and sync and indexing with it, when they close the window. Works on X11 and Wayland with StatusNotifierItem trays; its developer has tested only KDE Plasma.

liuyujie0136/zotero-updateifse.does: Fetches journal rankings and impact data from easyScholar into the Extra field, including JCR and CAS quartiles, impact factor and Chinese core-journal lists. Also updates journal abbreviations and item metadata, and adds author-formatting tools.
liuyujie0136/zotero-updateifse.pain: Looking up journal ranks by hand is slow, especially for Chinese-language research. Needs an easyScholar key. A fork of redleafnew/zotero-updateifsE that its developer says is for self use only; it stops overwriting title fields.

wwsh123/zotero-zotadata.does: Fills in missing metadata from CrossRef, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, OpenLibrary, Google Books and DBLP, and finds DOIs and ISBNs. It also finds PDFs from Unpaywall, CORE, arXiv, Library Genesis and Sci-Hub, and removes broken attachment links.
wwsh123/zotero-zotadata.pain: Cleaning up incomplete libraries by hand is slow. Note that Library Genesis and Sci-Hub distribute copyrighted papers without permission, which is illegal in many places. Needs Zotero 8 or later. A fork of janbaykara/zotero-zotadata.

112345brian/zotero-zotflow-autosync.does: Updates the annotations section of your ZotFlow Obsidian vault files as soon as you add or edit an annotation in Zotero. It finds notes by Better BibTeX citekey and keeps your own notes above the annotations.
112345brian/zotero-zotflow-autosync.pain: ZotFlow only imports annotations into Obsidian when you trigger a sync. This pushes changes automatically. It only updates existing files, so ZotFlow must have synced each item once.

xiaogou1234/zoterocopilot.does: Connects AI assistants such as Codex and Claude Code to your local Zotero library through a localhost bridge and a helper app. They can search items, read metadata, notes and full text, and, if you allow it, write changes.
xiaogou1234/zoterocopilot.pain: Lets an AI agent manage and organise your literature without exports or copying. Needs the helper download for macOS or Windows and an MCP configuration copied into your AI tool.

bbutlerau/zotmeta.does: Updates selected items in bulk: journal articles from DOI records, books from ISBN records and arXiv preprints from their IDs. It can find DOIs in the PDF text and create parent items for loose PDFs.
bbutlerau/zotmeta.pain: Fixing incomplete metadata one item at a time is slow. Failed and skipped items get tags for follow-up. A fork of RoadToDream/ZotMeta; its README doesn't say what it changes.

cedar-wood/formula-forge.does: Extracts figures, tables and display formulas from PDFs with a layout model bundled in the plugin, running locally. Results appear in a reader sidebar and a library view; you can copy images, export them as ZIP or add them to notes.
cedar-wood/formula-forge.pain: Pulling figures and equations out of papers means screenshots. Optional formula-to-LaTeX recognition needs your own API key for an OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic service. Requires Zotero 10.

jackwpp/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research assistant in the Zotero reader. Chat with the open PDF, selection or figures, compare papers, and use an agent mode for library-wide tagging and notes. It works with API providers, local models, Codex and Claude Code.
jackwpp/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero aimed at single-paper reading. It adds quick translation of selected text with its own model and an Overview tab that builds a structured Paper Brief.

qingyun0118/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research assistant in the Zotero reader. Chat with the open PDF, selection or figures, compare papers, and use an agent mode for library-wide tagging and notes. It works with API providers, local models, Codex and Claude Code.
qingyun0118/llm-for-zotero.pain: A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that its maintainer says adds syncing of conversation titles and fixes for image and character-diagram rendering.

liupcmail/lpcteam-translate.does: Translates text you select in the PDF or EPUB reader into the right sidebar with streaming output. Uses built-in Bing and Google or your own OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints, and also translates item titles and abstracts.
liupcmail/lpcteam-translate.pain: Reading in another language means constant copying into a translator. Chinese text is translated into English and other languages into Chinese. LLM endpoints such as DeepSeek need your own API key.

lidayunzhongjun-cell/paper-assistant-nex.does: A reading workbench for Zotero 9 that translates and explains selected passages, supports follow-up questions and builds a section-by-section map of the PDF. It uses a DeepSeek or other OpenAI-compatible API and renders LaTeX formulas.
lidayunzhongjun-cell/paper-assistant-nex.pain: Helps Chinese-language readers work through hard papers instead of getting a one-off summary. It also imports AI-written digests as navigation. Needs an API key unless you use a local endpoint.

zcybeijing/patent.does: Extracts patent metadata from local Chinese patent PDFs: title, application number, dates, inventors, applicant, abstract and IPC class. It handles invention, utility model and design patents in batches and can try to download PDFs from CNIPA.
zcybeijing/patent.pain: Chinese patents are tedious to enter by hand. Its developer notes that automatic CNIPA search currently fails because of cookie restrictions, so it falls back to opening the site in Zotero's browser.

chenbin98/sci-download-for-zotero10.does: Downloads PDFs by DOI, PMID or title through mirror sites, tried in parallel and checked as real PDFs before attaching. Metadata comes from CrossRef and PubMed. Works from the item menu, toolbar and reader, and skips items that already have a PDF.
chenbin98/sci-download-for-zotero10.pain: Researchers without access hit paywalls. The mirrors are third-party and may serve papers you have no right to; follow your local law and publisher terms. A Zotero 10 fork of chen7447/sci-download-for-zotero.

ils-research/seekbook-zotero.does: Builds a full-text index of your books, by meaning and by keyword, that knows each passage's chapter and printed page number. Other plugins, SeekChat and ZotSeek, use it through a local REST API. Needs an Ollama or OpenAI-compatible embedding server.
ils-research/seekbook-zotero.pain: Books are long, split into chapter PDFs and full of running headers that spoil ordinary search. This indexes whole books cleanly so answers can cite chapter and page.

xiling951/zotero-.does: A Windows bundle of Zotero 10 with an AI sidebar, translation plugins and a dark-mode fix. It adds a local PDF2zh translation server with formula protection and an offline command-line OCR tool for scanned PDFs.
xiling951/zotero-.pain: Setting up whole-document translation and AI reading from separate parts is fiddly. This packages them for Windows x64. You supply your own AI service address, model and API key.

suresh-inbit/zotero-ai-chat.does: Adds an AI Chat section to the item pane for asking questions about the selected item. The model gets the metadata, PDF full text and your annotations. Works with Claude, OpenRouter, Requesty and OpenAI-compatible APIs including local Ollama or LM Studio.
suresh-inbit/zotero-ai-chat.pain: Saves copying papers into a separate chatbot. You can send cropped figures, save answers as child notes and see LaTeX rendered. Needs an API key unless you use a local model.

northws/zotero-ai-pdf-assistant.does: Adds AI Translate and AI Chat buttons to the popup shown when you select text in the PDF reader. Answers stream in with Markdown and maths. Uses OpenAI-compatible APIs or a local Ollama model.
northws/zotero-ai-pdf-assistant.pain: Translating or asking about a passage normally means leaving Zotero. Selected text goes to your configured endpoint, so a local Ollama model keeps it on your machine.

magicdakeai/zotero-ai-reader.does: Translates only the PDF pages you choose into Chinese, shown beside the original paragraphs with a one-line summary each. Translations are cached locally. Uses DeepSeek, OpenAI, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow or Ollama.
magicdakeai/zotero-ai-reader.pain: Translating a whole paper wastes tokens when you only need a few pages. Formulas can be copied as Markdown for Obsidian. Cloud services need your own API key. Requires Zotero 10.

sperwe/zotero-annotation-manage.does: Manages PDF annotations by tag and colour. Add annotations with fixed tags, export them as notes, link annotations across PDFs, highlight chosen words and merge annotations. Export needs the Better Notes plugin.
sperwe/zotero-annotation-manage.pain: Gives readers who annotate heavily a way to sort highlights by colour and tag and gather them for reviews. Built mostly for Chinese-language research workflows.

wentiangodlike/zotero-askpage.does: Select text in the reader and ask an AI to explain or translate it, or type your own question. Answers stream into the sidebar with formulas typeset. It can send a screenshot of the selection and your annotations as context.
wentiangodlike/zotero-askpage.pain: Pasted PDF formulas often turn into garbage, and switching to a chatbot loses context. Works with DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama and others; you bring a key. Its developer has tested it only on Zotero 10 and Ubuntu.

c-lyu/zotero-attanger.does: Attaches the newest file from a download folder to an item, matches files to items by title and renames them with Zotero's templates. It can also move them into folders built from metadata or collections.
c-lyu/zotero-attanger.pain: Keeps PDFs in a readable folder tree that cloud services can sync. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger; its README doesn't say what it changes. Works with Zotero 7 to 10.

guoyingwei6/zotero-backup-vault.does: Makes disaster-recovery snapshot backups of Zotero libraries.
guoyingwei6/zotero-backup-vault.pain: People with large libraries who want a restorable copy in case of loss or corruption.

lcneyc/zotero-copy-pdfs-to-clipboard.does: Adds a right-click command that copies the PDF files of selected items to the system clipboard as real files. Pasting works in Finder, email and AI chat windows. Multi-file copy works on macOS and Windows.
lcneyc/zotero-copy-pdfs-to-clipboard.pain: Dragging PDFs out of Zotero is awkward. A fork of esihaj/zotero-copy-pdf-to-clipboard that adds copying several PDFs at once.

stevenshen3641/zotero-core-ranking.does: Shows the CORE or CCF ranking of each paper's conference or journal in a Rank column and an item pane section. The rank and venue acronym are saved on a line of the Extra field. New items are ranked automatically.
stevenshen3641/zotero-core-ranking.pain: Checking venue rankings by hand is slow for computer science researchers. You can correct a rank manually, and the lists ship with the plugin so it works offline. Requires Zotero 10.

ipconfig2023/zotero-elsevier-pdf-helper.does: Downloads Elsevier and ScienceDirect PDFs you can legally access and attaches them to selected items, one by one or for the current view. Opens institutional login in Zotero and tags items with the download result.
ipconfig2023/zotero-elsevier-pdf-helper.pain: Fetching publisher PDFs one at a time is tedious. Batches use random delays to reduce blocking. It does not use Sci-Hub or cookie extraction.

xin-yi6/zotero-folder-collapse-all.does: Adds a Collapse All and Expand All toggle to the collections pane, also under Tools. Expand All reopens exactly the folders that were open before. Leaves group libraries, saved searches and the trash alone.
xin-yi6/zotero-folder-collapse-all.pain: After a long session the collection tree fills with open sub-folders. This folds it up in one click and restores it with the next.

go00ood/zotero-hanja-readings.does: Adds Korean readings as annotations to selected text that contains Hanja in the reader.
go00ood/zotero-hanja-readings.pain: Helps Korean-language readers who meet Hanja in papers and want the reading without looking each character up.

tmarquez-mx/zotero-hook-releases.does: A Spanish-language research assistant for Zotero 10 for study, research and teaching. It converses about a text, examines arguments, compares readings and builds reading guides, saving results as notes. Connects to Groq, OpenRouter, LM Studio, Ollama or a lab server.
tmarquez-mx/zotero-hook-releases.pain: Supports informed reading and critical thinking in Spanish. Its developer calls it experimental; Groq and OpenRouter need your own API key, and there is a simulation mode that sends nothing.

shaowen-ye/zotero-inbox-tag-triage-manag.does: Sends items to an Inbox collection from the right-click menu, tracks status tags such as to-read and classified, and assigns items to project folders. A cleaner lists suspicious tags such as URLs, DOIs and duplicates for you to confirm.
shaowen-ye/zotero-inbox-tag-triage-manag.pain: Imports from many sources leave libraries unsorted and tags messy. It never auto-deletes tags and does not delete items, attachments or notes.

nicozheng/zotero-item-key-column.does: Adds an Item Key column to the items list and advanced search results, and a read-only Item Key row to the Info pane.
nicozheng/zotero-item-key-column.pain: The item key is Zotero's internal identifier, useful for scripting, API work and debugging. A fork of roderickvella/Zotero-Item-Key-Column; its README doesn't say what it changes.

raymondxu-civiltechlabs/zotero-item-type.does: Converts selected items to another type from the right-click menu: journal article, thesis, book, conference paper, proceedings, report or patent. It carries over title, date, abstract, DOI, URL, Extra and creators, and maps the publisher field.
raymondxu-civiltechlabs/zotero-item-type.pain: Zotero's item type changes can drop data when fields don't match. Its developer advises backing up first. Attachments and notes are not converted, and incompatible fields are ignored.

czh-studio/zotero-language-mark.does: Sets the Language field of items in bulk to a code you choose, and can set it automatically on newly imported items. By default it only fills empty fields, with an option to overwrite existing values.
czh-studio/zotero-language-mark.pain: Citation styles that depend on language, such as Chinese national standard styles with CSL-M, need correct language values. A fork of the plugin template.

audanstu/zotero-magic-digest-papers.does: Analyses a paper page by page with AI and shows structured cards beside the text in the PDF reader, for background, methods, results, terms and limitations. Figures can be analysed by vision models. Needs llm-for-zotero for MinerU parsing.
audanstu/zotero-magic-digest-papers.pain: Gives a quick structured read of long papers. Needs an API key for DeepSeek, Volcano Engine Ark or Qwen DashScope. Its developer has tested only Zotero 9.0.3.

waingram/zotero-metadata-scraper.does: Fetches and updates item metadata from the right-click menu by searching titles in CrossRef, DBLP, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex or arXiv. When there are several matches you pick the right one. A Semantic Scholar API key is optional.
waingram/zotero-metadata-scraper.pain: Fixes incomplete or wrong metadata without retyping it, choosing the source that suits the paper type. A maintained fork of Creling/Zotero-Metadata-Scraper that adds Zotero 9 support.

cjhonlyone/zotero-odh.does: Looks up words you select in the PDF reader across 25+ dictionary sources and creates Anki flashcards from the definitions, with audio. Needs Anki with AnkiConnect running.
cjhonlyone/zotero-odh.pain: Learning vocabulary while reading papers means switching to a dictionary and typing cards by hand. It can also show your existing Anki card content instantly and move cards between decks. A fork of 1ywan/zotero-odh.

wubanshui/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates text selected in the PDF, EPUB or web reader, plus item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ translation services. Includes a dictionary for single words and sentence-by-sentence translation.
wubanshui/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes. Reading in a second language otherwise means copying text into a separate translation site.

234pk/zotero-pdf-translate-gene-search.does: Translates text selected in the PDF, EPUB or web reader, plus titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services, and adds a UniProt protein search.
234pk/zotero-pdf-translate-gene-search.pain: Biology readers get translation and protein lookup in the same plugin. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate that adds the UniProt search.

helingfeng-hub/zotero-pdf-translate-thin.does: An unofficial build of Translate for Zotero 2.4.7 that adds a thinking-level setting (default, off, low, medium, high) for LLM translation services. Also adds a font-size slider to the selection pop-up.
helingfeng-hub/zotero-pdf-translate-thin.pain: Models such as DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi reason by default, which wastes time and tokens on a simple translation. Setting thinking to off gets the translation straight back. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate.

w1457344108-coder/zotero-pdf2zh-annotati.does: Copies Zotero annotations, comments and note links from a PDF2zh translated PDF to the English original attachment on the same item. Works with a companion Codex Skill that checks both PDFs and plans the sync.
w1457344108-coder/zotero-pdf2zh-annotati.pain: Annotations made on a machine-translated copy otherwise have to be redone on the original. Needs Windows, Zotero 9, Codex Desktop and Python 3.12 or later.

tvpoet/zotero-pdf2zh-oneclick.does: Adds a translate button to the PDF reader that starts a local PDF2zh server, translates the open paper and attaches the bilingual result. Includes settings to pick a Python environment and install missing dependencies.
tvpoet/zotero-pdf2zh-oneclick.pain: Setting up the PDF2zh backend needs terminals and separate environments. This simplifies startup and setup. A Windows preview, and a fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh.

ta-gu/zotero-plugin-hover-translation.does: Translates every sentence of a PDF with an LLM and shows the translation in a tooltip when you hover over the sentence in the reader. Translations are cached locally. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key or a local Ollama.
ta-gu/zotero-plugin-hover-translation.pain: Select-then-translate interrupts reading papers in a foreign language. Hovering keeps you in the text. Its developer says it is in early development, and the PDF text is sent to the API you configure.

ardiandideyashidiq/zotero-plugin-metacle.does: An early-stage plugin to normalise and clean metadata. It is meant to cover titles, journals, publishers and creators; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
ardiandideyashidiq/zotero-plugin-metacle.pain: Inconsistent metadata makes libraries messy to search and cite, which is presumably the problem this aims at.

danieleongari/zotero-podcast.does: Turns selected items or whole collections into an English multi-voice podcast MP3 using OpenAI. Shows a cost estimate before you submit, runs in the background, and saves the prompts and outputs beside the audio.
danieleongari/zotero-podcast.pain: Lets you listen to a pile of papers instead of reading them. Needs an OpenAI API key, and the document text is sent to OpenAI after you submit. It reads at most 10 documents per podcast.

rockcor/zotero-reference.does: Shows the reference list of the PDF you are reading in a floating panel, from the PDF itself, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv or ReadPaper. You can add references to your library and link them both ways.
rockcor/zotero-reference.pain: Checking and importing a paper's citations by hand is slow. This adds them in a click and supports Chinese references through CNKI. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-reference.

xia-yh/zotero-reference-additions-stats.does: Opens a statistics tab from the Tools menu showing how many items you added per month, as a bar chart or a daily heatmap. You can filter by collection and time range.
xia-yh/zotero-reference-additions-stats.pain: Zotero has no view of how your library grows over time. This gives monthly totals, averages and peaks for tracking reading and collecting habits.

victoralensai/zotero-rsvp.does: Adds an RSVP speed-reading panel to the PDF reader that flashes words one at a time with a highlighted focus letter, at 150 to 900 words per minute. Starts from your current page or from selected text.
victoralensai/zotero-rsvp.pain: For people who want to skim papers faster without moving their eyes. Needs a PDF with a text layer. A fork of Amogh-Joshi/zotero-rsvp.

samshott/zotero-scihub.does: Downloads PDFs from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI, from a right-click command or automatically when you add new items. For Zotero 6 and Juris-M.
samshott/zotero-scihub.pain: Researchers without journal access hit paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many places. A fork that fixes batch downloading errors.

tausackhn/zotero-scihub.does: Downloads PDFs from Sci-Hub for items with a DOI, from a right-click command or automatically when new items are added. The Sci-Hub address and auto-download can be changed in the config editor.
tausackhn/zotero-scihub.pain: Researchers without journal access hit paywalls. Note that Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many places. A fork of ethanwillis/zotero-scihub for Zotero 6.

v7qx/zotero-si-docx-to-pdf.does: Converts supplementary Word attachments to PDF when they are added to an item. It uses Microsoft Word or LibreOffice for .doc and .docx files and attaches the PDF to the same item.
v7qx/zotero-si-docx-to-pdf.pain: Word supplements can't be read or annotated in Zotero's PDF reader. Converting them automatically saves doing it by hand. Its developer says it was built with AI assistance.

jkroes/zotero-to-thymer.does: Syncs your Zotero library into Thymer as pages: items, creators, tags, collections and PDF annotations, with links back to Zotero. Needs Thymer with its MCP server set to read and write.
jkroes/zotero-to-thymer.pain: For Thymer users who want references in their notes without retyping them. Its developer calls it early alpha, tested on one personal library.

jykiki/zotero-topic-focus-sync.does: Imports PDFs from local topic folders as linked files and sorts them into topic collections and a yearly focus-topics view. Scans only new files and can run on startup or at an interval.
jykiki/zotero-topic-focus-sync.pain: For researchers who keep PDFs in folders by topic and want Zotero to follow that layout without moving files. Its developer says to back up first, as it is a personal beta.

zhangxincode/zotero_web.does: Opens a web sidebar beside Zotero so you can use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek or any other site there. Includes saved prompts you can copy and a button to copy the current PDF.
zhangxincode/zotero_web.pain: Lets you use the web version of an AI service next to your papers without any API key. It sends nothing itself, and you still log in to each site.

levitk/zotero2readwise.does: Exports your Zotero annotations and notes to Readwise. Needs a Readwise token plus your Zotero API key and library ID.
levitk/zotero2readwise.pain: For people who review highlights in Readwise and would otherwise copy them over by hand.

pmartinolli/zotflag.does: Adds tags to selected items automatically when their journal, publisher, authors, DOI or keywords match lists in CSV files that you keep. Runs from the right-click menu or with F12.
pmartinolli/zotflag.pain: Tagging a large library by hand is slow and inconsistent. A CSV list lets you tag whole journals, publishers or authors in one pass. Matching is strict, so you list each variant.

martindisley/zotpdf2md.does: Converts selected PDF or image attachments to Markdown files using Mistral OCR. Offers page selection, batch progress and filename templates that can use the Better BibTeX citation key. Needs a Mistral API key.
martindisley/zotpdf2md.pain: Gets text out of scanned or complex PDFs as Markdown for notes or LLM use. Results are cached so repeat runs don't call the API again.

brycewg/zotseek-online.does: Semantic search for your library: find papers by meaning, find similar documents, and search from selected PDF text. Embeddings come from an online provider you set up with your own API key. Includes an MCP server for AI agents.
