brycewg/zotseek-online.pain: Keyword search misses papers that use different wording. A fork of introfini/ZotSeek that sends text to an online embedding provider rather than computing it locally.

booknary/ai-related-papers.does: Finds related papers in your library, scored from titles, abstracts, authors and tags, with optional AI re-ranking. You choose which to link, view the links as a network, and can generate AI keyword tags. AI features need an API key.
booknary/ai-related-papers.pain: Zotero's related-items links are made by hand. This suggests candidates you confirm, and it only searches your own library.

janetckm/bionic-for-zotero-color.does: Bionic reading in the Zotero reader, bolding the start of each word, with optional colours on the bold parts. Offers preset palettes and up to three custom colours.
janetckm/bionic-for-zotero-color.pain: A fork of windingwind/bionic-for-zotero that adds colour options to the bionic text.

l-konrad/calibre-highlights-to-zotero.does: Fetches metadata for e-books uploaded by a companion Python script that copies Calibre highlights into Zotero. The script needs your Zotero API key, library ID and Calibre database.
l-konrad/calibre-highlights-to-zotero.pain: E-reader annotations can't be imported into Zotero directly. This is a rough workaround, shown with a Kobo example.

bakasayaka/douban-to-zotero.does: Imports books from a Douban wish list into Zotero by user ID, with a review step for incomplete and duplicate records. Optional OpenAI-compatible metadata cleaning runs through a separate script.
bakasayaka/douban-to-zotero.pain: Entering Chinese book records by hand is slow. Mainly for Chinese-language readers who track books on Douban. Targets Zotero 9.

evanma1/llm-for-zotero.does: A research assistant in the reader: ask about the open PDF, selected text or figures, get cited answers, and save notes to Zotero or Markdown folders. An Agent Mode works across your library. Needs an API key, local model, or a Codex or Claude Code setup.
evanma1/llm-for-zotero.pain: Lets you question papers without leaving Zotero. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

phs008/llm_papaerassistance_for_zotero8.does: Analyses selected papers and chats about them in a sidebar using Ollama or OpenAI, based on extracted PDF text, and saves the answers as child notes.
phs008/llm_papaerassistance_for_zotero8.pain: Gives people running a local Ollama server a way to use an LLM on their papers. The OpenAI option needs an API key.

wang-wen-hui/notebook-zotero-backlink.does: Links Gemini Notebook (NotebookLM) with Zotero through a Chrome extension. It saves selected text or Studio output as Zotero notes and finds cited passages in the matching PDF with a highlight. Talks to Zotero locally.
wang-wen-hui/notebook-zotero-backlink.pain: Keeps Notebook answers and their sources in your library. You select the Zotero item yourself, and the extension may break when the Notebook page changes.

chengcheng-cx/obsidian-zotero-vault-brid.does: The Zotero half of a bridge to Obsidian. It links PDFs kept in your vault, runs Zotero's metadata recognition, stores citation keys and serves citation search to the Obsidian plugin. Both apps must run on one computer.
chengcheng-cx/obsidian-zotero-vault-brid.pain: Keeps PDFs in the vault while Zotero holds the metadata. Obsidian then creates literature notes and citation links. Needs Zotero 10.

gw19ddd/paperflow.does: Right-click translation of PDFs with the PaperFlow desktop app, which then attaches the translated PDF to the item as a linked file next to the original. Needs the PaperFlow app.
gw19ddd/paperflow.pain: Gives a translated paper that keeps the original layout without setting up Python. The app is based on PDFMathTranslate and works with several AI services.

noaul/paperpulse.does: Sends selected Zotero items to a PaperPulse server, which scores them with AI, and writes the scores as tags plus an analysis note. PaperPulse tracks journal RSS feeds, matches keywords and sends email digests.
noaul/paperpulse.pain: For researchers who screen many new papers for relevance. You must run the PaperPulse backend and set up an AI API. The Zotero part is a prototype.

emi-dm/readed-zotero.does: Adds a Read column with a checkbox to the item list. Clicking it marks an item as read or unread by adding or removing a _read tag.
emi-dm/readed-zotero.pain: Zotero has no read status, and tags are slow to manage by hand. Because it uses a tag, the status syncs with your library.

cxing-fdu/reader-ai.does: An AI chat section in the item pane and reader side pane that uses the item's metadata, notes, annotations and indexed PDF text. Includes a Quote in chat button and saving answers as notes. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
cxing-fdu/reader-ai.pain: Lets you ask about the paper you are reading without leaving Zotero. A Context panel shows what text was sent.

rebelpotato/readmate.does: Adds a reader toolbar button that opens PowerShell in the paper's folder and starts an AI agent command you choose, by default pi. Windows only.
rebelpotato/readmate.pain: For people who read papers with a coding agent in the terminal. The agent starts next to the paper's cached full text.

ils-research/seekchat-zotero.does: Chat with a PDF, web page snapshot, EPUB or text file, with answers that cite pages and link to them. Uses a language model you run yourself, Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server. Includes a chat that can act on your library.
ils-research/seekchat-zotero.pain: Lets you question papers and books without sending them to a cloud service, unless you allow that server. Works with the ZotSeek and SeekBook indexes.

scarnecchia/semblero.does: Shares selected items to Semble, a social reading platform on the AT Protocol, as cards linked to the URL or DOI. Skips items already shared. Needs a Bluesky handle and app password.
scarnecchia/semblero.pain: Posting references to Semble by hand means copying titles and links. Shared items are marked in the Extra field.

sprice/stratum-zotero.does: Serves image and area annotation pictures through Zotero's local API for the Stratum plugin in Obsidian. Needs Zotero's setting for other applications to communicate with it.
sprice/stratum-zotero.pain: For Obsidian users who want Zotero image annotations to appear in their notes.

eiskola/translook.does: Shows a panel beside text you select in the PDF or EPUB reader: a dictionary entry for a word, or a translation for a sentence, from any OpenAI-compatible LLM. Optional Youdao, Baidu or Google channels.
eiskola/translook.pain: Lookups stay beside the text and can be added as an annotation comment. Needs an API key for cloud models, or a local Ollama.

sleep-nobad/your_zotero.does: A floating AI chat for the paper you are reading. It builds a full-text index and answers from that paper, with background filling, translation, and Markdown notes. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API, and Ollama can supply embeddings.
sleep-nobad/your_zotero.pain: Keeps answers grounded in the current paper instead of drifting. It covers one paper at a time, not your whole library.

giaogiaogiaoluan/zhiyi-pdf.does: Translates PDFs from the right-click menu into translation-only or bilingual PDFs, and trims white margins. Handles paragraphs that run across pages and glossaries. Needs a local zotero-pdf2zh server and engine.
giaogiaogiaoluan/zhiyi-pdf.pain: A PDF2zh-based translator that uses either free services or your own DeepSeek or OpenAI-compatible API. Tested only on macOS with Zotero 10.

lwmlw004/zotero-attachment-hub.does: Processes a local attachment queue from a Tools submenu. You can attach supplementary files to the selected item, fill missing PDFs, and list the DOIs of items that lack a PDF.
lwmlw004/zotero-attachment-hub.pain: Helps fill gaps in a library when you already have the files locally. Nothing runs unless you pick a menu command.

williamjkyuan/zotero-batch-add-info.does: Adds text to a chosen field of many selected items at once, at the start or end, keeping the existing content. Shows a preview first, and the whole batch is one undo step.
williamjkyuan/zotero-batch-add-info.pain: Adding the same note, tag-like text or label to a field for many items means editing each one. Mainly for Chinese-language users, on Zotero 10.

jasumin/zotero-bbt-pdf-mirror.does: Mirrors the PDFs of one collection into a folder tree beside a Better BibTeX export, with a manifest file and consistency check. Needs Better BibTeX. Windows paths only, pre-release.
jasumin/zotero-bbt-pdf-mirror.pain: Keeps a .bib file and its PDFs together for LaTeX or other tools. Its developer says to test on a spare profile.

petrbouchal/zotero-biblio-html.does: Exports selected items or a collection as one HTML bibliography page with online and PDF links, and copies the attachments into a folder next to it. Uses your Quick Copy citation style.
petrbouchal/zotero-biblio-html.pain: Shares a bibliography with files with a colleague without setting up Zotero sharing. Simpler than Zotsite.

rickwashon/zotero-citation-map.does: Builds an interactive citation map of your library, a collection or chosen papers, shows citation counts as columns, and finds missing papers to add. Exports the graph as PNG, CSV or JSON.
rickwashon/zotero-citation-map.pain: Exploring connections otherwise needs tools such as ResearchRabbit. This fork of AlessMor/zotero-citation-map adds NASA ADS as a data source for astronomy, which needs an ADS token.

shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-quick-jumpe.does: A keyboard popup, opened with Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+J, to search collections by name or path and jump to one. Remembers recent and favourite collections.
shaowen-ye/zotero-collection-quick-jumpe.pain: Big libraries have deep collection trees that are slow to click through. Its developer has stopped maintaining it and moved the features elsewhere.

ericjin2002/zotero-convert-to-arxiv.does: Converts selected items to verified arXiv preprints in place, keeping attachments, notes, tags and collections. Finds the arXiv ID in fields and indexed PDF text, or searches arXiv by title. Adds an arXiv ID column.
ericjin2002/zotero-convert-to-arxiv.pain: Replaces an old or wrong record with arXiv metadata without making duplicates. It writes directly to the database, so back up first.

juniorxxue/zotero-copypath.does: Adds an item list button that copies the item's local PDF as a Markdown link titled with the paper. Shows a notice if there is no PDF or more than one.
juniorxxue/zotero-copypath.pain: Lets you link papers from Markdown notes without finding the file path by hand.

anurag-dalal/zotero_custom_columns.does: Adds your own item list columns that you edit in place: checkboxes, ratings, links, text and coloured options. Includes templates, per-collection columns, bulk editing and CSV export.
anurag-dalal/zotero_custom_columns.pain: Zotero has no columns for your own tracking, such as reading status or screening decisions. Values are stored in local files that Zotero sync doesn't carry.

mzhyui/zotero-excalidraw.does: Opens an Excalidraw whiteboard canvas from the right-click menu of an item. A side panel lists your notes, and a category tree lets you drop entries, notes and comments onto the canvas. Exports text, PNG and SVG.
mzhyui/zotero-excalidraw.pain: Zotero has no place to sketch concept maps beside your references. A fork of 018/zotero-excalidraw; its README doesn't say what it changes.

zhi-11/zotero-fulltext-translate.does: Turns a PDF into a readable HTML page and translates it, adding the result back to the item as an attachment. Parsing uses MinerU, translation uses Translate for Zotero, and the page can be Chinese only or bilingual.
zhi-11/zotero-fulltext-translate.pain: Reading a whole paper in another language usually means copying text out piece by piece. This produces one translated page that keeps images and figures. Its developer warns that output may contain errors and should be checked.

wang-wen-hui/zotero-gemini-notebook.does: Sends Zotero source files to Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM). A Tools menu dialog lets you browse collections and stage items, and a companion Chrome extension uploads them. Needs Google Chrome.
wang-wen-hui/zotero-gemini-notebook.pain: Zotero stores PDFs in folders with opaque names, so gathering a collection to upload by hand is tedious. A fork of peterdresslar/zotero-gemini-notebook; its README doesn't say what it changes.

pad-mac/zotero-group-linked-files.does: Keeps a group library's PDFs in a shared folder or on a WebDAV server instead of Zotero Storage, while you still open and annotate them in Zotero's reader. New files are renamed by a scheme and copied across.
pad-mac/zotero-group-linked-files.pain: Zotero doesn't allow linked files in group libraries, and group file sync uses the owner's storage quota. This lets a team share PDFs through Seafile or WebDAV while items and annotations sync normally.

spullk/zotero-gruvbox-soft.does: A muted, warm Gruvbox-style dark theme for Zotero 7 and later. It applies only when Appearance is set to Dark, so Light mode stays unchanged.
spullk/zotero-gruvbox-soft.pain: For people who use Gruvbox colours in their editor and terminal and want Zotero's dark mode to match.

haraldsu/zotero-hide-scrollbar.does: Hides the horizontal and vertical scrollbars in the Zotero PDF reader, with a Hide PDF Scrollbars toggle in the Tools menu. E-books and web snapshots keep their scrollbars.
haraldsu/zotero-hide-scrollbar.pain: Scrollbars add clutter to a distraction-free reading view. It is meant to sit alongside the Zotero Focused Mode plugin, which doesn't hide them. Its developer tested it on Zotero 9.0.3.

anfang886/zotero-info-compact.does: Adds a toggle to the item pane's Info header that shows only fields with content or every field. The choice is remembered, and the same switch is in the View menu.
anfang886/zotero-info-compact.pain: Field-heavy item types such as Journal Article, Case and Statute fill the Info section with empty rows. This hides them until you need to fill one in. Its developer tested it on Zotero 9.

sorinhostiuc/zotero-instant-cite.does: Searches your library and scholarly sources for a paper and cites it in Word or LibreOffice. You can search by title, author, keyword, DOI or PMID, and it adds the item to Zotero if it isn't there.
sorinhostiuc/zotero-instant-cite.pain: Citing a paper you don't yet own means leaving the document to search, import and cite in separate steps. This does it in one pass, and the bibliography stays linked to Zotero. Needs Zotero's word-processor plugin.

fusman60/zotero-institutional-pdf-bridge.does: Adds an institutional proxy resolver to Zotero's Find Available PDF command, using your university's WebVPN or SSO login. After you sign in, a hidden browser reuses the session. It can optionally fetch PDFs for new items.
fusman60/zotero-institutional-pdf-bridge.pain: Off-campus users hit paywalls even when their institution subscribes. Many Chinese university gateways aren't supported by stock Zotero. A fork of as-zdq/zotero-institutional-pdf-bridge; its README doesn't say what it changes.

myshevchuk/zotero-jcode.does: Adds a jcode line to the Extra field of selected items, looked up from a tab-separated table of journal titles and abbreviations. Run it from the right-click menu or with Ctrl+Alt+J. You can supply your own table.
myshevchuk/zotero-jcode.pain: Tagging many items with journal codes by hand, or with a pasted script that stops at the first unknown journal, is slow. Unmatched items are skipped, and existing Extra lines are kept.

practiceearnestly/zotero-literature-flow.does: Runs a three-level AI reading workflow on your papers. New PDFs enter level one, and a rating of 2 to 5 in the Extra field triggers deeper levels. It needs OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and MinerU if you want it for parsing.
practiceearnestly/zotero-literature-flow.pain: For people who triage many papers and want the amount of AI reading to follow their own rating. It only adds AI:L1, AI:L2 and AI:L3 tags and never creates topic tags from model output.

jasperyep/zotero-llm-selection-translate.does: Translates text you select in the Zotero reader through an OpenAI-compatible API, with a Summary mode that explains hard passages. Results are cached locally, and a shortcut key toggles the Highlight tool. Needs an API key.
jasperyep/zotero-llm-selection-translate.pain: Reading papers in a second language means switching to a translation site. This puts a translation or plain-text explanation in a popup next to the passage, using the model you choose.

y-0768/zotero-manuscript-grid.does: Inserts Chinese manuscript-paper text boxes into the PDF reader, with 25 characters per row and one character per cell. Rows snap as you resize, and existing text annotations can be converted. Grid lines show only inside Zotero.
y-0768/zotero-manuscript-grid.pain: For writing Chinese in the style of an exam answer sheet directly on a PDF. The boxes are native Zotero text annotations, so they sync and appear in the annotation list.

lightwindw/zotero-normalize.does: Cleans up item metadata in bulk from the right-click menu. It splits, merges or swaps author names, separates authors stored on one line, converts dates to YYYY-MM-DD, sets the language and clears Extra.
lightwindw/zotero-normalize.pain: Imported records often have swapped names, all authors on one line or inconsistent dates. It handles cases the Linter plugin leaves behind. A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template.

fedefrc/zotero-paper-viewer.does: A dark, keyboard-driven gallery of the papers in your current collection or search, with first-page thumbnails and a page-image PDF preview inside the gallery. You can also open the PDF in Zotero's reader in the background.
fedefrc/zotero-paper-viewer.pain: Zotero's list view is poor for skimming many papers visually. The preview isn't a full reader: it has no text selection, search, annotations or zoom yet. Its developer targets Zotero 9.

zhoas/zotero-paperlist-csv.does: Keeps a PaperList CSV file in each collection, with title, journal, URL and year, plus blank columns for research content and innovations. It appends rows as papers are added and opens the file in Excel.
zhoas/zotero-paperlist-csv.pain: Researchers who keep a reading spreadsheet otherwise retype every paper. Your notes in the CSV are never overwritten, and the file syncs with the collection as a Zotero attachment. Aimed at Chinese-speaking researchers.

git-deprecated/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates selected text in the PDF reader, plus item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services. It has a dictionary for single words, a standalone translation window and sentence-by-sentence mode.
git-deprecated/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading papers in a second language means constant copy-paste into a translation site. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes.

footgod368/zotero-pdf-translate-duck.does: Translates selected text in the PDF, EPUB or web reader, plus item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, using 20+ services. It has a dictionary for single words and a window to compare engines.
footgod368/zotero-pdf-translate-duck.pain: Reading papers in a second language means constant copy-paste into a translation site. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes.

tano2003/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates PDFs into Chinese from Zotero using PDF2zh and PDF2zh_next, keeping the original layout. It talks to a Python server you install and run locally, set up with uv or conda.
tano2003/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: Papers in English are hard to read in full, and plain text translation loses figures and formulas. A fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh; its README doesn't say what it changes.

liuyujie0136/zotero-reference.does: Shows the references of the paper you are reading in the sidebar, with pop-ups drawn from the PDF, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and ReadPaper. You can add a reference to your library and link it both ways.
liuyujie0136/zotero-reference.pain: Checking or collecting a paper's references normally means copying titles into a search. A Zotero 6 fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-reference that makes the pop-up text clearer and keeps it on screen longer. Its author says it is for self use only.

suri-codes/zotero-remarkable-plugin.does: Syncs PDFs and annotations both ways with a reMarkable tablet through the reMarkable cloud. Zotero highlights go onto the pages, and highlights, handwriting and typed text come back as annotations or notes.
suri-codes/zotero-remarkable-plugin.pain: Reading and marking up papers on an e-ink tablet normally means moving files and annotations by hand. This keeps both sides current without overwriting what you wrote on either.

yu5-novaiuk/zotero-research-framework.does: A visual canvas for building research frameworks of constructs and relationships. You attach Zotero papers or selected reader passages as supporting or contradicting evidence, and evidence opens back in Zotero.
yu5-novaiuk/zotero-research-framework.pain: Planning a theoretical model with its supporting literature usually means a drawing tool separate from your library. This keeps the evidence linked to each variable and hypothesis. Targets Zotero 9, with a Chinese interface.

18126295767-cell/zotero-review-reminder.does: Schedules review reminders and stores Completed, Corrected, End and Next Review dates in each item's Extra field. A Tools menu sets dates for selected items and lists items that are due.
18126295767-cell/zotero-review-reminder.pain: For people who revisit papers or study material on a schedule and want the review dates kept inside Zotero. It has a Chinese interface.

luorory/zotero-review-tab.does: A Review tab that builds a daily queue from your notes and PDF annotations using the FSRS spaced-repetition scheduler. You answer Continue or Did not remember, and an arbitrary-review mode logs practice.
luorory/zotero-review-tab.pain: Notes and highlights are rarely read again. This brings them back at spaced intervals and keeps its state in one note. Its developer advises backing up your library before testing.

nbtkmy/zotero-rvk-classifier.does: Predicts RVK (Regensburger Verbundklassifikation) notations for a book from the right-click menu. It looks up the ISBN in German library catalogues, then an LLM picks the top three, written to Extra. Works with Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI or OpenRouter.
nbtkmy/zotero-rvk-classifier.pain: Classifying books for a German-language library is slow to do by hand. It suggests notations from catalogue data and needs either a local model or a cloud API key.

frimpsjoek/zotero-second-brain.does: Markdown notes on each paper inside Zotero, with pasted images, [@citekey] links to other papers and highlights added as quotes. It also finds similar papers by meaning on your computer and fetches free PDFs.
frimpsjoek/zotero-second-brain.pain: Zotero's notes are weak for linked, long-form paper writing. This keeps notes as plain Markdown files and can sync them with an Obsidian vault if you run its separate server. Marked removed in the directory.

xiaoyang0103/zotero-split-view-reader-z1.does: Shows the same PDF or two different PDFs side by side in one reader tab. Each pane scrolls on its own, or you can set a master view so the other follows. A Zotero 10 build of Fuling Lin's Split-View Reader.
xiaoyang0103/zotero-split-view-reader-z1.pain: Comparing two papers, or reading a paper beside its appendix, otherwise needs separate windows. Its developer notes an accessibility setting that may reduce stuttering on Windows, and tested only on Windows.

pfriedric/zotero-symlinks.does: Creates mirror collections that appear under several parent collections and share the same items. Adding an item to any of them adds it to all, and a menu action removes items from every linked copy.
pfriedric/zotero-symlinks.pain: Zotero collections form a strict tree, so one set of papers can't sit in two places. Its developer calls it highly experimental and says to back up your library first.

xuanhuliming/zotero-terminal.does: Adds a Terminal button to Zotero 9 that opens a persistent shell in a panel on the right. It writes the current PDF's metadata and full text into a context file that Claude or Codex can read.
xuanhuliming/zotero-terminal.pain: For people who use command-line AI tools on papers and want a shell inside Zotero. On Windows it uses plain pipes rather than a true terminal, with a Chinese interface.

jimmyjuan/zotero-vim-half-scroll.does: Adds Vim-style half-page scrolling to the Zotero reader: Cmd-D scrolls down and Cmd-U scrolls up. It works in reader tabs and separate reader windows, including split views.
jimmyjuan/zotero-vim-half-scroll.pain: Arrow keys and page-down move too little or too much when reading a long PDF. Its developer tested mainly the macOS shortcuts, and it needs Zotero 8 or later.

yanfeifan723/zotero-zotskim.does: Has an LLM read a paper's full text and write a structured Skim note with an overview, section-by-section summary and key takeaways. It can also suggest or create the collection to file the item in. Needs your own API key.
yanfeifan723/zotero-zotskim.pain: Triaging many papers by reading each one is slow. It works with OpenAI-compatible services, Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini, and with local models. Its developer calls it beta, and its interface is in Chinese.

jeanwsr/zotmeta.does: Updates the metadata of existing items, looking up articles by DOI and books by ISBN.
jeanwsr/zotmeta.pain: Records saved with missing or poor metadata can be refreshed without re-importing them. A fork of RoadToDream/ZotMeta; its README doesn't say what it changes.

arrancurran/zotrim.does: Hides metadata fields that have no value in an item's Info section. Existing values stay editable, and disabling the add-on restores Zotero's normal display. Supports Zotero 7 to 10.
arrancurran/zotrim.pain: The Info pane lists every field for the item type, so most of it is blank for many items. This leaves only the fields you have filled.

cloneorcopy/zsearch.does: A search window inside Zotero covering Scopus, PubMed, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, Springer, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar. It merges results, imports in one click and exports in batches. Some sources need API keys.
cloneorcopy/zsearch.pain: Searching several databases means jumping between sites before importing. It adds journal rank badges from EasyScholar, a PDF download chain that includes Sci-Hub (which distributes papers without permission), and a Chinese interface.

aknahin/annosync.does: Creates one linked Zotero note per PDF annotation and updates it when the annotation changes. Notes use a template with native Zotero citations, copy the annotation's tags and can be limited to chosen highlight colours.
aknahin/annosync.pain: Turning highlights into citable notes is manual copying. A fork of koenigderorangen/AnnoSync; its README doesn't say what it changes. Needs Zotero 8, and synced notes are overwritten on the next sync.

24kmengxin/atr-zotero-workbench.does: Projects research topics from an external ATR pipeline into Zotero as collections, notes and item pane sections, so you can read and annotate evidence natively. It exports CSL-JSON and reading prompts.
24kmengxin/atr-zotero-workbench.pain: For researchers who use the separate ATR research tool and want to check its evidence inside Zotero. It needs ATR run output, and its documentation is in Chinese.

yejiangnan1029/attachment-recover.does: Records recovery details for each PDF in a note under its parent item. On another device it finds missing PDFs, downloads them again, checks the SHA-256 hash and re-attaches them to the item. It currently handles arXiv sources first.
yejiangnan1029/attachment-recover.pain: Where network limits stop PDFs uploading to WebDAV or Zotero Storage, other devices see items without files. This restores the PDFs without creating duplicate items. Its interface is in Chinese.

cyandyue/babeldoc_zotero_translate.does: Translates PDFs with BabelDOC through Immersive Translate (沉浸式翻译), or locally with your own OpenAI or DeepSeek key. Needs an Immersive Translate Pro key by default.
cyandyue/babeldoc_zotero_translate.pain: Translating a whole paper while keeping its layout is hard in stock Zotero. It is a modified version of zotero-immersivetranslate that adds local BabelDOC translation.

hyooeewee/codex-bilingual-reader-for-zot.does: Turns a PDF into a bilingual English and Chinese PDF that keeps the layout, figures and formulas, and imports it as a child attachment. It uses the local Codex CLI or an OpenAI-compatible API such as DeepSeek.
hyooeewee/codex-bilingual-reader-for-zot.pain: Reading papers in a second language is slow with plain text translation. Setup downloads about 600 MB of PDFMathTranslate-next, currently on Windows. A fork of Mengqi97/codex-bilingual-reader-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

hbpeking-tks/good-note-for-zotero.does: A Markdown note workspace on the right of the Zotero 9 window, with a collection tree, visual and source editing, and tabs. It also has literature summary tables, mind maps and knowledge graphs, exporting to Markdown, PDF, CSV, PNG and SVG.
hbpeking-tks/good-note-for-zotero.pain: Zotero's notes are plain, and organising reading notes across a library needs a separate app. This keeps them as native Zotero notes. It has no AI features, and its interface is in Chinese.

jaaaahan/kernai.does: A chat sidebar for asking questions about your papers. Type @ to add items from the current collection as context, and past conversations are kept. Needs an API key for a model provider such as OpenAI, or a local model.
jaaaahan/kernai.pain: Asking questions about papers normally means pasting text into a separate chat tool. It can also expose Zotero to other AI clients through a local API and MCP server.

rhmteo/llm-for-zotero-linuxmint.does: An AI assistant in the Zotero reader that answers questions about the open PDF, selected text and figures, with citations back to the source. An Agent Mode works across your library. It supports API providers, local models and Claude Code.
rhmteo/llm-for-zotero-linuxmint.pain: Using an LLM on papers otherwise means copying text out of Zotero. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that, according to its description, fixes platform-related issues.

ronghaihe/marginalia.does: A sidebar AI chat that uses the paper's full text as context, with one-click translation of selected text and quoted passages for focused questions. You can link a Zotero collection so the AI can search it. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
ronghaihe/marginalia.pain: Reading papers with an AI normally means pasting text into a separate chat. A fork of sheny-bio/marginalia that adds GitHub Copilot and Zotero 9 support. Its documentation is in Chinese.

pmmendoza/notero.does: Syncs items from chosen Zotero collections into a Notion database, one page per item, with a notion tag and a link attachment back. Notes sync as page content, and PDF annotations can be added through a Zotero note.
pmmendoza/notero.pain: People who write and plan in Notion otherwise retype references. A fork of dvanoni/notero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

wqytommy666/paper-library-zotero.does: Uploads items, with their metadata and PDFs, from Zotero to the Paper Library collaboration platform. Right-click to upload, or turn on automatic sync for new items. Large PDFs go up in chunks. Needs a personal access token from Paper Library.
wqytommy666/paper-library-zotero.pain: Moving papers from Zotero into a shared reading and discussion platform is otherwise manual. It only reads your library and never writes back or deletes anything. Its documentation is in Chinese.

sstraume97/pdf-ai-bookmarks.does: Generates a nested table of contents for a PDF using Google Gemini and writes the bookmarks into the file. Run it from the Tools menu. Large files are split and merged. Needs a Gemini API key.
sstraume97/pdf-ai-bookmarks.pain: Many PDFs have no outline, which makes long books and reports hard to navigate. Highlights and notes are left alone. A fork of edwintuan/pdf-ai-bookmarks; its README doesn't say what it changes.

orbital188/pubpeer_zotero_plugin.does: Shows whether the references in your library have comments on PubPeer.
orbital188/pubpeer_zotero_plugin.pain: Readers can see post-publication discussion of a paper without searching PubPeer by hand. A fork of PubPeerFoundation/pubpeer_zotero_plugin; its README doesn't say what it changes.

booknary/zaichat.does: A chat assistant for your local library: find papers from vague descriptions, ask questions with cited passages and compare abstracts. It can add notes, tags and relations after you approve. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
booknary/zaichat.pain: Finding a half-remembered paper or checking it against a question is slow in a big library. It reads only selected passages, not the whole library. Its optional local semantic search is built for Windows x64.

jingyangyuan/zotero-agent-mcp.does: Lets local AI agents such as Claude Code or Cursor work with your library. A token-protected HTTP API and an MCP bridge let them search, read full text and annotations, and create or edit items, notes and tags.
jingyangyuan/zotero-agent-mcp.pain: Letting a coding agent work with your library normally means going through the slower web API. Scopes, a library allowlist and rate limits can be tightened, but all features are on by default.

cocmin/zotero-anki-bridge.does: Adds a button to the PDF reader that saves the selected word or phrase, with the current Translate for Zotero result, as an Anki note. It checks the deck and fields, and warns about duplicates.
cocmin/zotero-anki-bridge.pain: Collecting vocabulary while reading papers means copying words into Anki by hand. Needs Translate for Zotero, plus Anki open with AnkiConnect, and its interface is in Chinese.

inactinique/zotero-archive-plugin.does: Groups your library's references into themes and shows how those themes follow one another over the years, using the date each reference was added. Needs a library of at least 60 references.
inactinique/zotero-archive-plugin.pain: A library records what caught your attention over time, but Zotero gives no view of how your interests shifted. Analysis runs locally with Ollama or a model inside Zotero, so library data stays on your machine.

aspray166/zotero-archiver.does: Archives selected papers into a separate named archive library that keeps tags, notes, attachments and collections, with optional scheduled backups. Switch between libraries or restore papers to the main one. Mainly for Chinese-language users.
aspray166/zotero-archiver.pain: Moving old papers out of a working library by export and import resets dates and breaks Word citations. This copies the data directory instead, so archived items stay complete and can be deleted from the main library to free space.

heniancheng/zotero-author-browser.does: Lists every author in your library by number of items and lets you show all items for one author from the creator context menu or by double-clicking a row. An early-development fork; author aliases are still planned.
heniancheng/zotero-author-browser.pain: Zotero has no way to see who you cite most or to jump to everything by one author. A fork of StevenGLee/zotero-author-browser; its README doesn't say what it changes.

tianlanvera/zotero-autonote.does: Creates an AI reading note as a child note when a new item has a readable PDF, retrying while the PDF downloads or indexes. You can also generate notes by hand. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint and key.
tianlanvera/zotero-autonote.pain: Writing a summary note for every new paper is slow. This drafts one automatically from the PDF text, with your own prompt, output language and model. Metadata, abstract and attachment text are sent to the endpoint you configure.

jiezhuzzz/zotero-better-venues.does: Adds a Venue column to the item list that shows each publication venue as a short name such as NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR or arXiv. Includes about 50 CCF-A venues and accepts your own JSON overrides.
jiezhuzzz/zotero-better-venues.pain: Full conference and journal titles are long and inconsistent, which makes the item list hard to scan. A fork of zotero-better-authors; the project is marked as removed.

xiaoducomrade/zotero-browser-tabs.does: Opens web pages in tabs inside the Zotero window, next to PDF reader tabs. Has back, forward, refresh, home and an address bar that takes URLs, domains or search terms.
xiaoducomrade/zotero-browser-tabs.pain: Looking something up while reading means switching to a separate browser. This keeps pages next to your papers. Its developer says it is a page viewer only, and some sign-in sites may refuse it. Targets Zotero 9.

ok-feng-hash/zotero-card-view.does: Turns the item list into a sortable grid of literature cards showing title, date, journal, impact factor, ratings and tags, with expandable details. Reads metrics from Zotero Style when it is installed.
ok-feng-hash/zotero-card-view.pain: Zotero's plain list shows little at a glance. Cards give a browsable overview while keeping native search, collections and the item pane. Its developer calls it a public beta and advises backing up first. Targets Zotero 9.

my-sec/zotero-ccf-info.does: Looks up the CCF rating, the conference or journal and the citation count for selected papers from a right-click menu. Missing venues can be added in the source file.
my-sec/zotero-ccf-info.pain: Computer science researchers often need the CCF rank of a venue when choosing or citing papers. A fork of TimeTrapzz/zotero-ccf-info; its README doesn't say what it changes.

janbaykara/zotero-citation-map.does: Builds an interactive citation network graph for a library, collection or chosen papers, and adds citation and reference counts as columns. Pulls data from Crossref, Semantic Scholar, OpenCitations, INSPIRE-HEP and OpenAlex.
janbaykara/zotero-citation-map.pain: Exploring how papers cite each other usually means switching to tools like ResearchRabbit or Litmaps. This keeps the map in Zotero, with export to PNG, CSV or JSON. OpenAlex needs an API key. A fork of AlessMor/zotero-citation-map.

ahzs645/zotero-cite-gen.does: Imports AI-generated citations from JSON, checks them against their DOIs and maps the reasoning behind each into Zotero notes.
ahzs645/zotero-cite-gen.pain: AI tools often invent references. This lets you check each generated citation before it enters your library. Little is documented beyond the manifest description.

lfd-byte/zotero-citetally.does: Fetches citation counts from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar and shows them as sortable columns, also saving them in the Extra field. Works on selected items, collections or whole libraries, and can fetch automatically for new items.
lfd-byte/zotero-citetally.pain: Zotero has no citation counts of its own, and Google Scholar blocks scraping. This uses open scholarly APIs instead. An OpenAlex API key is strongly advised; a Semantic Scholar key is optional.

upcreat/zotero-code-link.does: Adds a Code section to the item pane for repository links, and a Code column in the item list. Recognises GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Codeberg, Hugging Face and SourceForge.
upcreat/zotero-code-link.pain: Code links saved as attachments mix in with PDFs. This keeps them separate, so you can see at a glance which papers have code.

hugogene/zotero-column-optimization.does: Adds an Abstract column to the item list and trims the item-type menus in the item pane, new-item menu and advanced search to the types in your library.
hugogene/zotero-column-optimization.pain: Zotero lists dozens of item types you never use, which clutters menus, and offers no abstract column. This shortens the lists and lets you scan abstracts in the list.

kirinhcl/zotero-copilot.does: An AI assistant with Explain, Summarize, Translate and Take Note actions on selected PDF text, plus a sidebar chat per paper with slash commands. Works with OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
kirinhcl/zotero-copilot.pain: Asking an AI about a paper otherwise means copying text out of Zotero. Needs an API key or a ChatGPT or Claude sign-in. Its developer says only OpenAI sign-in has been tested.

johnmuin/zotero-export-collection-tsv.does: Exports a collection, or a collection with its subcollections, to a TSV file from the collection right-click menu. Columns include authors, DOI, abstract, tags, notes and impact factors saved by the Green Frog plugin.
johnmuin/zotero-export-collection-tsv.pain: Zotero's built-in exports don't give a flat table of fields and journal metrics. A fork of windingwind/zotero-plugin-template; the impact-factor columns only fill if Green Frog has already collected them.

williamjasmine211-netizen/zotero-figure-.does: Click a figure, table or equation number in the PDF reader and a small pinned window shows the matching content from the same PDF. Handles Chinese and English labels such as Figure 3.4 or Fig. S3b.
williamjasmine211-netizen/zotero-figure-.pain: Reading means scrolling back and forth between a reference to Figure 3 and the figure itself. This keeps your place while showing it. Scanned PDFs need OCR first. Targets Zotero 9.

nrb171/zotero-library-set-ops.does: Changes how several selected libraries, collections or saved searches are combined: intersection, deduplicated union, difference or exclusive items. A side-pane box switches modes. Needs Zotero 10.
nrb171/zotero-library-set-ops.pain: Zotero 10 shows the union of several selected rows, with no way to ask what two collections share or how they differ. Papers are matched by DOI, ISBN or normalised title and year.

raymonsc/zotero-local-backup.does: Backs up your library, PDFs, notes and annotations to a folder you choose, with a daily scheduled task, checksum checks and a restore helper for a new computer. Needs Windows, Python 3.10 or later and Zotero 9.
raymonsc/zotero-local-backup.pain: Zotero sync doesn't give you an offline copy of your files and database. This keeps one verified mirror on your own drive. Backups are unencrypted, and it is not a history of versions.

huanongfish/zotero-normalize-date.does: Rewrites messy date fields into one ISO format from the item right-click menu, with a preview of every change before anything is saved. Choose to keep precision, pad to a full date or keep the year only.
huanongfish/zotero-normalize-date.pain: Imported items carry dates like 04/2022 or April 1, 2017, which sort and cite inconsistently. Dates that can't be parsed are left alone and listed in the preview.

urtzienriquez/zotero.nvim.does: A Zotero-side companion for the zotero.nvim Neovim plugin. It adds an update endpoint to Zotero's connector API so Neovim can edit item metadata, add items and attach files; browsing and searching need no companion.
urtzienriquez/zotero.nvim.pain: People who write in Neovim can browse and manage their Zotero library from the editor. Needs Neovim, the sqlite3 command-line tool and Zotero's option to allow other applications to communicate with it.

guoduan3727-alt/zotero-obsidian-scholar-.does: Saves vocabulary from PDF text selections into Obsidian dictionary notes. A floating workbench also analyses sentences and answers questions about the paper with page-checked evidence. Needs an AI model service.
guoduan3727-alt/zotero-obsidian-scholar-.pain: Reading papers in a second language means copying words and sentences into separate tools. This keeps vocabulary and paper Q&A in the reader and in your Obsidian vault. Text is sent to the model you configure. Targets Zotero 9.

adamsghaier/zotero-open-in-obsidian.does: Opens a paper's Obsidian literature note from a right-click, finding it by Better BibTeX citekey in your vaults. An optional Obsidian companion plugin switches to the note if it is already open.
adamsghaier/zotero-open-in-obsidian.pain: Jumping from a Zotero item to its note otherwise means searching in Obsidian. It is read-only, never writes to your vault, and needs Better BibTeX and Obsidian on the same computer.

astralscarsmoonshadow/zotero-paper-mind.does: Analyses the open paper with an OpenAI-compatible model. It builds a profile, structure and mind map, then explains selected paragraphs with that context and answers follow-ups. Results are cached locally per item.
astralscarsmoonshadow/zotero-paper-mind.pain: Understanding a dense paper often means pasting text into an AI tool again and again. Needs your own API key, DeepSeek by default. Selected text and paper text are sent to that endpoint. Its developer says it is in active development.

ming-321/zotero-paper2md.does: Converts a PDF to a Markdown file with extracted images and YAML front matter of title, authors, year, DOI and tags, using the MinerU API. Tags converted items and picks the original PDF when several exist.
ming-321/zotero-paper2md.pain: Markdown is easier to feed to notes, search tools and AI than a PDF. Needs a MinerU API key, with a free tier available. The PDF is sent to MinerU for conversion.

lalalaladam/zotero-parent-item-open-url.does: Double-clicking a regular item in the list opens its URL, or its DOI link if there is no URL, in your system browser. Attachments, notes and multiple selections keep Zotero's normal behaviour.
lalalaladam/zotero-parent-item-open-url.pain: Double-click normally opens the PDF, so reaching the publisher page takes extra clicks. It wraps an internal Zotero function, which its developer notes as the main upgrade risk.

yogurttospring/zotero-pdf-paratranslate.does: Translates PDF paragraphs from English into Chinese with DeepSeek. Hover a paragraph, click Translate this paragraph, and the result streams into the sidebar with formulas rendered. Needs a DeepSeek API key.
yogurttospring/zotero-pdf-paratranslate.pain: Reading English papers as a Chinese reader means copying paragraphs into a translator and losing the maths. Only English to Chinese and only DeepSeek, by design. Targets Zotero 10.

rugkeypro/zotero-pdf-translate.does: A fork of Translate for Zotero that saves a selection's translation in the highlight's comment. It adds US pronunciation playback using Edge online voices and a sidebar chat about the whole item through a CPA-compatible model server.
rugkeypro/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Keeps translations with your annotations and adds spoken pronunciation and paper Q&A to the original translator. Selected text is sent to Microsoft for speech and to your chosen model server for chat.

arthur-lucifer/zotero-plugin-nutstore.does: Logs you in to Nutstore (坚果云) in one click and sets up Zotero file sync through it. An enhanced WebDAV mode works with the Nutstore desktop client on Windows.
arthur-lucifer/zotero-plugin-nutstore.pain: Setting up WebDAV for Zotero by hand is fiddly. Useful for users in China who sync through Nutstore. A fork of nutstore/zotero-plugin-nutstore; its README doesn't say what it changes.

huddermr/zotero-rag.does: Chat with your library in a sidebar panel, answered from the paper passages most relevant to your question. Embeddings can run locally in Ollama or LM Studio while chat uses OpenAI-compatible cloud models or local ones.
huddermr/zotero-rag.pain: Plain AI chat tends to invent answers about your papers. Retrieval sends only matching passages and shows what was sent. A cloud chat model needs an API key. Its licence is proprietary freeware, not open source.

seasideccm/zotero-read-aloud-loop.does: Adds a loop toggle to Zotero's Read Aloud popup so the current sentence repeats until you turn it off. Previous and next buttons move the loop to the new sentence. Built for Zotero 11.
seasideccm/zotero-read-aloud-loop.pain: Useful for close reading, shadowing and language learning, where you want to hear one sentence several times. Zotero's reader has no repeat option.

adamsghaier/zotero-reader-window-focus.does: Keeps zotero://open-pdf links to a paper open in a separate reader window inside that window instead of bringing the main window to the front.
adamsghaier/zotero-reader-window-focus.pain: Page links from tools like Obsidian jump to the right page, then the main window hides the reader. This stops that. If Zotero's internals change, it does nothing.

kzssc/zotero-reading-list.does: Sets a read status on items: New, To Read, In Progress, Read or Not Reading, or your own. Change it by right-click or Alt+1 to Alt+5, show it as a column, and update it automatically when you open a PDF.
kzssc/zotero-reading-list.pain: Zotero has no way to track what you have read. A fork of Dominic-DallOsto/zotero-reading-list; its README doesn't say what it changes.

fulinrenjian/zotero-reliable-translate.does: A fork of Translate for Zotero with a selection popup that shows progress and failures, with retry, copy and service switching. An Add to note button saves the original, translation, source and page. Defaults to the Bing adapter.
fulinrenjian/zotero-reliable-translate.pain: Translations in the original popup could fail silently or overwrite one another. Text goes to the online service you choose, and its developer notes these web endpoints may change. Targets Zotero 10.

maxvonmustermann/zotero-spotlight.does: A command palette opened with Cmd+P or Ctrl+P that searches your whole library. It has type, tag and year filters and runs actions such as Copy Citation or New Note, in the main window, reader and note editor.
maxvonmustermann/zotero-spotlight.pain: Zotero search only covers the current collection, so jumping to a known paper takes several steps. A fork of Royshare/zotero-spotlight. Its developer calls it experimental.

kaergo/zotero_to_obsidian.does: Aims to link Zotero with Obsidian.md, according to its manifest. No features are documented yet, so what it actually does is unclear.
kaergo/zotero_to_obsidian.pain: Probably for people who keep literature notes in Obsidian; it is an early project.

ouyangguangqi/zotero-watch-folder.does: Watches one or more folders and imports new PDFs automatically with metadata lookup and a tidy filename, skipping duplicates. Optionally mirrors folders and collections both ways, with smart rules and a recoverable trash.
ouyangguangqi/zotero-watch-folder.pain: Saves dragging each downloaded PDF into Zotero. Its developer advises backing up first, since some modes can rename, move or delete files. A fork of josesiqueira/zotero-watch-folder with a separate collection per folder.

kobuster/bionic-for-zotero-sentence-mode.does: Shows PDFs in bionic reading mode, with the first letters of each word in bold, and lets you toggle it from the View menu.
kobuster/bionic-for-zotero-sentence-mode.pain: Some readers find bolded word beginnings help them read faster, though the evidence is debated. A fork of windingwind/bionic-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

loading500/codex-zotero-obsidian-bridge.does: Opens, creates and incrementally updates Obsidian literature notes from Zotero. Item notes and annotation comments sync into a marked block, and the rest of the Markdown is left untouched. Adds toolbar and reader buttons.
loading500/codex-zotero-obsidian-bridge.pain: Keeps Obsidian literature notes in step with Zotero without overwriting your own writing, and backs up before the first rewrite each day. Needs Obsidian vaults and a routes file. Targets Zotero 9 and 10.

shenghuang-123/cupertino-for-zotero.does: A macOS-style theme for Zotero with SF Pro-style fonts, system colours, rounded card panels, frosted menus and a cascading animation when items expand. Changes appearance only.
shenghuang-123/cupertino-for-zotero.pain: For people who want Zotero to look like a native Mac app. It makes no network requests and changes no data, and uninstalling restores the default look.

liyulia-droid/easycite.does: Syncs a Zotero collection and its subcollections to a LaTeX project in VS Code or Cursor. It updates refs.bib without deleting other entries and copies local PDFs. Citation keys are stable, with Pinyin for Chinese names.
liyulia-droid/easycite.pain: Moving references into a LaTeX project by hand is tedious. A fork of Sixsheepdad/Zotero-Cursor-Cite. The repository has no licence yet.

firefly-lyf/firefly-agent-zotero.does: A research agent in the item sidebar that plans tasks, searches your library and PDFs, reads notes and annotations, searches the web and edits Word documents. Runs through a local Python server on your computer.
firefly-lyf/firefly-agent-zotero.pain: Gives one place to ask questions across your papers. Needs a Windows install of the backend and an API key for an OpenAI-compatible model. Its developer says library data stays local apart from calls to that model.

annefou/fred_zotero.does: Checks your library for DOIs that have replication studies in the FORRT Replication Database. Matching sends only short hash prefixes, then tags items and adds notes with replication title, authors, journal and outcome.
annefou/fred_zotero.pain: Researchers rarely know whether a paper they cite has been replicated. Your DOIs are not sent in full. A fork of forrtproject/flora-zotero.

eliorfoy/hide-annotations.does: One click, or Ctrl+Shift+H, hides every annotation in the PDF reader so you can read the original, and a second click brings them back. Adds a toolbar button and View menu item.
eliorfoy/hide-annotations.pain: Highlights and ink can get in the way of the original page. It only hides them on screen and never changes the data. Exported PDFs still contain the annotations, and selection highlighting hides while you drag.

rsamv/jadense-in-zotero.does: A personal fork of Jadense (攻玉) with a collection review window. One model call over a collection gives an overview, per-paper points, comparisons and a 0 to 100 score; code and appendix checks run locally.
rsamv/jadense-in-zotero.pain: Reviewing many papers at once is slow. A fork of jadense-ai/jadense-in-zotero for non-commercial use only. Metadata and abstracts go to the model, but PDF text does not unless you confirm a single-paper deep read.

entrophase/llm-for-zotero.does: An AI research agent in the Zotero reader. Chat with the PDF, figures and selected text, compare papers, search the web with Tavily and save notes to Zotero or Markdown folders. Works with API keys, local models, Codex or Claude Code.
entrophase/llm-for-zotero.pain: Lets you ask about papers and organise your library without leaving Zotero. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero that adds Google Antigravity CLI support.

jerry-li-j/llm-for-zotero-paper-companio.does: A fork of llm-for-zotero with a manual full-text reading step that builds a background and glossary. Adds per-task model choices, translation and explanation of selections, usage display and notes saved to Zotero or Obsidian.
jerry-li-j/llm-for-zotero-paper-companio.pain: Opening a paper triggers no model request until you start the reading. The full extracted text is sent to the chosen model, and the workflow targets Codex sessions. Replaces the original plugin.

s1nyon/margin-markdown.does: Shows PDF annotation comments as margin cards joined to their annotation by a line, rendering Markdown and LaTeX maths. Click a card to edit the raw text. Targets Zotero 9.
s1nyon/margin-markdown.pain: Annotation comments in Zotero are plain text, so formulas and lists are hard to read. Comments stay stored as Markdown, so they remain readable if you remove the plugin. Based on Zotero Margin Comments.

archwindos/metadata-search-for-zotero.does: Finds where a paper was published from its title, then fills missing metadata from publisher pages, conference databases, Crossref and arXiv. Can create parent items for loose PDFs, and flags conflicts for you to review.
archwindos/metadata-search-for-zotero.pain: PDFs and preprints often lack the published venue and DOI. This adds them without overwriting what is there. It queries web search and public sites, and some pages may not be readable. Targets Zotero 10.

tjr-ustc-hub/paper-workbench-for-zotero.does: Turns the PDF reader into three columns: the paper, an automatic Chinese translation of your selection, and notes with an AI chat. Chat answers only from the selected text. Needs an OpenAI-compatible Base URL and API key.
tjr-ustc-hub/paper-workbench-for-zotero.pain: Reading and translating, noting and asking questions normally means juggling windows. This keeps them side by side. Selected text and your questions are sent to your chosen endpoint.

yuchenlogin/paperflow-zotero-obsidian.does: Writes detailed Chinese reading notes in Obsidian from a Zotero paper. Notes cover background, methods, result tables, source-page links and links to related notes. Needs Python, Poppler and an OpenAI-compatible API or Codex CLI login.
yuchenlogin/paperflow-zotero-obsidian.pain: Makes notes that build into a knowledge base rather than a pasted summary. Its developer says it is a public preview for macOS and Linux, with no Windows or scanned PDF support. Full text is sent to the model.

yihengli333-netizen/paperpilot.does: Generates an AI summary of a paper and marks the verified key points on its PDF as colour-coded highlights with Chinese comments. It also builds a clickable reading index, a mind map and a reading note, and can export a separate annotated PDF. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
yihengli333-netizen/paperpilot.pain: Skimming a long paper means hunting for its question, method, results and limits. This marks them in the PDF itself, in Chinese, and skips quotes it cannot locate in the text.

gw19ddd/pdf2zh-desktop.does: Right-click a PDF in Zotero to translate it with the PaperFlow desktop app and attach the translated PDF back to the item. The desktop app, based on PDFMathTranslate, keeps formulas and layout and works with many AI engines.
gw19ddd/pdf2zh-desktop.pain: Translating a whole paper otherwise means setting up Python and command-line tools, then re-attaching the result by hand. A fork of AaronGIG/pdf2zh-desktop; the app handles setup and sends the translation back to Zotero.

0frost0/research-assistant-zotero.does: Builds collection-based knowledge bases from papers and reading notes. A web reader translates full texts or selections into Chinese and keeps source-linked notes. Runs on a self-hosted server with a model API key you configure.
0frost0/research-assistant-zotero.pain: For researchers who read English papers in Chinese and want notes that trace back to the original passage. Setup is heavy: it describes a personal server deployment.

sfk8815-create/sovena.does: Sends Zotero collections to a local Sovena server that converts attachments to Markdown with page numbers, runs OCR on scans and builds a vector index. AI clients such as Claude Desktop can then search your library over MCP.
sfk8815-create/sovena.pain: Scanned and photocopied PDFs, common in the humanities, can't be searched or cited by page. This makes them queryable in natural language, with answers traced to a page. Needs the server and an embedding service.

nickdu32/termground.does: Extracts English-Chinese terms with source evidence from PDFs. You review them in a term manager, and confirmed translations feed PDF2zh and Translate for Zotero's CNKI service.
nickdu32/termground.pain: Machine translation renders the same technical term differently from paper to paper. A local glossary built from your own reading keeps term translations consistent. The CNKI link is experimental.

sjtuhdt/z-o-bridge.does: Sends selected Zotero items to Obsidian: copies the PDF, writes or updates a Markdown literature card, and can generate an AI-written card. A companion Obsidian plugin searches Zotero, inserts citations and imports annotations.
sjtuhdt/z-o-bridge.pain: Moving references from Zotero into an Obsidian vault by hand is slow. The AI import sends the PDF's full text to a third-party OpenAI-compatible service whose address, model and key you supply.

yiwushan/zotero-ai-butler.does: Reads new PDFs with a large language model and saves a structured Markdown summary as a note on the item. Also offers deeper reading, mind maps, one-image summaries and multi-paper reviews. Needs your own model API key. Archived and no longer maintained.
yiwushan/zotero-ai-butler.pain: A fork of steven-jianhao-li/zotero-AI-Butler, tailored to Doubao (Volcano Ark) and MinerU, with the agent and chat turned off. Its developer has stopped maintaining it.

arc816/zotero-ai-hub.does: A multi-provider AI side panel for summaries, explanations, critical analysis, smart annotations, question answering, translation, mind maps and reviews. It embeds an MCP server so outside AI clients can use your library.
arc816/zotero-ai-hub.pain: Lets you switch between AI providers and models in one place instead of using a separate plugin for each task. Answers can be saved as child notes on the item.

fangfren/zotero-ai-organization.does: Adds a Research Workbench tab to the item pane for notes, tags, AI chat and documentation reading. Chat uses the local Codex CLI, and you can import documentation files from GitHub and link them to items.
fangfren/zotero-ai-organization.pain: For people who already use the Codex CLI with a ChatGPT login and want to chat about papers without an API key. It needs Codex installed and signed in.

leike0813/zotero-attanger.does: Manages attachments and places PDFs in a tidy folder tree. Pick a source folder and link or store files, then use Zotero's renaming and subfolder rules, with a target root for linked files.
leike0813/zotero-attanger.pain: A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger; its README doesn't say what it changes. Stock Zotero stores files under opaque key-named folders, which this replaces with readable ones.

tutuchanxd/zotero-attanger.does: Manages attachments and places PDFs in a tidy folder tree. Pick a source folder and link or store files, then use Zotero's renaming and subfolder rules, with a target root for linked files.
tutuchanxd/zotero-attanger.pain: A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-attanger; its README doesn't say what it changes. Stock Zotero stores files under opaque key-named folders, which this replaces with readable ones.

shaexys/zotero-auto-tag.does: Tags new papers with an LLM against a hierarchical taxonomy kept in a Markdown file, and rejects any tag the taxonomy doesn't contain. Runs on import or from the right-click menu. Needs an OpenAI-compatible API key.
shaexys/zotero-auto-tag.pain: Hand-tagging hundreds of papers is inconsistent, and letting a model tag freely invents tags that fragment the library. Here the model only picks from your own tag list.

moeiniamir/zotero-better-notes.does: A note-management suite: links between notes, templates and a better editor. It also syncs notes two ways with Markdown files, exports to Markdown, Word, PDF and mind maps, and integrates GPT.
moeiniamir/zotero-better-notes.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-better-notes; its README doesn't say what it changes. It turns Zotero's basic notes into linked, templated notes you can keep in sync with outside files.

frankrcastillo/zotero-books-to-sections.does: Splits a book item into separate book-section items, for example one per chapter of an edited volume. Its developer says it is a work in progress, with outline-based splitting still planned.
frankrcastillo/zotero-books-to-sections.pain: Citing single chapters of an edited book by different authors needs a separate item for each. This is meant to create them without typing each one.

wfssll/zotero-browser.does: An academic browser in a Zotero side panel with tabs for web pages and PDFs. It fetches NASA ADS BibTeX, saves arXiv records, keeps bilingual vocabulary notes and copies local PDFs to the clipboard. A pre-release for Zotero 9.0.x; the interface is mostly Chinese.
wfssll/zotero-browser.pain: Lets you look up papers, get ADS citations and collect vocabulary while reading without leaving Zotero. The vocabulary feature needs Translate for Zotero.

jianghao-zhang/zotero-cli.does: Pairs the zcli command-line tool with an optional helper plugin. zcli searches your local Zotero library, finds and triages new papers, plans dry-run imports, builds reading context for AI agents and mirrors the library to files.
jianghao-zhang/zotero-cli.pain: For people who work with Codex, Claude Code or similar agents and want fast local access to their library. Changes to Zotero are previewed before they run. This plugin is only the optional bridge.

qiangqianglab/zotero-docling.does: Converts PDF attachments to structured Markdown through a docling-serve server and attaches the .md file to the same item. Offers re-conversion, optional auto-convert on import, status tags and a ZIP export of Markdown files.
qiangqianglab/zotero-docling.pain: Gives RAG pipelines, note apps and literature reviews clean text instead of PDFs. A fork of max3925vats/zotero-docling; its README doesn't say what it changes. You must run docling-serve.

huanongfish/zotero-doi-dedup-import-plug.does: Takes over the Add Item by Identifier popup so you can paste many DOIs, or text containing them, and skips any already in your library. Existing items are added to the selected collection, and items can be tagged by relevance.
huanongfish/zotero-doi-dedup-import-plug.pain: Importing a reading list by DOI normally creates duplicates of papers you already have. This checks the whole library first, by DOI and by title.

cshao07/zotero-doi-enrich.does: Corrects existing items from their DOI using Crossref and OpenAlex. Fills empty volume, issue, pages, ISSN, URL and abstract, fixes journal names and repairs swapped author names. Previews first, and writes can be undone.
cshao07/zotero-doi-enrich.pain: Metadata from some sources, especially for Chinese journals, has gaps and swapped names. This repairs items in place without re-importing or touching attachments.

steven04hub/zotero-explain.does: Select a passage in the PDF reader and a floating panel translates it into Chinese, highlights technical terms and explains them, with follow-up questions. It signs in with your ChatGPT account through the Codex App Server, so no API key is needed.
steven04hub/zotero-explain.pain: Dense passages are hard to read in a second language. This explains them beside the text and sends only the selection and title, not the whole paper. The interface is mainly Chinese.

gaspardderoyan/zotero-focused-mode.does: Toggles a distraction-free reading mode with a shortcut that hides the tab bar, annotation toolbar and sidebars while Zotero stays windowed. Hovering at the top or left edge reveals them again.
gaspardderoyan/zotero-focused-mode.pain: Gives a clear reading view without full-screen mode. A fork of dschaehi/Zotero-Focused-Mode; this version keeps the window size and position, where the upstream 0.6.7 enters fullscreen.

konichan-7/zotero-glass.does: Gives Zotero's library, reader sidebars and annotation popups a native macOS glass look by inserting real NSVisualEffectView layers. Transparency, blur, tint and material can be adjusted in the app. macOS only, Zotero 9.
konichan-7/zotero-glass.pain: Makes Zotero match the look of other Mac apps without CSS tricks. A fork of Avi7ii/Zotero-glass; its README doesn't say what it changes.

isaksamsten/zotero-hamburger.does: Hides Zotero's menu bar and moves its menus into a hamburger menu in the tab bar, opened with Alt+M. Keeps other plugins' menu entries and restores the layout when disabled. For Zotero 10 on Linux and Windows.
isaksamsten/zotero-hamburger.pain: Frees a row of screen space on small displays. Because the window-control buttons are hidden too, you use your system's window shortcuts to minimise or close.

huanongfish/zotero-incremental-pdf-expor.does: Right-click a collection to export its PDFs to a chosen folder, copying only new files and replacing changed ones, compared by checksum. Unchanged files are skipped, and files that no longer exist in the library can be moved to a pruned folder.
huanongfish/zotero-incremental-pdf-expor.pain: Re-exporting a collection to a synced folder or tablet normally copies everything again. This brings the folder up to date and does not duplicate files.

frankhumbleble/zotero-itemtree-expand.does: Wraps long item titles across several lines in the library list so they show in full. The maximum number of lines is 1 to 10, default 5, and it can be switched off in preferences.
frankhumbleble/zotero-itemtree-expand.pain: Zotero cuts long titles off at the column edge, so similar titles are hard to tell apart without widening the column.

neonoenone/zotero-journal-suffix-cleaner.does: Removes a trailing phrase such as ': an official journal of the Transplantation Society' from the Publication field of newly added journal articles. Titles, abstracts, abbreviations and existing records are left alone.
neonoenone/zotero-journal-suffix-cleaner.pain: Some databases save journal names with society descriptions attached, which breaks consistent journal names and metric lookups. This keeps new items tidy automatically.

xu281530-rgb/zotero-lit-synapse-gpu.does: Runs an MCP server inside Zotero 9 so AI clients such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor can search, read, annotate and optionally edit your library. Adds hybrid keyword and semantic search, MinerU PDF parsing and an LLM wiki memory.
xu281530-rgb/zotero-lit-synapse-gpu.pain: Lets an AI assistant work with your own references over a local connection with no separate server. Writing features are off by default, and remote access needs an explicit opt-in and token.

lichong0429/zotero-llm-wiki-obsidian.does: Uses a large language model to turn selected papers or whole collections into structured wiki pages in an Obsidian vault. Also exports notes, PPT outlines, mind maps and LaTeX tables, extracts methods and syncs annotations. Needs a model API key.
lichong0429/zotero-llm-wiki-obsidian.pain: Building a personal knowledge base from many papers is slow by hand. Its developer calls this an early version that is not fully verified and advises backing up first.

xiaoxuan353/zotero-maimemo-sync.does: Syncs highlighted words from Zotero annotations to a cloud word list in the Maimemo vocabulary app, appending or overwriting, filtered by annotation colour. It can also export the words as a TXT file for other vocabulary apps. Needs a Maimemo API token.
xiaoxuan353/zotero-maimemo-sync.pain: Vocabulary met while reading papers otherwise has to be retyped into a word-learning app. A fork of bulletproof-system/zotero-maimemo-sync; its README doesn't say what it changes.

anurag-dalal/zotero_map_papers.does: Builds an interactive similarity graph of related papers for any item, using OpenAlex data, along with lists of prior works and derivative works. You can add papers to your library from the graph. Free, with an optional OpenAlex API key.
anurag-dalal/zotero_map_papers.pain: Gives a Connected Papers style view of a field's neighbourhood inside Zotero, so you can find foundational and follow-up work without leaving it.

sebastian-rink/zotero-metasync.does: An early-stage plugin for enriching and correcting Zotero metadata from online library sources. Its README is still the template's and documents no features yet; Google Books lookups can use an optional API key.
sebastian-rink/zotero-metasync.pain: Probably aims to fix incomplete or wrong bibliographic records in your library.

jh-chen0/zotero-move-to-collection.does: Adds a Move to Collection submenu to the item right-click menu that shows your collection tree and up to five recent targets. It adds the items to the destination and removes them only from the collection you are viewing. For Zotero 10.
jh-chen0/zotero-move-to-collection.pain: Zotero's drag and drop only adds items to another collection, so moving takes an extra removal step. This does it in one click and keeps other memberships.

hyiker/zotero-pdf-optimizer.does: Uses the CPDF command-line tool to remove the private PieceInfo data from PDF attachments, optionally with lossless compaction. It replaces a file only if the result is valid, has the same page count and saves enough space. Runs automatically or by hand.
hyiker/zotero-pdf-optimizer.pain: Some PDF producers embed large editing data that bloats storage. Savings vary, and rewriting may invalidate digital signatures. You install CPDF yourself.

zhaokun91/zotero-pdf2zh.does: Translates PDFs from Zotero with PDF2zh and PDF2zh_next, keeping formulas and layout. It works with a local Python server that you install and start, and the translated files come back to Zotero.
zhaokun91/zotero-pdf2zh.pain: A fork of guaguastandup/zotero-pdf2zh; its README doesn't say what it changes. It lets you translate whole papers into Chinese without leaving the library.

unbearablefate/zotero-pick2anki.does: Shows dictionary definitions for a word selected in the PDF or EPUB reader, then adds it to Anki with its original sentence. Draws on Youdao, Bing, Cambridge, Oxford and Collins; Anki needs the AnkiConnect add-on. No API key.
unbearablefate/zotero-pick2anki.pain: Looking up words and making vocabulary cards while reading papers takes two disconnected steps. A fork of soyami/zotero-pick2anki; its README doesn't say what it changes.

huanongfish/zotero-search-plus.does: Makes the quick search box search the whole library even when a subcollection is open, then returns to your collection when you clear it. Also keeps a clickable dropdown of your last 25 searches.
huanongfish/zotero-search-plus.pain: Zotero searches only the collection you are in, so you must click the library root first. This does that step for you and saves retyping repeat searches.

sstraume97/zotero-site-metadata.does: Fills in metadata for web pages that have no site translator, using patterns learned from similar pages already in your library.
sstraume97/zotero-site-metadata.pain: Saving blog posts and personal sites leaves empty fields to fill by hand. A fork of BarishNamazov/zotero-site-metadata; its README doesn't say what it changes.

shenghuang-123/zotero-table-reader.does: Opens CSV, TSV, Excel and ODS attachments in a Zotero tab on double-click. Keeps merged cells, can freeze rows and columns, and detects delimiters and encodings automatically.
shenghuang-123/zotero-table-reader.pain: Zotero otherwise hands spreadsheet attachments to an external program. This lets you glance at data files inside Zotero.

mrcsvg/zotero-triage.does: Adds a sortable Priority column with a 0 to 100 score, set by right-click levels or Alt+arrow shortcuts and stored in the Extra field so it syncs. Optionally scores a collection with an Anthropic or OpenAI key.
mrcsvg/zotero-triage.pain: Zotero has no way to order a reading backlog by priority; tags and collections don't sort numerically. Scoring is local unless you run the AI option.

exhilarating0411/zotero-txt-md-to-epub.does: Converts selected TXT and Markdown attachments into EPUB files, saved beside the originals and added to Zotero. It supports headings, paragraphs, quotes, code blocks, bold and italics. For Zotero 9.
exhilarating0411/zotero-txt-md-to-epub.pain: Plain text and Markdown files can't be read comfortably in Zotero's reader. EPUB can be opened there. Tables, images and math are not fully supported.

zenon-lzz/zoterobaidupansync.does: Syncs Zotero attachments to Baidu Pan (百度网盘) instead of Zotero storage or WebDAV. Uses incremental MD5 comparison, chunked uploads, scheduled sync and a manifest for several devices. Needs a Baidu app key and secret.
zenon-lzz/zoterobaidupansync.pain: Mainly for users in China who find Zotero's storage or WebDAV hard to use. Files live only under an app folder in your Baidu Pan.

solivayne/zoterodict.does: Shows English-Chinese dictionary entries when you select a word in the PDF or EPUB reader. Draws on Youdao, Bing, Cambridge and Oxford, with a short Chinese gloss on top. No account or API key.
solivayne/zoterodict.pain: A trimmed version of zotero-pick2anki without the Anki card feature. It suits Chinese-speaking readers who want quick word lookups while reading papers.

sheng-liu/annotation-count.does: Adds item-list columns that count PDF marks, written comments, newest native annotation date and migrated ReadCube records. A Tools command indexes embedded PDF annotations so they count too, without rewriting the PDF.
sheng-liu/annotation-count.pain: Lets you sort papers by how much you have annotated them, so you can find the ones you actually studied. A fork of Zotero Annotations Count.

clef233/asktranslate-for-zotero.does: Translates selected passages and adds AI follow-up questions in a side panel, with streaming answers and copying or saving to notes. Works with ChatGPT, Azure, Claude, Gemini and custom services using your keys.
clef233/asktranslate-for-zotero.pain: A fork of Translate for Zotero that adds AI question and answer. You can ask for a term, a formula or the reasoning of a passage right after translating it.

z1hawl89/cueb-journal-tier.does: Adds a column showing each journal's CUEB university ranking plus CSSCI, CSCD, UTD24, FT50, AJG, JCR and SSCI tags, from built-in data matched by ISSN or name. A browser extension is included.
z1hawl89/cueb-journal-tier.pain: Made for CUEB staff and students who must check journal tiers for evaluation. Clarivate data for SSCI and JCR is not bundled.

guoxinlu17-cmyk/dsh-bridge.does: Connects Zotero to your local DeepSeek Harness (dsh) so you can ask about items or passages. Citations are checked against the text actually sent, and answers can be saved as notes. Needs Node and dsh.
guoxinlu17-cmyk/dsh-bridge.pain: Other AI plugins use their own model. This runs your own dsh profile, with its tools and knowledge base, from a Zotero dialog.

dobby-was-free/feedrank_for_zotero.does: Scores papers from your Zotero journal and arXiv feeds from 0 to 100 against a research profile you write, with an explanation and a sortable Score column. Needs Awesome GPT with a model; email digest optional.
dobby-was-free/feedrank_for_zotero.pain: Feeds pile up faster than you can read. This ranks them so you can decide what to read first. Model calls may cost money and your profile is sent to the model.

hugogene/intra-collection-invert-selecti.does: Adds right-click commands to invert the selection inside the current collections or saved searches, or to select items without a chosen tag. It clears view filters only if they hide items, and says so.
hugogene/intra-collection-invert-selecti.pain: Zotero has no invert selection. This is a rewrite of Collection Invert Selection 0.6.2 that works with several collections at once.

hzxwonder/llm-for-zotero.does: Chat with the current PDF, selected text, figures and uploaded files inside Zotero, with citations that jump to the source passage. Agent Mode searches, tags and organises the library. Works with API keys, local models, ChatGPT WebChat, Codex or Claude Code.
hzxwonder/llm-for-zotero.pain: Reading and questioning papers otherwise means pasting text into a separate chat. A fork of yilewang/llm-for-zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

liamzhao710/paper-statistics-for-zotero.does: Computes statistics locally from a paper's PDF: pages, words, figures, tables, theorem-like statements, algorithms, numbered equations and references. Shows them as item-list columns and in a sidebar. No uploads, LLMs or keys. For Zotero 10.
liamzhao710/paper-statistics-for-zotero.pain: Lets you judge a paper's length and structure at a glance, or sort by it. Some labels and settings are still in Chinese.
