21aq/paperpet.does: Tells the PaperPet desktop pet which paper you are reading in Zotero. It passes the current page, your text selection, highlights and the extracted full text to PaperPet, a floating Windows companion that answers questions through DeepSeek or any OpenAI-compatible API.
21aq/paperpet.pain: Reading maths-heavy papers means pasting passages and formulas into a chatbot by hand. This lets a pet on your desktop already know the paper, page and selection you are on.

allinonein/patent-outline-4-zotero.does: Builds a clickable PDF outline for long patents from MinerU-parsed files, then writes it into the PDF as bookmarks shown in Zotero's reader.
allinonein/patent-outline-4-zotero.pain: Patents run to hundreds of pages with no table of contents, so finding the claims or a specific example means endless scrolling. It needs an OpenAI-compatible API key, previews the outline first and backs up the PDF before writing. Tuned for chemical and siRNA patents.

seraphina523/zotero-ai-assistant.does: An AI panel in the item pane for summaries, translation, critical appraisal and tags. It also explains figures and tables, and answers questions about the full text with clickable page citations.
seraphina523/zotero-ai-assistant.pain: Slow reading of English papers and forgetting what you read. It also searches your whole library for research gaps and conflicting findings, and builds comparison tables across papers. Needs an API key for OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Qwen or similar.

yaokensky-maker/zotero-ai-sidebar.does: An AI research sidebar for discussing the current paper. It uses PDF text, arXiv LaTeX sources, annotations and images, translates while you read and saves answers to notes.
yaokensky-maker/zotero-ai-sidebar.pain: A fork of xuhan-rgb/zotero-ai-sidebar; its README doesn't say what it changes. It works with Anthropic, OpenAI or compatible APIs, or through ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Kimi websites via a local Web Agent that needs Node.js.

caipio/zotero-better-notes.does: Note management inside Zotero: note links, templates, two-way Markdown sync, export to Markdown, Word, PDF and mind maps, and a better note editor.
caipio/zotero-better-notes.pain: A fork of windingwind/zotero-better-notes. Its developer says that right-clicking an item to import a note from Markdown defaults to the folder holding the item's PDF.

aht02/zotero-blank-drag.does: Lets you drag a PDF page around by pressing and moving the mouse over blank areas, images or the grey gap between pages in Zotero's reader.
aht02/zotero-blank-drag.pain: With the default selection tool, you can't pan without switching to the hand tool. Text selection, links and annotations keep working as normal. Built for Zotero 10 and overlaps with the author's Smart Hand plugin, so enable only one.

gulubao/zotero-easyread.does: Sends PDFs to the EasyRead reading app with a right-click and skips duplicates by file hash. It syncs your EasyRead notes, highlights and saved AI answers back into a Zotero child note.
gulubao/zotero-easyread.pain: Lets you manage papers in Zotero but read in EasyRead without losing your reading notes. Sync is manual and one-way. A fork of apple5089/zotero-easyread that adds macOS and Ubuntu support and a settings page.

peash182/zotero-for-wordcraft.does: Inserts citations and a bibliography from selected Zotero items into a running WordCraft document, from a right-click menu.
peash182/zotero-for-wordcraft.pain: Citations are formatted by Zotero in any installed style and sent over WordCraft's local control port, so nothing leaves your computer. For WordCraft users who want Zotero references. Early release: citations go in as plain text.

dragonlau0924/zotero-hover-bars.does: Hides the top tab bar and the reader toolbar to give you more reading space, and brings each back when you hover where it normally sits.
dragonlau0924/zotero-hover-bars.pain: Zotero's bars take up room on small screens. Toggles live in the View menu and work with PDF, EPUB and snapshot readers in Zotero 8 to 10.

heart-ttt/zotero-maimemo.does: Double-click an English word in the Zotero reader to add it to a MaiMemo (墨墨背单词) cloud word list and your study plan.
heart-ttt/zotero-maimemo.pain: Looking up words and adding them to a vocabulary app by hand interrupts reading. The plugin reduces words to their base form and queues offline. You need a MaiMemo open-API token.

ffff2004/zotero-mineru.does: Runs MinerU on selected PDFs and stores the result as a Markdown attachment, with images and JSON output kept beside it. The source PDF is never changed.
ffff2004/zotero-mineru.pain: Gets structured Markdown out of PDFs inside Zotero. Needs a separately installed local runtime. The current release targets Linux, Zotero 10 and Python 3.13, with CPU or NVIDIA profiles.

guochengran464-byte/zotero-orange-transl.does: Translates a PDF with a local PDFMathTranslate-next and BabelDOC setup, then attaches bilingual and Chinese-only PDFs beside the original, with progress shown.
guochengran464-byte/zotero-orange-transl.pain: Gives full-layout PDF translation into Chinese without leaving Zotero. You bring an OpenAI-compatible API key. Windows x64 and Zotero 10 only; a one-click installer fetches the engine.

hebruce1005/zotero-parallel-reader-plugi.does: Opens a PDF and a local HTML translation side by side in Zotero, with page-linked scrolling, a vocabulary list, HTML annotations and reading colour themes.
hebruce1005/zotero-parallel-reader-plugi.pain: Reading an English paper next to its Chinese translation otherwise means juggling two windows. The HTML runs in an isolated sandbox and annotations stay on your machine.

npasquier/zotero-pdf-shortcut.does: Copies Finder aliases to the PDFs of selected items, so you can paste them into any Finder folder.
npasquier/zotero-pdf-shortcut.pain: Zotero's storage folders are hard to keep next to your project files. Aliases keep working when Zotero renames or moves the file. macOS only.

ipbes-data/zotero-safe-edit.does: Lets local applications propose changes to fields of existing Zotero items. Changes apply only after you approve them in Zotero, with backups, a change log and undo.
ipbes-data/zotero-safe-edit.pain: For tools that find library problems, such as wrong DOIs, and offer fixes without risking data. Each app needs its own token, and editing is refused unless auto-sync is off and a recent backup exists.

tom3410/zotero-scipdf-enhanced.does: Downloads PDFs from Sci-Hub mirrors by DOI and attaches them to the item. Has a mirror list editor and a window for completing human-verification checks by hand.
tom3410/zotero-scipdf-enhanced.pain: A fork of syt2/zotero-scipdf that improves mirror management and verification handling. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

aht02/zotero-smart-hand.does: Improves the hand tool in the PDF reader: over text the cursor becomes a text cursor so you can select it, and blank areas drag the page as usual.
aht02/zotero-smart-hand.pain: With the hand tool on, you can't select text without switching tools. Built for Zotero 10 and overlaps with the author's Blank Drag plugin, so enable only one.

jieyi9538-dot/zotero-snapshot2pdf.does: Converts web page snapshots into PDF attachments from a right-click menu, using headless Edge or Chrome.
jieyi9538-dot/zotero-snapshot2pdf.pain: Snapshots can't be read or processed by tools that expect PDFs. Only selected items are converted and items that already have a PDF are skipped. Windows is supported out of the box.

meteor0108/zotero2obsidian-autosync.does: Creates an Obsidian paper note for each Zotero paper and syncs your Zotero Pass 2 note into it, following the three-pass method from How to Read a Paper.
meteor0108/zotero2obsidian-autosync.pain: Keeps paper notes in Zotero and Obsidian from drifting apart. Properties such as authors, year and links are filled in automatically. Templates are in Korean, with English versions included.

rch-huang/citeloom-zotero-plugin.does: Shows how the papers in a Zotero collection cite one another, with a Cited by count and red arrows to the collection papers each one cites.
rch-huang/citeloom-zotero-plugin.pain: When choosing a baseline or surveying a field, you want to see which of your saved papers build on each other. It matches references from attached PDFs by DOI or title, with no API key. It does not run OCR.

yezery/idea_for_zotero.does: Generates three AI summaries per item: limitations the authors state, possible follow-up research ideas, and an overview of the paper. Results go into item columns.
yezery/idea_for_zotero.pain: Quickly scanning gaps and next steps across many papers. Uses indexed PDF text, or the abstract if there is none, with an OpenAI-compatible API key and model you choose.

acruxis/latest_pdf_first.does: Opens the most recently added PDF that exists locally when you double-click a parent item.
acruxis/latest_pdf_first.pain: Zotero opens whichever attachment it picks, which may be an old version of a PDF. It has no settings and falls back to normal behaviour when no PDF is available. Developed for Zotero 10.

archwindos/llm-for-zotero.does: A reading sidebar that translates selected text and answers questions about a paper. It sends the original PDF to DeepSeek, Gemini or OpenAI models, using an API key or your ChatGPT login.
archwindos/llm-for-zotero.pain: Gives separate model setups for translating and for Q&A, with saved history and Markdown note export. Its developer says this is a pre-release not yet fully tested in the Zotero interface.

mrygoodenough/paperbridge-zotero-plugin.does: Translates a paper into Chinese with DeepSeek and shows it beside the original with synchronised scrolling. Figures, tables and formulas stay as in the original.
mrygoodenough/paperbridge-zotero-plugin.pain: Gives a laid-out bilingual reading view without leaving Zotero. You need a DeepSeek API key. Builds for macOS Apple Silicon and Windows x64 bundle their own Python.

asperatus22/zotero-annotation-color-cust.does: Replaces the default annotation colour names and tooltips in Zotero's reader with names you choose.
asperatus22/zotero-annotation-color-cust.pain: A fork of aidecameron/zotero-annotation-color-customizer; its README doesn't say what it changes. Colour meanings, such as yellow for definitions, are easier to remember with your own labels.

mingf23/zotero-annotation-manage.does: Manages annotations and tags: add tagged annotations, export them as notes, link annotations, highlight words, and run summary statistics. Exporting needs Better Notes.
mingf23/zotero-annotation-manage.pain: Helps turn annotations into organised notes by colour and tag. A fork of zzlb0224/zotero-annotation-manage that supports Zotero 10 and uses a fixed set of personal tags and colours.

soliviantar/zotero-apa7-uoc.does: Adds the Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC) variant of APA 7, with each author's full first name in square brackets after the initials.
soliviantar/zotero-apa7-uoc.pain: UOC students must use this variant, which Zotero lacks. A fork of aramosalv/zotero-apa7-uoc; its README doesn't say what it changes. It drops access dates and adapts the final conjunction to the language.

lzjin426/zotero-feishu.does: Syncs Zotero items to a Feishu (飞书) Base table, with their PDFs, or publishes them to Feishu cloud documents. Sync is automatic or from a right-click menu.
lzjin426/zotero-feishu.pain: Keeps a Feishu literature table in step with Zotero. A fork of wu-uk/zotero-feishu that adds Base sync and Zotero 10 support. You need a Feishu application and a table with specific field names.

eziou/zotero-glass.does: Gives Zotero's windows and sidebars native macOS glass blur, with opacity, blur and colour adjustable in its settings.
eziou/zotero-glass.pain: Makes Zotero match the look of macOS. A fork of Avi7ii/Zotero-glass for Zotero 10. Works only on macOS and only with the dark theme, which it switches on.

kaifeng0922/zotero-linksync.does: Saves new PDFs as linked attachments in a separate synced folder, from drag and drop, the Connector or local imports, instead of Zotero's storage.
kaifeng0922/zotero-linksync.pain: Lets Zotero sync items while a tool like Syncthing syncs the PDFs, so your data directory stays off cloud drives. Early release, tested only on macOS.

sparklemuff1n/zotero-note-to-book-sectio.does: Adds a Copy Note to Book Section item in the right-click menu to copy a note, such as one made from annotations, into a Book Section item.
sparklemuff1n/zotero-note-to-book-sectio.pain: Zotero has no direct way to move a note into another item type. This suits people who collect book chapter notes in separate items.

imxiaotaoya/zotero-paper-partner.does: Answers questions you write as Q: lines inside a note, quietly in the background. It reads the paper's PDF, cites pages and uses an OpenAI-compatible API such as Kimi or DeepSeek.
imxiaotaoya/zotero-paper-partner.pain: A fork of QinSihan/zotero-paper-partner. It makes the model read the PDF rather than only your notes, keeps follow-up context, and fixes Kimi and Zotero 9 problems. You need an API key.

rsln-creator/zotero-pdf-associate.does: Opens a PDF you double-click in your file manager in Zotero. It matches the file to a library copy by content hash, or imports it into a collection named after its folder.
rsln-creator/zotero-pdf-associate.pain: Zotero can't take file paths from the command line or file associations, so this adds a small Python launcher. Everything stays on localhost. The setup shown is for Windows.

rant003/zotero-pick2anki-no-dictionary-d.does: Looks up an English word selected in Zotero's reader in five online dictionaries and adds a card with the sentence to Anki through AnkiConnect.
rant003/zotero-pick2anki-no-dictionary-d.pain: A fork of soyami/zotero-pick2anki. Its developer says it can also write the Translate for Zotero result when no dictionary definition is found. Needs Anki with AnkiConnect, and no API key.

felipebocajr/zotero-reader-local-ai.does: Explains selected PDF text or answers questions about it in a popup, sending the paper's full text to a local LFM2.5 model that runs on your machine.
felipebocajr/zotero-reader-local-ai.pain: Answers need no external service, so papers stay on your computer. Answers can be saved as a purple highlight annotation. You must set up a local server from the project, and its developer calls it personal.

martinekv/zotero-safe-mcp.does: An MCP server inside Zotero for AI agents: they can read your library and add notes, highlights, tags and papers by DOI, arXiv ID or PMID.
martinekv/zotero-safe-mcp.pain: Gives agents access with limits: they can change or remove only what they added, nothing is deleted outright, and writes are rate limited. Access uses a token you can regenerate.

alexanderjfink/zotero-voice-annotator.does: Turns spoken quotes into PDF highlights, from audio recordings attached to an item or live from your microphone. Trigger phrases map to highlight colours.
alexanderjfink/zotero-voice-annotator.pain: Annotating by speaking is quicker than selecting text. Transcription runs locally with Whisper, so you need Python with faster-whisper, pymupdf and sounddevice installed.

boschiffer/zotero-vrtl-reader.does: Reads PDFs in book order in Zotero's reader: two-page spreads with page order from right to left, plus an in-window full-screen mode.
boschiffer/zotero-vrtl-reader.pain: Suited to vertical-text Chinese and classical books. It changes page order only and does not reflow text. Toggled with Ctrl+Shift+V and F11.

jiangshuguo/zotero-unify.does: Normalises venue names for Ethereal Style tags, fills in USENIX metadata, and retries PDF recognition.
jiangshuguo/zotero-unify.pain: Keeps publication tags consistent for people who use the Ethereal Style plugin. The developer's page shows no further documentation.

sachajw/aiops-lmstudio-zotero-plugin.does: Connects Zotero to local LLMs such as LM Studio or Ollama to chat with a document, summarise items into notes, ask questions and extract key points.
sachajw/aiops-lmstudio-zotero-plugin.pain: For keeping AI research help on your own machine. It adds an item pane section, right-click actions and a local HTTP API for other tools.

htysky/annotation-filter-for-zotero.does: Adds a filter button to the annotation panel, planned to filter annotations by type such as highlight, underline or note, and by whether they have comments.
htysky/annotation-filter-for-zotero.pain: Zotero's annotation filters are limited. This is under development: only the button is done so far.

zotero/arkivo-sufia.does: A plugin for the Arkivo service that sends items from a Zotero collection to Sufia, a Project Hydra repository, over its API.
zotero/arkivo-sufia.pain: For repository managers who want Zotero library items deposited in a Sufia repository. It runs as a Node.js service, not inside Zotero.

muisedestiny/chartero.does: A charting plugin for Zotero. Its developer announces a preview that supports only the Zotero 7 developer beta, with older versions on another branch.
muisedestiny/chartero.pain: A fork of volatile-static/Chartero; its README doesn't say what it changes. Intended for people who want charts built from their Zotero library.

takluyver/cite2c.does: Adds Zotero citations and bibliographies to Jupyter Notebook Markdown cells, with toolbar buttons to find a reference and insert it.
takluyver/cite2c.pain: Writing notebooks that cite sources normally means typing references by hand. Citations are stored in the notebook and rendered with citeproc-js. Needs Jupyter Notebook 4.2 or later.

crsh/citr.does: An RStudio addin and R functions that search a BibTeX file or a Zotero library and insert formatted Markdown citations into the document.
crsh/citr.pain: Citing from R Markdown without leaving the editor. For Zotero it needs the Better BibTeX extension. It also removes unused entries from a bibliography file.

zotero-chinese/configs.does: Shared configuration files for the Zotero Chinese community's tooling, covering Prettier, MarkdownLint, AutoCorrect and Renovate settings.
zotero-chinese/configs.pain: For developers of the community's projects who want consistent code and text formatting. It is not a plugin for end users.

pekideer/controlled-tagger.does: A script for the zotero-gpt plugin that asks GPT to give a paper three to five tags from a controlled vocabulary of Field, Object, Method and Type.
pekideer/controlled-tagger.pain: Keeps tags standard instead of free-form. It matches existing library tags and works with Chinese and English keywords. Requires zotero-gpt and an API key.

windingwind/doc-for-zotero-plugin-dev.does: Developer documentation for writing Zotero plugins, giving an overview of the plugin development process.
windingwind/doc-for-zotero-plugin-dev.pain: Aimed at people building plugins. Its authors warn it may be out of date, so check the official Zotero documentation.

rikblok/dokuwiki-plugin-zotero.does: A DokuWiki plugin that lets you cite references saved in Zotero with a LaTeX-like syntax.
rikblok/dokuwiki-plugin-zotero.pain: For wiki authors who want citations from their Zotero library on DokuWiki pages. It runs in DokuWiki, not in Zotero.

stefanmacke/dokuwiki-zotero-plugin.does: A DokuWiki plugin that shows bibliography entries from Zotero, caching them in a wiki page or a file and fetching new entries when you cite one not yet cached.
stefanmacke/dokuwiki-zotero-plugin.pain: For wiki authors who want references from Zotero on DokuWiki pages. You need your Zotero user ID and API key. It runs in DokuWiki, not in Zotero.

programmfabrik/easydb-custom-data-type-z.does: An easyDB 5 plugin that adds a data type for references to bibliography entries kept in Zotero. It reads Zotero through an API key limited to read access and shows each entry in a CSL style you choose.
programmfabrik/easydb-custom-data-type-z.pain: Teams running an easyDB collection database can cite literature without remodelling bibliographic metadata, because the bibliography stays managed in Zotero.

ife-ensl/ep_zotero.does: Inserts Zotero references into the Etherpad editor. It is a plugin for etherpad-lite that you install into your Etherpad server's plugins directory.
ife-ensl/ep_zotero.pain: People writing collaboratively in Etherpad otherwise have to look up and paste references by hand.

altusepa/epa-zotero-plugin.does: Disables Zotero's built-in cloud sync features, for Zotero 7 only. It also includes a Windows installer script for organisation-wide deployment.
altusepa/epa-zotero-plugin.pain: Built for use at the US Environmental Protection Agency, where Zotero's cloud sync must be switched off before the software can be used.

lasertron/firetray.does: Minimises Zotero to the Linux system tray, with options to hide to tray on close or minimise, start minimised and restore windows to their previous position. A fork of FireTray with its install.rdf edited to mark it compatible with Zotero 5.
lasertron/firetray.pain: FireTray was discontinued, and this fork keeps it installable for Zotero 5 on Linux, where it is the only way to send Zotero to the tray. A fork of foudfou/FireTray.

wangwenkai2003/gemmin-zotero-plugin.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
wangwenkai2003/gemmin-zotero-plugin.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

muisedestiny/jasminum.does: Fetches metadata for Chinese-language PDFs and CAJ files from CNKI by file name, splits or merges Chinese author names, and adds bookmarks to CNKI thesis PDFs. Also updates Chinese translators and pulls citation counts and core-journal status.
muisedestiny/jasminum.pain: Zotero handles Chinese literature poorly, so CNKI downloads often arrive without metadata. A fork of l0o0/jasminum; its README doesn't say what it changes.

whiskyechobravo/kerko.does: A web application component, not a Zotero add-on, that publishes a Zotero bibliography as a searchable website. It offers facets, keyword search and full-text search of PDFs, built with Python and Flask over the Zotero API.
whiskyechobravo/kerko.pain: Teams who keep a bibliography in Zotero can share it with readers through a browsable web interface, without asking readers to use Zotero.

tran-khoa/krunner-zotero.does: A KRunner plugin for KDE Plasma that searches your Zotero library as you type. It matches titles, authors, DOI, year, tags, collections, notes, abstracts and publisher or journal fields.
tran-khoa/krunner-zotero.pain: Linux KDE users can find a paper from the desktop launcher without opening Zotero first.

p2p-ld/kysely-zotero-dialect.does: A developer library that lets a Zotero plugin use the kysely query builder. It creates a separate SQLite database in Zotero's data directory and runs queries through Zotero's own SQLite driver.
p2p-ld/kysely-zotero-dialect.pain: Plugin authors who need their own tables get type-safe schemas and migrations, without touching Zotero's main database or inventing a storage system.

liozhang/leadero.does: An AI assistant for Zotero 8 with a chat panel, switchable personas and long-term memory. Over 100 skills search the library, create notes, tag and analyse papers. Needs an API key for OpenAI, Claude, Gemini and others, or a local model.
liozhang/leadero.pain: Lets you ask an AI agent to work on your library from inside Zotero, and also reach it from Telegram, Discord, Slack and similar channels or an MCP client.

micheletobias/literaturemapper.does: A QGIS plugin, not a Zotero add-on, that connects QGIS to a Zotero library and attaches GeoJSON geometries to individual citations.
micheletobias/literaturemapper.pain: Researchers who work with maps can record where each cited study took place and view their literature spatially.

schubsijan/logseq-better-zotero-plugin.does: A Logseq plugin that searches your Zotero library from a slash command and creates literature pages from templates written in Nunjucks. It reads a Better BibTeX JSON export, so it works fully offline.
schubsijan/logseq-better-zotero-plugin.pain: Logseq users get customisable literature pages without an API key or internet connection. Needs the Better BibTeX add-on for Zotero.

vyleung/logseq-logtero-plugin.does: A Logseq plugin that creates a page for a Zotero item, with a page title and properties built from templates. It reads a Better BibTeX JSON export, which Zotero keeps updated.
vyleung/logseq-logtero-plugin.pain: Saves Logseq users from typing each reference's author, year, DOI and other fields by hand. Needs the Better BibTeX add-on for Zotero.

xyhp915/logseq-zotero-plugin.does: A Logseq plugin that searches your Zotero library and inserts citations, pages or imported highlights. It connects with an API key or the local connector and supports a citation style (CSL) of your choice.
xyhp915/logseq-zotero-plugin.pain: Brings Zotero references into Logseq notes. Its developer says it is a work in progress and only for the Logseq DB version.

benjypng/logseq-zoterolocal-plugin.does: A Logseq plugin that connects to Zotero 7 or later running on your machine and pulls items into your graph, with fuzzy search, templates and annotation sync. It works on both Logseq DB and file-based graphs.
benjypng/logseq-zoterolocal-plugin.pain: Logseq users can import references without Zotero Cloud sync or an API key. Citation keys need the Better BibTeX add-on.

jasonzou/make-it-red-ts.does: A sample Zotero 7 plugin written in TypeScript, based on Zotero's Make It Red example. It demonstrates a bootstrapped plugin and update manifests for upgrading across versions.
jasonzou/make-it-red-ts.pain: A demo for plugin developers rather than a tool for researchers.

windingwind/note-editor.does: The source code of Zotero's note editor, with build and development instructions. It produces web and Zotero builds of the editor.
windingwind/note-editor.pain: For developers who want to modify or test the note editor outside Zotero. A fork of zotero/note-editor; its README doesn't say what it changes.

hans/obsidian-citation-plugin.does: An Obsidian plugin that searches references from a BibTeX or CSL-JSON export, such as one from Zotero with Better BibTeX. It creates literature notes, inserts links to them and inserts Pandoc-style citations.
hans/obsidian-citation-plugin.pain: Obsidian users writing about papers can cite and open literature notes from the editor with keyboard shortcuts, instead of copying keys by hand.

piedpipr/obsidian-piedpiprs-mod.does: An Obsidian plugin of personal automations for a Zotero and Pandoc workflow, including citation insertion and automatic hiding of note properties. Needs Zotero with Better BibTeX and Pandoc installed.
piedpipr/obsidian-piedpiprs-mod.pain: Aimed at one researcher's reading, annotating and writing routine in Obsidian, replacing Templater scripts with a plugin.

stone-home/obsidian-plugin-zotero-annota.does: An Obsidian companion to the Zotero Integration plugin. It shows a review panel of a paper's annotations with one-click conversion into atomic notes, links notes to projects, sends data through webhooks and manages calls for papers.
stone-home/obsidian-plugin-zotero-annota.pain: Helps Obsidian users turn imported Zotero highlights and images into separate notes, instead of working through them by hand.

anoopkcn/obsidian-zotero-annotations.does: An Obsidian plugin that creates or updates notes holding a Zotero item's metadata and PDF annotations, using an optional template. Needs Zotero 6 with Better BibTeX and its JSON export. Its developer marks it deprecated.
anoopkcn/obsidian-zotero-annotations.pain: Brings Zotero highlights and comments into Obsidian notes. Its developer recommends mgmeyers/obsidian-zotero-integration instead.

duanxianpi/obsidian-zotero-reader-plugin.does: An Obsidian plugin that embeds the Zotero reader to read and annotate PDF, EPUB and HTML files inside Obsidian. It can copy links to annotations and selections and saves annotations as plain Markdown.
duanxianpi/obsidian-zotero-reader-plugin.pain: Lets you read and annotate in the same app as your notes. Its developer calls it fragile and beta, and recommends a newer project instead.

shangtingyou/obsidian-zoteroid-plugin.does: A copy of the Obsidian sample plugin, named for Zotero IDs, with no documented features of its own.
shangtingyou/obsidian-zoteroid-plugin.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

omeka/plugin-coins.does: An Omeka plugin that adds COinS metadata to item pages, so that Zotero can read them.
omeka/plugin-coins.pain: Omeka site owners can let visitors save items into Zotero with one click.

caioaugustobrg/plugin-to-zotero.does: A copy of the NestJS starter project with no documented features of its own. Its GitHub description says the author is making a plugin for Zotero.
caioaugustobrg/plugin-to-zotero.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

onlyoffice/plugin-zotero.does: Inserts Zotero citations and bibliographies into ONLYOFFICE editors. You search your Zotero library by author, title or year, choose a style and language, and press Insert citation. Needs a Zotero API key.
onlyoffice/plugin-zotero.pain: People writing in ONLYOFFICE can cite from Zotero without leaving the editor. The repository is archived and the plugin has moved to ONLYOFFICE's marketplace repository.

r7-consult/plugin-zotero.does: Inserts Zotero citations and bibliographies into R7-Office editors, with buttons to refresh them and to unlink citations into plain text. Works with a Zotero API key, or offline through the Zotero desktop app.
r7-consult/plugin-zotero.pain: People writing in R7-Office can cite from Zotero without leaving the editor. A fork of onlyoffice/plugin-zotero adapted for R7-Office.

univaultoffice/plugin-zotero.does: Inserts Zotero citations into UNIVAULTOFFICE editors. You search your Zotero library by author, title or year, choose a style and language, and insert the citation. Needs a Zotero API key.
univaultoffice/plugin-zotero.pain: People writing in UNIVAULTOFFICE can cite from Zotero without leaving the editor. The repository is archived and the plugin has moved to a marketplace repository.

citation-js/plugin-zotero-translation-se.does: A Citation.js plugin that sends web page addresses to a Zotero Translation Server and returns the scraped citation data. It also adds support for Zotero API JSON as an input format.
citation-js/plugin-zotero-translation-se.pain: JavaScript developers can turn a URL into structured citation data without writing scrapers. You can use the default server or run your own.

omeka/plugin-zoteroimport.does: An Omeka Classic plugin that imports Zotero libraries and collections, including items, notes, files and web snapshots. It reads the library's Atom feed and needs a private key for private libraries or attachments.
omeka/plugin-zoteroimport.pain: Lets you move Zotero research into Omeka to organise and exhibit it, with Zotero's fields kept as their own element set.

paleolimbot/rbbt.does: An R package, with RStudio addins, that inserts Zotero citations and BibLaTeX entries into Markdown, R Markdown or LaTeX documents. It talks to the Better BibTeX connector, so Zotero must be running.
paleolimbot/rbbt.pain: R users writing papers can search Zotero and keep the bibliography file in step with the citations in the current document.

windingwind/reader.does: The source code of Zotero's PDF, EPUB and HTML reader and annotator, with build and development steps for web and Zotero builds.
windingwind/reader.pain: For developers who want to modify or test the reader outside Zotero. A fork of zotero/reader; its README doesn't say what it changes.

etshaw-zh/rsscopilot.does: Generates summaries or daily reports from your RSS feeds inside Zotero. Its acknowledgements mention a SQLite vector search extension.
etshaw-zh/rsscopilot.pain: Helps people who follow many feeds in Zotero's feed reader keep up without reading every entry.

achalmed/scripts_for_zotero.does: A set of scripts to paste into Zotero's Run JavaScript window for tidying a library. Only series_organizer is still in use, which sorts items into subcollections and has a dry-run mode. Documentation is in Spanish.
achalmed/scripts_for_zotero.pain: The author retired the other scripts, which cleaned tags and author names, because a Calibre to Zotero sync replaced them. Back up before a real run.

informatics-uiuc/seasr-zotero-plugin.does: An experimental Zotero extension from the University of Illinois informatics group. Its features are not described anywhere in the repository; only the release and signing steps are written down.
informatics-uiuc/seasr-zotero-plugin.pain: Probably of interest only to the group's own project, since no features are documented.

ch-sander/semantic-html.does: A Python library that parses HTML notes into RDF-compatible JSON-LD and RDFa HTML. It needs only lxml, and a Jupyter notebook demonstrates its use.
ch-sander/semantic-html.pain: For people who write Zotero notes as HTML and want to turn them into linked data.

zotero-plugin-dev/setup-zotero.does: A GitHub Action that downloads and sets up Zotero in continuous integration. You choose the version, release channel and platform, and it caches the install and reports the path to the Zotero executable.
zotero-plugin-dev/setup-zotero.pain: Plugin developers can run tests against a real Zotero on Windows, macOS or Linux in CI without scripting the download themselves.

zotero-chinese/styles.does: A collection of Chinese-language CSL citation styles for journals and theses, most derived from GB/T 7714-2015, with a browsable style store. Styles use CSL-M features, so Zotero warns that they are not valid CSL 1.0.2.
zotero-chinese/styles.pain: Chinese journals and universities require specific citation formats that stock Zotero styles don't match. Aimed at Chinese-language research.

l0o0/translators_cn.does: Zotero translators for Chinese academic and other websites, including CNKI, Wanfang and RefWorks exports. It is a community repository maintained apart from the official translators.
l0o0/translators_cn.pain: Official translators for Chinese sites are often old and unmaintained, so saving items from CNKI and similar sites fails. Aimed at Chinese-language research.

liuxiawei/trilium_zotero_plugin.does: Inserts Zotero citations into Trilium Notes through a button or shortcut, in the form (Smith, 2020), and keeps a reference list under a References heading. An export script produces a Word file. Needs Better BibTeX.
liuxiawei/trilium_zotero_plugin.pain: Trilium users can cite from Zotero while writing notes and export finished text with citations resolved.

adam-coates/typora-plugin-zotero.does: Suggests Zotero references in Typora when you type @, and inserts the one you pick. It reads Zotero and Better BibTeX databases directly and adds the entry to a .bib file in your folder. Needs the Typora Community Plugin Framework.
adam-coates/typora-plugin-zotero.pain: Typora users writing in Markdown can cite from their Zotero library without leaving the editor.

zotero-chinese/wiki.does: The source of the Zotero Chinese community's documentation site. It holds user guides, plugin development documentation and Chinese translations of the CSL specification.
zotero-chinese/wiki.pain: Gives Chinese-speaking users and plugin developers Zotero documentation in their own language.

shivams/zim-zotero-plugin.does: A plugin for the Zim desktop wiki that searches your Zotero library and inserts matching items as links. Links can show the Better BibTeX key, the item key or a formatted bibliography entry. Needs the zotxt add-on in Zotero.
shivams/zim-zotero-plugin.pain: Zim users can cite from Zotero while writing wiki pages. The link format changed, and a script converts links from older versions.

folozz/zoclau.does: Embeds Claude Code in the Zotero 7 item pane as a chat panel with streaming replies, conversation history and a picker for local folders. You can mention items with @. Needs the Claude Code CLI installed.
folozz/zoclau.pain: Lets you chat with Claude Code about your reading and local files without leaving Zotero, with permission modes from confirm-first to run-immediately.

jdidion/zooper.does: Fills in missing metadata from a DOI through Crossref, or by scraping an item's URL, and unloads attachments to separate storage and reloads them later. Its developer warns it is incomplete and may not work on recent Zotero.
jdidion/zooper.pain: Helps with items missing metadata and with libraries that outgrow cloud storage. The old item is moved to the trash after an update.

davidswelt/zot_bib_web.does: Generates an interactive, searchable web bibliography from Zotero collections as static files. A Python script reads the collections through the Zotero API and can order by collection, year or type, with BibTeX and EndNote records.
davidswelt/zot_bib_web.pain: Researchers can keep a publication list on their own website, maintained in Zotero, without a database or third-party server.

ka1/zot2indd.does: Lets you cite Zotero references in Adobe InDesign with LaTeX-like \cite{key} syntax and build a linked reference list. It includes two Zotero export translators and an InDesign script. Tested only with Zotero 4.0.11.
ka1/zot2indd.pain: InDesign has no citation support, so designers laying out books or papers otherwise format references by hand.

northword/zotero.does: A fork of the Zotero desktop application's source code. Zotero is a reference manager that collects, organises, cites and shares research sources.
northword/zotero.pain: A fork of zotero/zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

windingwind/zotero.does: A fork of the Zotero desktop application's source code. Zotero is a reference manager that collects, organises, cites and shares research sources.
windingwind/zotero.pain: A fork of zotero/zotero; its README doesn't say what it changes.

ozdemirmelih/zotero-5.0.58-citiation-plu.does: An edited zotero.dotm, the Microsoft Word template for Zotero's Word integration, kept at the last version that works under Wine. Its page gives no further detail.
ozdemirmelih/zotero-5.0.58-citiation-plu.pain: Probably for people running Zotero 5.0.58's Word citation tools through Wine on Linux or macOS, where later versions stopped working.

doitian/zotero-actions-tags-scripts.does: A collection of scripts for the Zotero Actions & Tags plugin by windingwind. Its page gives no detail on what the scripts do.
doitian/zotero-actions-tags-scripts.pain: For users of Actions & Tags who want ready-made scripts to plug into it rather than writing their own.

windingwind/zotero-add-collection-tag.does: Tags a newly saved item with the name of the collection you have selected in Zotero. The tag also goes on the item's attachments, such as the PDF.
windingwind/zotero-add-collection-tag.pain: Items saved with the Zotero Connector otherwise arrive untagged, so you tag by hand to keep collection names as tags. A fork of Zar-rok/Zotero-Add-Collection-Tag; its README doesn't say what it changes.

funkydan2/zotero-addons.does: A set of citation styles (CSL files) based on the Society for Biblical Literature style guide, modified for the requirements of Moore Theological College. A second, experimental version is included.
funkydan2/zotero-addons.pain: For students and writers at Moore Theological College or anyone needing a close variant of SBL style. Its author says the styles don't work perfectly.

sasaju/zotero-ai.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
sasaju/zotero-ai.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet, as the name hints at AI features.

centerofci-archive/zotero-anot8-plugin.does: Opens a PDF from your Zotero library in anot8, an annotation tool. It is built on code from the scite plugin.
centerofci-archive/zotero-anot8-plugin.pain: Lets you move from Zotero to anot8 for a paper without finding and uploading the file yourself.

dchalhub/zotero-autorefresh-addon.does: Updates the metadata of selected items from online DOI and ISBN databases through a right-click menu, and can delete the PDFs of selected items. Progress symbols appear in the Archive field and a menu entry clears them.
dchalhub/zotero-autorefresh-addon.pain: Fixes items with missing or wrong fields in one batch instead of editing each by hand. Its developer says it is a personal project without ongoing support, tested only on Zotero 6.0.26 on Windows 10.

whitewatercn/zotero_awesome_addons.does: A short list of recommended add-ons: Zotero Scihub for automatic PDF downloads, GB/T 7714-2015 citation styles, and the Zotero Night dark theme.
whitewatercn/zotero_awesome_addons.pain: A pointer list for Chinese-speaking users looking for productivity and appearance extras. Sci-Hub distributes copyrighted papers without permission, and using it is illegal in many jurisdictions.

windingwind/zotero-better-bibtex.does: Generates stable citation keys and exports clean BibTeX and BibLaTeX. It converts between Unicode and LaTeX, auto-exports collections or libraries when they change, and offers a pull-export web server and journal abbreviations.
windingwind/zotero-better-bibtex.pain: People writing in LaTeX or Markdown need clash-free keys and clean exports that Zotero's built-in exporter doesn't give. A fork of retorquere/zotero-better-bibtex; its README doesn't say what it changes, and it notes that Zotero 7 beta 70 and later were not yet supported.

muisedestiny/zotero-better-notes.does: Note management inside Zotero. It has a workspace with an outline, links between notes, note templates, two-way sync with Markdown files, and export to Markdown, Docx, PDF and mind maps, plus GPT integration.
muisedestiny/zotero-better-notes.pain: Zotero's note editor has no linking, templates or Markdown sync, which makes building a reading and writing workflow awkward. A fork of windingwind/zotero-better-notes; its README doesn't say what it changes.

jackhanyuan/zotero-better-plugin.does: A curated list of recommended Zotero plugins and links, plus ready-made note templates, Zotero Actions & Tags actions and GPT command tags. Many are aimed at Chinese-language research.
jackhanyuan/zotero-better-plugin.pain: Helps newcomers to Zotero 7, 8 and 9 find and set up a useful plugin collection without searching one by one.

vanakat/zotero-bridge.does: An Obsidian plugin that connects to Zotero and gives other Obsidian plugins an API. It lets them search your library and read item details such as title, authors, date and key.
vanakat/zotero-bridge.pain: Lets Obsidian templates and plugins pull Zotero references without each one building its own connection. Needs Zotero 7's local API enabled, or the ZotServer add-on for Zotero 6.

retorquere/zotero-bulk-mas-import.does: A translator that imports a CSV file of titles by searching each on Microsoft Academic and adding the first hit as a new item. You need a Microsoft Academic Knowledge API key.
retorquere/zotero-bulk-mas-import.pain: Saves looking up a long list of paper titles one at a time. Microsoft Academic has since shut down, so it may no longer work.

ndrsn/zotero-classify-articles.does: Tags journal articles with the discipline of the journal they appeared in, by matching each publication title against a built-in list. For instance, an article gets a tag like Discipline: Social Sciences / Defense.
ndrsn/zotero-classify-articles.pain: Gives a large library a subject breakdown without classifying each paper by hand. Its developers say it was written to meet a deadline and could be improved.

muisedestiny/zotero-connected-papers.does: A Connected Papers integration for Zotero. Its developer says it is not currently open source and asks people not to download it.
muisedestiny/zotero-connected-papers.pain: Probably for exploring related papers from within Zotero; the developer offers a paid closed beta.

retorquere/zotero-devonthink-export.does: A Zotero export translator that saves attachments and notes as files in folders matching your library or collection hierarchy, for use with DEVONthink. You edit a root folder setting in the file first.
retorquere/zotero-devonthink-export.pain: Gets your PDFs and notes into a folder tree that DEVONthink can index. Files are duplicated if an item sits in several collections.

pateljunaid/zotero-extended.does: Adds batch editing of tags (add, remove, rename, merge) and a built-in editor to download, edit and install custom citation styles. Built as a university course project.
pateljunaid/zotero-extended.pain: Tag clean-up in stock Zotero is slow, one tag at a time. It targets the old Zotero 4 and 5 era; its usage section is unwritten.

daidaishengweinan/zotero-file.does: Brings ZotFile's core features to Zotero 7: automatic renaming of attachments and moving them to a folder you choose, with a settings pane. Reads your old ZotFile settings.
daidaishengweinan/zotero-file.pain: ZotFile's author won't update it for Zotero 7. This keeps its renaming and moving, but leaves out the tablet sync.

retorquere/zotero-file-hierarchy.does: A Zotero export translator that saves attachments as files in folders matching your library or collection hierarchy. You pick it from Export Library as File Hierarchy.
retorquere/zotero-file-hierarchy.pain: Gives you a readable folder tree of your PDFs outside Zotero's storage. Files are duplicated if an item belongs to several collections.

dalanicolai/zotero-find.does: An Emacs package that searches the titles and author names of items in your Zotero database and opens the matching file. It uses Ivy or Helm to narrow results.
dalanicolai/zotero-find.pain: Lets Emacs users open papers without switching to Zotero. It cannot run while Zotero is open, as Zotero locks the database, and only finds items that have a parent.

flyingpumba/zotero-folder-size-plugin.does: Adds a Folder Size entry to the collection right-click menu. It adds up the size of every PDF in the collection and its subcollections and shows the total in a popup.
flyingpumba/zotero-folder-size-plugin.pain: Zotero has no way to tell how much disk space a collection uses. It expects the PDFs to be on disk and raises an error if one is missing.

windingwind/zotero-format-metadata.does: Cleans up and standardises item metadata. Features include rich text shortcuts for titles, sentence case conversion, journal abbreviations, university place lookup, language detection and DOI-based filling of volume, issue and pages, and checks for duplicates and wrong item types.
windingwind/zotero-format-metadata.pain: Messy imported fields cause wrong citations, and Zotero offers no easy way to insert formatting tags. A fork of northword/zotero-format-metadata; its README doesn't say what it changes.

dr-kd/zotero-hello-world.does: A minimal example plugin for Zotero with no documented features.
dr-kd/zotero-hello-world.pain: Probably a starting point for learning how Zotero plugins are written.

hiberlink/zotero_hiberlink.does: Archives your references to a web archiving service as you work, with a choice of service and of whether to show original or archive links first. Archived references appear in a table and export as an HTML file.
hiberlink/zotero_hiberlink.pain: Web links in references go dead over time. This archives them proactively without interrupting your usual workflow.

zibrr/zotero-if-pro-max_cracked.does: A modified version of the paid Zotero IF Pro Max plugin with its licence activation removed. It adds a recent-items list, reader shortcut buttons, and a menu item to jump to an item's collection.
zibrr/zotero-if-pro-max_cracked.pain: Aimed at Chinese-language users who want Zotero IF Pro Max without paying. It circumvents a paid licence, which may be unlawful, and its developer claims the original has risky code.

northword/zotero-itemtree-expand.does: Wraps long titles in the library item list so you can read them in full. Its developer says it is in development and not ready for production use.
northword/zotero-itemtree-expand.pain: Long titles are cut off in the item list, forcing you to widen the column or open each item.

xiaoluo-coder/zotero-kg-plugin.does: An early-stage plugin for a knowledge-graph based reference manager; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
xiaoluo-coder/zotero-kg-plugin.pain: Probably aims to help organise literature through a knowledge graph, but nothing is documented yet.

chenyuz-hub/zotero-literature-star-citat.does: Adds a 0 to 5 star importance rating to items, shown in a Star column and set from the item pane. Also previews a bibliography entry in any installed citation style and copies it.
chenyuz-hub/zotero-literature-star-citat.pain: Lets you rank papers by importance and grab a formatted reference quickly. Stars are stored in the Extra field. Alpha release, tested only on Zotero 9.0.6 on Windows.

schuyler/zotero-maps.does: Shows items on an OpenStreetMap map from their Place field, using GeoNames to find coordinates. Choose Actions then View as Map for an item or collection.
schuyler/zotero-maps.pain: Lets you see where your sources are from geographically. Built for the old Firefox-based Zotero; its developer says only about 100 items display at once.

wellsdurant/zotero-md.nvim.does: A Neovim plugin that browses and searches your Zotero library in a Telescope picker and inserts formatted citations into Markdown files. Reads Zotero's local SQLite database.
wellsdurant/zotero-md.nvim.pain: Lets people who write Markdown in Neovim cite papers without leaving the editor. Needs telescope.nvim, plenary.nvim and sqlite3.

sudip-bhujel/zotero-metarefine.does: Repairs and enriches metadata for selected items, creates parent items from PDFs, and finds DOI, PMID, arXiv and ISBN identifiers in fields and PDF text. Falls back to Crossref, OpenAlex, Open Library and arXiv.
sudip-bhujel/zotero-metarefine.pain: Goes beyond plugins that only update from a DOI or ISBN, and records why each item succeeded or failed. No API key needed. It has been removed from its source.

medmouine/zotero-metrics-fetcher-plugin.does: Fetches journal metrics such as SJR, CiteScore and SNIP for publications, including impact factor and ranking figures.
medmouine/zotero-metrics-fetcher-plugin.pain: For researchers who want impact and ranking figures for journals shown next to their items.

automation-scripting/zotero-mirroring-pl.does: Mirrors the hierarchical structure of your Zotero library onto the filesystem, with no further features documented.
automation-scripting/zotero-mirroring-pl.pain: Probably for keeping a folder tree on disk that matches your collections.

windingwind/zotero-night.does: A dark theme for the Zotero interface and its PDF reader, with two PDF colour modes and a quick toggle. It also cleans up the tab bar and adds animations. Based on the Nord colour scheme.
windingwind/zotero-night.pain: Zotero's bright interface is hard on the eyes late at night. Its developer notes that the PDF darkening is slow and some popup menus look wrong. A fork of tefkah/zotero-night; its README doesn't say what it changes.

knowbodynos/zotero-notebooklm-plugin.does: Adds Add to NotebookLM to the item right-click menu, sending the URLs of selected items to a NotebookLM notebook you choose. Needs a Google account, Python 3.10 or later and a local Python server running.
knowbodynos/zotero-notebooklm-plugin.pain: Moving sources from Zotero into NotebookLM otherwise means pasting links by hand. Requires Zotero 8 or higher.

yatli/zotero-onenote-plugin.does: Intended to integrate OneNote with Zotero. Its developer says it is a work in progress and nothing works yet.
yatli/zotero-onenote-plugin.pain: Aims to bring OneNote note-taking into Zotero, but it is blocked on embedding the OneNote web interface.

retorquere/zotero-opds-ts.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
retorquere/zotero-opds-ts.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that serves an OPDS catalogue of your library, but nothing is documented yet.

raabf/zotero-open-with.does: Adds an Open With entry to the right-click menu of attachments so you can open a file in a chosen application instead of the system default.
raabf/zotero-open-with.pain: Zotero opens each file type only in its default app. This lets you send a PDF to a different viewer or editor when you want.

mtillman14/zotero_openalex_plugin.does: Finds the OpenAlex work ID of selected items, using the DOI if there is one and otherwise the title and publication year.
mtillman14/zotero_openalex_plugin.pain: Useful for linking your library to OpenAlex records for citation and metadata lookups.

xtdzs/zotero-pagewise-import-tool.does: A separate crawler tool that collects every paper on an arXiv search results page. It copies their identifiers to the clipboard, ready to paste into Zotero's Add Item by Identifier.
xtdzs/zotero-pagewise-import-tool.pain: The Zotero Connector in Edge imports only a few of the fifty papers on an arXiv search page. This gets them all. Available in English and Chinese.

muisedestiny/zotero-pdf-preview.does: Previews PDF attachment pages in the item pane, either under the Info tab or in its own Preview tab. Settings control the pages shown, annotations, dark mode and zoom shortcuts.
muisedestiny/zotero-pdf-preview.pain: You can see a paper's pages without opening the reader. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-preview; its README doesn't say what it changes.

muisedestiny/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader using 20+ services. It also translates item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, and has a dictionary for single words and a standalone comparison window.
muisedestiny/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading in a second language means copying text into a translation site. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate for Zotero 6; its README doesn't say what it changes.

volatile-static/zotero-pdf-translate.does: Translates text you select in the PDF reader using 20+ services. It also translates item titles, abstracts, annotations and notes, and has a dictionary for single words and a standalone comparison window.
volatile-static/zotero-pdf-translate.pain: Reading in a second language means copying text into a translation site. A fork of windingwind/zotero-pdf-translate; its README doesn't say what it changes.

dianzuan/zotero-pdf2md.does: Converts PDF attachments to Markdown with OCR or vision-model services: GLM-OCR, Mistral OCR, Qwen-VL, Gemini Flash, or local MinerU and Marker. Saves the result as a child attachment and maps highlights into it.
dianzuan/zotero-pdf2md.pain: PDFs with formulas, tables and multiple columns are hard to reuse as text. Early development, and cloud backends need their own API keys.

zotero-plugin-dev/zotero-pdfjs-types.does: TypeScript type definitions for Zotero's fork of pdf.js, generated daily from Zotero's latest source. It is a developer resource, not a feature for end users.
zotero-plugin-dev/zotero-pdfjs-types.pain: Plugin developers who work with the PDF reader get type checking. It is already included in the zotero-types package.

retorquere/zotero-pkg.does: Packages Zotero and Juris-M for Debian-based Linux, including Chromebooks with Crostini, through an apt repository, plus a nightly zotero-beta package. Also offers experimental Nix packages.
retorquere/zotero-pkg.pain: Zotero offers only a tarball for Linux, so there is no system-wide install or updates through the package manager. These packages track new releases within about 30 minutes.

demonwu/zotero-plugin.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
demonwu/zotero-plugin.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

eranhirs/zotero-plugin.does: Searches Zotero for a tag when you click it while holding Alt, and adds a new tag when you press Ctrl+N. You build the XPI yourself with the included create_xpi.sh script.
eranhirs/zotero-plugin.pain: Stock Zotero has no quick keyboard route to tag an item or to jump from a tag to matching items. Someone who tags heavily would use this.

junaidsarfraz/zotero-plugin.does: A mirror of the original Zotero source code, exported from the old Google Code project. It is the Zotero application itself rather than an add-on with its own features.
junaidsarfraz/zotero-plugin.pain: Mostly of historical interest: an archived copy of early Zotero code, with no plugin functions of its own.

lplalbert/zotero_plugin.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
lplalbert/zotero_plugin.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

retorquere/zotero-plugin.does: Developer scripts that release Zotero plugins from GitHub Actions. Tagged builds become releases, and branch builds go to a pre-release and are announced on an issue. Also adds a Help menu entry for sending a plugin debug log.
retorquere/zotero-plugin.pain: Plugin authors otherwise publish builds and collect users' debug logs by hand. This is a tool for developers, not for Zotero users.

jonecorreia/zotero-plugin-1.does: An early-stage first plugin for Zotero by a Portuguese-speaking author; no feature description is provided.
jonecorreia/zotero-plugin-1.pain: Probably a learning project; nothing in it says what problem it solves.

z2332677/zotero-plugin-affiliation-extra.does: Extracts and standardises author affiliation information from academic papers in your library.
z2332677/zotero-plugin-affiliation-extra.pain: Affiliations are written inconsistently across papers, so analysing where research comes from means cleaning them up by hand. How it works is undocumented.

tanjxzzz/zotero-plugin-aireader.does: An early-stage plugin, apparently for AI-assisted reading; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
tanjxzzz/zotero-plugin-aireader.pain: Probably a starting point for an AI reading tool that hasn't been written yet.

sunfire-chris/zotero-plugin-annotation-e.does: An early-stage plugin, apparently for improving PDF annotations; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
sunfire-chris/zotero-plugin-annotation-e.pain: Probably a starting point for an annotation tool that hasn't been written yet.

lyrad913/zotero-plugin-assistant.does: An early-stage plugin, apparently an assistant for Zotero; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
lyrad913/zotero-plugin-assistant.pain: Probably a starting point for an assistant that hasn't been written yet.

liupy525/zotero-plugin-dr-can.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
liupy525/zotero-plugin-dr-can.pain: Probably a starting point for a plugin that hasn't been written yet.

mistobaan/zotero-plugin-explain-this.does: Lets you select text and ask an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to explain it. Its README is still the template's, so settings and usage are not documented.
mistobaan/zotero-plugin-explain-this.pain: Explaining a hard passage otherwise means copying it into a chatbot. This aims to do it from inside Zotero, though it is early-stage.

annefou/zotero-plugin-nanopub.does: Adds support for nanopublications to Zotero 8 and later. Its features are not documented.
annefou/zotero-plugin-nanopub.pain: Aimed at researchers who publish or cite machine-readable assertions as nanopublications alongside their references.

dawaltconley/zotero-plugin-pinenote.does: Adjusts Zotero to work well on Pine64's PineNote e-ink tablet. The specific changes are not documented; the repository holds a personal Zotero 7 plugin template.
dawaltconley/zotero-plugin-pinenote.pain: Zotero's interface is not designed for a slow e-ink screen, so reading papers on the PineNote needs tweaks like these.

shaw9379/zotero-plugin-search.does: An early-stage plugin that appears to search Wikipedia and Baidu from Zotero; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
shaw9379/zotero-plugin-search.pain: Probably meant for quick web lookups without leaving Zotero, though it is not yet documented.

ronces/zotero-plugin-test-.does: A French author's test of Zotero plugin development; its README is still the template's and documents no features yet.
ronces/zotero-plugin-test-.pain: A practice project, not a tool with its own features.

windingwind/zotero-plugin-toolkit.does: An npm package of helper APIs for Zotero plugin developers: building menus, columns, dialogs, prompts and more. Supports Zotero 7 and 8 and is used by the plugin template.
windingwind/zotero-plugin-toolkit.pain: Zotero's own plugin APIs are low-level and change between versions. This gives developers ready-made wrappers; it has no use for ordinary Zotero users.

inertia42/zotero-plugins.does: A repository of the author's private Zotero plugins. Nothing more is documented about what they do.
inertia42/zotero-plugins.pain: A personal collection, not a single documented plugin.

jiyeonnn0502/zotero-plugins.does: A parent repository for managing the source code of several Zotero plugins, according to its Chinese description.
jiyeonnn0502/zotero-plugins.pain: A collection of plugin sources for developers rather than one plugin with its own features.

kaqijiang/zotero-plugins.does: A collection of modified Zotero plugins, including settings for a Semantic Scholar API and an AI API key. The details are undocumented.
kaqijiang/zotero-plugins.pain: A personal set of tweaked plugins, apparently adding AI and Semantic Scholar features.

snowingwolf/zotero_plugins.does: A repository for storing Zotero plugins, according to its Chinese description. Nothing more is documented.
snowingwolf/zotero_plugins.pain: A personal file store rather than a plugin with documented features.

xiayouran/zotero-plugins.does: A collection of Zotero plugins gathered in one repository, according to its Chinese description.
xiayouran/zotero-plugins.pain: Saves hunting for several plugins separately, but it is not a plugin with features of its own.

luascfl/zotero-plugins-6.0.36-or-7.does: A collection of plugin files that work on Zotero 6.0.36, the last Zotero 6 release, or on Zotero 7. It has been removed and is undocumented.
luascfl/zotero-plugins-6.0.36-or-7.pain: For people who stayed on old Zotero 6 and wanted plugins that still run there.

dandandanshifu/zotero-plugins-collect.does: A collection of frequently used Zotero plugins from 2019, including ZotFile, ShortDOI, Zotero Scholar Citations, Zotero Storage Scanner and Zotero Autofetch.
dandandanshifu/zotero-plugins-collect.pain: A convenient download list for people setting up an older Zotero, though the bundled versions are from 2019.

qiuhan-star/zotero-plugins-collection.does: A repository for storing various Zotero plugins so they are easy to manage and find. Nothing more is documented.
qiuhan-star/zotero-plugins-collection.pain: A personal archive of plugin files, not a plugin with its own features.

corajr/zotero-prevent-duplicates.does: Checks for a matching item when you import and asks you to confirm before adding it. It looks for the same DOI, the same URL, or the same title and first author surname.
corajr/zotero-prevent-duplicates.pain: Duplicates pile up when Zotero only finds them afterwards. This stops them at import, but items sent from browser connectors bypass the check. Unmaintained, and built for old Zotero.

aziff90/zotero-rag-plugin.does: Chat with selected PDFs and items in a NotebookLM style: it reads their text, builds embeddings locally and answers from them with source citations. Needs an API key for Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic, or a local Ollama model.
aziff90/zotero-rag-plugin.pain: Asking questions across several papers otherwise means pasting text into a chatbot. This keeps answers tied to the sources you chose. Built for Zotero 7.

ch-sander/zotero_rdf_server.does: A server that loads several Zotero libraries into an RDF graph and exposes a local SPARQL endpoint with a visual query builder. Exports the graph, converts RDF in notes and imports or exports CSV. Needs a Zotero cloud library and API key.
ch-sander/zotero_rdf_server.pain: Zotero can't search across libraries or treat creators, places and tags as linked entities. This is for digital humanities and linked-data work.

retorquere/zotero-safetylit-mods.does: Adds a SafetyLit MODS export format to Zotero. Install the translator file in the translators folder, restart, then choose it in the Export dialog.
retorquere/zotero-safetylit-mods.pain: For researchers who need to send references to SafetyLit in its MODS format, which Zotero does not offer.

beloglazov/zotero-scholar-citations.does: Fetches the number of citations for your items from Google Scholar, stores it in the Extra field and lets you sort by it. Updates can be run in batches to refresh the counts.
beloglazov/zotero-scholar-citations.pain: Zotero has no citation count field. Google Scholar may block many automated requests and asks you to solve a captcha. For old Zotero versions.

thalient-ai/zotero-scripts.does: Scripts for bulk and batch work in Zotero 7. They edit fields and tags, rename attachments, merge duplicates, detect similar author names and change title case. Run them in the Run JavaScript tool or the Actions and Tags plugin.
thalient-ai/zotero-scripts.pain: Zotero has no bulk editing for many fields and tags. These scripts handle large libraries in one pass.

retorquere/zotero-seektable-export.does: A CSV export format for Zotero that outputs a permutation of each item's tags, collections and creators. The delimiter used when bundling tags is set by a hidden preference.
retorquere/zotero-seektable-export.pain: For people who feed Zotero data into SeekTable, which needs one row for each combination.

zhilu1/zotero-splitview-multiver-plugin.does: A copy of the Zotero plugin template with no documented features of its own.
zhilu1/zotero-splitview-multiver-plugin.pain: Probably a starting point for a split view plugin that hasn't been written yet.

chi-kai/zotero-tabs-group.does: A plugin for grouping open tabs in Zotero's tab bar. Its documentation is still the plugin template's, so how it works is not described.
chi-kai/zotero-tabs-group.pain: Many open PDFs make the tab bar hard to manage, and grouping them is the apparent aim. It is early-stage.

muisedestiny/zotero-tag.does: Manages tags with custom rules, such as adding /unread to new items and removing it once read. Also batch-edits tags from the right-click menu, imports and exports tags as CSV, and uses Alt+1 to 9 as shortcuts.
muisedestiny/zotero-tag.pain: Zotero has no automatic tagging or batch tag rules. A fork of windingwind/zotero-actions-tags; its README doesn't say what it changes.

retorquere/zotero-thebrain-export.does: Exports your Zotero items in a format that TheBrain can import.
retorquere/zotero-thebrain-export.pain: People who map their notes in TheBrain otherwise have to rebuild their references there.

tiderfang/zotero-toreadlists-plugin.does: Aims to create reading to-do lists inside Zotero. Its README is still the template's, so features are not documented.
tiderfang/zotero-toreadlists-plugin.pain: Collecting many books in Zotero makes it easy to lose track of what to read. A reading plan list gives you a focus.

windingwind/zotero-types.does: TypeScript type definitions for Zotero, installed with npm install for plugin development.
windingwind/zotero-types.pain: Zotero is written in JavaScript, so plugin authors get no editor hints or type checks without these. This is for developers, not Zotero users.

muisedestiny/zotero-types.does: TypeScript type definitions for Zotero plugin development, installed from npm. A fork of windingwind/zotero-types; its README doesn't say what it changes.
muisedestiny/zotero-types.pain: Gives plugin authors editor hints and type checks for Zotero's JavaScript code.

windingwind/zotero-updateifse.does: Fetches journal rankings from easyScholar and saves them to the Extra field. Covers JCR and CAS quartiles, impact factors, SSCI and Chinese core journal lists. Also bolds authors and updates abbreviations. Needs an easyScholar key.
windingwind/zotero-updateifse.pain: Looking up journal rankings by hand is slow, and mostly useful to Chinese researchers. This is the easyScholar edition of Green Frog, a fork of redleafnew/zotero-updateifsE; its README doesn't say what it changes.

haotruongnhat/zotero-useful-plugins.does: A reading list of recommended Zotero add-ons: ZotFile, Better Notes, PDF Preview, Reference, Style and Tag.
haotruongnhat/zotero-useful-plugins.pain: Saves new users searching for a good starting set of plugins. It is not a plugin itself.

xianwenchen/zotero-word-for-wine-linux-i.does: Provides a modified Zotero.dotm so Microsoft Word running under Wine on Linux can talk to standalone Zotero. You copy the file matching your Zotero version into Word's startup folder.
xianwenchen/zotero-word-for-wine-linux-i.pain: Zotero has no Word plugin for Linux, so people running Word under Wine need this workaround to insert citations.

whiskium/zotero_word_plugin_zh-cn.does: Translates the Zotero Word plugin's toolbar into Chinese, covering Add/Edit Citation, Bibliography, Refresh and Unlink Citations. You replace the customUI.xml inside Zotero.dotm.
whiskium/zotero_word_plugin_zh-cn.pain: For Chinese-speaking users who want the Word toolbar labels to match their interface language.

l0o0/zotero-wps.does: Connects the WPS Office word processor to Zotero for inserting citations. This version, modified by wangrui5015, works with current WPS on Windows, Linux and macOS.
l0o0/zotero-wps.pain: The original tankwyn version only worked with older WPS on Windows and Linux. This is for Chinese-speaking researchers who write in WPS rather than Microsoft Word.

ntu-ncs-lab/zoterocitationplugin.does: A thesis-writing setup for Microsoft Word. It supplies an NCSLab citation style for Zotero, then you add citations and a bibliography through Zotero's Word toolbar.
ntu-ncs-lab/zoterocitationplugin.pain: For students at the NCS lab who need their thesis citations to follow one house style. Its developer lists a known issue with line breaks in the bibliography.

inserm-cri-lbi/zoterokeywordsgraphvisual.does: A proof of concept for a clickable network graph of your Zotero keywords, linked by how often they occur together. It currently works from an exported CSV, converted with a Python script and drawn with d3.
inserm-cri-lbi/zoterokeywordsgraphvisual.pain: A long tag list is hard to browse in Zotero's tag selector. This aims to turn it into an interactive keyword map; running inside Zotero is still on the to-do list.

l0o0/zoteroplugins.does: A list of Zotero plugins for the Chinese Zotero community, with a bot that reads a sources file daily and downloads each plugin's latest package. Its maintainer has stopped updating it in favour of a newer directory.
l0o0/zoteroplugins.pain: Gave Chinese-language users one place to find plugins that Zotero itself doesn't list. It is no longer maintained.

muisedestiny/zoteroplugins.does: A collection of Zotero plugins, with a bot that reads a sources file daily and downloads each plugin's latest package. Contributors add a plugin by listing its name, description and repository.
muisedestiny/zoteroplugins.pain: A fork of l0o0/ZoteroPlugins; its README doesn't say what it changes. It gives Chinese-language users one place to find plugins.

saona-raimundo/zoteroplugins.does: A guide to developing Zotero plugins, for people who want to write their own. No further detail is given.
saona-raimundo/zoteroplugins.pain: For developers who want to learn how to write a Zotero plugin.

zoroaster1x/zoteroplus.does: Adds a citation sidebar to OnlyOffice Desktop Editors. It has the six LibreOffice-style actions: add or edit citation, add note, bibliography, refresh, document preferences and unlink.
zoroaster1x/zoteroplus.pain: OnlyOffice's own Zotero plugin brings deleted citations back on refresh and needs Zotero's local API enabled. This tracks deletions, keeps the bibliography in sync and can use local Zotero or a web API key.

windingwind/zoterostyle.does: Restyles Zotero's item list: right-aligns tags as circles, adds a button that shows only titles, and shades titles by how long you have read each page. Also adds a settings panel for colours and fields.
windingwind/zoterostyle.pain: Items with different numbers of tags look uneven and push titles out of view. A fork of MuiseDestiny/zotero-style; the plugin is documented in Chinese.

janvogt/zoterosublime.does: A Sublime Text package for citing from Zotero. It reads your library through the Zotero web API for Markdown (converted with Pandoc) or LaTeX cite keys, and writes a matching .bib file.
janvogt/zoterosublime.pain: For writers who work in a text editor and want references from Zotero without leaving it. Its developer says it is in early development and has undocumented conventions.

l0o0/zotfile.does: The classic attachment manager. Renames and moves PDFs into a custom folder, attaches new downloads, syncs PDFs to a tablet reader and extracts highlighted text and annotations.
l0o0/zotfile.pain: A fork of jlegewie/zotfile; its README doesn't say what it changes. The original solved file clutter and mobile reading for Zotero 5 and earlier.

deanishe/zothero.does: An Alfred workflow that searches your Zotero database as you type and copies formatted citations in any CSL style you have installed. It also copies Better BibTeX citekeys and opens items or attachments.
deanishe/zothero.pain: For macOS users who cite while writing in other apps. They can find a reference and paste it into Word or a Markdown file without opening Zotero. Needs Alfred 4 or later.

peumartino/zotif.does: Reads a CSV file of journal names, abbreviations and impact factors, and writes the matching value into each selected item's Extra field. You choose the file in the add-on's preferences.
peumartino/zotif.pain: Zotero has no impact factor field, so you can't show it in citations or sort by it. The value can be used in a citation style, and you can match other fields.

katieseaborn/zotpress.does: A WordPress plugin, not a Zotero add-on, that shows your Zotero items on a site. Shortcodes in posts or pages give in-text citations, bibliographies and searchable libraries.
katieseaborn/zotpress.pain: For academics who blog or keep a publications page and want it to follow their Zotero library. Needs your Zotero API details. Its developer says updates come one to three times a year.

plandes/zotsite.does: A Python tool, not a Zotero add-on, that exports your library to a stand-alone website. It has a navigation tree, search, and viewers for PDFs, snapshots and notes. Needs Better BibTeX.
plandes/zotsite.pain: Zotero has no built-in way to share a browsable copy of your library on the web. This builds a static site you can publish, and can export only collections matching a pattern.
